article_content: At the start of 2008, Hillary Clinton appeared to be the frontrunner in the presidential race. She had substantial campaign funds, important endorsements, experience, and the prominent Clinton name. Many expected Bill Clinton to return to the White House as the first gentleman. However, Barack Obama, then a first-term senator from Illinois, surprised observers by defeating Hillary in the Iowa caucuses, dramatically changing the course of the campaign. Bill Clinton was initially stunned by Obama's rapid rise, viewing him as an obstacle to his wife's path to the presidency. The 2008 race brought considerable tension between Bill Clinton and Obama. Clinton felt Obama had denied Hillary the opportunity to become president and believed Obama played the 'race card.' In reality, criticism mounted when Bill Clinton publicly compared Obama's victory in the South Carolina primary to Jesse Jackson's wins there in previous years. Many interpreted this as an attempt to label Obama as 'the black candidate,' leading to backlash, especially among African-American voters, who had long supported Clinton. Obama also contrasted himself with Bill Clinton by comparing the impact of his presidency with that of Ronald Reagan, claiming Reagan 'changed the trajectory' of the nation in greater ways than Clinton had. This comparison irritated Bill Clinton, as Reagan was a leading figure in the opposing party. Obama’s approach challenged the Clintons' campaign in several ways, including criticisms about Hillary’s stance on the Iraq War and other issues. Some felt that Obama received more favorable media coverage compared to the scrutiny Bill Clinton had faced in past campaigns. Once Hillary Clinton lost the nomination, she moved past any disagreements with Obama, soon becoming his Secretary of State. However, insiders suggest that Bill Clinton held onto his frustration, and his relationship with Obama remained cool well into Obama’s presidency. In contrast, Bill Clinton maintained a noticeably warmer relationship with Presidents George H.W. and George W. Bush, as their political roles did not compete. Eventually, shared interests brought Bill Clinton and Obama together, especially as Obama sought Clinton's support to connect with working-class and white voters, groups that had strongly identified with Clinton's approach. Clinton, meanwhile, remained eager to play a significant role in Democratic politics. In his post-presidency, Clinton had achieved public recognition for his humanitarian work and gave well-compensated speeches, but influencing elections remained his passion. If Hillary Clinton decided to run for president again in 2016, Bill's political connections could prove valuable. Bill Clinton also provided Obama with campaign advice, particularly on focusing his critique of Mitt Romney’s conservative positions rather than on inconsistencies, drawing from Clinton’s own strategy during the 1996 campaign against the Republican-led Congress and Speaker Newt Gingrich. This approach helped Clinton win re-election after the 1994 Republican midterm victories. During the 1995 government shutdown, Clinton’s team successfully portrayed his opponents as extreme, contributing to Bob Dole’s election defeat. Obama now had an opportunity to position himself as a centrist versus a perceived radical Republican opposition. The piece concludes by recommending that Obama heed Bill Clinton’s advice. The opinions in this commentary are solely those of Michael Takiff.

According to Engadget, the PlayStation Phone features 512 MB of RAM, 1 GB of ROM, a Qualcomm MSM8655 Snapdragon 1GHz chip, a multitouch touchpad, trigger buttons, and support for microSD cards. The device is being developed by Sony Ericsson. As the Android-based gaming phone is still a prototype, it is unlikely to launch before the end of the year and is expected in the first or second quarter of 2011. Enthusiasts are eager to see if the PlayStation Phone can transform Android into a gaming powerhouse like the iPhone or whether it will face a fate similar to Nokia's N-Gage.

article_content: The Sirena 78 made its world debut at the recent Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show, rather than at a European event closer to its Turkish shipyard. This decision highlights both Turkey's emerging reputation for high-quality yet cost-effective yacht construction and the strength of demand for yachts in the United States. Sirena Yachts is among the shipyards showcasing the benefits of Turkish craftsmanship and investment. "This is the first time we're showcasing this exciting model in the US," said Constantinos K. Constantinou, Head of Sirena Yachts USA. "I'm confident our clients will appreciate the Sirena 78 for its innovation and unique features, including an open-plan main deck unrivaled in its size category, a versatile flybridge, spacious accommodations, and an advanced hull design for efficient, high-performance cruising." The Sirena 78 is noted for its spacious and airy interior layouts, which offer excellent views and ample relaxation areas by moving the helm station from the main deck and providing owners with flexible, movable furniture options. Owners can choose from three interior décor themes created by Cor D Rover: Inspiration (light and airy), Serenity (warm, with honey-toned wood and semi-gloss lacquer), or Elegance (dark wood and anthracite for a sophisticated yet inviting look). Below the waterline, the Sirena 78 features a semi-displacement hull designed by the renowned naval architect German Frers, building upon the proven geometry of the 68 model. The yacht offers various power options, a maximum speed of 27 knots, and a cruising range of 1,550 nautical miles at 10 knots. This is the sixth model designed by Frers for Sirena Marine, a brand recognized for excellent workmanship and outstanding value.

article_content: An Egyptian TV channel dedicated to broadcasting belly-dancing clips 24 hours a day, called al-Tet, has been ordered off the air for operating without a license and airing advertisements said to 'arouse viewers.' The channel, which often shows women in revealing costumes, was also accused by an Egyptian court of promoting matchmaking services and advertising sexual-enhancement products. However, the channel's director, Baleegh Hamdy, denies the allegations and claims the station does not air unapproved sexual product ads, asserting that al-Tet is being unfairly targeted as similar advertisements are shown on over 150 other Egyptian channels. After Noorsat, a Bahraini satellite provider, ceased broadcasting al-Tet following the court's decision, Hamdy maintained that the channel had the necessary broadcasting license with Noorsat. Despite this setback, he plans to launch new channels, including 'Bom Tak' and a YouTube platform, both of which will feature belly-dancing content. Al-Tet began operation after Egypt's 2011 uprising against then-president Hosni Mubarak, and now also broadcasts in the United States and Canada; the channel's owner is believed to be American. A spokesman for Egypt’s Muslim Brotherhood welcomed the court’s decision, stating that the judicial system can help protect societal values shared by both Muslims and Christians.

La chaîne, qui montre fréquemment des femmes en costumes révélateurs, a également été accusée par un tribunal égyptien de promouvoir des services de rencontres et d’annoncer des produits pour améliorer la performance sexuelle. Cependant, le directeur Baleegh Hamdy réfute ces accusations, affirmant qu’al-Tet ne diffuse pas de publicités non autorisées pour des produits sexuels et qu’elle est injustement ciblée puisque plus de 150 autres chaînes égyptiennes diffusent des publicités similaires. Après la décision du tribunal, Noorsat, un fournisseur de satellite basé à Bahreïn, a arrêté la diffusion d’al-Tet, mais Hamdy affirme que la chaîne détenait la licence requise. Malgré ce revers, il prévoit de lancer de nouvelles chaînes, comme « Bom Tak », et une chaîne YouTube proposant également de la danse du ventre. Al-Tet a vu le jour après le soulèvement de 2011 contre Hosni Moubarak et diffuse maintenant aussi aux États-Unis et au Canada ; le propriétaire de la chaîne serait américain. Un porte-parole des Frères musulmans a salué la décision, estimant que la justice contribue à préserver des valeurs communes aux musulmans et aux chrétiens.

article_content: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) released an Airworthiness Directive for Boeing's 787-8 Dreamliner on Thursday, outlining the necessary steps for these aircraft to return to service following battery problems that caused a global grounding earlier this year. The directive takes effect upon its publication in the Federal Register and mandates that 787s can only resume flights after agency-supervised modifications and inspections. United Airlines—the only U.S. airline currently operating the Dreamliner with six aircraft—intends to restart flights with the 787 in May and has allocated about $2.8 million for the required fixes. FAA spokesman Les Dorr stated that each plane must pass FAA inspection before being deemed compliant. Nearly 50 Dreamliners worldwide have been grounded for over three months due to battery safety incidents on Japanese-operated jets. The aircraft's lightweight composite materials and improved fuel economy make it especially popular for long-haul routes in Asia and the Middle East. United is developing plans to return the Dreamliners to service and considering launching the Denver-Narita (Japan) route as early as June 10. United spokeswoman Christen David called the FAA action an important step forward. Meanwhile, Boeing is sending specialized teams to support repairs and retrofits, according to spokesman Marc Birtel, who underscored the significance of the FAA’s directive. The FAA's order requires installation of new main and auxiliary battery enclosures, environmental control ducts, and replacement of the main battery, auxiliary power unit battery, and their chargers. After these updates, airlines and relevant regulatory authorities will determine when each 787 can return to operation. Though the FAA mandate applies only to U.S. airlines, international regulators are expected to consider adopting similar measures. Boeing CEO Jim McNerney indicated that the company has already started retrofits on 10 in-service planes and nine still being built, aiming to finish most upgrades and resume deliveries by mid-May.

article_content: A promising new medication derived from Norwegian seaweed could become an effective treatment for cystic fibrosis (CF), a serious genetic disease. The drug, OligoG, contains a highly purified form of alginate—an ingredient already found in some heartburn medicines and food thickeners—which helps break down the thick, sticky mucus typical of CF. Untreated, this mucus causes digestive problems and makes the lungs more vulnerable to severe bacterial infections, which are the main cause of death for most CF patients. OligoG is inhaled much like some asthma medications. In a recent British trial with 26 patients, it was found to be safe and showed no side effects. More studies are needed, but if results remain positive, the drug could become available within three years. Ed Owen, chief executive of the Cystic Fibrosis Trust in the UK, said, 'This discovery promises hope to thousands of families desperate for improved treatments for CF. While life expectancy has improved, it's concerning that half of patients still don't reach their 40th birthday.' The research was announced by AlgiPharma at the European Cystic Fibrosis Society conference in Gothenburg, Sweden, and was conducted with UK and Irish hospitals. Over 10,000 Britons have CF, 70% of whom are adults. On average, they can now expect to live to 41, a dramatic improvement compared to 60 years ago when most didn't survive past age ten. Recent advances, including better drugs and routine infant screening, have further increased life expectancy. CF is primarily caused by a faulty gene that disrupts fluid transport in cell membranes, leading to blockages in various organs. Treatment usually involves a combination of medications to manage complications. OligoG works by binding to calcium in the mucus, thinning it so it can be cleared more easily. This may help reduce lung damage and the frequency of infections, potentially decreasing reliance on antibiotics as drug-resistant bacteria become a bigger concern. Anna Ermund, a researcher from the University of Gothenburg, described OligoG as 'a unique drug and the first of its kind.' Other recent treatments include Kalydeco, a drug targeting the genetic root of CF. Kalydeco is very expensive and only benefits a small percentage of CF patients. The NHS has negotiated a lower price for eligible British patients. Several new treatments are in trials, with some combinations showing hopeful results. It is not yet clear how much OligoG will cost, but experts hope it could complement other drugs in patients’ treatment regimens. Dr Janet Allen, research director at the Cystic Fibrosis Trust, said, 'We're not talking about a cure, but there is real potential for CF to become a manageable illness similar to type 1 diabetes.'

article_content: Sharad Pawar, president of the Nationalist Congress Party, felt unwell during a meeting in his hometown of Baramati, Maharashtra’s Pune district. According to party sources, doctors immediately examined Pawar and advised him to rest. The 82-year-old leader was in Baramati for Diwali, attending an event at Vidya Pratishthan, a trust managed by his family. His scheduled visit to Purandar in Pune district on Sunday was canceled due to his health. Elsewhere, Indian companies are celebrating Diwali by gifting employees—including third-party blue-collar workers—items such as hampers, sustainable products, electronics, and silver coins, aiming to boost festive morale. Meanwhile, several Indian businesses in banking, healthcare, and telecom sectors are concerned that a new data law may limit their ability to cross-sell products using customer data, according to legal experts. On the international front, Moody’s has revised its outlook on the US credit rating from ‘stable’ to ‘negative’, citing large fiscal deficits and declining debt affordability. The Biden administration quickly criticized the move.

article_content: Steve Smith aims to lead by example as he takes over as Australia’s Test captain, following Michael Clarke’s injury. At 25, Smith was promoted to vice-captain on Monday and selected to captain the team ahead of veteran Brad Haddin for the second Test against India in Brisbane on Wednesday. Cricket Australia indicated this decision reflects a focus on the future, given the uncertainty surrounding Clarke’s long-term fitness. Smith is now the third youngest player in the squad to play at the Gabba and becomes Australia’s youngest Test captain since Kim Hughes in the 1970s. He has assured that his approach to the game will not change due to the added responsibility. Smith will lead Australia for the remainder of the Test series against India. He and teammates, including Ryan Harris, prepared at the Gabba ahead of the match. Smith was also seen practicing with Josh Hazelwood and sharing a light moment with Mitchell Johnson during training. Speaking to the media, Smith said, 'First and foremost, I’ll try to lead from the front with my performances. Our on-field tactics have been strong this year under 'Pup' (Clarke).' He added that he sees no need for major changes. Despite not being in the squad at the start of the previous year, Smith has established himself as a leading batsman, highlighted by his unbeaten scores of 162 and 52 in Australia’s 48-run victory over India in the first Test, taking his Test average to 46.03. Smith described the past 18 months as a 'whirlwind' and expressed excitement about leading Australia in a Test match, saying it was a dream come true. Smith has previous captaincy experience with New South Wales and the Sydney Sixers, and he is confident in stepping up to Test level with the support of senior players. He frequently discusses on-field strategy with Clarke and Haddin. For now, Smith has been confirmed as captain for the three remaining Tests against India. Haddin, who previously served as Clarke’s vice-captain and briefly captained when Clarke was injured, will serve as Smith’s vice-captain for this series. Clarke has expressed doubt about his future in cricket due to ongoing injuries. Cricket Australia sees Smith’s appointment as a step toward securing leadership longer-term. Pat Howard, head of team performance, noted that Clarke's injury influenced the decision. Smith shared that Haddin was supportive of his appointment and that he will look to Haddin for guidance on the field, appreciating his experience and cricketing acumen.

Smith a qualifié les 18 derniers mois de « tourbillon » et a exprimé son enthousiasme à l’idée de diriger l’Australie lors d’un match de Test, affirmant que c’est un rêve devenu réalité. article_content: Prince William of Britain will begin a two-month assignment with the Royal Navy on Monday, as part of his ongoing training across the military, the Ministry of Defense announced. At 25, the prince will start with a basic sea safety course, which covers sea survival, firefighting, and ship damage repair. Upon passing, William is expected to join HMS Iron Duke in the Caribbean, where the ship assists British territories during hurricanes and conducts counter-narcotics operations. During his stint, he will be known as Sub Lieutenant Wales and will serve aboard a frigate, a mine hunter, a submarine, and helicopters, with his assignment ending August 1. Earlier this year, Prince William spent four months attached to the Royal Air Force, earning his pilot's wings in April and learning to fly three different aircraft. Within the RAF, he is known as Flying Officer Wales. He also holds a position as second lieutenant in the Army's Blues and Royals regiment. These military experiences are intended to prepare him for his future role as the head of the armed forces. Rear Admiral Bob Cooling noted, 'When he becomes king, he needs to instinctively know his armed forces, so he is participating in this Royal Navy assignment.' The royal family has a longstanding history with the military: Prince Charles served five years in the navy in the 1970s and commanded HMS Bronington; Prince Andrew served 22 years, including active duty in the Falklands War; and Prince Philip, William’s grandfather, spent over 13 years in the navy, serving throughout World War II and present at Japan’s surrender in Tokyo Harbor.

Pendant sa mission, il sera appelé sous-lieutenant Wales et servira à bord d’une frégate, d’un chasseur de mines, d’un sous-marin et d’hélicoptères. Sa mission se terminera le 1er août. L’amiral Bob Cooling a souligné : « Lorsqu’il deviendra roi, il devra instinctivement bien connaître ses forces armées ; c’est pourquoi il effectue cette mission avec la Royal Navy. » La famille royale a une longue tradition militaire : le prince Charles a servi cinq ans dans la marine dans les années 1970 et a commandé le HMS Bronington ; le prince Andrew a servi 22 ans, notamment pendant la guerre des Malouines ; et le prince Philip, grand-père de William, a passé plus de 13 ans dans la marine, servant pendant toute la Seconde Guerre mondiale et étant présent à Tokyo lors de la capitulation du Japon.

article_content:
South Korea intends to ban the consumption of dog meat by 2027, aiming to resolve long-standing controversy over the practice as awareness of animal protection grows. On Friday, government officials and the ruling People Power Party announced plans to introduce legislation before the end of the year to end dog meat consumption by 2027. The tradition of eating dog in Korea has drawn international criticism and is facing mounting opposition domestically, particularly from younger generations.

Yu Eui-dong, policy chief of the People Power Party, stated at a meeting with government officials and animal protection activists, "It is time to put an end to social conflicts and controversies around dog meat consumption through the enactment of a special act to end it." The proposed law would ban breeding dogs for slaughter as well as the sale of dog meat, according to local media. A three-year grace period is planned, along with financial support to help businesses transition out of the dog meat trade.

Yu also noted the bill is expected to gain bipartisan support, likely enabling it to pass smoothly through parliament. Agriculture Minister Chung Hwang-keun said the government would move swiftly to enforce the ban and offer as much assistance as possible for those involved in the dog meat industry to close their businesses.

South Korea's First Lady, Kim Keon-hee, has been vocal in her opposition to dog meat consumption, and, along with her husband President Yoon Suk-yeol, has adopted stray dogs. Previous attempts to ban dog meat have failed due to protests from industry participants and concerns for the livelihoods of farmers and restaurant owners.

Although eating dog meat has become much less common, particularly among the youth, some older South Koreans still favor it, and the dish is still served in select restaurants. Animal rights organizations have welcomed the proposed ban, with Humane Society International calling it "a dream come true for all of us who have campaigned so hard to end this cruelty." However, representatives from the national dog meat farmers association expressed anger, calling the move "threatening" to their livelihoods.

According to government figures, there are about 1,150 dog-breeding farms, 34 slaughterhouses, and 219 dog meat distributors in South Korea. About 1,600 restaurants continue to serve dog meat. A Gallup Korea poll last year reported that 64% of South Koreans oppose dog meat consumption, while 8% had eaten dog in the previous year, down from 27% in 2015.

La Corée du Sud prévoit d’interdire la consommation de viande de chien d’ici 2027, dans le but de mettre fin à une longue controverse alors que la sensibilisation à la protection des animaux augmente. Vendredi, des responsables gouvernementaux et le parti au pouvoir, le Parti du pouvoir du peuple, ont annoncé leur intention de présenter une législation avant la fin de l’année pour mettre fin à la consommation de viande de chien d’ici 2027. La tradition de manger du chien en Corée a suscité des critiques internationales et fait face à une opposition croissante dans le pays, surtout parmi les jeunes générations.

Yu Eui-dong, chef de la politique du Parti du pouvoir du peuple, a déclaré lors d’une réunion avec des responsables gouvernementaux et des défenseurs de la protection animale : « Il est temps de mettre fin aux conflits sociaux et aux controverses autour de la consommation de viande de chien grâce à une loi spéciale. » Selon les médias locaux, la loi proposée interdira l’élevage de chiens pour l’abattage ainsi que la vente de viande de chien. Une période de transition de trois ans est prévue, accompagnée d’un soutien financier pour aider les entreprises à quitter ce commerce.

Yu a également souligné que le projet de loi devrait bénéficier d’un large soutien bipartisan, ce qui devrait permettre son adoption facile au parlement. Le ministre de l’Agriculture, Chung Hwang-keun, a indiqué que le gouvernement agirait rapidement pour faire respecter l’interdiction et fournirait autant d’aide que possible aux personnes travaillant dans l’industrie de la viande de chien pour fermer leurs activités.

La première dame de la Corée du Sud, Kim Keon-hee, s’est exprimée à plusieurs reprises contre la consommation de viande de chien et, avec son mari, le président Yoon Suk-yeol, a adopté des chiens errants. Les tentatives précédentes d’interdire la viande de chien ont échoué en raison des protestations des acteurs concernés et des inquiétudes quant aux moyens de subsistance des agriculteurs et des restaurateurs.

Bien que la consommation de viande de chien soit devenue beaucoup moins courante, notamment parmi les jeunes, certains Sud-Coréens plus âgés y sont encore attachés et des plats à base de chien sont encore servis dans certains restaurants. Les organisations de défense des animaux ont salué l’interdiction proposée, la Humane Society International la qualifiant de « rêve devenu réalité pour nous tous qui avons tant œuvré pour mettre fin à cette cruauté ». Cependant, des représentants de l’association nationale des éleveurs de chiens ont exprimé leur colère, qualifiant la mesure de « menaçante » pour leurs moyens de subsistance.

Selon les chiffres du gouvernement, il y aurait environ 1 150 fermes d’élevage de chiens, 34 abattoirs et 219 distributeurs de viande de chien en Corée du Sud. Environ 1 600 restaurants continuent de servir de la viande de chien. Un sondage Gallup Korea réalisé l’an dernier a révélé que 64 % des Sud-Coréens s’opposaient à la consommation de viande de chien, tandis que 8 % en avaient mangé au cours de l’année écoulée, contre 27 % en 2015.

article_content: Demonstrations erupted in Amman, Jordan on Wednesday as hundreds of protestors clashed with riot police following the government's decision to increase fuel and gas prices. The unrest, concentrated in the Jabal al Hussein area along the capital’s main Soukaina road, grew intense as authorities deployed tear gas and water cannons to disperse the crowd. In a rare act, some protestors chanted slogans directly criticizing King Abdullah II, calling for the monarchy’s downfall—an unusual occurrence in Jordan where public criticism of the king is uncommon and can carry legal consequences. Most demonstrators fled after the police intervention, but a small group remained and confronted officers. CNN reporters observed police detaining protestors, including one instance where a man was beaten and arrested, and two young men were taken away by plainclothes intelligence officials, as some protestors responded by throwing rocks. According to Jordan’s Public Security Department, previous protests have resulted in at least 14 injuries, including 10 caused by police gunfire, as well as property damage. Many Jordanians, interviewed by CNN, expressed deep concern about rising prices, government corruption, and fears over the nation’s stability and future. The protests follow a series of demonstrations that have sporadically occured since December 2010, generally focusing on frustrations toward parliament and the government. However, public criticism of the king is a growing, though still minority, sentiment. Crowds rallied for the government to reverse its decision to cut fuel subsidies, which drove up prices for gasoline, diesel, kerosene, and cooking gas. Unleaded gas increased from about $3.80 to just over $4.25 per gallon, while diesel rose from $2.80 to roughly $3.70 per gallon. Cooking gas prices climbed from just over $9 to more than $14 per canister. The government announced cash payments of nearly $600 for the country’s poorest families to soften the impact. Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour, recently appointed, addressed the nation, attributing the subsidy cuts to budgetary pressures caused by instability in neighboring countries, which has disrupted Jordan’s petroleum supplies. He accused Islamist groups, particularly the Islamic Action Front, of seeking to exploit unrest for political advantage. Jordan’s teacher’s union responded to the price hikes by launching an indefinite strike, while demonstrations spread across at least seven cities, according to state news agency Petra. Jordan faces rising unemployment and inflation along with mounting refugee numbers—over 200,000 Syrians have recently entered the country—further straining resources. King Abdullah II, who has repeatedly reshuffled his government amid the unrest and made gestures toward political reform, remains under pressure as both economic challenges and demands for reform intensify. Despite Jordan’s reputation for stability and strong ties to the West, ongoing protests fueled by economic hardship, corruption allegations, and regional instability raise concerns over the kingdom’s future and highlight its significance in the geopolitics of the Middle East.

Des journalistes de CNN ont observé la police arrêter des manifestants, y compris un homme battu et arrêté, et deux jeunes hommes emmenés par des agents de renseignement en civil, tandis que d’autres protestataires jetaient des pierres. Les manifestants demandent que le gouvernement revienne sur la suppression des subventions, ce qui a fait grimper les prix de l’essence, du diesel, du kérosène et du gaz de cuisson. L’essence sans plomb est passée d’environ 3,80 $ à plus de 4,25 $ le gallon ; le diesel, de 2,80 $ à environ 3,70 $ le gallon. Le gaz de cuisson a grimpé de plus de 9 $ à plus de 14 $ la bonbonne. Pour compenser, le gouvernement a promis des paiements de près de 600 $ aux familles les plus pauvres. Le Premier ministre Abdallah Ensour, récemment nommé, a expliqué à la nation que la baisse des subventions est due à des pressions budgétaires provoquées par l’instabilité chez les pays voisins, qui a perturbé l’approvisionnement en pétrole de la Jordanie. Il a accusé les groupes islamistes, notamment le Front d’Action Islamique, de vouloir exploiter les troubles à des fins politiques. Le syndicat des enseignants de Jordanie a lancé une grève illimitée en réaction aux hausses, tandis que les manifestations se sont étendues à au moins sept villes, selon l’agence officielle Petra. La Jordanie affronte une hausse du chômage et de l’inflation, ainsi qu’un afflux de réfugiés – plus de 200 000 Syriens sont récemment entrés dans le pays – exerçant une pression supplémentaire sur les ressources nationales. Le roi Abdallah II, qui a fréquemment remanié son gouvernement et promis des réformes politiques en réponse à l’agitation, fait face à une intensification des demandes de changement. Malgré la réputation de la Jordanie pour sa stabilité et ses relations avec l’Occident, la persistance des manifestations, attisées par les difficultés économiques, la corruption alléguée et l’instabilité régionale, soulève des inquiétudes sur l’avenir du royaume et met en lumière son rôle géopolitique au Moyen-Orient.

article_content:
The UK government is set to introduce stricter checks for sex offenders after it was revealed that more than 850 individuals are missing from police oversight. The Home Office aims to close several loopholes in the sex offenders register, including one that previously allowed offenders without a permanent address to register locations such as park benches as their address for up to a year.

Under the new regulations, sex offenders will be required to report to the police weekly and must inform authorities before moving. Those travelling abroad—even for trips as short as a day—will have to notify the police, an update from previous rules that only required notification for absences longer than three days. Offenders must also disclose if they move into a residence with children or attempt to change their names by deed poll.

These changes follow data obtained through a Freedom of Information request, showing that more than 700 sex offenders have been unaccounted for over a year, with some missing for almost a decade. The total number of missing individuals on the Sex Offenders Register has more than doubled in the past two years. Critics, including victims’ groups, have raised concerns about the effectiveness of current monitoring, with claims that offenders remain ‘underground and undetected’.

Currently, anyone sentenced to 30 months or more in prison for sex crimes is placed on the register for life. The register now contains over 37,000 names. Despite the rising number of missing offenders, only a few are publicly listed on police wanted websites. As of September 1 of the previous year, 843 registered offenders were missing, with 690 untraceable for more than a year. Two examples include Jason Waller and Stephen Clare, both missing for multiple years and featured on the Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre’s ‘Most Wanted’ page.

Authorities report, however, that improved monitoring techniques have led to fewer serious offences among known dangerous offenders. Cumbria Assistant Chief Constable Michelle Skeer highlighted the UK’s advanced methods for managing registered sex offenders.

Additionally, due to a 2010 Supreme Court ruling, offenders placed indefinitely on the register now have the right to appeal for removal after 15 years if they no longer pose a threat. Home Secretary Theresa May criticized the ruling, stating it contradicts common sense. If removal requests are denied by police, offenders can further appeal to the Magistrates' Court.

Malgré l'augmentation du nombre de disparus, peu sont signalés publiquement sur les sites de la police. Au 1er septembre de l'année précédente, 843 délinquants inscrits étaient portés disparus, dont 690 restaient introuvables depuis plus d'un an. Jason Waller et Stephen Clare, disparus depuis plusieurs années, sont présentés sur la page « Most Wanted » du Centre de protection de l'enfance contre l'exploitation en ligne.

article_content: An 85-year-old American man, Merrill Newman, has been detained in North Korea for more than a month, according to North Korea's state-run news agency. KCNA reported Saturday that Newman, a resident of Palo Alto, California, issued an apology for his actions during the Korean War, including allegations of killing civilians and soldiers. A statement published by KCNA, attributed to Newman, claimed responsibility for actions against North Korean forces and civilians during the war. The statement ends with a pledge to share the reality of life in North Korea if allowed to return to the United States. KCNA also alleged that Newman traveled to North Korea with a tourist group in October and subsequently committed acts that, according to them, infringed on the dignity and sovereignty of North Korea. Further, the report accused Newman of seeking out spies and engaging in espionage and subversive activities while a member of the U.S. military during the war. Investigators said these activities led to the deaths of Korean People's Army personnel and civilians and that evidence supported their claims. They state that Newman admitted to these actions and apologized. Before this report, North Korean authorities had not provided an official explanation for Newman’s detention. There has been no immediate comment from the U.S. government regarding the apology or North Korea’s statement. Since the U.S. does not have diplomatic relations with North Korea, it has been working through Sweden, its protecting power, to obtain information and advocate for Newman's release. Merrill Newman, a retired financial consultant, was last seen boarding a flight from Pyongyang to Beijing, but was removed by North Korean authorities shortly before departure. According to his family, he was on a 10-day organized tour in North Korea, and there had been no indication of any trouble before his detention. The family has publicly expressed concern for Newman's health and called for his release. His wife, Lee Newman, told CNN she hoped he would be home for Thanksgiving and noted that he only packed enough medication for the trip. She has since sent more, but it is unclear if he has received it. Merrill Newman is one of two Americans currently detained in North Korea. Kenneth Bae was arrested in November 2012 and sentenced to 15 years of hard labor for 'hostile acts.' CNN's Chelsea J. Carter contributed to this report.

article_content:
British royal observers are abuzz over reports that Prince Charles compared Russian President Vladimir Putin to Adolf Hitler. The Daily Mail reported that Marienne Ferguson, a 78-year-old Holocaust survivor, claims Prince Charles made the remark during his visit to the Canadian Museum of Immigration in Halifax, Nova Scotia. Ferguson, who fled to Canada in 1939 before Germany seized Gdansk, said she discussed her background with the Prince. “The prince then said, ‘And now Putin is doing just about the same as Hitler,’” Ferguson recounted, referencing Russia’s disputed annexation of Crimea. She expressed agreement with the Prince, adding, “I must say that I agree with him and am sure a lot of people do. I was surprised he made the comment since royals usually avoid such statements, but it felt heartfelt and honest.”

CNN has not independently confirmed the conversation, and Prince Charles’ representatives declined comment. Clarence House stated, “The Prince of Wales would not seek to make a public political statement during a private conversation.”

Although the Queen serves as head of state in the UK, foreign policy is set by the elected government. As heir to the throne, it’s unusual for Prince Charles to offer political opinions. Russia has not officially responded, and when contacted, a Putin spokesman declined comment, according to The Guardian. Online, British MP Mike Gapes criticized Prince Charles, arguing that policy and diplomacy should remain the domain of Parliament and government. Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg defended Charles in a BBC interview, stating that royal family members are not required to remain silent in private discussions.

Some observers warn that comparisons to Hitler are inflammatory, given ongoing tensions over Russia’s actions in Ukraine. Earlier in the year, Hillary Clinton faced criticism for drawing similar parallels. Such remarks also evoke memories of failed efforts in the 1930s by European governments to contain Hitler, including the annexation of Austria and the Sudetenland before the invasion of Poland—a history often cited in debates over the dangers of appeasement.

article_content: Former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, 86, appeared frail but defiant in an Egyptian courtroom, seated in a caged dock on a hospital stretcher and dressed in a blue prison uniform. Facing retrial for his role in the killing of protesters during the 2011 uprising, Mubarak denied ordering the deaths of hundreds and emphasized that he had stepped down voluntarily to prevent bloodshed and preserve national unity. In his first extended statement to the court, he asserted that his 29-year rule helped stabilize Egypt. Photographs from the hearing show Mubarak and his son Alaa behind bars, as Mubarak defended his actions in the final days of his presidency. After leaving court, Mubarak was escorted by medics and armed forces back to Maadi Military Hospital. Mubarak originally received a life sentence in June 2012 for failing to stop the killing of over 900 protesters during the uprising, but his conviction was overturned in January 2013, leading to a retrial. Prosecutors appealed the decision, and the retrial began in April 2013. Also on trial are his security chief, Habib el-Adly—convicted and sentenced to life on similar charges—and six of el-Adly’s senior aides, who were acquitted in a previous trial. The judge has set the final verdict announcement for September 27. During the early days of the 'Arab Spring,' demonstrations in Egypt sparked clashes with authorities, during which police allegedly used lethal force. Nearly 200 police officers and security officials were put on trial but acquitted, citing insufficient evidence or claims of self-defense. These acquittals have become part of Mubarak's legal defense. Mubarak argued that although the 2011 protests began peacefully, outside and religious groups—widely understood to refer to the Muslim Brotherhood—turned the demonstrations violent. Mohammed Morsi, a leader of the Muslim Brotherhood, won Egypt's only freely contested presidential election in 2012, before being deposed by the military in response to mass protests. Following Morsi’s ouster, the government designated the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization and launched a crackdown on its supporters, resulting in hundreds killed and thousands imprisoned. Morsi faces charges that could carry a death sentence, and the Muslim Brotherhood has planned demonstrations on the anniversary of the violent break-up of pro-Morsi sit-ins. Human Rights Watch has accused Egyptian authorities of using excessive lethal force during these crackdowns, saying the deaths amounted to crimes against humanity—a charge the Egyptian government strongly rejects.

Dans sa première déclaration détaillée au tribunal, il a affirmé que ses 29 ans au pouvoir avaient contribué à stabiliser l'Égypte. article_content:
The opening scenes of Leave the World Behind introduce an average American family embarking on a vacation getaway. The trip seems uneventful until a strange event occurs at the beach: a massive ship named White Lion comes dangerously close to shore and crashes into the sand, causing panic among onlookers. This alarming incident hints at deeper trouble ahead. Despite the unsettling moment, the family, having rented a luxurious contemporary beach house, try to enjoy their time off. Amanda Sandford (Julia Roberts) is a proactive, observant figure, often more perceptive than her well-meaning but passive husband, Clay (Ethan Hawke), especially as odd events start unfolding. Their daughter Rose (Farrah Mackenzie), obsessed with television, is the first to notice unusual signals coming from the screen. Along with their son, Archie (Charlie Evans), the family encounters a surprising late-night visit from G.H. Scott (Mahershala Ali) and his outspoken daughter, Ruth (Myha’la). The Sandfords are initially skeptical, especially since G.H. and Ruth, dressed formally, claim to be the owners of the house and request to stay for shelter from unexplained crises affecting the area. Subtle racial dynamics emerge during this tense encounter. G.H. Scott ultimately proves that he owns the property and asserts his rights, hoping to manage the household during the ongoing upheaval. Director Sam Esmail, who previously worked with Roberts on Homecoming, adapts Rumaan Alam’s acclaimed novel into a film that functions as both a disaster movie and a social thriller. The story is less about the spectacle of catastrophe and more focused on human anxiety, suspicion, and the dilemmas posed by our dependency on technology. Esmail employs special effects sparingly, prioritizing character-driven drama. Performances stand out across the cast. Julia Roberts portrays Amanda as a cautious, quick-thinking lead; Ethan Hawke brings depth to Clay’s passivity; Mahershala Ali effectively plays G.H. as a composed and authoritative figure; Myha’la impresses as the driven, rule-challenging Ruth (originally G.H.’s wife in the book, now his daughter for generational context); and Kevin Bacon makes an impact as survivalist Danny. Barack and Michelle Obama are credited as executive producers through their Higher Ground company, reflecting the film’s broader social message. The film debuted as the opening night feature at AFI Fest and is scheduled for a theatrical release on November 22, 2023, followed by streaming on Netflix from December 8, 2023. Leave the World Behind offers both a suspenseful cinematic experience and a timely warning about the vulnerabilities of modern society. Title: Leave the World Behind
Festival: AFI Fest
Distributor: Netflix
Release date: November 22, 2023 (theatres); December 8, 2023 (streaming)
Director/Screenwriter: Sam Esmail
Cast: Julia Roberts, Mahershala Ali, Ethan Hawke, Myha’la, Kevin Bacon, Farrah Mackenzie, Charlie Evans
Rating: R
Running time: 2 hr 18 min

article_content: Oscar Health reported a net loss of $65.7 million in its latest quarter, a significant improvement over the $193.5 million loss in the same period last year. The company, which provides individual health insurance through the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare), is working toward profitability under new management. Earlier this year, Oscar appointed former Aetna CEO Mark Bertolini as its new leader to help steer the company towards a financial turnaround. Company executives remain optimistic, forecasting profitability next year and emphasizing their confidence in the individual health insurance market. Bertolini stated that Oscar achieved notable year-over-year improvements in key financial metrics for the third quarter. He announced, ‘We are pleased with our year-to-date performance and have raised our outlook for 2023 InsuranceCo Adjusted EBITDA and consolidated Adjusted EBITDA. We are well-positioned to deliver $155 million to $165 million in profit in our insurance business in 2023 and to reach total company adjusted EBITDA profitability in 2024.’ Oscar's membership fell below 1 million, reaching 983,160 as of September 30, due in part to nearly 3,000 fewer Medicare Advantage members and over 100,000 fewer individual customers. The company finished the quarter with 912,761 members in its core individual and small group offerings, and 1,840 in Medicare Advantage plans. Despite these declines, Oscar reported an improved medical expense ratio and increased premium revenue, the latter boosted by higher insurance rates. Total direct and assumed policy premiums for the quarter were $1.6 billion, down 5% from the previous year, mainly because of lower membership numbers, but somewhat offset by rate increases.

article_content: Most baby animals dislike baths, and this bear cub was no exception after being doused with cold water by its mother at Kuril Lake in Russia. Following an unsuccessful salmon fishing trip, the mother bear lifted her spirits by energetically shaking off the water from her fur—directly onto her two cubs. The young bears tried in vain to escape the chilly droplets, their small paws no match for their mother’s strength. The playful and endearing moment was captured by Russian amateur wildlife photographer Sergey Ivanov, 51, who had spent over a month at the picturesque lake. Ivanov explained that his presence had become familiar to the bears, allowing him to photograph them behaving naturally, though he remained cautious not to disturb them. After their watery encounter, the bear family settled down together on the lakeshore.

article_content: Many people find it challenging to distinguish AI-generated images from authentic ones. An AI-created image of the late Hawaiian singer Israel Kamakawiwoʻole currently appears as the top search result on Google when his name is searched. Ethan Mollick, a professor at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School, noticed this and shared a screenshot on X (formerly Twitter) on Sunday. 'Seriously, don't trust anything you see online anymore. Faking stuff is trivial. You cannot tell the difference,' Mollick warned. Business Insider also searched for 'Israel Kamakawiwoʻole' on Sunday evening and observed that AI-generated images continued to appear at the top of the results. AI-generated content is increasingly appearing in search results beyond just text. The main image shown in Google search results for Kamakawiwoʻole is currently a product of Midjourney, an AI image-generation tool, originally posted on Reddit. However, these AI-generated images are not entirely accurate. Noah Giansiracusa, a professor at Bentley University, pointed out on X that the images incorrectly depict Kamakawiwoʻole playing guitar, even though he was known for playing the ukulele. Giansiracusa remarked, 'Google's got to up its game to keep AI content out of top results like this.' Kamakawiwoʻole became famous for his emotional rendition of Judy Garland's 'Over the Rainbow' and died in 1997 at the age of 38. The AI-generated images were initially posted on Reddit in July, within a community dedicated to the Midjourney AI tool. The original post received little attention, with only nine comments and 90 upvotes. This is not the first time AI-generated images have ranked at the top of Google searches. In September, 404 Media reported that an AI-created image of the Tiananmen Square 'tank man' appeared as the top image search result, also from the Midjourney Reddit community. The fictional image showed the 'tank man' taking a selfie in front of a tank. Google stated to 404 Media that it had removed the image from search results. Similarly, searches for artists Edward Hopper and Johannes Vermeer have also surfaced AI-generated images as top results, according to Futurism. In May, Google announced plans to introduce a tool to provide more context about image search results, helping users distinguish real photos from AI-generated ones. Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider, which was sent outside regular business hours.

Launched to coincide with New York Fashion Week, the app analyzes top models’ makeup trends, suggesting popular looks for users to try. The app utilizes advanced facial detection and skin analysis to apply convincing cosmetic effects, offering a variety of virtual makeup products such as eye shadows, mascaras, eyeliners, lipsticks, blush, and foundation. Olivia also experimented with Gisele’s look, featuring a glowing complexion and blue eyes.

article_content: An assault trial in Philadelphia was declared a mistrial after the victim’s prosthetic eye fell out during his testimony, shocking the jury. John Huttick, a 48-year-old former bouncer, became emotional while testifying in the Court of Common Pleas about losing his eye during a fight in August 2011. As he wept on the witness stand, his $3,000 artificial eye came out, causing jurors to gasp before Huttick caught it. Judge Robert Coleman called the event an 'unfortunate, unforeseen incident' and granted a mistrial at the request of defense attorney Eileen Hurley. Huttick told the Philadelphia Inquirer, 'I couldn’t believe it just came out.' The court heard that Huttick and defendant Matthew Brunelli, a 23-year-old chef, had been drinking at the New Princeton Tavern in Burholme when a fight erupted in the parking lot. Prosecutor Mark Gilson stated that Brunelli, during the altercation, hit Huttick’s left eye—possibly with a metal key protruding between his fingers, blinding Huttick. Brunelli denies using a key, claiming he only punched Huttick in self-defense. Huttick said the injury cost him his job, led to depression, and nearly ended his relationship. Brunelli is charged with aggravated assault. The retrial is scheduled for March 4.

article_content: Samsung has officially announced the integration of artificial intelligence in its forthcoming smartphones, with the Galaxy S24 set to highlight these capabilities. Recently introduced at the Samsung AI Forum 2023, Samsung Gauss is the company's new generative AI platform named after the mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss. It includes three main components: Gauss Language for advanced conversation, Gauss Code to support software development, and Gauss Image for creating and editing images. The Galaxy S24 is expected to use AI to deliver tailored experiences, such as recognizing user habits, suggesting app actions, and streamlining tasks. For example, the AI could assess travel plans to provide information on weather and traffic or draft emails automatically based on user prompts. Samsung will process significant amounts of personal data on its devices to power these features, prioritizing user privacy by keeping data local. This is feasible thanks to the processing power of the latest Snapdragon and Exynos chipsets. Generative AI-powered products from Samsung may debut as early as next year, with the Galaxy S24 series likely being the first to feature them. These phones will utilize both the Exynos 2400 and Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chips, depending on the market. The S24 Ultra will exclusively use the Snapdragon chip, while the S24 and S24+ will offer either chipset according to region. There has previously been debate about the differences in performance and AI features between Qualcomm’s Snapdragon and Samsung’s Exynos chips. Samsung aims to ensure that all Galaxy S24 users have a consistent AI experience, regardless of chipset. AI technology is rapidly becoming a central part of smartphones. With competitors like Google leading in AI-oriented handsets, Samsung intends to solidify its position as an innovator. How the dual-chip design affects AI performance will attract attention in 2024. The Galaxy S24 series is expected to launch early in 2024, possibly in January, as Samsung showcases its advancements in on-device AI.

article_content: Bagheera, a black Collie and Belgian Shepherd mix with rare, vivid orange eyes, has spent much of her life waiting for a home. She first arrived as a puppy at a rescue center in Italy. Despite her striking features, her unusual eye color—a rare genetic trait—has discouraged many potential adopters. At eight years old, Bagheera now lives at Teckels Animal Sanctuaries in Gloucester, England, where staff remain hopeful about her chances. Alice Breaks, senior kennel technician, calls her "lovely" and says her orange eyes are unlike any she has seen. Though Bagheera is anxious and needs an experienced owner, she’s made progress, learning a few English commands and becoming more sociable. She would do best in a quiet, adult-only household in a rural area. Veterinary surgeon Phillip Robinson of Battersea Dogs & Cats Home notes that amber eyes are exceptionally rare in black-coated dogs, but hopes Bagheera’s standout look will help her find a family. To learn more about adopting Bagheera, contact Teckels Animal Sanctuaries at 01452 740300 or email enquiries@teckelsanimalsanctuaries.co.uk.

article_content: Avi Mehta, Vice-President at Macquarie Capital, has highlighted the growing trend of premiumisation in India’s consumer market, with brands like Titan and notable players in the auto sector leading this shift. Mehta emphasizes that increasing per capita income is changing consumer behaviour, leading many to spend more on premium and luxury goods. Data and charts indicate this trend spans various sectors — including spirits, wine, footwear, automobiles, and electricals. More Indian consumers are now brand-aware and aspire to own products that offer a sense of luxury and status. Luxury demand extends beyond just the wealthiest 1%-3% of the population; aspirational spending is now prominent in smaller towns and cities, reaching Tier 1 and Tier 2 urban centres in addition to traditional metros like Mumbai and Delhi. Mehta considers this a multi-year phenomenon, not a short-lived trend. Reviewing global consumption, Mehta compares India’s current stage to China’s, suggesting that India is 14-15 years behind but progressing faster. The trend is driven by a shift from unorganised to organised sectors, improving product mixes, and growing preference for distinctive luxury items. Luxury spending is strongest in high-ticket categories such as jewellery, and the aspirational mindset is also growing among small-town consumers. Consequently, the luxury market opportunity now spans from 20 to over 100 cities, rather than focusing solely on top metros. India is described as being at the beginning of the luxury growth 'S-curve,' offering an attractive investment horizon. The primary risk to this growth is a potential slowdown in GDP or real estate, which could affect wealth and consumer spending. Overall, Mehta is optimistic that luxury consumption in India will continue its upward trajectory, provided the country’s economic growth remains strong.

Mehta souligne que l'augmentation du revenu par habitant modifie le comportement des consommateurs, les poussant à dépenser davantage pour des biens premium et de luxe. Des données et graphiques montrent que cette tendance touche plusieurs secteurs – notamment les spiritueux, le vin, les chaussures, l’automobile et l’électroménager. De plus en plus d’Indiens sont sensibles aux marques et aspirent à posséder des produits offrant du luxe et du prestige. La demande de produits de luxe ne se limite plus aux 1 à 3% les plus aisés de la population ; elle s’étend désormais aux petites villes et centres urbains de niveau 1 et 2, en plus des métropoles comme Mumbai et Delhi. Mehta considère qu’il s’agit d’un phénomène qui va durer plusieurs années, et non d’une simple mode passagère. En analysant la consommation mondiale, Mehta compare l’étape actuelle de l’Inde à celle de la Chine, estimant que l’Inde a 14 à 15 ans de retard mais rattrape rapidement. Ainsi, l’opportunité sur le marché du luxe s’étend aujourd’hui de 20 à plus de 100 villes, et ne concerne plus seulement les grandes métropoles. L’Inde est décrite comme étant au début de la courbe de croissance du luxe – une 'courbe en S' – ce qui offre un horizon d’investissement séduisant. article_content: HANOI: Vietnamese authorities have arrested Luu Binh Nhuong, a prominent former member of Vietnam's National Assembly and current deputy chair of a parliamentary committee, on suspicion of involvement in an extortion scheme, the Ministry of Public Security announced on Wednesday. Nhuong, known for voicing criticism of government officials and security forces, was taken into custody on Tuesday night. His arrest coincided with a visit from the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the right to development, Surya Deva. At the end of his ten-day visit, Deva expressed concern about what he described as 'the selective use of the law' by Vietnamese authorities to target some human rights defenders and climate activists. When questioned about Nhuong's arrest, Deva said he had not been informed in advance, adding: 'The government should not use the law as a tool to target individuals for their political or religious views.' In September, soon after US President Joe Biden signed agreements with Vietnam and elevated bilateral relations, a local energy expert was detained for allegedly misappropriating government documents. Since 2021, five climate activists have also been arrested on tax evasion charges, indicating an apparent crackdown while Vietnam was in talks with G7 nations for financial support to reduce coal use. Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, responsible for communications with foreign media, did not immediately respond to questions regarding the timing of Nhuong's arrest.

article_content: Rachin Ravindra's remarkable World Cup run continued as he scored his third century of the tournament against Pakistan in Bengaluru. On July 14, 2019, Rachin watched New Zealand's narrow loss to England in the World Cup final at a pub on MG Road. Just a short distance from there, at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium, he produced a record-breaking performance on Saturday. With 523 runs so far, Rachin is currently the tournament's second-highest run-scorer. His 108 off 94 balls (including 15 fours and a six) made him the first New Zealand player to score three centuries in a single World Cup. At just 23 years old and born in Wellington, Rachin has impressed everyone with his talent and calm demeanor. He played with great maturity until one mistake led to his dismissal. For his first boundary, he dispatched a loose ball from Hasan Ali to fine leg, and later showcased elegant shots through extra cover. Rachin's batting reflects the years of training with his father Ravi Krishnamurthy, who is from Bengaluru. He reached his fifty in 51 balls and then dominated the bowlers, partnering well with captain Kane Williamson. He showed excellent footwork against Haris Rauf and patience against the spinners. When Rachin reached his third World Cup century with a single off Mohammad Wasim, his maternal grandparents TA Balakrishna Adiga and Poornima, along with other family members, celebrated in the stands. Adiga said, 'It was very touching to hear the spectators chant Rachin's name. Watching him score a century was special.' Rachin expressed his excitement about playing in his parents' hometown, saying, 'It feels surreal to play in the country of my parents' heritage. It's always special to play in India, especially in Bengaluru where my family is present.' In the land of Rahul Dravid, it was fitting for a boy named after him to make a lasting impact.

article_content: Katie Couric has been unsettled after discovering that a phone line still registered in her late husband's name has been making early-morning 911 calls. Each time, the calls happened at 2 a.m. on Tuesdays, prompting police officers to visit her Manhattan apartment. Police report that at least 10 such calls have been made from the line. Concerned, Couric contacted New York Police Commissioner Ray Kelly for help. The NYPD is investigating whether the calls are due to a technical fault or the work of a prankster, as reported by the New York Daily News. The phone in question is the landline for Couric's Upper East Side apartment, which is still under her late husband Jay Monahan's name. Monahan died from colon cancer in 1998. Couric discussed the incident with her show's audience before a taping, apologizing for being late and for her lack of sleep following the calls. She explained that the landline was repeatedly placing 911 calls, causing a patrol car to be sent to her apartment each time. Afterward, she received an automated call-back from a 911 operator. Couric likened her situation to celebrity 'SWAT' calls, noting that her phone made these calls at 2 a.m. on several Tuesdays, even when she wasn't home. She found the situation especially disturbing because the calls originated from her late husband's phone line. After discovering the situation, Couric notified her building staff, contacted the local police precinct, and also reached out to Commissioner Kelly. A police source confirmed that authorities are investigating to determine if the issue is a technical malfunction or a prank. A friend of Couric’s shared that she is worried these repeated calls may cause police to hesitate in responding to future emergencies. Couric was married to Monahan, a lawyer and NBC News legal analyst, from 1989 until his death. She has actively raised awareness about colon cancer, including having a colonoscopy broadcasted on television in 2000. After Monahan’s passing, Couric had a five-year relationship with Brooks Perlin and is currently linked to financier John Molner. She now lives with her two daughters, aged 21 and 17, and their dogs in her New York apartment.

article_content:
English football is once again under scrutiny due to allegations of racist abuse, fan violence, and attacks on players—issues reminiscent of past troubles that led to English clubs being banned from European competition in the 1980s. Following a turbulent Manchester derby, media outlets have described the sport as 'toxic' and 'out of control.' Football Association chairman David Bernstein labeled the incidents—including pitch invasion, coin throwing, racist abuse allegations, and 13 arrests during and after Manchester United’s 3-2 victory at Manchester City—as 'disturbing, deplorable, and unacceptable.'

That such events involved two top Premier League clubs has prompted public questioning of football leadership. Some coverage draws parallels to the atmosphere that led to the Heysel (1985) and Hillsborough (1989) stadium disasters. At Heysel, fan violence at a European Cup final resulted in 39 deaths, while at Hillsborough, 96 people died after a fatal crush linked to policing strategies.

Others argue that this recent attention signals football is finally confronting long-standing issues within the sport. Clarke Carlisle, chairman of the Professional Footballers’ Association, suggests that behaviors like aggressive chanting and throwing objects were long dismissed as part of the game, but societal tolerance for such conduct is now waning. Carlisle notes this leads both to increased reporting of incidents and more determined efforts to curb antisocial behavior. While overall arrests at Premier League matches have dropped 30% in the past season, race-related offenses are on the rise.

Worldwide media coverage intensified after Manchester United’s Rio Ferdinand was struck by a coin and confronted by a pitch invader. Carlisle highlights that such actions have been recurring for years, but only recently have they attracted major public condemnation and calls for accountability from all who participate in the game.

Key voices, including anti-racism group Kick It Out’s chairman Herman Ouseley and Carlisle, contend that football authorities must do more. Ouseley criticized the FA and Premier League for their inadequate response to high-profile racial abuse cases involving John Terry and Luis Suarez, referring to a ‘moral vacuum’ among top clubs that focus on player protection at the expense of principle.

Carlisle agrees that responsibility must extend to club officials, staff, and fans alike regarding discriminatory behavior. The FA is reviewing its sanctions and has proposed five-match bans for racial abuse, with these changes to be implemented next season.

Recent offenses, such as the racial abuse directed at Norwich defender Sebastien Bassong and anti-Semitic incidents involving West Ham fans, highlight ongoing challenges. Carlisle advocates for transparent protocols and guidelines that clearly define responses to discrimination, avoiding the ambiguity of ad hoc measures. He cites the handling of referee Mark Clattenburg’s investigated-but-cleared case as an example of improved procedures—though warns that media speculation can still damage reputations.

Cultural misunderstandings have also surfaced, such as the Suarez-Evra case, where language acceptable in one country is offensive in another. Carlisle supports cultural education for foreign players to eliminate such ambiguities.

Herman Ouseley’s expected resignation from the FA Council is seen as a significant loss but also an opportunity for new leadership in pursuing the FA’s diversity and anti-racism goals. Advocates stress that lasting progress requires consistent leadership, clear procedures, and a unified approach to eradicating racism and violence from English football.

Après un derby de Manchester tumultueux, plusieurs médias ont qualifié ce sport de « toxique » et d’« incontrôlable ». Le président de la Fédération anglaise (FA), David Bernstein, a jugé les incidents—intrusion sur la pelouse, jets de projectiles, accusations de propos racistes, et 13 arrestations pendant et après la victoire 3-2 de Manchester United sur Manchester City—« perturbants, déplorables et inacceptables ».

Le fait que deux des plus grands clubs de Premier League soient impliqués a suscité un débat sur la gouvernance du football. Certains font le parallèle avec les événements qui ont mené aux tragédies du Heysel (1985) et de Hillsborough (1989). Au Heysel, des violences lors d’une finale de Coupe d’Europe ont causé 39 morts ; à Hillsborough, 96 personnes ont trouvé la mort dans une bousculade, due en partie à la gestion policière.

D’autres estiment que l’attention récente marque enfin la volonté du football d’affronter des problèmes longtemps ignorés. Clarke Carlisle, président de l’Association des footballeurs professionnels, souligne que des comportements tels que les chants agressifs ou les lancers d’objets étaient tolérés sous prétexte que « c’est ainsi dans le football ». Désormais, la tolérance baisse, menant à davantage de signalements et à la volonté de sanctionner. Bien que les arrestations en Premier League aient chuté de 30% la saison passée, les actes racistes, eux, augmentent.

La diffusion mondiale des images du joueur Rio Ferdinand frappé par une pièce de monnaie puis confronté à un supporter sur la pelouse a intensifié le débat. Clarke Carlisle rappelle que ces abus existent depuis des années mais que la société exige désormais des mesures concrètes.

Des personnalités comme Herman Ouseley (Kick It Out) et Carlisle estiment que les instances dirigeantes doivent agir plus fermement. Ouseley a dénoncé la gestion des affaires comme celles impliquant John Terry ou Luis Suarez, parlant de « vide moral » quand les clubs protègent leurs intérêts au détriment des principes.

Pour Carlisle, la responsabilité doit inclure dirigeants, staff et supporters. La FA envisage des suspensions de cinq matchs pour insulte raciste dès la saison prochaine.

Les affaires récentes—abuse raciste contre Sébastien Bassong (Norwich) ou incidents antisémites liés à West Ham—montrent l’ampleur du défi. Carlisle plaide pour des protocoles transparents et connus de tous afin d’éviter les mesures improvisées, et cite la gestion de l’affaire Mark Clattenburg, blanchi après enquête, comme une amélioration, malgré les risques des spéculations médiatiques.

Les incompréhensions culturelles, telles que dans l’affaire Suarez-Evra, où un mot peut être banal dans un pays et offensant dans un autre, montrent selon Carlisle la nécessité de former les joueurs étrangers aux valeurs locales.

Le départ annoncé d’Herman Ouseley du Conseil de la FA est considéré comme une perte mais aussi une chance de renouveler l’engagement contre le racisme et pour la diversité. Les acteurs soulignent qu’avancer nécessite un leadership constant, des règles claires et une volonté collective pour éliminer le racisme et la violence du football anglais.

article_content: While many organizations send letters and care packages to deployed troops, one airman found a unique way to bring a little bit of his deployment home to his kids. Zackary Trissell, a member of the Oklahoma Air National Guard, recently returned from a nine-month assignment at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. Throughout his deployment, he stayed connected with his three stepchildren thanks to a cherished childhood toy and a camera. Before Trissell left, his stepson Matthew, who has muscular dystrophy, gave him three Lego figurines to represent himself and his siblings. Matthew, along with his older brother, lives with muscular dystrophy. Matthew’s mother, Linda Trissell, told CNN affiliate KOCO that Matthew once said that if he could walk and wasn’t in a wheelchair, he would have joined the military. While stationed overseas, Trissell decided to have some fun—he photographed the Lego figures in military settings, sometimes with pilots in cockpits, or in front of a Humvee. He paired the photos with captions like, “Hey, Matthew! This one’s for you!” and “Boots on the ground baby!!!” The kids loved the updates, and Trissell says it helped him stay close to them while he was away. “They need support getting through this deployment, just like we do over there,” he said upon reuniting with his wife.

article_content: Sky Sports presenter Jeff Stelling has announced his departure from Twitter after claiming that his 14-year-old son was insulted by another user, who allegedly called him a 'poor' goalkeeper. Stelling, who hosts Sky's Soccer Saturday and Champions League broadcasts, informed his 415,000 followers that he was leaving the platform because he could not trust himself to respond to certain users appropriately. The 58-year-old father of three described being left 'steaming' after confronting a user who, according to Stelling, had posted a critical message about his teenage son's football abilities. Stelling noted that the original tweet was deleted, and other users suggested that the individual behind the post had recently played against Stelling's son in a youth football cup match. Stelling addressed the user directly, stating that calling his son a 'poor keeper' and then deleting the comment was not banter but abuse, stressing that his son is only 14 years old. He subsequently issued apologies for his own language, clarifying that while he can handle criticism directed at himself, he draws the line when it involves his children. Further, the user identified as 'Zak', who is also thought to be a teenager, replied that his remarks were intended as banter and not to offend, expressing apologies to Stelling and complimenting his son. Stelling's decision to leave Twitter comes shortly after Jonathan Agnew, a BBC cricket presenter, also left the platform, citing issues with bullies and trolls. Agnew publicly stated his disappointment with how Twitter has changed since he joined and updated his profile to indicate that he would no longer tweet or interact on the site. However, following his announcement, Agnew returned briefly to promote a new, yet-to-be-launched sports-focused social network, Kicca.com.
