article_content: What does the future hold for humanity? Will our species grow, thrive, or slowly diminish? And what about India—how will its population evolve?  According to a 2019 United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) report, India was projected to surpass China as the world's most populous country by 2027. This milestone was reached in 2023. Alongside countries like Nigeria, Pakistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Indonesia, Egypt, and the United States, India will account for much of the global population increase through 2050—these nations collectively are expected to contribute over half of the world’s population growth. Furthermore, the population of Sub-Saharan Africa is set to double by 2050.  In contrast, other parts of the world face a different trend: rapid population aging. David Bloom, writing for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in 2020, described 'greying' as the dominant demographic trend of the 21st century, citing increased longevity, declining fertility, and aging cohorts. For example, over 28% of Japan's population is aged 65 or older. In the 1970s, there were more than three times as many young people (15–24 years old) as older individuals. By 2050, both age groups globally will reach parity.  Does this pattern apply to India as well? The UNFPA's India Aging Report 2023 states that, as of 2022, there were 1.1 billion people aged 60 and above globally (13.9% of the world’s 7.9 billion population). The number of people in this age group is expected to double to 2.1 billion by 2050, reaching 22% of the total population. In India, there were 149 million people aged 60+ (10.5% of the population) in 2022, projected to rise to 347 million (20.8%) by 2050.  This unprecedented growth in India’s elderly population will have major implications for health, the economy, and society. Both developing and developed countries are seeing declining fertility rates, but developing countries are experiencing these changes at much lower income levels. Historically, developed nations had higher per capita incomes to support their aging populations, whereas countries like India lack that economic cushion.  The report notes that in some developing countries, the old age dependency ratio (the number of elderly people compared to the working-age population) could more than double in 50 years—a process that took 150–200 years in developed nations. In India, the elderly population (over 60) is expected to grow by 41% between 2021 and 2031, and, by 2046, the number of elderly will surpass the number of children under 15.  An aging population implies fewer workers and taxpayers, diminishing economic productivity and increasing pressure on healthcare systems. With the 2022 National Family Health Survey showing that, apart from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, all major Indian states already have a fertility rate below the replacement level of 2.1, this trend seems set to continue. Urban India, in particular, has a fertility rate of 1.6, matching levels in developed countries.  A 2020 Lancet study on global population trends highlighted the strong connection between population patterns and geopolitics. While China may surpass the United States in total Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2035, its declining population could eventually lead the US to reclaim economic dominance—especially if it maintains liberal immigration policies.  According to Richard Horton, Lancet's editor-in-chief, by century’s end the world will likely be multipolar, with India, Nigeria, China, and the US as leading powers, supported by their sizable working-age populations. Moreover, immigration and robust reproductive and sexual rights for women will be crucial as global demographics undergo major shifts. He predicts the influence of Europe and Asia will wane, with several of their populations halved by 2100. For instance, China’s population may shrink from 1.4 billion in 2017 to 732 million in 2100; similar declines are expected in Thailand, Italy, and Japan.  Despite this, China’s current approach—encouraging women to focus on marriage and child-rearing to boost birth rates—runs counter to evidence-based solutions. Studies suggest reproductive choice, quality healthcare, work-life balance, affordable childcare, generous maternity leave, and educating men about sharing household responsibilities are more effective at supporting higher birth rates among working women.  Overall, expert research identifies clear trends: humanity is aging, global population growth will slow and eventually reverse, and these demographic changes will reshape the geopolitical landscape. For India, the question remains: Is the nation prepared to meet the challenges posed by these dramatic shifts in age structure?  The writer is a Senior Advocate at the Supreme Court.
translated_content: Quel avenir pour l’humanité ? Allons-nous croître, prospérer ou diminuer lentement ? Et qu’en est-il de l’Inde – comment sa population évoluera-t-elle ?  Selon un rapport du Fonds des Nations Unies pour la Population (UNFPA) publié en 2019, l’Inde devait dépasser la Chine en tant que pays le plus peuplé du monde d’ici 2027. Ce jalon a été franchi en 2023. Aux côtés de pays comme le Nigeria, le Pakistan, la République démocratique du Congo, l’Éthiopie, la Tanzanie, l’Indonésie, l’Égypte et les États-Unis, l’Inde représentera une grande partie de la croissance démographique mondiale jusqu’en 2050 – ces nations devraient ensemble contribuer à plus de la moitié de l’augmentation de la population mondiale. De plus, la population de l’Afrique subsaharienne devrait doubler d’ici 2050.  A contrario, d’autres régions du monde font face à une tendance différente : un vieillissement rapide de la population. David Bloom, écrivant pour le Fonds Monétaire International (FMI) en 2020, a décrit le vieillissement démographique comme la tendance phare du XXIe siècle, citant la longévité accrue, la baisse de la fécondité et l’avancée en âge des cohortes. Par exemple, plus de 28 % de la population japonaise a 65 ans ou plus. Dans les années 1970, il y avait plus de trois fois plus de jeunes (15-24 ans) que de personnes âgées. D’ici 2050, ces deux groupes d’âge atteindront la parité dans le monde.  Cette évolution concerne-t-elle aussi l’Inde ? Le Rapport sur le vieillissement en Inde 2023 de l’UNFPA indique qu’en 2022, il y avait 1,1 milliard de personnes âgées de 60 ans et plus dans le monde (13,9 % d’une population mondiale de 7,9 milliards). Ce chiffre devrait doubler pour atteindre 2,1 milliards d’ici 2050, soit 22 % de la population totale. En Inde, on comptait 149 millions de personnes âgées de 60 ans et plus (10,5 % de la population) en 2022, et ce nombre devrait passer à 347 millions (20,8 %) d’ici 2050.  Cette croissance sans précédent des seniors en Inde aura d’importantes conséquences sur la santé, l’économie et la société. Les pays en développement ainsi que les pays développés voient leurs taux de fécondité décliner, mais les premiers subissent cela à des niveaux de revenus bien plus faibles. Les nations riches disposaient historiquement de niveaux de vie plus élevés pour soutenir leurs populations vieillissantes, alors que l’Inde ne dispose pas de ce levier économique.  Le rapport souligne que dans certains pays en développement, le ratio de dépendance des personnes âgées (nombre de seniors par rapport aux actifs) pourrait plus que doubler en 50 ans – un processus qui a pris 150 à 200 ans dans les pays développés. En Inde, la population des plus de 60 ans devrait augmenter de 41 % entre 2021 et 2031, et d’ici 2046, le nombre de seniors dépassera celui des enfants de moins de 15 ans.  Le vieillissement implique moins de travailleurs et de contribuables, une baisse de la productivité économique et une pression croissante sur les systèmes de santé. Selon l’Enquête nationale sur la santé familiale de 2022, à l’exception de l’Uttar Pradesh et du Bihar, tous les grands États indiens affichent déjà un taux de fécondité en dessous du seuil de renouvellement (2,1). Cette tendance devrait donc se poursuivre. Dans les villes, la fécondité est à 1,6, un taux comparable à celui des pays développés.  Une étude du Lancet, publiée en 2020 sur les tendances démographiques mondiales, a souligné l’interdépendance entre démographie et géopolitique. Si la Chine pourrait dépasser les États-Unis en PIB d’ici 2035, son déclin démographique pourrait permettre aux États-Unis de reprendre la première place, surtout si une politique d’immigration ouverte se maintient.  Richard Horton, rédacteur en chef du Lancet, estime qu’à la fin du siècle, le monde sera probablement multipolaire avec l’Inde, le Nigeria, la Chine et les États-Unis comme principales puissances, grâce à leur forte population en âge de travailler. De plus, l’immigration et des droits reproductifs solides pour les femmes seront décisifs alors que la démographie mondiale évoluera fortement. Il prévoit que l’influence de l’Europe et de l’Asie déclinera, et que plusieurs populations pourraient chuter de moitié d’ici 2100. Par exemple, la population chinoise passerait de 1,4 milliard en 2017 à 732 millions en 2100 ; des baisses similaires sont attendues en Thaïlande, en Italie et au Japon.  Malgré cela, la politique actuelle de la Chine – pousser les femmes à privilégier le foyer et la maternité pour augmenter la natalité – s’oppose aux solutions validées par l’expérience. Les études montrent que la liberté reproductive, de bons soins de santé, l’équilibre travail-vie privée, la garde d’enfants accessible, des congés maternité suffisants et l’éducation des hommes à partager les tâches ménagères sont bien plus efficaces pour encourager la natalité des femmes actives.  Dans l’ensemble, la recherche souligne des tendances nettes : l’humanité vieillit, la croissance démographique mondiale va ralentir puis s’inverser, et cela va transformer la géopolitique. Reste à savoir si l’Inde est prête à faire face aux défis que posent ces profondes mutations démographiques.  L’auteur est avocat à la Cour suprême.

article_content: After serving a six-month tour in Afghanistan’s Helmand Province, facing a tense Aviva Premiership play-off, or even a potential Test debut, holds little fear for Semesa Rokoduguni. Balancing dual careers as a rugby player for Bath and a lance corporal in the British Army, Rokoduguni’s life recently connected both paths as he scored in the Army’s victory against the Navy before 80,000 fans at Twickenham. The 26-year-old Fijian-born winger is impressing for Bath, putting himself in contention for an England call-up, having already served his adopted country in dangerous combat situations. Rather than tackles and tries, his first service saw him dealing with bullets and bombs. Military life runs in Rokoduguni’s family; his younger brother, stationed with the Black Watch in Inverness, is set for deployment, while his father is currently on a UN peacekeeping mission in Egypt. Rokoduguni himself enlisted in the Royal Scots Dragoon Guards, trained as a tank driver, then served as a foot soldier on regular patrols in Helmand. Reflecting on the overlap between rugby and military life, Rokoduguni cites the camaraderie and mutual reliance central to both. 'In Afghanistan, it’s like rugby – you watch each other’s backs,' he explains. Dangerous moments were frequent, and the risks far exceeded those on the field. Two friends were wounded, and he witnessed the fatal aftermath of an IED explosion. Initially, he thought he’d need to choose between rugby and the army, but the military encouraged his ambitions. After turning heads in various Army rugby tournaments and impressing coaches Gary Gold and Mike Ford, Rokoduguni earned a contract with Bath. He’s now in his first full season, drawing interest from both Fiji and England for international duties. Despite Fiji’s interest, his current goal is to represent England. Bath’s upcoming clash with Harlequins for a play-off spot offers Rokoduguni another high-stakes challenge – though after his military experiences, such sporting pressure is familiar. Elsewhere, for Welsh rugby hopefuls, suspense about national selection will be short-lived. The Wales Rugby Union has scheduled a 'Probables v Possibles' trial on May 30 at Swansea’s Liberty Stadium, with Warren Gatland naming his squad for the South Africa tour immediately after the match. Meanwhile, France’s Sebastien Chabal, known for his rugged style and iconic beard, retires after a distinguished career with Lyon, Sale, and the French national team. His contributions, particularly at the 2007 World Cup, cemented his legend. Tributes highlight his unique personality and explosive playing style. The latest Aviva Premiership round produced 45 tries, reinforcing calls for summer rugby in England. Proponents argue that better weather increases excitement and crowd engagement, while critics claim it risks eroding rugby’s traditional variety. Advocates counter that improved conditions actually aid strategy and skills, maintaining that diverse playing styles can thrive regardless of season.
translated_content: Après avoir effectué une mission de six mois dans la province d’Helmand, en Afghanistan, une demi-finale tendue de la Premiership ou même un potentiel premier match international ne fait pas peur à Semesa Rokoduguni. Jonglant entre ses carrières de joueur pour Bath et de caporal dans l’armée britannique, la vie de Rokoduguni a récemment réuni ses deux passions lorsqu’il a marqué lors de la victoire de l’Armée contre la Marine devant 80 000 spectateurs à Twickenham. L’ailier fidjien de 26 ans impressionne chez Bath et se rapproche d’une sélection avec l’équipe d’Angleterre, après avoir déjà servi son pays d’adoption dans des situations de combat dangereuses. Avant d’affronter les plaquages et d’inscrire des essais, il faisait face aux balles et aux bombes. La vie militaire est une tradition chez les Rokoduguni : son frère cadet, basé à Inverness avec le Black Watch, doit être déployé prochainement, tandis que son père est actuellement en mission de maintien de la paix pour l’ONU en Égypte. Rokoduguni lui-même a rejoint les Royal Scots Dragoon Guards, a été formé comme conducteur de char, puis a servi comme fantassin en patrouille régulière dans le Helmand. En réfléchissant à la similitude entre le rugby et la vie militaire, Rokoduguni souligne l’esprit d’équipe et la confiance mutuelle essentiels aux deux mondes. « En Afghanistan, c’est comme au rugby : on veille les uns sur les autres », explique-t-il. Les situations dangereuses étaient fréquentes, et les risques bien supérieurs à ceux du terrain. Deux de ses amis ont été blessés et il a assisté aux conséquences fatales d’une explosion d’IED. Au départ, il pensait devoir choisir entre le rugby et l’armée, mais cette dernière a encouragé ses ambitions. Après s’être illustré dans différents tournois militaires et avoir impressionné les entraîneurs Gary Gold et Mike Ford, Rokoduguni a décroché un contrat avec Bath. Il vit actuellement sa première saison complète, suscitant l’intérêt de Fidji et de l’Angleterre pour évoluer au niveau international. Malgré l’intérêt des Fidji, son objectif reste de jouer pour l’Angleterre. Le choc à venir entre Bath et Harlequins pour une place en demi-finale offre à Rokoduguni un autre défi de taille – mais après ses expériences militaires, la pression sportive lui est familière. Ailleurs, pour les aspirants internationaux gallois, l’attente ne sera pas longue. La Fédération galloise a programmé un match Probables contre Possibles le 30 mai au Liberty Stadium de Swansea, et Warren Gatland dévoilera son groupe pour la tournée en Afrique du Sud juste après le match. Pendant ce temps, le Français Sébastien Chabal, célèbre pour son style rugueux et sa barbe emblématique, prend sa retraite après une carrière remarquable à Lyon, Sale et en équipe nationale. Ses performances, notamment lors de la Coupe du Monde 2007, l’ont définitivement rendu légendaire. Les hommages soulignent sa personnalité unique et son style explosif sur le terrain. La dernière journée de Premiership a vu 45 essais inscrits, renforçant les appels en faveur d’un rugby d’élite en été en Angleterre. Les partisans affirment que le beau temps offre plus de spectacle et attire les foules, tandis que les sceptiques évoquent une perte de variété traditionnelle. Les défenseurs répliquent que de meilleures conditions favorisent la stratégie et la technique, ce qui permet à tous les styles de jeu de s’exprimer, quelle que soit la saison.

article_content: This week marks the release of Spotify Wrapped, an annual event where users discover which songs have dominated their listening over the past year. More than just a marketing campaign, it highlights both individual preferences and the wide variety within Spotify’s expansive catalogue. Genres range from goth to punk rock, representing not just categories but sometimes lifestyles. In the digital era, about 100,000 new tracks are uploaded to Spotify every day, now sorted into over 6,000 genres—with hundreds of new ones added annually. Recent additions like Dream Plugg (a dreamy hip-hop style) and Zomi Pop (blending Myanmar's Zomi music with Western pop) show this growth. This diversity has reshaped how music-based subcultures work. As music critic Kelefa Sanneh explains, genres have long been a form of ‘virtual community’—connecting listeners and artists even before the internet. Sanneh, author of 'Major Labels: A History of Popular Music in Seven Genres,' points out genres also help companies and radio stations cater to audiences, but warns that rigid categorization can isolate fans and limit musical exploration. East London artist Murkage Dave challenges these divisions, gaining praise for blending genres in his music. Influenced by UK garage and pirate radio growing up, he finds streaming has broken barriers. 'My introduction to music depended on where I lived and who I knew,' he told the BBC. 'Now, everything comes through your phone—there’s no barrier.' For him, genre matters less than it did before streaming: 'Today, I think the industry cares more about genre than fans do.' Music remains a social experience, but Sanneh notes that tribalism has faded as music became more accessible. Still, genres are meaningful culturally—seen in hip-hop's 50th anniversary and debates over country music identity in the US. Nathaniel Cramp, founder of the label Sonic Cathedral, observes genres have become data-driven. Whereas in the past, genres were often assigned by outsiders, artists now often categorize their own music—a notable shift. Listeners themselves are also changing. Instead of following a genre, many become dedicated fans of specific acts—like 'Swifties' for Taylor Swift or the BTS Army for K-pop. Sanneh describes these intense artist-based communities as a new kind of micro-genre. Spotify editorial lead Sara Sesardic says the company adapts to shifting trends, with genres and artists becoming more fluid. Spotify now focuses on creating communities around artists rather than restrictive genre categories, but still uses genres for recommendations and searches. Still, genre misclassification can harm artists. Murkage Dave notes that streaming platforms may list his work under genres that don’t fit, limiting his audience. 'I’ve been in grime mixes, though I’ve never made a grime record in my life.' American musician and visual artist Joanna Sternberg takes a genre-agnostic stance, caring more about the listener's perspective than imposed categories. Sternberg welcomes listeners deciding for themselves how to classify music. Genres like Bronx drill, ambient lo-fi, and gym phonk saw notable growth on Spotify in 2023, showing the rise of hyper-specific categories. Sanneh argues that while genres may become less important, the sense of belonging to a musical community will last. Murkage Dave compares genres to cake ingredients—better when combined creatively. He prefers to be judged on his music’s merits, not forced into narrow boxes, describing the practice as demoralizing. As streaming services and personalized playlists expand, the number of micro-genres will likely keep growing through algorithmic curation. The biggest change may be a focus on recommendations based on mood or context instead of genre, with musical boundaries becoming increasingly blurred.

L’artiste londonien Murkage Dave casse ces cloisons en mélangeant les genres, ce qui fait sa réputation. Les auditeurs eux aussi évoluent : au lieu de suivre un genre, beaucoup deviennent fans de certains artistes en particulier — comme les 'Swifties' pour Taylor Swift ou l’« Army » de BTS pour le K-pop. Sanneh décrit ces communautés dédiées à un artiste comme des micro-genres. Sara Sesardic, responsable éditoriale chez Spotify, explique que l’entreprise s’adapte aux tendances, avec des genres et des artistes toujours plus fluides. Spotify cherche désormais à créer des communautés autour des artistes plutôt que de les enfermer dans des cases, tout en continuant d’utiliser le genre pour les recommandations et la recherche. Murkage Dave explique que les plateformes listent parfois ses morceaux sous des genres qui ne correspondent pas, ce qui réduit sa visibilité : « Je me retrouve dans des playlists grime, alors que je n’ai jamais fait de morceau grime de ma vie. » La musicienne et artiste visuelle américaine Joanna Sternberg préfère ignorer les étiquettes, laissant aux auditeurs le soin de décider eux-mêmes du genre auquel rattacher sa musique. Des genres comme Bronx drill, ambiance lo-fi ou gym phonk se sont fortement développés sur Spotify en 2023, illustrant la montée de catégories ultra-spécifiques. Sanneh pense qu’au-delà du genre, le sentiment de communauté perdurera. Murkage Dave compare les genres aux ingrédients d’un gâteau : il préfère les assembler de façon créative. Il souhaite que l’on juge son œuvre pour ce qu’elle est, sans être enfermé dans des cases restrictives — une expérience qu’il juge décourageante. Avec la montée du streaming et des playlists personnalisées, le nombre de micro-genres devrait continuer d’augmenter grâce aux algorithmes. Le vrai changement réside peut-être dans les recommandations selon l’humeur ou le contexte plus que le genre, les frontières musicales étant de plus en plus floues.

article_content: On Tuesday, Ohio voters will decide the fate of Senate Bill 5, a law limiting public employees' collective bargaining rights. Passed in March by the Ohio legislature and signed by Governor John Kasich, the law quickly faced opposition. Public employee unions and their allies gathered nearly one million signatures—three times the required amount—to put the law on the November ballot. The campaign to repeal Senate Bill 5, led by 'We Are Ohio,' gained national support. The National Education Association donated $2 million, while AFSCME and the Communication Workers of America each contributed over $1 million. Proponents of Senate Bill 5 also attracted outside backing, with Citizens United spending $100,000 on supportive commercials. Ohio's importance as a swing state has brought national focus to the issue. Although Ohio lost two congressional seats after the 2010 census, its electoral votes remain crucial for both parties. President Obama has visited Ohio frequently, yet Democrats suffered major losses in the 2010 midterm elections, as Republicans took control of the governorship, most statewide offices, and expanded their congressional majority. Republicans viewed the 2010 results as a mandate to reduce government and saw curbing public employee unions as part of that effort. However, this move also targeted groups that traditionally support Democrats. Polls now show Senate Bill 5 is widely unpopular, and even supporters doubt it will survive the vote. Republicans fear that repealing Senate Bill 5 could invigorate organized labor in Ohio, possibly harming their prospects in 2012. A historical comparison is often cited: In 1958, a proposed right-to-work amendment was overwhelmingly defeated, leading to significant Republican losses statewide. Current polling suggests Senate Bill 5 could lose by a similar margin to the 1958 measure. Although Governor Kasich and current officeholders are not up for re-election until 2014, the outcome could impact the 2012 presidential race. Ohio has long been viewed as essential for any successful presidential bid. These opinions are those of Paul Sracic.

article_content:
The Atlanta Braves will be leaving Turner Field for a new stadium in Cobb County, with their move planned for the 2017 MLB season. The forthcoming ballpark will hold 42,000 spectators and forms part of a $672 million, 60-acre development near the Cobb Galleria mall. Braves executives John Schuerholz, Mike Plant, and Derek Schiller reported that after talks with Atlanta officials about renewing their lease at Turner Field failed, the team began discussions with Cobb County authorities during the summer.

Turner Field, originally built for the 1996 Summer Olympics, has served as the Braves’ home since 1997. Team leadership noted that the stadium now faces significant infrastructure issues: critical upgrades, like new seating and improved lighting, would require around $150 million. Additional renovations focused on the fan experience would raise costs to over $200 million. Persistent challenges such as limited public transportation, insufficient parking, and poor highway access influenced the decision to relocate.

The new Cobb County stadium will sit at the intersection of I-75 and I-285, approximately 14 miles from downtown Atlanta and will anchor a vibrant entertainment complex open year-round. Project costs will be split between the Braves and the Cobb County government, with the Braves committing to covering any cost overruns. Executives expressed confidence that an agreement will be finalized soon.

On Saturday, the civil society organisation Yiaga Africa posted on its X (formerly Twitter) account, stating: “Dear @inecnigeria, we received a report of pre-filled result sheets discovered in PU 004, Eni Ward of Ogori/magongo in Kogi State before voting began. Kindly investigate and address this issue promptly to safeguard the integrity of the process.” In response via its X handle, INEC said it regards the situation with seriousness and is currently investigating the matter. The commission added: “Our attention has been drawn to a report that filled result sheets were discovered in some polling units in Kogi State. The Commission views this situation seriously. Our senior officials deployed to the State are currently investigating the incident(s). The Commission will communicate its decision earnestly.”

article_content: LYON, France: Uruguay ended their Rugby World Cup journey with a heavy 73-0 defeat to New Zealand on Thursday, but they depart the tournament with pride and memorable performances. The team opened their campaign strongly, challenging France’s reserve side before falling 27-12, followed by a competitive 38-17 loss to Italy. Uruguay’s match against Namibia, described by both sides as their 'World Cup final,' was a highlight. They won 36-26, scoring four tries in front of nearly 50,000 spectators—a number tournament organizers noted to illustrate strong neutral support, even for matches involving two lower-ranked nations. Uruguay initially frustrated New Zealand in their final group game, maintaining a record of scoring at least two tries per match until the 20-minute mark. After that, the All Blacks took control, scoring 11 tries. Despite not scoring for the first time in 19 World Cup games, Uruguay never stopped competing. Coach Esteban Meneses expressed his pride: 'I am very proud of the players and staff. New Zealand are the best team in the world, and we played well in the first 20 minutes. I love the passion of the players; they play with heart. They are great players and great people. The way they give everything for the shirt, the game, and the team is what stands out for me from this World Cup.' Captain Andres Vilaseca echoed the coach’s sentiments, saying, 'Today we faced the best team in the world, and sometimes you just have to keep pushing and do your best. Fatigue, both physical and mental, came into play, but we should be proud of ourselves. We had an amazing World Cup—playing against France, Italy, Namibia (which we won), and now New Zealand. It’s about learning, improving, and fostering rugby’s growth in Uruguay. It has been an incredible experience.' Like many coaches of Tier Two teams, Meneses concluded with a familiar call: 'To progress and grow, we need more matches against Tier One teams.'

L’équipe a bien commencé sa campagne, bousculant l’équipe réserve de la France avant de s’incliner 27-12, puis disputant un match accroché contre l’Italie (38-17). Le match contre la Namibie, décrit par les deux équipes comme leur « finale de Coupe du monde », fut un des moments forts. L’Uruguay l’a remporté 36-26, inscrivant quatre essais devant près de 50 000 spectateurs — un chiffre mis en avant par les organisateurs du tournoi, illustrant le soutien du public même lors de rencontres entre nations moins réputées. L’Uruguay a bien débuté face à la Nouvelle-Zélande lors du dernier match de poule, maintenant sa série d’au moins deux essais marqués par match jusqu’à la 20e minute. Ensuite, les All Blacks ont pris le dessus, inscrivant 11 essais. Malgré un score vierge pour la première fois en 19 matchs de Coupe du monde, l’Uruguay n’a jamais cessé de se battre. L’entraîneur Esteban Meneses a exprimé sa fierté : « Je suis très fier des joueurs et du staff. La Nouvelle-Zélande est la meilleure équipe du monde et nous avons bien joué pendant les 20 premières minutes. J’adore la passion des joueurs ; ils jouent avec le cœur. Ce sont d’excellents joueurs et d’excellentes personnes. Cette capacité à tout donner pour le maillot, le jeu et l’équipe, c’est ce que je retiens de cette Coupe du monde. » Le capitaine Andres Vilaseca a partagé cet avis : « Aujourd’hui, nous avons affronté la meilleure équipe du monde, et parfois il faut juste continuer à pousser et donner le meilleur de soi-même. La fatigue, physique comme mentale, s’est fait ressentir, mais nous pouvons être fiers de nous. Nous avons vécu une Coupe du monde incroyable — jouer contre la France, l’Italie, la Namibie (que nous avons gagnée), puis la Nouvelle-Zélande. Il s’agit d’apprendre, de progresser, de faire grandir le rugby en Uruguay. Ce fut une superbe expérience. » Comme beaucoup d’entraîneurs d’équipes de deuxième niveau, Meneses a conclu par un appel devenu habituel : « Pour progresser et se développer, nous avons besoin de plus de matchs contre les équipes du Tier One. »

article_content: The RM UP-01 Ferrari, born from the collaboration between Richard Mille and Ferrari, redefines the limits of mechanical watchmaking. While the shape of a fine watch or a striking supercar might reflect artistic flair, their designs are, above all, rooted in functionality. Elements such as engine layout, ergonomics, and performance shape the final product. Ferrari and Richard Mille are distinguished by their drive for performance and refusal to compromise. Their independence and commitment to innovation have led them to develop elegant, highly functional mechanisms—often setting trends rather than following them. Every Richard Mille watch is crafted with a specific context in mind—be it for motorsport, daily lifestyle, athletics, or artistic endeavors. Regardless of whether a model is tonneau-shaped, round, or ultra-flat, its form is always guided by its function, in line with the brand’s principles: strong architectural design, meticulous attention to detail, excellent ergonomics, and a focus on eliminating unnecessary elements. This philosophy was vital in creating the RM UP-01 Ferrari. According to Julien Boillat, Technical Director for Cases at Richard Mille, the real challenge wasn’t making a watch just 1.75mm thick, but ensuring it could endure daily wear. This required venturing into new technical territory, with traditional watchmaking standards for casing sometimes being pushed from 0.35mm down to just 0.18mm in certain sections. Intensive laboratory testing confirmed the model’s strength and rigidity despite its ultra-thin profile. Rather than redesign the fundamental structure, the RM UP-01 Ferrari retained a traditional approach, using a movement assembled within the case—not relying on the caseback as the baseplate. Inspired by the classic tonneau form of the RM 67-01 but even slimmer, the team increased the surface area to maintain integrity, iterating through many 3D prototypes and material tests. Ultimately, they chose Grade 5 titanium for its durability and machining characteristics. Engineers had only 0.57mm to accommodate both the bezel and caseback around the 1.18mm movement, removing all but the essential components. The design omits a conventional crown and skeletonization to optimize strength. Two sapphire crystals, each only 0.2mm thick, cover the indicators and balance wheel to showcase the watch’s mechanics. The crowns themselves are ingeniously integrated into the bezel and caseback, directly interacting with the gear trains. Testing was rigorous: the assembled prototypes had to withstand a 12kg weight—six times the weight of a standard brick—on the strap, confirming the RM UP-01 Ferrari’s durability and water resistance. Designers from Ferrari contributed to aspects like the hands, counters, engravings, and strap design. Notably, the time indicators borrow from Ferrari’s design spirit: rather than traditional hands, the hour and minute displays are directly integrated into the gear trains. As with all Richard Mille models, exquisite finishing—beveling, satin, polished, and micro-blasted surfaces—features throughout, alongside the signature spline screws and a refined interpretation of the brand’s famed tonneau shape. The RM UP-01 Ferrari stands as a testament to inventive engineering and shared passion for precision. For more details, visit www.richardmille.com.

Ceci a nécessité d’innover techniquement, certains standards horlogers passant de 0,35 mm à seulement 0,18 mm par endroits. Des tests poussés en laboratoire ont validé la solidité et la rigidité du modèle malgré sa finesse extrême. Plutôt que de réinventer la structure de base, la RM UP-01 Ferrari a conservé une conception classique, avec un mouvement monté dans le boîtier—et non un fond servant de platine. S’inspirant du tonneau emblématique de la RM 67-01 en version encore plus fine, l’équipe a élargi la surface pour garder de la solidité, passant par de nombreux prototypes 3D et essais de matériaux. Le titane Grade 5 a finalement été retenu pour sa robustesse et son usinabilité. Les ingénieurs ne disposaient que de 0,57 mm pour intégrer lunette et fond autour du mouvement de 1,18 mm, éliminant tout sauf l’absolu nécessaire. Le design laisse de côté la couronne traditionnelle et le squelettage pour préserver la rigidité. Deux verres saphir de 0,2 mm recouvrent les indicateurs et le balancier, mettant la mécanique en valeur. Les couronnes, elles, sont ingénieusement intégrées entre la lunette et le fond monobloc, agissant directement sur le train d’engrenages. Les tests ont été impitoyables : les prototypes complets ont dû résister à 12 kg—soit six fois le poids d’une brique standard—accrochés au bracelet, prouvant la solidité et l’étanchéité de la RM UP-01 Ferrari. Les designers Ferrari ont participé à la création des indicateurs, compteurs, gravures laser et du bracelet. Particularité : ici pas d’aiguilles classiques ; les heures et minutes sont affichées via les trains d’engrenages, directement inspirés du style Ferrari. Comme toute Richard Mille, la finition est soignée : biseautage, satinage, polissage, microbillage, vis spline caractéristiques, et une interprétation raffinée de la forme tonneau signature. La RM UP-01 Ferrari incarne l’ingéniosité technique et la passion partagée pour la précision. Plus d’info : www.richardmille.com.

Former Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh has criticized the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), stating that the party in the state has split into three groups: 'Maharaj BJP' (led by Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia), 'Shivraj BJP' (led by Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan), and 'angry BJP' (rebel members). Singh made these remarks while addressing Congress party workers at a candidate's office in Gwalior district on Wednesday.

Singh said, “This election is between those who betrayed Congress during the 2020 political crisis and the Congress itself. It is a contest between money power and manpower, between a traitor and an honest person. In 2018, former CM Kamal Nath and I had only five months, and the organization was not fully prepared, but now it is ready.”

He reiterated, “The BJP has split into three groups: Maharaj BJP, Shivraj BJP, and angry BJP. Earlier it was united. With five years to prepare for 2023, our party is fully prepared.”

Singh also claimed there is strong resentment against CM Chouhan, more so than in 2018, and argued that no other party has harmed laborers as much as the BJP.

Additionally, Singh warned Congress members not actively campaigning that they would not receive his support in the future. He raised concerns about Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), alleging potential irregularities and stating, “Any machine with a chip will follow its software, not its operator. Only the Election Commission has the information, which raises doubts.”

He added that EVMs have been abolished in countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh, and while machines cannot convert votes from Congress to BJP or vice versa, they could increase votes for one side.

Madhya Pradesh is among five states voting in assembly elections on November 17, with counting on December 3. Voters will select representatives for 230 Assembly constituencies.

article_content: Kelly Renee Gissendaner remains Georgia’s only female death row inmate after being convicted for organizing her husband Douglas's murder in 1997. While incarcerated at Georgia Diagnostic and Classification State Prison, she formed a remarkable pen-pal friendship with Professor Jürgen Moltmann, a distinguished theologian from Germany. Admitting her role in the crime, Gissendaner started theology studies after receiving her death sentence in 1998. Influenced deeply by theologian Dietrich Bonhoeffer and moved by Moltmann’s writings about hope and perseverance, she sent Moltmann an essay she had written. His response initiated a correspondence that has grown to around 30 letters, discussing faith and Gissendaner’s journey of personal transformation. Moltmann, speaking from Germany, described Gissendaner as sensitive, intelligent, and profoundly changed, standing apart from the negative public image shaped by media coverage. In 2011, the two met face-to-face during his visit to Atlanta, continuing their conversations about faith in a supervised setting. After her prison education program was discontinued, Gissendaner continued her theological studies independently, meeting a teacher weekly in her cell for several months. Her final appeal for clemency was recently denied. The crime centered on Gissendaner’s planning with her boyfriend, Gregory Owen, motivated by a desire for both her lover and financial gain via life insurance. Owen testified against her in exchange for a life sentence. The court heard details of their stormy relationship, prior divorce and remarriage, and Gissendaner’s involvement in evidence destruction after Owen carried out the murder. As authorities investigated, Gissendaner, who appeared on television to plead for public help, was found to have later tried bribing someone to falsely confess to the murder—an attempt exposed by a fellow inmate. Although her execution was postponed, she has selected her last meal. Professor Moltmann remarked that, while the state may not offer mercy, Gissendaner has already experienced spiritual mercy. This case has drawn attention for the stark divide between official condemnation and the acknowledgment by spiritual mentors of Gissendaner’s evolution while in prison.

Around 40,000 years ago, Neanderthals—long inhabitants of western Eurasia—coexisted with Homo sapiens, who had recently migrated from Africa. For thousands of years, both species shared the continent, leading to the integration of Neanderthal DNA into the modern human genome. Researchers at the University of Geneva (UNIGE) have studied how Neanderthal DNA has persisted and varied in the genomes of people across Eurasia for the past 40,000 years. Their research, published in Science Advances, shows subtle shifts in the percentage of Neanderthal DNA over different periods and between regions. Present-day Eurasians have about 2% Neanderthal DNA, with slightly higher levels in Asian populations compared to Europeans.

While some scientists propose that regional differences result from natural selection, Mathias Currat and his team at UNIGE present a migration-based explanation. According to their computer models, after interbreeding, the proportion of DNA from the local population tends to rise as you move farther from the origin of the migrating group.

In the case of Homo sapiens and Neanderthals, this means that Neanderthal DNA becomes more common the further one moves from Africa, as Neanderthals were most concentrated in Europe. The team tested their hypothesis using a database from Harvard Medical School with information from more than 4,000 ancient Eurasian genomes. Due to the abundance of archaeological discoveries in Europe, the study mainly focuses on European populations.

Findings indicate that right after modern humans spread out of Africa, Paleolithic European hunter-gatherers carried slightly more Neanderthal DNA than Asians did during the same era—a pattern that aligns with archaeological evidence, since Neanderthal remains have not been found beyond western Eurasia and the Altai region in Siberia.

During the shift to agriculture between 10,000 and 5,000 years ago, farmers migrated into Europe from Anatolia (present-day Turkey) and the Aegean, bringing less Neanderthal ancestry with them. As these farmers intermingled with local populations, the overall Neanderthal DNA among Europeans decreased, leading to the current pattern where Asians have marginally more Neanderthal DNA than Europeans.

Comparing ancient DNA with archaeological findings is helping scientists unravel the intertwined histories of Neanderthals and Homo sapiens. According to the study’s authors, their work creates a new reference for researchers hoping to identify genetic outliers that may influence health or evolutionary advantages.

Grâce à la richesse des découvertes archéologiques en Europe, l’étude se concentre principalement sur les populations européennes.

Les chercheurs ont constaté qu’immédiatement après la dispersion d’Homo sapiens hors d’Afrique, les chasseurs-cueilleurs européens du Paléolithique possédaient un peu plus d’ADN néandertalien que leurs homologues asiatiques de la même période — cohérent avec les données archéologiques, les restes néandertaliens n’ayant pas été retrouvés au-delà de l’Altaï en Sibérie.

En se mélangeant aux populations locales, la part d’ADN néandertalien chez les Européens a diminué, expliquant pourquoi, actuellement, les Asiatiques en présentent légèrement plus.

La combinaison de l’ADN ancien et des découvertes archéologiques aide les chercheurs à reconstituer l’histoire commune des Néandertaliens et d’Homo sapiens. Selon les auteurs de l’étude, leur travail sert désormais de référence pour repérer des profils génétiques particuliers pouvant influencer la santé ou donner un avantage évolutif.

article_content: Five Republican presidential candidates will participate in the third primary debate on Wednesday in Miami. NBC News is hosting the event at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. The debate will air from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. ET (0100 to 0300 GMT Thursday). Florida, the home state of both former President Donald Trump and Governor Ron DeSantis, now leans conservative after years of being considered a political battleground. Its Republican primary is set for March, but earlier contests in Iowa, New Hampshire, and South Carolina are expected to have a greater influence. Candidates who have qualified for the debate, according to the Republican National Committee, are DeSantis, former U.S. Ambassador Nikki Haley, entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy, former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, and Senator Tim Scott. North Dakota Governor Doug Burgum and former Arkansas Governor Asa Hutchinson did not qualify. Debate qualification required at least 4% in two national polls (since Sept. 1) or 4% in one national poll plus 4% in at least two early states (Iowa, New Hampshire, Nevada, South Carolina), alongside at least 70,000 unique donors (including at least 200 from 20 states or territories) and a pledge to support the eventual Republican nominee. Donald Trump will not participate in the debate, instead holding a rally in Hialeah, Florida—a community with a large Cuban-American population—starting at 7 p.m. ET. Trump, who leads in national polls by nearly 40 percentage points according to a recent Reuters/Ipsos survey, has said it does not make sense for him to join the debates given his commanding lead. The first two debates had little effect on Trump's position in the polls. DeSantis and Haley are vying for second place; while DeSantis leads nationally, Haley is ahead in New Hampshire and South Carolina. A strong performance in this debate might help one of them gain momentum, but both remain far behind Trump in national polls. In other news, Tata Group has acquired Wistron's manufacturing facility—a $750 million deal, including debt—making Tata the first Indian company to assemble iPhones. India has surpassed China in representation in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2024, reflecting growth in its higher education sector. Separately, independent directors of Religare Enterprises Ltd have raised allegations against the Burman family, which recently made an open offer to take control of the company.

Justice Clarence Thomas is quietly marking his 20th anniversary on the Supreme Court. His former law clerks are organizing a reunion, giving him a chance to reconnect with many of the young lawyers, whom he affectionately calls his "kids." As he prepares for the new court term, Thomas has spent his summer much as he always does: traveling the country in his 40-foot motor home with his wife, Virginia, and teaching at the University of Nebraska, where he is a devoted Cornhuskers football fan.

At 63, Thomas enjoys a professional resurgence, a contrast to the intense scrutiny he faced during the tumultuous October 1991 Senate confirmation hearings. The televised hearings, which became a national spectacle, brought his private life into the spotlight and signaled an era of intensified focus on the federal courts and the contentious politics surrounding them. According to appellate attorney Thomas Goldstein, ideological conflicts drove the hearings, with Thomas perceived as "extremely conservative." Opposition initially failed, but when Anita Hill accused Thomas of sexual harassment, the proceedings turned explosive.

Nominated by President George H.W. Bush to succeed Justice Thurgood Marshall, Thomas faced questions from both Republicans and Democrats regarding his limited judicial experience and ideological stance. The first Senate Judiciary Committee hearing saw little controversy, but Hill—a lawyer whom Thomas had supervised—came forward and described sexually inappropriate behavior, alleging sexual harassment. Hill's composed and detailed testimony received a mix of empathy and skepticism from senators. Thomas responded strongly to the accusations, famously calling the hearings a "high-tech lynching." Ultimately, the Senate confirmed him by a narrow 52-48 margin—the closest in a century for a Supreme Court justice.

After joining the court, Thomas maintained a low profile, rarely speaking from the bench and avoiding interviews. Some lawyers, like Carter Phillips, wish he were more vocal during oral arguments, arguing that his silence leaves a gap in the court's public deliberations. However, those close to Thomas describe him as a warm, engaging storyteller behind the scenes. Former clerk Carrie Severino notes that he often surprises people with his friendly and sociable nature, defying expectations both on and off the bench.

Thomas is widely recognized for knowing court employees by name and maintaining friendships across ideological lines, notably with Justice Stephen Breyer. His independence and frequent dissents on issues such as state-federal authority and government regulation have made him a quietly influential figure among conservative justices. CNN Senior Legal Analyst Jeffrey Toobin describes Thomas as an intellectual leader, with the court having followed his lead on free speech, gun rights, and federal power in recent years.

Controversy, however, continues to shadow Thomas. Liberal lawmakers have called for him to recuse himself from cases related to the Affordable Care Act, citing his appearances at conservative events and his wife's previously undisclosed income of about $700,000. Representative Louise Slaughter and others have formally requested a Justice Department investigation. Still, as Doug Kendall of the Constitutional Accountability Center notes, Supreme Court recusal is largely self-policed, with justices responsible for their own decisions to step aside.

While Thomas acknowledges concerns about his legacy, he remains committed to performing his duties according to his own judgment. Writing in his 2007 autobiography, Thomas described his life as "the story of an ordinary man to whom extraordinary things happened" and expressed enduring faith that his story may hold meaning for others.

À 63 ans, Thomas connaît un renouveau professionnel, contraste flagrant avec les difficultés rencontrées lors de ses auditions de confirmation houleuses au Sénat en octobre 1991. Retransmises à la télévision, ces audiences sont devenues un spectacle national, mettant sa vie privée au premier plan et marquant le début d’une ère où la justice fédérale et la politique conflictuelle sont davantage scrutées. Nommé par le président George H.W. Bush pour succéder au juge Thurgood Marshall, Thomas a dû faire face à des interrogations de la part des républicains comme des démocrates sur son expérience judiciaire limitée et sa position idéologique. La première audition du comité sénatorial s’est déroulée sans polémique, mais Hill — une avocate supervisée par Thomas — est venue témoigner, dénonçant des comportements à connotation sexuelle. Son témoignage calme et détaillé a suscité une réaction mitigée des sénateurs, entre empathie et scepticisme. Thomas a fermement répondu, qualifiant les auditions de « lynchage technologique ». Finalement, il a été confirmé par 52 voix contre 48, la marge la plus étroite depuis un siècle.

Certains avocats, à l’instar de Carter Phillips, aimeraient qu’il soit plus présent dans les débats publics, estimant que son silence crée un manque. Mais selon ses proches, il est, en privé, un conteur chaleureux et engageant. Carrie Severino, une ancienne assistante, souligne qu’il surprend souvent par sa convivialité, défiant toutes les attentes, tant à la Cour qu’en dehors.

Thomas est reconnu pour connaître chaque employé par leur nom et entretenir des liens amicaux avec tous, notamment le juge Stephen Breyer. Son indépendance et ses dissidences régulières sur les questions telles que l’autorité fédérale ou la régulation lui ont valu une influence discrète mais réelle parmi les juges conservateurs. L’analyste juridique Jeffrey Toobin de CNN le qualifie de leader intellectuel, soulignant que la Cour a suivi son approche sur la liberté d’expression, le droit aux armes et les pouvoirs fédéraux ces dernières années.

La controverse continue de l’entourer. Des élus libéraux ont demandé son retrait des affaires concernant la réforme de la santé, pointant ses participations à des événements conservateurs et le revenu de sa femme — près de 700 000 $ — non déclaré. La députée Louise Slaughter et d’autres ont officiellement saisi la justice. Pourtant, comme le rappelle Doug Kendall du Constitutional Accountability Center, la récusation à la Cour suprême relève avant tout du jugement du juge.

Si Thomas reconnaît s’interroger sur sa postérité, il reste avant tout concentré sur sa mission. Dans son autobiographie de 2007, il décrit sa vie comme celle « d’un homme ordinaire à qui il est arrivé des choses extraordinaires », convaincu que son histoire en inspirera d’autres.

A 73-year-old woman was attacked by a bear while walking with her husband and their dog near the U.S.-Canada border. The incident took place around 3 p.m. on Sunday, when officials from Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks were notified that a woman had been attacked along the bank of Trail Creek, a few miles west of North Fork Road.

Authorities reported that the woman, her husband, and their dog were on national forest land when a bear suddenly emerged from thick brush and attacked her. Her husband used bear spray, prompting the bear to retreat. The couple returned to their vehicle and drove to an area where they could contact emergency services.

An air ambulance responded promptly, arriving at the site about 20 miles south of the U.S.-Canada border. The injured woman was transported by helicopter to Logan Health Medical Center in Kalispell, Montana, located about 50 miles from the attack site.

Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks wardens and bear specialists are actively investigating the incident and monitoring the area along Trail Creek, known as the “Bubble ups,” where the creek flows underground before resurfacing. The site is currently closed during the ongoing investigation, and authorities have not yet identified the species of bear involved.

Officials emphasized that Montana is bear country, especially in the fall when bears are more active as they prepare for hibernation. This increased activity coincides with hunting season and other recreational activities. Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks advises that preventing encounters with bears is easier than dealing with conflicts after they occur.

article_content: Cap Haitien, Haiti – On Tuesday, Haiti’s government appeared to have lost control of Cap Haitien, as demonstrators angry over the United Nations’ alleged role in starting the current cholera epidemic controlled many city streets for a second day. Commercial flights at the airport in Haiti’s second-largest city were suspended. Police avoided wearing uniforms, apparently to escape the anger of residents after at least one police station was set on fire Monday. The only way to travel from the airport into town was by motorcycle. Numerous roads were blocked by barricades made of burning tires and vehicles. By sunset, smoke from multiple fires mixed with tear gas used by peacekeepers lingered over the city. Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Jean-Max Bellerive’s office announced it would send a delegation of ministers by helicopter from Port-au-Prince to Cap Haitien to restore order; however, they were not visible by nightfall. At least one protester was killed by a U.N. peacekeeper during Monday’s riots. Hotel guests remained inside, unwilling to risk the turmoil outside. Protesters blame Nepalese peacekeepers for introducing cholera to Haiti, an accusation the United Nations denies. More than 1,000 people have died from the outbreak, and Cap Haitien’s surrounding North Department has seen the highest cholera death rate in the country. According to the Ministry of Public Health, of the 1,578 people hospitalized in the North Department, 119 have died, representing a 7.5 percent death rate as of Tuesday. MINUSTAH, the UN peacekeeping mission in Haiti, suggested the unrest may be politically motivated ahead of national elections on November 28. Imogen Wall, a UN spokesperson, said at least one UN warehouse was looted, and a flight carrying cholera supplies to Cap Haitien was suspended. She stated, “Cap Haitien is very serious for cholera right now. You can't run cholera response in this atmosphere.” In the town of Hinche, about 400 people protested against the peacekeepers, and six were injured, according to MINUSTAH spokesperson Vincenzo Pugliese. Lesley Voltaire, a former education minister and presidential candidate, described how a child suffering from cholera died after help failed to arrive, sparking public outrage. He added that the protests were spontaneous and that Nepalese peacekeepers were the main target, as many believe cholera came from Nepal. In Quartier Morin, a municipality near Cap Haitien, a protester was shot and killed by a peacekeeper who reportedly acted in self-defense, according to the UN. An investigation is ongoing. Cholera, confirmed in seven of Haiti’s ten departments since last month, has killed 1,034 out of 16,799 hospitalized people, the health ministry reports. The government is working to improve data collection to get a clearer picture. Pan American Health Organization’s Dan Epstein noted the difficulty of counting deaths outside hospitals since many NGOs run their own facilities. Efforts are underway to standardize information gathering. The government has launched public health campaigns via radio and television to inform citizens about preventing and treating cholera, mainly through oral rehydration and good hygiene, both of which remain in short supply. The earthquake last January, which killed more than 200,000 people, further weakened Haiti’s infrastructure. Over a million people now live in makeshift camps around the capital. Many camps have latrines and access to clean water, but slums, like Cite Soleil, lack such resources and see faster disease spread. Nigel Fisher, deputy special representative for the UN, expressed more concern for slums than for camps. Despite the crisis, plans continue for the November 28 elections, with discussions on disinfecting polling booths and other safety measures. There are efforts to increase cholera treatment beds and to transport the sickest patients to care centers. However, some residents oppose moving patients amid fears of further spread. The U.S. CDC’s Dr. Jordan Tappero reported that the cholera strain found in Haiti is not unique to South Asia and could have reached Haiti via various routes. Identifying a single source is challenging, and the focus should be on preventing deaths. Health workers are being trained to manage severe cholera cases, aiming to lower the mortality rate to below 1 percent. As of Tuesday, the nationwide death rate among hospitalized cholera patients stood at 3.9 percent. The UN has sought $164 million in international aid, anticipating up to 200,000 cholera cases in Haiti in the coming months. Cholera, caused by drinking contaminated water, can have mild or severe symptoms, including diarrhea, vomiting, rapid dehydration, and potentially, death. CNN’s Tom Watkins contributed to this report.

Au coucher du soleil, la fumée des nombreux incendies se mêlait aux gaz lacrymogènes utilisés par les Casques bleus et planait sur la ville. Plus tôt dans la journée, le bureau du Premier ministre Jean-Max Bellerive avait annoncé l’envoi par hélicoptère d’une délégation de ministres depuis Port-au-Prince à Cap-Haïtien pour rétablir l’ordre ; toutefois, ils n’étaient pas visibles à la tombée de la nuit. Au moins un manifestant a été tué par un Casque bleu lors des émeutes de lundi. Les clients des hôtels sont restés à l’intérieur, ne voulant pas risquer la tourmente extérieure. Les manifestants accusent les Casques bleus népalais d’avoir introduit le choléra en Haïti, une accusation niée par les Nations Unies. Selon le ministère de la Santé publique, sur 1 578 personnes hospitalisées dans le département du Nord, 119 sont décédées, ce qui représente un taux de mortalité de 7,5 % à la date de mardi. La MINUSTAH, mission onusienne de maintien de la paix en Haïti, a suggéré que les troubles pourraient être motivés politiquement avant les élections nationales prévues le 28 novembre. Imogen Wall, porte-parole de l’ONU, a indiqué qu’au moins un entrepôt onusien avait été pillé et qu’un vol transportant des fournitures de choléra à destination de Cap-Haïtien était suspendu. Elle a déclaré : « La situation de choléra à Cap-Haïtien est très grave en ce moment. Il est impossible de répondre à la crise du choléra dans cette ambiance. » À Hinche, environ 400 personnes ont manifesté contre les Casques bleus et six ont été blessées, selon Vincenzo Pugliese, porte-parole de la MINUSTAH. Lesley Voltaire, ancien ministre de l’Éducation et candidat à la présidence, a expliqué qu’un enfant atteint de choléra est décédé après que l’aide n’est jamais arrivée, déclenchant l’indignation du public. Il a ajouté que les protestations étaient spontanées et que les Casques bleus népalais étaient la principale cible, beaucoup croyant que le choléra venait du Népal. À Quartier Morin, une commune près de Cap-Haïtien, un manifestant a été abattu par un Casque bleu qui aurait agi en légitime défense, selon l’ONU. Une enquête est en cours. Le choléra, confirmé dans sept des dix départements d’Haïti depuis le mois dernier, a tué 1 034 personnes sur 16 799 hospitalisées selon le ministère de la Santé. Le gouvernement cherche à améliorer la collecte de données pour obtenir une vue plus précise. Dan Epstein, de l’Organisation panaméricaine de la santé, a souligné la difficulté de recenser les décès hors des hôpitaux car de nombreuses ONG gèrent leurs propres structures. Des efforts sont en cours pour harmoniser le recueil des informations. Le gouvernement a lancé des campagnes de sensibilisation via la radio et la télévision pour informer les citoyens sur la prévention et le traitement du choléra, principalement via la réhydratation orale et une bonne hygiène, toutes deux encore rares. Le séisme de janvier dernier, qui a tué plus de 200 000 personnes, a encore affaibli les infrastructures déjà précaires du pays. Plus d’un million de personnes vivent désormais dans des camps de fortune autour de la capitale. Beaucoup de ces camps disposent de latrines et d’eau propre, mais les quartiers défavorisés comme Cité Soleil manquent de telles ressources et voient la maladie se propager plus rapidement. Nigel Fisher, représentant adjoint du Secrétaire général de l’ONU, a exprimé davantage d’inquiétudes pour les quartiers défavorisés que pour les camps. Malgré la crise, les préparatifs pour les élections du 28 novembre continuent, avec des discussions sur la désinfection des bureaux de vote et d’autres mesures de sécurité. Des efforts sont en cours pour augmenter le nombre de lits disponibles contre le choléra et acheminer les cas les plus graves vers des centres de soins. Certains habitants s’opposent cependant à ces transferts, craignant une propagation accrue. Le Dr Jordan Tappero des CDC américains rapporte que la souche de choléra retrouvée en Haïti n’est pas spécifique à l’Asie du Sud et a pu arriver selon différents moyens. Identifier une source unique est difficile ; l’essentiel est de prévenir les décès. Le personnel soignant est formé à la prise en charge des cas graves, l’objectif étant de ramener la mortalité à moins de 1 %. Au mardi, le taux de décès national parmi les patients hospitalisés atteints de choléra était de 3,9 %.  L’ONU a sollicité 164 millions de dollars d’aide internationale, prévoyant jusqu’à 200 000 cas de choléra en Haïti dans les mois à venir. Le choléra, causé par l’ingestion d’eau contaminée, peut présenter des symptômes bénins ou graves : diarrhée, vomissements, déshydratation rapide et parfois la mort. Tom Watkins de CNN a contribué à ce reportage.

Nvidia is at the forefront of the AI revolution—and is ramping up hiring to keep pace. The Santa Clara-based tech giant produces GPUs, specialized computer chips that power AI models for companies such as Microsoft. These pivotal chips have driven Nvidia's stock price up over 200% in the past year. To meet rising demand, Nvidia plans to triple production of its $40,000 chips, build AI factories, and launch its latest, most advanced GPU—the H200—in 2024.

This major expansion requires more talent, so Nvidia is actively recruiting. As of November 14, the company has 1,810 job openings worldwide. Most are in engineering—chip design, software engineering, and AI product development—but more than 100 roles are open in operations, sales, and program management.

 "We have many opportunities," said Lindsey Duran, Nvidia's VP of global recruiting, in an interview with Insider. "A lot of our goals continue to be focused on engineering and AI."

Here are 5 tips on getting hired at Nvidia, according to Duran:

1) Highlight your skills on your résumé. Be sure to list your specific, relevant skills. For technical roles, Nvidia looks for strengths in math, computer vision, programming, machine learning, deep learning, data handling, and working with GPUs. This is especially key for applicants with non-technical degrees. Positions like AI developer, security architect, and generative AI performance engineer can pay up to $333,500.

2) Show you're more than your degree. Stand out by highlighting your career milestones, leadership, and achievements on your résumé or in interviews. Emphasize past projects to demonstrate problem-solving skills and impact. This is particularly important for those from unconventional educational backgrounds.

3) Demonstrate genuine interest in generative AI—but use it wisely. Nvidia values familiarity with tools like ChatGPT, but adaptability and a keen interest in the field are more important than tool-specific expertise. Do not use AI tools to shortcut the application process or in interviews—Nvidia discourages this.

4) Leverage your professional network. Connections within Nvidia can boost your hiring chances, as the company maintains a strong employee referral program.

5) Pursue an internship. If you're at the start of your career or lack specific skills, consider applying for an internship. Nvidia welcomes undergraduate, master's, PhD candidates, and those from varied backgrounds. As of mid-November, there were 154 internship openings, including in sales and research. U.S.-based internships pay between $19 and $93 per hour, depending on background.

article_content: Sony announced it will release the Seth Rogen and James Franco comedy 'The Interview' just days after previously canceling its scheduled Christmas release due to threats from hackers. Last week, Sony canceled the film's release after cinemas received threats of real-world attacks for screening the film. Company attorney David Boies confirmed on NBC's 'Meet the Press' that the release was only delayed and not canceled. President Obama later stated that Sony made a mistake by canceling the movie, expressing he would have intervened to ensure its release. Hackers leaked emails between Sony Pictures co-chair Amy Pascal and producer Scott Rudin, which included racially inappropriate jokes about President Obama's film preferences. These leaks also exposed internal conflicts at Sony, including private criticisms between executives and negative comments about actress Angelina Jolie's abilities and her project ideas. Pascal used harsh language in private emails, while Jolie was described as a 'minimally talented spoiled brat' concerning her 'Cleopatra' project. David Boies called the cyberattack on Sony 'a state-sponsored criminal attack on an American corporation and its employees.' He stated Sony appreciated FBI assistance and urged more government support to protect national security. According to reporting from The Daily Beast and Vox, one distribution option could be Crackle, Sony's own streaming platform, though Boies said the method of release had not yet been finalized. Most cinema chains that were set to show the movie withdrew following the threats. The leaked documents also included information about upcoming films and internal debates within Sony. Following the incident, North Korea reportedly threatened additional attacks against the U.S. government and other institutions. President Obama announced that considerations were being made to return North Korea to the list of state sponsors of terrorism. North Korea denied any involvement in the Sony hack, called it a 'righteous deed,' and in a statement from KCNA, issued threats towards the U.S. while attributing the film to U.S. propaganda against the country.

Michael Bradley led the United States to a 2-0 victory over Panama in Los Angeles on Sunday with an impressive goal scored directly from a corner kick, known as an 'Olimpico.' Bradley’s remarkable strike came in the 27th minute when he curled the ball over Panama goalkeeper Jaime Penedo and into the far corner for his 13th international goal. Initial confusion over a possible touch by Jozy Altidore was dispelled after replays showed the ball sailed directly over his head into the net. Ten minutes later, Clint Dempsey doubled the lead with a composed finish following some skilled footwork.

Panama struggled offensively—a pattern continuing from their previous encounter, when the US knocked them out of World Cup contention in 2013 with two stoppage-time goals. Panama has managed only one win against the US in 15 meetings, with the US winning the last six. This victory marked Jurgen Klinsmann’s first as US coach since their 2-1 win over Ghana in the opening group game at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. However, some US supporters expressed dissatisfaction with Klinsmann, displaying banners such as 'JK OUT' and 'Red Card the Coach.'

With important matches ahead, including the Gold Cup and World Cup qualifying, the result offers Klinsmann a timely boost. The US next faces friendlies against Denmark and Switzerland in March.

Une confusion initiale à propos d’une éventuelle déviation de Jozy Altidore a été vite dissipée : les ralentis ont montré que le ballon avait bien filé au-dessus de sa tête avant d’entrer dans le but. Dix minutes plus tard, Clint Dempsey a doublé l’avance des Américains grâce à une finition tranquille après une belle action technique.

Le Panama a connu des difficultés offensives—une tendance déjà vue lors de leur précédente confrontation, quand les États-Unis les avaient éliminés des qualifications à la Coupe du Monde 2013 grâce à deux buts dans le temps additionnel. Le Panama n’a gagné qu’une seule fois en quinze rencontres face aux États-Unis, qui restent sur six victoires consécutives. Ce succès marque la première victoire de Jurgen Klinsmann comme sélectionneur américain depuis celle contre le Ghana (2-1) lors du match d’ouverture à la Coupe du Monde 2014 au Brésil. Cependant, certains supporters des États-Unis ont exprimé leur frustration envers Klinsmann, brandissant des banderoles telles que « JK OUT » et « Red Card the Coach ».

Avec des échéances majeures à venir, notamment la Gold Cup et les qualifications à la Coupe du Monde, ce résultat arrive au bon moment pour Klinsmann. Les États-Unis joueront ensuite des matchs amicaux contre le Danemark et la Suisse en mars.

article_content: Champion cyclist Lance Armstrong has refiled a lawsuit against the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency (USADA) in an effort to halt a doping case against him. This follows a federal judge's dismissal of his initial suit, which criticized Armstrong for including legally irrelevant claims meant to attract media coverage and generate hostility toward USADA. The judge, U.S. District Judge Sam Sparks, advised Armstrong to refile without improper arguments or irrelevant material. The revised lawsuit is much shorter, about 55 pages less than the original, and seeks a court injunction before USADA’s Saturday deadline for Armstrong to either contest the charges or face sanctions. USADA has accused Armstrong of using performance-enhancing drugs. Armstrong maintains he has never tested positive throughout his more than 20-year career, stating in the suit that he underwent 500 to 600 drug tests without a positive result. He argues USADA lacks the right to force him into arbitration without a valid, enforceable legal agreement. Armstrong, 40, could face a lifetime ban and the loss of his Tour de France victories if found guilty by USADA. He won the Tour each year from 1999 to 2005, mostly for a team sponsored by the U.S. Postal Service. Armstrong retired twice from cycling—first in 2005, returning four years later, and again in 2011. USADA, a quasi-governmental agency, serves as the official anti-doping authority for Olympic, Pan American, and Paralympic events in the United States. In a June letter to Armstrong, USADA stated that blood samples from 2009 and 2010 showed evidence consistent with blood manipulation, including EPO use or blood transfusions. EPO (erythropoietin) increases red blood cell counts, boosting oxygen delivery to muscles. Armstrong has faced ongoing allegations of doping, notably from Floyd Landis—who was stripped of his own 2006 Tour de France title for doping—and from Tyler Hamilton, who on CBS News’ '60 Minutes' in 2011 said he witnessed Armstrong use EPO in 1999. In February, the Justice Department closed a criminal investigation into Armstrong after determining there was insufficient evidence to bring charges. Armstrong has recently competed in two half-distance Ironman events, although he is currently suspended from World Triathlon Corporation competitions. Armstrong was also a U.S. triathlon champion as a teenager.

article_content: Three U.S. Army soldiers have been reprimanded for their involvement in a prostitution scandal in Cartagena, Colombia, the military announced Friday. The incident occurred shortly before President Barack Obama's visit to the city for the Summit of the Americas in April and also implicated members of the U.S. Secret Service and other federal agents. According to U.S. Southern Command, all three soldiers received letters of reprimand. One was ordered to forfeit half of his base salary for two months, while the other two were assigned 45 days of extra duties and must forfeit their base salaries for two months. The identities of the soldiers were not disclosed. Previously, four other soldiers and two Marines received similar non-judicial punishments, and an Air Force member was also reprimanded. Two Navy personnel declined non-judicial punishment and are awaiting court-martial. In total, thirteen Secret Service agents were implicated; most have resigned or retired, while three were cleared of serious misconduct. Three agents from the Drug Enforcement Administration also admitted to paying for sexual services, according to the Justice Department’s inspector general. While prostitution is legal in Colombia, reports of Secret Service agents engaging in heavy drinking and bringing prostitutes to their hotel rooms led to security concerns and tarnished the agency’s reputation. However, an investigation concluded that presidential security was not compromised.

At least 22 passengers drowned on Monday following a boat accident in Niger State. The victims were traveling from Kasabu village in Agwara Local Government Area, Niger State, to Yauri in Kebbi State when their boat capsized due to a heavy downpour and strong winds. As of Tuesday night, search and rescue teams had recovered six bodies, including that of a pastor from Kebbi based in Niger State.

The Niger State Emergency Management Agency (NSEMA) reported that most of the victims had been heading to Yauri’s Monday Market and likely were not wearing life jackets at the time of the accident. According to NSEMA spokesman Hussaine Ibrahim, rescue operations have been severely hampered by ongoing rain. Four bodies were recovered Tuesday morning, with two more found later in the day. Most of the victims are from Niger State, while at least one is from Zuru in Kebbi State.

Authorities continue search and rescue efforts despite challenging weather conditions.

Mardi soir, les équipes de secours n’avaient retrouvé que six corps, dont celui d’un pasteur originaire du Kebbi mais basé dans l’État du Niger.

L’Agence de gestion des situations d’urgence de l’État du Niger (NSEMA) a indiqué que la plupart des victimes se rendaient au marché du lundi de Yauri et ne portaient probablement pas de gilets de sauvetage au moment du naufrage. A married teacher at a prestigious New York girls' school has been suspended following allegations of an affair with a teenage student. Jonathan Fuller, 55, was removed from his teaching position at the Upper East Side's Nightingale-Bamford School last Friday, after a complaint about an alleged relationship with a former pupil. Staff and parents expressed shock, as the suspension came just days after the start of the school year.

The Nightingale-Bamford School, among the most elite and expensive private schools in New York, is known to have inspired the TV show 'Gossip Girl'. Children of prominent families, such as film producer Harvey Weinstein and members of the Tisch and Bronfman families, have attended the school.

Fuller, a popular science and psychology teacher, was suspended after a letter from the school's new headteacher, Paul Burke, was sent to parents. The letter did not disclose the details of the alleged inappropriate behavior or the teacher’s identity but stated that the faculty member had been suspended due to reports received in the previous two days.

Headteacher Burke wrote, 'I am sorry to have to tell you that this morning I suspended an Upper School faculty member in light of reports received over the past two days that, if true, describe behavior that is not only inappropriate, but also completely inconsistent with our rules and values.' He added that dismissal was possible if the allegations were confirmed.

An independent investigator has been appointed to determine whether the former pupil was underage when the alleged relationship began and if there were any other similar incidents. While not named in the letter, Jonathan Fuller’s identity was confirmed by school officials in a staff meeting. His class schedule, syllabus, and name have been removed from the school’s website. Fuller declined to comment.

With the arrivals of Cesc Fabregas and Diego Costa, Mourinho is confident that Chelsea can add the necessary creativity and finishing touch up front. Pre-season preparations have heavily focused on tactics to unlock packed defenses encountered in the league.

Mourinho explained that playing against teams that allow little space or time makes the game far more challenging, and his team must show greater skill and nuance under pressure. The squad is actively working on these qualities. Fabregas is expected to bolster midfield creativity and mesh well with the team’s energetic runners, while Costa should give Chelsea a decisive edge in front of goal, addressing last year’s striker concerns.

Given the demanding schedule—spanning the Premier League, various cup competitions, and international fixtures—Mourinho emphasized that every midfielder, including Mikel, Matic, Ramires, Schurrle, and Van Ginkel, will be involved. Squad rotation will be vital for balance and success.
