article_content: WASHINGTON — Speaker Mike Johnson assumed control of a fractured House Republican majority following the sudden removal of his predecessor, Kevin McCarthy, last month. As Johnson, R-La., attempts to unify the party’s narrow majority, he faces the same hard-right factions and internal divisions that undermined McCarthy, R-Calif. This ongoing discord is stalling the party’s legislative agenda and fueling questions about any leader’s effectiveness. This past week, rising tensions on Capitol Hill led to several incidents—including a Republican senator challenging a Teamsters union boss to a fight. The new speaker was forced to cancel legislative business and dismiss lawmakers early for Thanksgiving. "This place is a pressure cooker,” Johnson said, in hopes that the atmosphere would cool down. However, unity still appears out of reach. House Republicans who pledged to cut federal spending, investigate President Joe Biden, and reverse Democratic initiatives have made limited headway. Earlier this year, McCarthy struck an agreement with Biden to reduce deficits by $1.5 trillion over ten years, but most of those reductions remain on paper since connected bills haven’t fully passed. Some legislation has been withdrawn due to disagreement, as centrists argue proposed cuts go too far while hard-right members demand deeper reductions. With a government shutdown looming, Congress passed another temporary funding measure—a continuing resolution—that prolongs current spending levels for a few more months. This averted an immediate shutdown, but sets up the next debate for January. Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, voiced frustration after the vote, saying, "We haven’t done anything!" Many conservatives criticized the stopgap bill for preserving spending levels set when Democrats controlled the House under Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif. Roy and others questioned when Republicans would fulfill their promises and exercise their majority. Similar criticism led to McCarthy's historic ouster in October—a risk now facing Johnson. The spending standoff highlights the gap between calls for a smaller government and the reality of cutting programs that impact constituents. Rep. Nick LaLota, R-N.Y., a centrist, opposed funding for the Justice Department, arguing public safety cuts would hurt his district. “My constituents don’t want me voting for that,” he stated. Republicans are also frustrated by frequent late-night voting and hundreds of amendments on legislation that rarely advances. LaLota noted, after ten months in the majority, the approach isn’t working. “My constituents want us to cut, but they want us to cut in the right areas,” he added. Meanwhile, external crises demand Congress’s attention. President Biden requested nearly $106 billion for aid to Ukraine, Israel, humanitarian relief in Gaza, and border security—a top issue when Congress returns. Ahead of the funding vote, Johnson outlined a stopgap proposal modeled on the Freedom Caucus’ idea to split deadlines, with funding running out January 19 for some agencies and February 2 for others. Conservatives widely rejected the plan and criticized the decision not to tie in the Israel aid bill to force Senate action. Still, some conservatives are willing to give Johnson time to adjust. “The new speaker is respected. He’s admired, he’s trusted,” said Rep. Bob Good, R-Va. “He’s human. He’s imperfect, like we all are.” Republicans know their slim House majority is increasingly vulnerable ahead of the 2024 elections if promises go unfulfilled. More lawmakers from both parties are opting to retire rather than persist in partisan fights. Johnson defended his first three weeks as speaker, saying, “I can't turn an aircraft carrier overnight,” and asserting that his situation differs from McCarthy’s. “We have some great plans,” he told reporters. But Rep. Garrett Graves, R-La., a McCarthy ally, urged caution. “The idea that by electing a new speaker, you are going to suddenly have all these new options—I think is now being realized this is not factual,” he said, forecasting ongoing difficulties. After House Democrats helped Johnson prevent a shutdown, Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, whose party assisted in ousting McCarthy, said he hoped to foster a good relationship with Johnson. When asked for advice for the speaker, Jeffries replied, “Good luck.”
translated_content: WASHINGTON — Le président de la Chambre, Mike Johnson, a pris la tête d’une majorité républicaine fracturée après la destitution soudaine de son prédécesseur, Kevin McCarthy, le mois dernier. Alors que Johnson (Républicain-Louisiane) tente de rassembler sa mince majorité, il se heurte aux mêmes factions d’extrême droite et divisions internes qui ont déstabilisé McCarthy (Républicain-Californie). Ce désaccord continu freine l’agenda législatif du parti et soulève des questions sur la capacité de tout chef à gouverner efficacement. Cette semaine au Capitole, la tension est montée d’un cran, notamment lorsqu’un sénateur républicain a défié un chef du syndicat des Teamsters à un duel. Le nouveau président a été contraint d’annuler les travaux législatifs et de renvoyer les députés chez eux plus tôt à l’occasion de Thanksgiving. « Cet endroit est une cocotte-minute », a estimé Johnson, espérant que le climat finirait par se détendre. Pourtant, l’unité semble toujours hors de portée. Les Républicains de la Chambre, qui avaient promis de réduire les dépenses fédérales, d’enquêter sur le président Joe Biden et d’annuler les initiatives démocrates, n’ont que peu progressé. Plus tôt cette année, McCarthy avait conclu un accord avec Biden pour réduire le déficit de 1,5 billion de dollars sur dix ans, mais la plupart des mesures nécessaires n’ont pas été adoptées. Certains projets ont été retirés à cause de désaccords : les centristes estiment que les réductions vont trop loin, tandis que l’aile droite réclame davantage. Pour éviter la fermeture du gouvernement, le Congrès a adopté une nouvelle mesure temporaire prolongeant les dépenses actuelles pour quelques mois (résolution continue). Cela évite une fermeture immédiate, mais reporte la prochaine échéance à janvier. Le représentant Chip Roy (Républicain-Texas) a exprimé sa frustration après le vote, déclarant : « Nous n’avons rien fait ! » De nombreux conservateurs ont critiqué la mesure provisoire qui maintient les dépenses décidées lorsque les démocrates contrôlaient la Chambre sous Nancy Pelosi (Démocrate-Californie). Roy et d’autres se sont demandé quand la majorité républicaine tiendrait ses promesses. Ces critiques ont déjà mené à la destitution historique de McCarthy en octobre — une menace qui pèse désormais sur Johnson. Cette crise des finances publiques met en évidence le fossé entre la volonté d’un gouvernement réduit et la difficulté de couper dans les programmes qui touchent l’électorat local. Nick LaLota (Républicain-New York), centriste, s’est opposé au financement du ministère de la Justice, affirmant que ces réductions nuiraient à la sécurité publique. « Mes électeurs ne veulent pas que je vote pour cela », a-t-il expliqué. Les Républicains sont aussi lassés des sessions de vote tardives et des centaines d’amendements sur des lois rarement adoptées. LaLota note qu’après dix mois de majorité, la stratégie ne fonctionne pas. « Mes électeurs veulent des coupes, mais dans les bons domaines », a-t-il ajouté. Dans le même temps, les crises internationales dominent l’ordre du jour du Congrès. Biden a demandé près de 106 milliards de dollars pour l’aide à l’Ukraine, à Israël, pour l’aide humanitaire à Gaza et la sécurité à la frontière — un sujet clé lorsque le Congrès reprendra. Avant le vote, Johnson a présenté une extension des financements selon la proposition du Freedom Caucus, avec deux échéances différentes : le 19 janvier pour certains organismes, le 2 février pour d’autres. Les conservateurs l’ont massivement rejetée, critiquant aussi l’absence de lien avec l’aide à Israël pour inciter le Sénat à agir. Certains conservateurs accordent néanmoins du temps à Johnson pour prendre ses marques. « Le nouveau président est respecté, admiré, digne de confiance », a déclaré Bob Good (Républicain-Virginie). « Il est humain, imparfait, comme nous tous. » Les Républicains savent que leur faible majorité à la Chambre est de plus en plus fragile à l’approche des élections 2024 s’ils ne tiennent pas leurs engagements. De plus en plus de parlementaires de tous bords choisissent la retraite plutôt que la poursuite de ces confrontations partisanes. Johnson a défendu ses trois premières semaines : « Je ne peux pas faire virer un porte-avions du jour au lendemain », a-t-il assuré, soulignant que sa situation diffère de celle de McCarthy. « Nous avons de bons plans », a-t-il affirmé à la presse. Mais Garrett Graves (Républicain-Louisiane), un proche de McCarthy, recommande la prudence : « Imaginer qu’un nouveau président permettra magiquement de nouvelles options n’est pas la réalité », affirme-t-il, prévoyant la persistance des difficultés. Après que les démocrates ont aidé Johnson à éviter la fermeture, Hakeem Jeffries (Démocrate-New York), qui a également contribué à la destitution de McCarthy, déclare vouloir de bonnes relations avec Johnson. À la question de savoir s’il avait un conseil pour le nouveau président, Jeffries a répondu : « Bonne chance. »

article_content: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Southern Region is launching a comprehensive strategy to transform South India by 2047. According to CII Southern Region Chairman Kamal Bali, the organization will focus on nine key tracks aimed at driving economic growth. The strategy, unveiled at the inauguration of CII’s new Mangaluru office, is themed 'Transformation through Competitiveness, Growth, Sustainability, Trust, and Globalization' for 2023-24. The nine pillars of this plan include: rejuvenating people and culture; promoting holistic sustainability and ESG; advancing technology adoption and digital transformation; facilitating the energy transition, innovation, and startup ecosystems; achieving manufacturing excellence; fostering partnerships and collaborations; supporting MSMEs; brand building; and driving sectoral promotion. CII will collaborate closely with state governments to create state-level industrial and manufacturing policies. It also plans to establish state task forces for digital transformation to support industries with their digitalization efforts. Further, CII will assist 2,000 MSMEs by guiding them on competitiveness in partnership with its centres of excellence. With the new office in Mangaluru, CII’s office network in South India now has 17 locations. The organization will extend specialized support to MSMEs and stakeholders in the Mangaluru region. CII Karnataka Chairman Vijaykrishnan Venkatesan stated that the expanded office network enables the organization to better serve its members at the grassroots level. In related economic news, India has outperformed other Asia-Pacific markets, including China, for major global consumer goods companies in recent quarters, according to management commentaries. Additionally, employee productivity in India Inc. has steadily risen over the past five years while staff costs have remained stable at 10% of revenues. In regulatory developments, the government has banned 22 illegal betting and gambling apps and websites, including Mahadev Book Online, which is reportedly linked to bribery allegations involving Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel.

article_content: CNN recently featured several health stories that prompted strong reader reactions. Nearly 400 people commented on Rafi Kopelan's struggle with the rare disease epidermolysis bullosa (EB), as well as the efforts of her neighbors to use social media to raise funds for a cure. Many noted how government action and community support are important in finding treatments, while others shared their own health challenges. One reader, RumMonkeyMama, expressed gratitude for CNN highlighting the issue, mentioning her friend whose husband and son have EB. She described the challenges her friend's family faces and celebrated their son's progress, stating that greater awareness could lead to increased research funding for EB. Another widely discussed story covered Brittni Garcia, who lost 107 pounds after realizing her clothes no longer fit during college. The story sparked hundreds of supportive comments, with readers sharing personal weight loss experiences. Focusmm emphasized the role of healthy eating habits, claiming diet accounts for about 80% of weight loss success. Guneun agreed, stating, 'You lose ounces in the gym, but pounds in the kitchen.' Both suggested a combined approach of nutrition and exercise is key. A CNN report about the effectiveness of the flu vaccine, particularly among the elderly, led to a debate among readers. One commenter, tinytall, shared their negative experience with flu vaccinations in the military, while DrDougFC responded that nothing in medicine is absolute and that preventative measures, like vaccines, improve one's odds but are not guarantees. Discussion around a newly approved breast cancer drug also drew many comments, especially on the roles of the FDA, drug pricing, and pharmaceutical research. Rs1201, a research scientist, explained that drug development involves significant costs and risks, with many failures along the way. Drug pricing, they argued, reflects the high investment required to bring new treatments to market.

article_content: South Korean officials reported seven new cases of foot-and-mouth disease on Sunday, despite ongoing nationwide quarantine efforts, according to Yonhap News Agency. Investigators identified the disease at several dairy, beef, and pig farms, prompting the government to order the culling of more than 120 animals to prevent further spread. Foot-and-mouth disease is a highly contagious viral illness affecting cattle, swine, sheep, goats, deer, and other animals, as noted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. It typically causes fever and blister-like lesions or erosions in affected animals. The current outbreak began on November 28 at a pig farm in Andong, a city in southern South Korea, and has since spread to areas near Seoul. To date, authorities have ordered the culling of more than 662,647 livestock nationwide, with at least 81 confirmed cases—the country's highest outbreak since 2002, when 160,000 animals were slaughtered. Livestock markets remain closed across the country as officials oversee mass vaccination campaigns. Government ministers recently stated that meat is still safe to eat, emphasizing that foot-and-mouth disease does not spread to humans. Reporting contributed by CNN's Jiyeon Lee.

La fièvre aphteuse est une maladie virale hautement contagieuse qui touche les bovins, porcs, moutons, chèvres, cerfs et autres animaux, selon le ministère américain de l’Agriculture. Elle cause généralement de la fièvre et des lésions ou érosions semblables à des cloques chez les animaux concernés. La flambée actuelle a débuté le 28 novembre dans une ferme porcine à Andong, une ville du sud de la Corée du Sud, et s’est depuis propagée jusqu'aux environs de Séoul. À ce jour, les autorités ont ordonné l’abattage de plus de 662 647 têtes de bétail dans tout le pays, avec au moins 81 cas confirmés—la pire épidémie du pays depuis 2002, année où 160 000 animaux avaient été abattus. Les marchés de bétail restent fermés alors que les responsables supervisent de grandes campagnes de vaccination. Des ministres du gouvernement ont récemment déclaré que la consommation de viande reste sûre, en précisant que la fièvre aphteuse ne se transmet pas à l’homme. Reportage avec la contribution de Jiyeon Lee de CNN.

article_content: Brian Flynn, whose brother died in the Pan Am Flight 103 bombing, described the death of former Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi as a moment of justice. 'For more than 20 years, Gadhafi continued to haunt the world,' Flynn said. 'We can take some satisfaction that justice can be done.' The bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 killed 270 people when a bomb exploded aboard the Boeing 747 over Lockerbie, Scotland, less than a week before Christmas in 1988. The attack was ultimately linked to Libyan intelligence officials. Flynn's brother, John Patrick, was among 35 university students killed in the disaster. Syracuse University in New York dedicated a permanent memorial to the victims. Flynn said he's been in touch with other families of victims, sharing a range of emotions after hearing news of Gadhafi's death. 'We’re all together on this,' he said. 'When John Patrick died, I promised him and myself I wouldn’t let it go, that there would be justice. Today is an example that after 22 years, finally, justice is done. I owed him that.' Flynn also expressed appreciation for the Libyan people, saying, 'They have helped me fulfill my promise to him.' He commended the courage of Libyans and recognized the Obama administration's leadership in the NATO operation against Libya during a challenging period. In March of this year, U.S. and European warplanes began a campaign against Libyan government forces supporting rebel groups, which eventually resulted in Gadhafi’s ouster in August after over 40 years in power. Two years earlier, the only person convicted in the Lockerbie bombing, Abdelbaset al-Megrahi, was freed from a Scottish prison after serving eight years, due to terminal prostate cancer. Upon returning to Tripoli, he received a hero's welcome, angering many in the United States and the UK. The current Libyan government cited his poor health and said they were unlikely to return him. Despite doctors’ predictions that he had only months to live, al-Megrahi was still alive, though visibly ill, as of a few weeks ago. Flynn said that after hearing news of Gadhafi’s death, he felt it was worth it to achieve justice. U.S. President Barack Obama said, 'Today we can definitely say the Gadhafi regime has come to an end.' He announced U.S. support for Libya’s democratic transition and addressed the Libyan people, saying, 'You have won your revolution.' Syracuse University archivist Amy S. Doherty contacted families of the university's victims two years after the bombing to invite them to donate items, such as correspondence, diaries, photos, and creative works, to the archives. The first collection arrived in September 1990, and over time, materials related to all 35 students were added. In 2006, the scope was expanded to include information on all 270 victims.

Marie Doyle, 24, bought the ready-cooked chicken for a family Sunday lunch. After removing it from its packaging, she discovered a blue first-aid plaster attached to the underside. Marie and her mother, Andrea, were both almost physically sick when they saw it. Marie refused Asda's offer of a refund and a £50 gift voucher, insisting instead on a full investigation. Ms. Doyle said, 'It wasn't about the money; it was about making sure this didn't happen to anyone else.' An Asda spokesperson apologized for the incident, stating, 'We regret that Miss Doyle had this experience. This does not meet our usual high standards. Following the discovery, staff have had additional health and safety briefings to ensure this does not happen again.'

article_content: Roger Bainton, a surgeon, was suspended after allegations of 88 botched operations, with 26% of his patients experiencing surgical complications. Bainton attributed these failures to patients' lifestyles, claiming that smoking, drinking, and drug use were to blame. He also suggested that patients from Stoke-on-Trent had a 'weaker genetic make-up,' according to a Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) report. Bainton, who had previously been struck off the dental register and suspended by the General Medical Council due to a death in Scotland in 1999, moved to Stoke-on-Trent to continue practicing. At the University Hospital of North Staffordshire, he used an experimental bone substitute on 33 out of 123 patients without their informed consent. This material, previously used only on non-facial bones, was first implanted by Bainton in 2007. The use of this unproven technique was halted in 2012 after concerns were raised by his colleagues. Bainton was suspended in February 2013, and the RCS conducted an internal review, which criticized both Bainton's practices and the lack of oversight by hospital leadership and the maxillofacial department. The RCS report highlighted a lack of effective clinical leadership at the hospital, noting that the lack of oversight allowed surgeons to operate independently without sufficient scrutiny. Thirty-three of the affected patients were recalled after receiving the bone substitute. Another 36 patients underwent jaw surgery when non-surgical measures could have sufficed, and 19 may have had unnecessary eye socket surgery. Karen Reynolds of Freeth Cartwright LLP, representing 30 patients, emphasized the significance of the failings in both Bainton's practice and the hospital's overall management. Medical Director Robert Courteney-Harris stated that the hospital created and implemented a comprehensive action plan in response to RCS recommendations, including appointing a new oral and maxillofacial consultant specializing in trauma. He reaffirmed the hospital's commitment to transparency and maintaining high standards of patient care. Roger Bainton was unavailable for comment.

Kim Clijsters demonstrated her strong tennis comeback by decisively beating third seed Venus Williams in the Sony Ericsson Open final in Miami on Saturday. Having been seeded 14th after a two-year hiatus, the Belgian, who is a former world No. 1, will advance to 10th in the world rankings next week. Clijsters’ overwhelming 6-2, 6-1 victory at Key Biscayne secured her second Miami title after her 2005 win, with the match concluding in just 58 minutes. Williams, who was vying for her fourth win at this event and had won her two most recent tournaments, struggled on court, which allowed Clijsters to notch her 37th WTA Tour title—28 of which are on hard courts.

At 26, Clijsters collected her third tournament championship since returning to tennis after giving birth to her daughter, Jada, who cheered from the stands. Winning the 2009 US Open, Clijsters surpassed $17 million in career earnings by taking the $700,000 top prize—almost $100,000 more than what Andy Roddick or Tomas Berdych will earn in the men’s final. In the semifinals, Clijsters had overcome Justine Henin in a tight match. She sealed her latest victory by breaking Williams’s serve cleanly in the final game.

After the match, Clijsters thanked her fitness coach and husband for their support and spoke of the joy of returning to a winning venue like Miami. Meanwhile, Williams, with her sister Serena watching from the stands, made 29 unforced errors versus Clijsters’ 12, stalling her recent momentum. Williams reflected on her faulty play, noting it can be hard to recover once errors accumulate, especially against an opponent like Clijsters, but she will still move up to fourth in the rankings.

Published by Ruth Styles on 23 September 2013, this article reviews the standout fashion moments from the 2013 Emmy Awards, focusing on both the best- and worst-dressed celebrities.

Top Trends: Christina Hendricks and Elisabeth Moss from ‘Mad Men’ received widespread acclaim for their red carpet looks. Moss wore a striking monochrome gown with textured details, complemented by her new blond hair and bold red lipstick. Hendricks opted for a classic, figure-flattering black gown. Claire Danes was also celebrated for her daring Armani Prive couture dress, paired with a retro faux-bob hairstyle and minimal jewelry. Helen McCrory impressed with a cream gown that showed off her toned arms and chic accessories.

In other highlights, Zooey Deschanel remained true to her quirky style in a sky-blue J Mendel dress featuring a playful bow and thigh-high slit. Kerry Washington and January Jones evoked timeless Hollywood glamour in nude lace dresses. Rose Byrne wore a modern pale pink ensemble with a cropped shell top, revealing her toned midriff. Other notable looks included Kelly Osbourne in crimson red, Alyson Hannigan in purple Marchesa, and Julianna Margulies in a strapless monochrome gown.

Fashion Misses: Some stars earned less favorable reviews for their attire. Lena Dunham's floral Prada gown and visible tattoos drew criticism for style and fit. Zosia Mamet's printed gown with an unusual leather bust detail was also poorly received. Heidi Klum’s maroon sequinned dress and Lena Headey’s sheer black gown were considered unflattering by critics. Carrie Underwood's green gown was said to wash out her complexion. Michelle Dockery’s two-tone Prada dress split opinions, though the claret color was noted as striking. Paula Abdul’s gold lame ensemble was described as excessive, and Kaley Cuoco’s claret gown, plus experiments with sheer fabrics by Julianne Hough and Lena Headey, also faced critique.

Public Feedback: Readers expressed a variety of opinions in the comments, sometimes agreeing or disagreeing with the article’s choices and critiquing specific style elements. Remarks addressed tattoos, color choices, and the decision-making behind certain outfits.

Note: Reader opinions are their own and do not necessarily reflect those of MailOnline.

article_content: Luxembourg, among the richest countries in the world, is facing a worsening housing crisis. Protests are becoming more common as locals deal with rents and property prices that many simply cannot afford. Jean-Michel Campanella of the Mieterschutz Association highlights that, while the issue isn't recent, it's grown more severe year by year. He notes that Luxembourg's strong economy continues to attract large numbers of foreign workers, which adds even more pressure to the housing market in this small, populous country. Antoine Paccoud from the Housing Observatory at the Ministry of Housing explains that for 30 years, most new homes have been built for investors instead of people buying their first home. With rising interest rates, investors are leaving the market, so housing development has nearly stopped—making the crisis even worse. Minimum wage is above 2,300 euros monthly, but buying a home typically starts at 10,000 euros for each square meter, keeping ownership out of reach for many.

Jean-Michel Campanella, de l’Association Mieterschutz, rappelle que ce problème persiste déjà depuis longtemps mais qu’il empire chaque année. Selon lui, l’économie florissante du Luxembourg attire toujours plus de travailleurs étrangers, ce qui pèse sur le marché immobilier de ce petit pays très densément peuplé. Antoine Paccoud, de l’Observatoire de l’Habitat au Ministère du Logement, précise que depuis 30 ans, la majorité des nouveaux logements ont été construits pour les investisseurs plutôt que pour les primo-accédants. article_content: Martin Schur, a 93-year-old World War II medic living in Bay City, Michigan, froze to death last month in his home after his electricity was limited due to unpaid bills. Schur left his entire estate to Bay Regional Medical Center, according to an estate attorney. While the precise value hasn’t been disclosed, Schur’s nephew said Martin told family members he had saved over half a million dollars. Schur and his wife, Marian, who passed away over a year ago, had no children. Cathy Reder, representing both the Schur family and the hospital, said she is filing paperwork in probate court to validate the will, with a hearing scheduled for March 17. She confirmed the estate was left entirely to the hospital, though she wouldn’t disclose the amount. Schur was remembered as a frugal man, reportedly not eating at restaurants for over 30 years. His nephew, William Walworth, said Martin was proud of his savings and his contributions to the community. He hopes that Schur’s story encourages others to care for their neighbors. Schur’s death shocked Bay City, a town of about 37,000. On January 17, his body was discovered at home in a house with a temperature of 32 degrees, just days after a device restricting power—installed due to unpaid utility bills—shut off his electricity. The medical examiner described his death from hypothermia as 'slow and painful.' Local and state officials, including the mayor and Michigan State Police, have launched investigations. Bay City Electric Light & Power has since stopped cutting off customers’ power for unpaid bills and removed all 'limiters'—devices used to restrict electricity to nonpaying customers. Previously, Schur’s limiter was never reset, and it is unclear if he knew how to do it. Neighbors and officials called his death avoidable, and community protests followed. Bay City has also reassessed its procedures, as its utilities are not regulated by Michigan’s public service commission. Private utility companies are required by law to maintain service for senior citizens during winter months if they register for protection programs. Schur’s case has prompted calls for major policy changes. Walworth expressed hope that his uncle's death leads to improvements, saying, 'Hopefully, some good can come out of this.'

Schur a légué l'ensemble de son patrimoine au Bay Regional Medical Center, selon un avocat en charge de la succession. Bien que la valeur exacte n’ait pas été révélée, le neveu de Schur a indiqué que Martin avait confié à sa famille avoir économisé plus d’un demi-million de dollars. Schur et son épouse, Marian, décédée il y a plus d’un an, n’avaient pas d’enfants. Cathy Reder, représentant la famille Schur et l’hôpital, indique qu’elle dépose les documents nécessaires auprès du tribunal successoral pour valider le testament. L’audience est prévue pour le 17 mars. Elle a confirmé que l’héritage était entièrement destiné à l’hôpital, sans en divulguer le montant. Schur était reconnu pour sa grande frugalité, certains affirmant qu'il n’avait pas mangé au restaurant depuis plus de 30 ans. Le cas de Schur a suscité des appels à des changements majeurs de politique. Walworth a exprimé l'espoir que la mort de son oncle mène à des améliorations, en déclarant : 'Espérons que quelque chose de bon résultera de tout cela.'

Language and communication experts evaluated President Obama's recent Oval Office address on the Gulf oil spill, focusing on clarity and accessibility. Ron Yaros, assistant professor at the Philip Merrill College of Journalism, University of Maryland, praised the speech for being straightforward and largely free of technical jargon. Yaros analyzed the speech by dividing it into 1,200 'idea units,' finding only one potentially confusing term, 'relief well,' which was not explained.

The term 'relief well' refers to BP's ongoing effort to drill a separate well that is expected to intersect with the damaged well in August, at which point BP plans to stop the flow by pumping heavy drilling fluid.

Paul J.J. Payack, president of Global Language Monitor, offered a different perspective after analyzing the address. He reported the speech was written at a 9.8-grade level, higher than Obama's previous significant speeches, and gave it a 'solid B' rating. Payack suggested the language was overly academic at times, providing an example and recommending a less professorial tone. He also highlighted sentences that compared the spill to natural disasters and epidemics, noting they might be insensitive to those affected by events like Hurricane Katrina. However, he praised Obama's vivid language in describing the spill.

The length and complexity of sentences were also discussed. Payack argued that the speech's sentence structure increased difficulty for the average listener, while Mark Liberman, linguist at the University of Pennsylvania, challenged this criticism, noting that previous presidential speeches used similarly long sentences.

There was debate over the use of grade-level metrics for spoken addresses. Yaros and Liberman argued these calculations overlook important aspects of speech delivery, such as pauses and emphasis. Yaros maintained that it's more important to assess how well the audience understands the content rather than simply the grade level of the text. He emphasized that clear explanations of key information are what truly matter in effective communication, rather than surface-level metrics.

Supermodel Coco Rocha is renowned for her striking poses, but she reveals her skills were not always appreciated. Her modeling journey began with catalog jobs in Asia, where she recalls sometimes doing as many as 25 to 75 photos each day. 'At castings, it was almost like a pose-off,' she said in a recent interview. 'Imagine vogue-ing, but as a 15-year-old with little experience in movement. Clients might say, "Today, do a sexy pose," or, "Today, do something natural or cutesy." You had a minute to interpret each direction.'

Recently pictured at Milan Fashion Week, Rocha created 1,000 different poses for her new coffee table book, 'Study of Pose,' co-produced with photographer Steven Sebring. Last week, she attended a book signing in Toronto, Canada, eager to engage with fans.

When Rocha moved to New York, her expressive posing was met with skepticism. 'Some people told me, "What are you doing? This is wrong and weird. This is how you model,"' she recalled. 'Luckily, there were also supporters who encouraged me to continue.'

Now 26, Rocha has graced the covers of Vogue, W, and Harper's Bazaar, and walked the runway for designers like Oscar de la Renta and Jean Paul Gaultier. She has also starred in campaigns for Versace, Zac Posen, and Yves Saint Laurent. Her book, 'Study of Pose' (Harper Design), will be released on November 20. 'We covered a wide variety of genres, and actually finished the book in just three days,' she said.

Rocha hopes readers realize that it's fine to have fun in front of the camera. 'Having personality in photos is important, especially now with so much life being documented,' she explained. 'We all get a bit insecure, thinking we have to pose a specific way. I want to tell people: you can be goofy and have fun.'

Earlier this month, Rocha and her husband, James Conran, announced her pregnancy in a YouTube video. In a later Instagram post, she shared: 'We are absolutely thrilled and elated to announce that after four years of marriage we are expanding our family and expecting our first child in spring 2015!'

article_content: Serena Williams delivered a commanding performance to defeat Maria Sharapova 6-0, 6-1 in the Olympic women's singles final at Wimbledon on Saturday. The 30-year-old American built on her Wimbledon victory from the previous month on the same courts, preventing her Russian opponent from finding rhythm. Williams secured victory in just 63 minutes, closing out the match with a powerful ace. With this win, Williams equaled Steffi Graf's record as the only players in tennis history to achieve a 'Golden Slam'—winning all four Grand Slam titles and an Olympic singles gold. In addition to her two Olympic doubles golds with her sister Venus, Williams becomes the first woman to win all three honors. Williams ranked this accomplishment among her greatest, telling reporters, 'This one is so high up there—being Olympic gold champion, Golden Slam champion in singles and doubles, that's pretty awesome.' Williams started with three aces in her opening service game and immediately broke French Open champion Sharapova in the next game. She dominated throughout, with Sharapova scoring only in the ninth game. Sharapova showed resistance in Williams's next service game, but Williams, a 14-time Grand Slam champion, held serve for a 4-1 lead before breaking again. Now ranked world number four, Williams defeated Sharapova, current world number one Victoria Azarenka, and former number ones Caroline Wozniacki and Jelena Jankovic en route to gold, losing only 17 games in six matches. After an unexpected first-round loss to Virginie Razzano at the French Open, questions were raised about Williams, but she answered with her fifth Wimbledon title and now Olympic gold. Victoria Azarenka claimed the bronze medal by defeating Maria Kirilenko of Russia 6-3, 6-4. American success continued at Wimbledon as brothers Bob and Mike Bryan captured their first Olympic gold in men's doubles, defeating French duo Jo-Wilfried Tsonga and Michael Llodra 6-4, 7-6 in the final. Previously, the Bryan brothers had won bronze in Beijing four years earlier.

article_content: Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger states he intends to fly again once he has processed the events of Flight 1549. Alongside First Officer Jeffrey Skiles, Sullenberger safely executed an emergency landing of US Airways Flight 1549 in the Hudson River in January, ensuring the survival of all 155 passengers. The crew, including flight attendants Sheila Dail, Doreen Welsh, and Donna Dent, discussed their experiences in an interview with CNN's Larry King. Sullenberger mentioned ongoing disruptions to his sleep and difficulty relaxing since the incident. His colleagues echoed similar sentiments, though all except Welsh expressed intentions to eventually return to work. Welsh, injured during the emergency, said she could not yet wear her uniform and remains uncertain about her return to flying. Earlier this month, the National Transportation Safety Board confirmed both engines ingested birds, causing their failure just minutes after takeoff. The flight data recorder indicated no anomalies prior to the bird strike, and the resulting loss of thrust was consistent with the pilots' account. Sullenberger described bird strikes as generally not rare, but emphasized that this incident was exceptional due to the size and number of birds involved, which severely damaged both engines. At the time of the bird strike, Skiles was piloting and attempted to restart the engines as Sullenberger took control. Within minutes, Sullenberger decided to land in the Hudson River. Skiles rejected the characterization of the event as a miracle, instead attributing the successful outcome to the crew's training and good fortune. The crew praised the passengers for remaining calm and cooperative during the ordeal, with flight attendant Donna Dent noting their remarkable composure and experience as frequent fliers.
translated_content: Le capitaine Chesley « Sully » Sullenberger déclare qu’il a l’intention de reprendre les airs dès qu’il aura assimilé les événements du vol 1549. Aux côtés du copilote Jeffrey Skiles, Sullenberger a effectué un atterrissage d’urgence réussi du vol US Airways 1549 sur le fleuve Hudson en janvier, sauvant ainsi les 155 passagers à bord. L’équipage, comprenant les agents de bord Sheila Dail, Doreen Welsh et Donna Dent, a partagé son expérience lors d’une interview avec Larry King sur CNN. Sullenberger a évoqué ses nuits perturbées et la difficulté à se détendre depuis l’incident. Ses collègues ont fait état de ressentis similaires, bien qu’ils aient tous, sauf Welsh, exprimé leur volonté de retourner travailler. Welsh, blessée lors de l’urgence, a expliqué qu’elle ne pouvait pas encore remettre son uniforme et reste incertaine quant à son retour en vol. Plus tôt ce mois-ci, le Conseil national de la sécurité des transports a confirmé que les deux moteurs avaient aspiré des oiseaux, provoquant leur panne quelques minutes après le décollage. Les enregistreurs de vol n’ont révélé aucune anomalie avant la collision avec les oiseaux, et la perte de puissance observée correspondait au récit des pilotes. Sullenberger a expliqué que les collisions avec des oiseaux ne sont généralement pas rares, mais a souligné que cet incident était exceptionnel en raison du nombre et de la taille des oiseaux impliqués, qui ont gravement endommagé les deux moteurs. Au moment de l’impact avec les oiseaux, Skiles pilotait et a tenté de redémarrer les moteurs pendant que Sullenberger reprenait les commandes. Quelques minutes plus tard, Sullenberger a décidé d’amerrir sur l’Hudson. Skiles a écarté la description de « miracle », attribuant plutôt le succès à la formation de l’équipage et à la chance. L’équipage a salué le calme et la coopération des passagers pendant l’épreuve, l’agente de bord Donna Dent soulignant leur incroyable sang-froid et leur expérience de voyageurs fréquents.

article_content: At 160 million years old, 'Misty' the diplodocus was recently sold for nearly £488,000 at a West Sussex auction. The enormous 55-foot skeleton, taller than most vehicles, was unearthed in Wyoming, USA, in 2009 by the children of German paleontologist Raimund Albersdoerfer. Their surprising find prompted a nine-week excavation of the rare specimen. Fully assembled diplodocus skeletons are extremely uncommon in museums, where replicas are often on display. Misty was meticulously cleaned and rebuilt in the Netherlands before making her way to Summers Place Auctions in the UK—an auction house better known for garden statues and decorative fossils. Overseeing the sale was Errol Fuller, a natural history specialist and co-author with Sir David Attenborough. A private buyer, whose identity remains undisclosed, purchased Misty but has pledged to keep the skeleton available for public viewing. Enthusiastic potential buyers came from around the world, especially from China, Asia, and the Middle East. While some in America might regret losing Misty, the auction curator emphasized that similar skeletons remain in US collections.

Leur découverte inattendue a donné lieu à neuf semaines de fouilles pour extraire ce spécimen rare. Des squelettes de diplodocus entièrement assemblés sont extrêmement rares dans les musées, qui exposent souvent des répliques. Misty a été soigneusement nettoyée et reconstituée aux Pays-Bas avant de rejoindre Summers Place Auctions au Royaume-Uni, une maison d’enchères habituellement spécialisée dans les statues de jardin et fossiles décoratifs. Même si certains Américains regrettent de voir Misty partir, le commissaire-priseur rappelle que des squelettes similaires figurent toujours dans des collections américaines.

article_content: On Monday, members of the Judiciary Staff Union of Nigeria (JUSUN) in Osun State staged a protest against the state’s Chief Judge, Justice Adepele Ojo, accusing her of abuse of office and high-handedness. The protesting judiciary staff carried placards, blocked the entrance to the state high court, and picketed the Chief Judge’s office. The protest followed the Osun State House of Assembly’s recommendation last Thursday to suspend the Chief Judge over allegations of corruption and misconduct. In a statement by Tiamiyu Olamide, Press Secretary to the Speaker, the Assembly insisted its actions were justified by several petitions it had received about the Chief Judge. Speaker Adewale Egbedun reiterated that the House would have been negligent had it ignored the petitions, which included allegations of diversion of funds for the State Judiciary Library, misappropriation of a N5 million robe allowance, unlawful suspension of judicial staff without the involvement of the Judicial Service Commission, and diversion of salaries and other revenues. Other accusations included appointing a consultant for electronic affidavits that resulted in revenue losses for the state, disobedience to court judgments, and diversion of proceeds recovered from a robbery case. The protest began at 7 a.m., leaving lawyers and litigants unable to access the high court. JUSUN chairman, Gbenga Eludire, led the protest, with workers displaying placards reading, 'Judiciary staff deserve better' and 'Unlawful suspension of judiciary staff is barbaric.' Police were present around the court premises. Addressing journalists, Eludire accused the Chief Judge of suspending workers for lengthy periods—up to 59 months—without due process or reference to the Judicial Service Commission, despite some staff being cleared by the courts. He further alleged that several dismissed workers had died during the period of suspension. Eludire also highlighted the non-payment of wardrobe allowances for 2021, 2022, and 2023, despite budgetary provisions, and claimed that there had been no training for judiciary staff at the National Judicial Institute since 2015. When asked about any connection between the face-off involving the Chief Judge and the state government, Eludire stated he was unaware of any such issues, insisting the protest was unrelated to recent petitions. Meanwhile, the Osogbo branch of the Nigerian Bar Association criticized Governor Ademola Adeleke's handling of the Chief Judge's suspension in a letter, warning against actions that could trigger a constitutional crisis and harm the state's image.

Les agents du judiciaire ont brandi des pancartes, bloqué l’entrée du palais de justice et organisé un sit-in devant le bureau de la juge en chef. Cette manifestation fait suite à la recommandation de l’Assemblée de l’État d’Osun, jeudi dernier, de suspendre la juge en chef pour diverses accusations de corruption et de mauvaise gestion. Dans un communiqué signé par Tiamiyu Olamide, secrétaire de presse du président de l’Assemblée, l’institution a affirmé que sa décision était motivée par de nombreuses pétitions reçues concernant la juge en chef. Le président de l’Assemblée, Adewale Egbedun, a réaffirmé que l’Assemblée aurait failli à ses obligations si elle avait ignoré ces plaintes, qui incluent des allégations de détournement de fonds de la bibliothèque du judiciaire, de mauvaise utilisation d’une allocation de toge de 5 millions de nairas, de suspension arbitraire du personnel sans avis de la Commission de service judiciaire, ainsi que de détournement de salaires et autres revenus. Les accusations portent également sur la nomination d’un consultant pour les affidavits électroniques, ce qui aurait causé une perte de revenus à l’État, sur le non-respect des décisions de justice et le détournement des produits récupérés lors d’une affaire de vol. La manifestation a commencé à 7h, empêchant avocats et justiciables d’entrer au tribunal. Le président du JUSUN, Gbenga Eludire, a conduit la protestation, et les travailleurs arboraient des pancartes comme « Le personnel judiciaire mérite mieux » ou « Suspensions illégales du personnel judiciaire : c’est barbare ». Une forte présence policière a été remarquée autour du palais de justice. Devant la presse, Eludire a accusé la juge en chef de suspendre certains agents pendant de longues périodes—jusqu’à 59 mois—sans procédure régulière ni recours à la Commission de service judiciaire, même après que certains aient été blanchis par la justice. Il a aussi déclaré que plusieurs agents révoqués étaient décédés pendant leur suspension. Eludire a également fait remarquer que les allocations vestimentaires pour 2021, 2022 et 2023 n’avaient pas été versées, malgré les budgets prévus, et qu’aucune formation n’avait été organisée pour le personnel depuis 2015 à l’Institut national du judiciaire. Interrogé sur un éventuel lien avec un conflit entre la juge en chef et le gouvernement d’État, Eludire a affirmé ne pas être au courant d’une telle situation et a insisté sur le caractère indépendant de la protestation. Par ailleurs, la branche d’Osogbo de l’Association du Barreau du Nigéria a critiqué la gestion du gouverneur Ademola Adeleke, avertissant dans une lettre que ces actions pourraient entraîner une crise constitutionnelle et porter atteinte à l’image de l’État.

article_content: Bitcoin and other major cryptocurrencies are rising sharply, with Bitcoin approaching an 18-month high near $38,000. According to CoinGecko, struggling coins like Terra have climbed 66%, while FTX’s FTT token soared nearly 80% in a single day. Investors appear increasingly optimistic about the possible approval of US spot Bitcoin ETFs by the SEC. Stephane Ouellette, CEO of FRNT Financial, noted that Bitcoin faces little resistance and reacts strongly to even minor positive news, especially regarding ETFs. This points to solid price support since last year’s FTX collapse. This Friday saw Bitcoin jump 2.5% to $37,465, coming within close range of $38,000—a level last seen in May 2022 before sector-wide turmoil caused by events like the TerraUSD crash and the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX. Analysts at Bloomberg Intelligence predict that the SEC could greenlight a spot Bitcoin ETF as soon as January 10, which has contributed to roughly a 40% increase in Bitcoin prices over the last month. Crypto’s recent performance is also tied to a better economic outlook, with rising stock markets and falling bond yields fueling appetite for riskier assets such as cryptocurrencies. Even after these gains, Bitcoin still sits far below its all-time peak of almost $69,000 in 2021. Nevertheless, experts like Matt Hougan from Bitwise Asset Management remain bullish about crypto’s long-term prospects and anticipate new record highs within the next year. Elsewhere, SAP has launched an interactive metaverse initiative in India to speed up cloud technology adoption and help businesses improve their processes. Additionally, India’s Income Tax Department is investigating local subsidiaries of Google, Amazon, and Apple for potential tax underpayments and has requested details about their transfer pricing practices. Simultaneously, Indian investors have become the largest foreign buyers in Dubai’s real estate market. Digital payments provider Razorpay is reportedly planning to move its parent company to India, a transition that could trigger substantial US tax obligations.

Selon CoinGecko, des coins comme Terra ont bondi de 66 %, tandis que le token FTT de FTX a augmenté de près de 80 % en une seule journée. Les investisseurs semblent de plus en plus confiants quant à une possible approbation des ETF spot sur le Bitcoin par la SEC aux États-Unis. Stephane Ouellette, PDG de FRNT Financial, a noté que le Bitcoin rencontre peu de résistance et réagit fortement à la moindre nouvelle positive, surtout concernant les ETF. Cette dynamique témoigne du solide soutien des prix depuis la chute de FTX l'an dernier. Ce vendredi, le Bitcoin a progressé de 2,5 % pour atteindre 37 465 $, se rapprochant du seuil des 38 000 $ – un niveau atteint pour la dernière fois en mai 2022, avant la crise du secteur provoquée par l'effondrement du TerraUSD et de la plateforme FTX de Sam Bankman-Fried. Les analystes de Bloomberg Intelligence prédisent que la SEC pourrait approuver un ETF spot sur le Bitcoin dès le 10 janvier, ce qui a favorisé une hausse d'environ 40 % du cours du Bitcoin sur le mois écoulé. La bonne dynamique des cryptos s'explique aussi par un contexte économique plus favorable : les marchés boursiers montent et la baisse des rendements obligataires stimule l'appétit des investisseurs pour les actifs plus risqués comme les cryptomonnaies. Même avec ces progressions, le Bitcoin reste loin de son record historique de près de 69 000 $ établi en 2021. Cependant, des experts comme Matt Hougan de Bitwise Asset Management restent optimistes à long terme et prévoient de nouveaux sommets d'ici l'année prochaine. Par ailleurs, SAP a lancé une initiative interactive dans le métavers en Inde afin d'accélérer l'adoption du cloud et d'aider les entreprises à améliorer leurs processus. De plus, le fisc indien enquête sur les filiales locales de Google, Amazon et Apple pour de possibles arriérés d'impôts, demandant des précisions sur leurs pratiques de prix de transfert. En parallèle, les investisseurs indiens sont devenus les plus gros acheteurs étrangers sur le marché immobilier de Dubaï. Le spécialiste des paiements numériques Razorpay envisagerait de déplacer sa maison mère en Inde, une opération pouvant entraîner d'importantes obligations fiscales aux États-Unis.

article_content:
Homeland Security Secretary Janet Napolitano apologized Thursday after veterans groups expressed offense at a Department of Homeland Security report concerning right-wing extremism. The report indicated that extremist groups might seek to recruit veterans returning from Iraq and Afghanistan, and may also exploit conditions such as the recession and the election of President Obama to attract new members.

The American Legion, among other organizations, objected to the report’s mention of veterans. David K. Rehbein, the American Legion's national commander, wrote to Napolitano, stating, “Americans are not the enemy. The terrorists are.”

Napolitano, appearing on CNN’s 'American Morning,' addressed the issue: “I know that some veterans groups were offended by the mention of veterans in this assessment, so I apologize for that offense. It was certainly not intended.” She emphasized the report was an assessment rather than an accusation, and she planned to meet with veterans group leaders the following week.

The Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) defended the report’s intention, though its national commander Glen M. Gardner Jr. stated it “should have been worded differently” but served a necessary purpose. “A government that does not assess internal and external security threats would be negligent of a critical public responsibility,” Gardner said in a statement.

The report, developed with the FBI, was released to federal, state, and local law enforcement officials. It referenced several factors believed to contribute to right-wing extremism, such as anger over illegal immigration and economic troubles. However, it was the section on veterans that drew the most controversy, especially among conservative politicians and some veterans.

The report noted: “the return of military veterans facing significant challenges reintegrating into their communities could lead to the potential emergence of terrorist groups or lone-wolf extremists capable of carrying out violent attacks.” Timothy McVeigh, who bombed the Oklahoma City federal building in 1995 after returning from military service, was cited as an example.

In response, Rehbein wrote, “Timothy McVeigh was only one of more than 42 million veterans who have worn this nation’s uniform during wartime. To continue to use McVeigh as an example of the stereotypical ‘disgruntled military veteran’ is as unfair as using Osama bin Laden as the sole example of Islam.”

Mainstream media covered the report after it was highlighted by conservative bloggers. The report itself noted there was “no specific information that domestic right-wing terrorists are currently planning acts of violence,” but suggested worsening economic conditions could create a “fertile recruiting environment” and possibly spark confrontations between groups and government authorities, similar to past clashes. It compared the current climate to the 1990s, suggesting the threat from lone actors or small cells is now more pronounced than in previous years.

Prominent conservative radio hosts, such as Rush Limbaugh and Michael Savage, sharply criticized the report. Limbaugh claimed the report unfairly portrays everyday conservatives as greater threats than foreign enemies. Savage argued that individuals concerned about issues like immigration and government overreach were being targeted.

In a written statement, Napolitano insisted that the agency monitors criminal and terrorist activity, not ideology or beliefs, and noted her personal connection to the McVeigh prosecution. She also stated she would personally reassure the American Legion that DHS honors and employs many veterans, including Deputy Secretary Jane Holl Lute.

A similar report warning about left-wing extremism was issued in January. Both reports were initiated during President George W. Bush’s administration.

Ce rapport expliquait que des groupes extrémistes peuvent chercher à recruter des vétérans revenant d’Irak et d’Afghanistan, et à exploiter des facteurs tels que la récession et l’élection du président Obama pour attirer de nouveaux membres.

L’American Legion, entre autres organisations, s’est opposée à la mention des vétérans dans ce rapport. David K. Rehbein, commandant national de l’American Legion, a écrit à Napolitano : « Les Américains ne sont pas l’ennemi. Ce sont les terroristes. »

Sur CNN dans l’émission « American Morning », Napolitano a déclaré : « Je sais que certains groupes de vétérans ont été offensés par la mention des vétérans dans ce rapport, et je m’en excuse. Ce n’était pas notre intention. » Elle a précisé que le rapport était une évaluation et non une accusation, et a prévu de rencontrer les dirigeants de groupes de vétérans la semaine suivante.

Les Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) ont défendu l’objectif du rapport tout en critiquant la formulation : leur commandant national Glen M. Gardner Jr. a déclaré qu’il « aurait dû être rédigé autrement », mais qu’il remplissait une mission importante. « Un gouvernement qui n’évalue pas les menaces à la sécurité, internes et externes, manquerait à sa responsabilité publique », a-t-il déclaré.

Le rapport, élaboré avec le FBI, a été diffusé auprès des forces de l’ordre à tous les niveaux. Il évoquait plusieurs facteurs susceptibles de nourrir l’extrémisme de droite, comme la colère face à l’immigration illégale ou les difficultés économiques. Pourtant, c’est la section sur les vétérans qui a causé la plus grande controverse, surtout chez les conservateurs et certains anciens combattants.

Selon le rapport : « Le retour de vétérans militaires confrontés à d’importants défis de réintégration pourrait entraîner l’émergence potentielle de groupes terroristes ou de “loups solitaires” capables de commettre des actes violents. » Timothy McVeigh, auteur de l’attentat d’Oklahoma City en 1995 après son service militaire, y était cité.

En réaction, Rehbein a écrit : « Timothy McVeigh faisait partie des plus de 42 millions de vétérans ayant porté l’uniforme pendant les conflits armés. Prendre McVeigh en exemple pour représenter le ‘vétéran mécontent’ est aussi injuste qu’utiliser Oussama ben Laden comme seul modèle des musulmans. »

Les médias traditionnels ont repris l’histoire après sa mise en avant par des blogueurs conservateurs. Le rapport soulignait qu’il « n’existait pas d’indication précise que des terroristes nationaux de droite planifient actuellement des attaques », mais estimait que la crise économique pourrait servir de « terrain fertile » au recrutement et potentiellement provoquer des affrontements avec les autorités comme par le passé. La situation était comparée à celle des années 1990, mais le texte considérait la menace des acteurs isolés ou des petites cellules comme plus marquée aujourd’hui.

Les animateurs radio conservateurs Rush Limbaugh et Michael Savage ont vivement critiqué le rapport. Limbaugh lui a reproché de présenter les conservateurs ordinaires comme plus dangereux que les ennemis étrangers. Savage a dénoncé la surveillance ciblant selon lui les gens préoccupés par l’immigration ou les pouvoirs du gouvernement.

Dans une déclaration, Napolitano a affirmé que le département surveillait le crime et le terrorisme, pas les convictions politiques ou idéologiques, rappelant aussi son implication dans l’affaire McVeigh. Elle s’est engagée à rassurer l’American Legion sur le respect et l’emploi de nombreux vétérans au sein du département, dont la sous-secrétaire Jane Holl Lute.

Un rapport similaire sur l’extrémisme de gauche est sorti en janvier. Les deux rapports avaient été lancés sous la présidence de George W. Bush.

article_content: LAS VEGAS -- After a breakthrough agreement was reached early Wednesday between the Las Vegas hotel workers union and Caesars Entertainment, a tentative contract began taking shape for 20,000 hospitality workers at rival MGM Resorts International. Experts say such deals will likely prevent an unprecedented strike on the Las Vegas Strip. "I believe we will come to a deal today. Our employees are looking for a pay increase to address inflation and other concerns," said MGM Resorts CEO Bill Hornbuckle during an earnings call held concurrently with ongoing negotiations. The Culinary Workers Union had threatened to strike early Friday morning if negotiations failed. However, the union's reach with Caesars appears to have provided the momentum needed to secure new contracts for all 35,000 members working under expired contracts at 18 hotel-casinos. "As soon as one company reaches a deal, the others just fall right in line," said Bill Werner, associate professor at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas who studies hospitality law and labor relations. "But this is as close as we've come in a long time to an actual strike." The deal with Caesars followed 20 straight hours of bargaining that began Tuesday and continued into Wednesday, the union reported. Caesars stated the agreement recognizes the significant contributions of its team members in Las Vegas with impactful wage increases and growth opportunities, including plans to expand union jobs. Once approved by union members, the contract would cover properties including Caesars Palace, Flamingo, Harrah’s, Horseshoe, Paris Las Vegas, Planet Hollywood, Cromwell, and Linq. Outside Caesars Palace on Wednesday, visitor Joshua Guray, who had flown in from Los Angeles for a brief stay, remarked he hadn't known about the negotiations but would have canceled his dinner reservation if a strike affected his plans. "I try to stand in solidarity with other workers," Guray said. Union spokesperson Bethany Khan said the detailed terms of the deal would be released after member approval, with a vote expected soon. A strike could still occur if agreements with MGM Resorts and Wynn Resorts (the state's largest private employers) are not reached by 5 a.m. Friday. Talks with Wynn are scheduled for Thursday. A walkout would strike at the core of the city's economy and significantly disrupt operations at major hotel-casinos, especially as Las Vegas prepares for the incoming Formula 1 Grand Prix. This year has seen several notable labor actions nationwide in sectors like film, delivery, and other casinos. The Las Vegas Grand Prix circuit will showcase several at-risk properties, including Aria, Bellagio, Excalibur, Luxor, Mandalay Bay, MGM Grand, New York-New York, Park MGM, Wynn, and Encore. Hospitality workers, from housekeepers to cocktail servers, state they are willing to strike as long as necessary for fair contracts. Tiffany Thomas, a guest room attendant at Mandalay Bay, emphasized her motivation: "I am willing to go on strike because I have a 10-year-old daughter who comes to negotiations with me. I want her to see I fought for a better future." Negotiations over pay, benefits, job security, and working conditions have been ongoing since April and ramped up after a strike authorization vote in September. This led to rallies and protests, including a recent one that resulted in 58 worker arrests. Union members currently earn about $26 an hour including benefits. The union has not disclosed its exact wage demands but is seeking its largest-ever increases. They also want improved job security amid technological changes and enhanced safety measures, such as more safety buttons on casino floors.

Selon des experts, de tels accords devraient probablement empêcher une grève sans précédent sur le Strip de Las Vegas. « Je pense que nous parviendrons à un accord aujourd’hui. Nos employés attendent une augmentation de salaire pour faire face à l’inflation et à d’autres préoccupations », a déclaré Bill Hornbuckle, PDG de MGM Resorts, lors d’une conférence téléphonique sur les résultats alors que les négociations se poursuivaient. Le syndicat Culinary Workers avait menacé de faire grève tôt vendredi matin si les négociations échouaient. Cependant, l’entente avec Caesars semble avoir donné l’élan nécessaire pour obtenir de nouveaux contrats pour les 35 000 membres travaillant avec des contrats expirés dans 18 hôtels-casinos. « Dès qu’une entreprise trouve un accord, les autres suivent le mouvement », a déclaré Bill Werner, professeur associé à l’Université du Nevada à Las Vegas, spécialiste du droit de l’hôtellerie et des relations du travail. « Mais c’est la première fois depuis longtemps que nous sommes aussi proches d’une vraie grève. » L’accord avec Caesars a été conclu après 20 heures de négociations entamées mardi et poursuivies jusqu’à mercredi, selon le syndicat. Caesars a déclaré que l’accord valorise les contributions importantes de ses employés à Las Vegas grâce à des augmentations de salaire notables et à de nouvelles opportunités de croissance, notamment avec l’extension des emplois syndiqués. Une fois approuvé par les membres du syndicat, le contrat couvrira des établissements comme Caesars Palace, Flamingo, Harrah’s, Horseshoe, Paris Las Vegas, Planet Hollywood, Cromwell et Linq. Devant Caesars Palace mercredi, le visiteur Joshua Guray, arrivé de Los Angeles pour un court séjour, a déclaré qu’il ignorait les négociations mais aurait annulé sa réservation de dîner si une grève avait perturbé son voyage. « J’essaie de soutenir les autres salariés », a-t-il indiqué. La porte-parole du syndicat, Bethany Khan, a précisé que les détails de l’accord seraient publiés après l’approbation des membres, avec un vote attendu prochainement. Une grève reste possible si des accords ne sont pas conclus avec MGM Resorts et Wynn Resorts (plus grands employeurs privés de l’État) avant vendredi 5h du matin. Les discussions avec Wynn sont prévues jeudi. Un débrayage toucherait de plein fouet l’économie locale et perturberait considérablement les opérations des grands hôtels-casinos alors que Las Vegas se prépare à accueillir le Grand Prix de Formule 1. Cette année, de grandes mobilisations syndicales ont également eu lieu dans d’autres secteurs comme le cinéma, la livraison et d’autres casinos. Le circuit du Grand Prix de Las Vegas mettra en valeur plusieurs établissements concernés : Aria, Bellagio, Excalibur, Luxor, Mandalay Bay, MGM Grand, New York-New York, Park MGM, Wynn et Encore. Les travailleurs de l’hôtellerie, qu’ils soient femmes de chambre ou serveurs, affirment être prêts à faire grève aussi longtemps que nécessaire pour obtenir des contrats équitables. Tiffany Thomas, femme de chambre à Mandalay Bay, souligne son engagement : « Je suis prête à faire grève car j’ai une fille de 10 ans qui assiste aux négociations avec moi. Je veux qu’elle voie que je me suis battue pour un meilleur avenir. » Les négociations sur les salaires, les avantages, la sécurité de l’emploi et les conditions de travail durent depuis avril et se sont intensifiées après un vote d’autorisation de grève en septembre, suivi de manifestations lors desquelles 58 travailleurs ont été arrêtés. Les membres du syndicat gagnent actuellement environ 26 dollars de l’heure, avantages compris. Le syndicat n’a pas révélé ses revendications salariales exactes mais vise la plus forte augmentation de son histoire. Ils veulent aussi une meilleure sécurité de l’emploi face aux évolutions technologiques et de meilleures mesures de sécurité, comme davantage de boutons d’alerte sur les casinos.

article_content: Ed Balls’ Labour Party has announced a plan to guarantee jobs for every 18- to 24-year-old who has been unemployed for a year. However, Work and Pensions Secretary Iain Duncan Smith criticized the proposal, calling it unrealistic and saying it would create only short-term public sector roles at a high cost to taxpayers. Under the scheme, young people out of work for a year would be offered a taxpayer-funded job for six months, with those who refuse losing benefits. The plan would be funded by limiting pension tax relief for higher earners and reintroducing a tax on bankers’ bonuses, with Labour estimating the cost at £5.5 billion. Shadow Chancellor Ed Balls and Labour leader Ed Miliband maintain that the plan is fully funded and fair, but critics from the Conservative Party argue its costs are underestimated. Conservatives claim the policy could cost £1.7 billion more than Labour says, and that Labour has previously earmarked similar taxes for other commitments. Iain Duncan Smith noted that Labour expects 80 percent of jobs would be in the private sector, yet no private employers have committed to the scheme so far. He argued that Labour’s proposal is similar to the earlier Future Jobs Fund, which largely created short-term public sector placements at a cost of £6,500 each, with many participants returning to unemployment afterward. In contrast, Duncan Smith states the government’s current work experience programme is available from day one, costs around £325 per placement, and is more effective in moving people off benefits and into work. Ed Miliband insists that, with 56,000 young people unemployed for over a year, the plan is justified and will be funded by taxes on bank bonuses. Experts such as James Sproule of the Institute of Directors and Paul Johnson of the Institute for Fiscal Studies have expressed concerns, arguing the scheme does not address the root causes of long-term youth unemployment and may be too complex or expensive.
translated_content: Le Parti travailliste, dirigé par Ed Balls, a annoncé un plan visant à garantir un emploi à chaque jeune de 18 à 24 ans au chômage depuis un an. Cependant, le secrétaire au Travail et aux Retraites, Iain Duncan Smith, a critiqué cette proposition, la qualifiant d’irréaliste et affirmant qu’elle ne créerait que des emplois publics de courte durée à un coût élevé pour les contribuables. Dans le cadre de ce plan, les jeunes sans emploi depuis un an se verraient proposer un emploi financé par l’État pour six mois, ceux qui refuseraient perdraient leurs allocations. Le financement proviendrait de la réduction de l’allègement fiscal sur les retraites pour les hauts revenus et d’une nouvelle taxe sur les bonus des banquiers, avec une estimation de coûts à 5,5 milliards de livres selon le Labour. Le chancelier fantôme Ed Balls et le chef du Labour Ed Miliband affirment que le plan est entièrement financé et juste, mais les critiques du Parti conservateur soutiennent que ses coûts sont sous-estimés. Les conservateurs avancent que la politique pourrait coûter 1,7 milliard de livres de plus que ce qu’annonce le Labour et rappellent que les mêmes taxes ont déjà été prévues pour d’autres projets. Iain Duncan Smith souligne que le Labour prévoit que 80 % des emplois seraient dans le secteur privé, mais qu’aucun employeur privé ne s’est encore engagé dans ce programme. Il affirme que la proposition du Labour ressemble à l’ancien Future Jobs Fund, qui créait principalement des emplois publics de courte durée coûtant 6 500 livres chacun, de nombreux participants retournant au chômage après leur passage dans le programme. En comparaison, Duncan Smith indique que le programme d’expérience professionnelle du gouvernement commence dès le premier jour, coûte environ 325 livres par place, et s’avère plus efficace pour aider les jeunes à quitter les allocations et à retrouver un emploi. Ed Miliband insiste sur le fait qu’avec 56 000 jeunes au chômage depuis plus d’un an, le plan est justifié et sera financé par une taxe sur les bonus bancaires. Des experts comme James Sproule de l’Institute of Directors et Paul Johnson de l’Institute for Fiscal Studies expriment des doutes, estimant que le plan n’aborde pas les causes profondes du chômage des jeunes sur le long terme et risque d’être trop complexe ou coûteux.

Harvard scientists have made a significant advance toward understanding why some people develop neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s, while others remain dementia-free even into their 100s. Published in the journal Nature, their research centers on a protein called REST, which was previously believed to operate primarily in the brains of developing fetuses. The team discovered that REST also plays a protective role in healthy older adults, shielding neurons from age-related stress.

However, in the brains of people with Alzheimer’s and other forms of dementia, the levels of REST are drastically reduced in critical regions. According to Professor Bruce Yankner of Harvard Medical School, who led the study, these results raise the possibility that traditional markers of Alzheimer’s—such as abnormal protein aggregates—may not be enough to cause dementia by themselves. A failure of the brain’s stress response system, marked by decreased REST, might also be necessary.

Yankner emphasized that this insight could guide new treatment strategies for the more than five million Americans currently living with Alzheimer’s disease. He is known for pioneering work on amyloid beta, a hallmark abnormal protein in Alzheimer’s. This research highlights a novel perspective, focusing not just on negative brain changes but also on how the brain’s self-protection mechanisms may fail over time.

The study suggests that individuals could resist Alzheimer’s disease if their REST levels stay elevated. Drugs that can activate this protective gene network might allow early intervention, although much remains to be learned—including whether declining REST is a cause or effect of brain deterioration and whether it is specific enough to Alzheimer’s for targeted therapy.

Yankner noted that lithium, a medication considered relatively safe, appears to stimulate REST activity and could offer a potential treatment approach. As dementia rates are projected to nearly double by 2030 to almost 70 million cases worldwide, researchers stress the importance of preventative studies such as this.

Commenting on the study, Li-Huei Tsai, director of the Picower Institute for Learning and Memory at MIT, praised the research as the first to offer a plausible explanation for why some people are more susceptible to Alzheimer’s than others.

Des scientifiques de Harvard ont réalisé une avancée majeure pour comprendre pourquoi certaines personnes développent des maladies neurodégénératives comme Alzheimer, alors que d’autres restent exemptes de démence même en atteignant 100 ans. Publiée dans la revue Nature, leur étude se concentre sur une protéine appelée REST, autrefois considérée comme active principalement dans le cerveau du fœtus en développement. L’équipe a découvert que REST joue aussi un rôle protecteur chez les personnes âgées en bonne santé, protégeant les neurones contre le stress dû au vieillissement.

Toutefois, chez les personnes atteintes d’Alzheimer ou d’autres démences, les niveaux de REST sont fortement réduits dans des régions cérébrales clés. Selon le professeur Bruce Yankner de la Harvard Medical School, qui a dirigé l’étude, ces résultats suggèrent que les marqueurs classiques de la maladie d’Alzheimer – tels que les agrégats de protéines anormales – ne suffisent peut-être pas à provoquer la démence à eux seuls. Une défaillance du système de réponse au stress du cerveau, matérialisée par une baisse du REST, pourrait aussi être nécessaire.

Yankner souligne que cette découverte pourrait mener à de nouvelles stratégies thérapeutiques pour les plus de cinq millions d’Américains actuellement atteints de la maladie d’Alzheimer. Il est reconnu pour ses travaux pionniers sur la protéine bêta-amyloïde, marqueur clé de la maladie. Cette recherche apporte une perspective nouvelle, en mettant en lumière non seulement les altérations négatives du cerveau, mais aussi l’échec possible de ses mécanismes naturels de protection au fil du temps.

L’étude suggère que si les niveaux de REST restent élevés, certaines personnes pourraient résister à la maladie d’Alzheimer. Des médicaments capables d’activer ce réseau de gènes protecteurs pourraient permettre une intervention précoce, même s’il reste beaucoup à apprendre — notamment sur le lien de cause à effet entre la baisse du REST et la dégradation cérébrale, et sur la spécificité de ce marqueur dans les maladies neurologiques.

Yankner a également indiqué que le lithium, un médicament généralement sûr, semble stimuler l’activité du REST et représente une piste thérapeutique prometteuse. Puisque le nombre de cas de démence devrait presque doubler d’ici 2030 pour atteindre près de 70 millions dans le monde, les chercheurs insistent sur l’importance des études de prévention comme celle-ci.

En commentaire, Li-Huei Tsai, directrice du Picower Institute for Learning and Memory du MIT, a salué cette étude qui offre, selon elle, une piste crédible pour expliquer pourquoi certains individus sont plus vulnérables à Alzheimer.
post_content: Why do some people get Alzheimer’s while others stay sharp at 100? Harvard scientists found that a protein called REST may protect the brain as we age. Could new treatments be on the horizon? #Alzheimers #BrainHealth #ScienceNews

Temporary repairs began on the Benin-Agbor Road this Tuesday, following a protest by local residents who had blocked the route a week earlier due to its poor state. Workers say their efforts should ease travel for motorists and commuters, though only a complete overhaul from the Federal Government will provide a lasting solution. One worker said, "We're making the road passable for now, but there's still a lot to do to fix it fully. Hopefully, this work will make life a bit better for locals."

Sam, a truck driver, pointed out that neglect is a major part of the problem. He remarked, "It wouldn't have gotten this bad if the government maintained the roads. We shouldn't have to protest to see repairs—this delays us and affects our livelihood. I hope the work continues, especially since Christmas, a busy season for travel, is near."

For the first time in its 76-year history, the Fields Medal has been awarded to a woman. Maryam Mirzakhani, a 37-year-old Stanford University professor who grew up in Tehran, Iran, has also made history as the first Iranian to receive this esteemed mathematics prize. The award was presented at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Seoul, South Korea.

Mirzakhani was recognized for her pioneering work on the dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces and their moduli spaces—a field of research for which the Fields Medal is internationally renowned as the top honor in mathematics. Since its inception, the prize has been given every four years to mathematicians under 40, a stipulation some believe has presented challenges for women’s recognition due to overlap with prime child-rearing years.

Displaying exceptional mathematical talent from a young age, Mirzakhani secured gold medals for Iran at the International Mathematics Olympiad, where she became the team’s first female participant and achieved a perfect score. Her academic path included earning an undergraduate degree from Sharif University in Tehran and a Ph.D. from Harvard University, after which she held research and teaching positions at Princeton and later joined Stanford University.

Though celebrated globally, Mirzakhani maintains a modest outlook, at first doubting the legitimacy of her Fields Medal notification. She expressed hope that her win would motivate more young women to pursue studies and careers in mathematics, and she believes many more will earn this recognition in the future. The Fields Medal’s broader cultural recognition has been boosted by its mention in the film 'Good Will Hunting.'
