article_content: Scientists are forecasting a major geomagnetic storm set for Thursday, with the potential for northern lights sightings at much lower latitudes than usual—possibly as far south as Oregon, Wyoming, and Illinois. This storm is the result of a recent solar flare generating three distinct coronal mass ejections (CMEs), all aimed at Earth in what's called a 'halo CME.' These CMEs, which are clouds of magnetic fields and charged particles, travel through space at speeds approaching 1,900 miles (3,000 kilometers) per second. According to NASA's predictions, the coming storm could reach G3 (strong storm) levels or higher, which would result in vibrant aurora displays. The NOAA model, however, foresees a somewhat milder G2 event. Updated forecasts indicate aurora visibility in the U.S. on Thursday night and in the U.K. around 4:00 a.m. GMT Friday, with another opportunity to witness the spectacle on Friday night. Dr. Ryan French of the National Solar Observatory explains that a G3 event may bring auroras to areas as far south as Illinois and Oregon, while G2 storms typically are seen in places like New York and Idaho. This G3 prediction is based on NASA's model, whereas NOAA expects less intense conditions. French points out the forecast carries uncertainty since several CMEs are expected to hit Earth within a short timespan, which could either boost or diminish the resulting auroras. SpaceWeather.com, a space weather monitoring site, recommends watching for auroras both Thursday and Friday nights, given timing uncertainties. Once released, CMEs generally take a few days to travel from the sun to Earth. When they arrive, the charged particles move along Earth's magnetic field lines, fueling geomagnetic storms. These storms can create impressive green and red auroral ovals around polar regions and, if strong enough, extending into lower latitudes. Though solar flares themselves reach Earth in just eight minutes and can trigger radio blackouts, auroras are produced when the CME's slower particles interact with the planet's atmosphere. While G1 and G2 geomagnetic storms are relatively routine, the potential for G3 or even G4 activity—defined as strong to severe—is higher this week. Dr. Tamitha Skov notes that the approaching CME might overtake slower-moving ones, resulting in a 'cannibal CME' that could intensify the impact. With two additional storms en route, conditions may align for an especially vivid display, extending auroras deeper into the mid-latitudes if the magnetic orientation is favorable. Aurora sightings have become more common as the sun approaches the maximum phase of its 11-year cycle. People in regions south of the Arctic Circle usually see auroras as a faint northern glow, so it’s best to seek out the darkest skies away from city lights when trying to view them—using resources such as the Light Pollution Map is recommended. Those wanting the most frequent and brilliant auroras should consider visiting the Arctic Circle in places like Alaska, northern Canada, or northern Scandinavia within the next few years. Wishing clear conditions for everyone hoping to experience the beauty of the aurora!

La prévision G3 vient du modèle de la NASA, tandis que la NOAA table sur un scénario moins fort. Au sud du cercle arctique, l’aurore paraît souvent comme une faible lueur au nord, donc mieux vaut viser un ciel sombre loin des villes—et consulter la carte de la pollution lumineuse. article_content: Washington (CNN) – The day after 25 House Republicans attempted to prevent Speaker John Boehner from securing a third term, Boehner announced he is starting a 'family conversation' with his critics. The Speaker and his allies were angered by GOP members who publicly opposed him on the opening day of the new session of Congress by voting for other candidates or withholding support. Hours after the vote, it became clear that some dissenters would face consequences. Two Florida Republicans who did not back Boehner—Rep. Daniel Webster, who received 12 votes for his own bid to become Speaker, and Rep. Richard Nugent, who supported Webster—were removed from their positions on the House Rules Committee. The committee, an extension of the Speaker's office, determines which bills reach the floor and defines debate parameters. Boehner indicated that Webster and Nugent might eventually return to the committee. Boehner discussed the divisive vote and a closed-door meeting of all House Republicans on Wednesday morning. He told reporters, 'I have not had a chance to talk to them.' He added, 'We’re going to have a family conversation, which we had this morning, about bringing our team together. And I expect those conversations over the next couple of days will continue and we’ll come to a decision about how we go forward.' During the meeting, several Boehner allies urged against giving dissenters a second chance, arguing that there should be consequences for those who embarrassed the Speaker as Republicans assumed control of both chambers of Congress. However, Louisiana Rep. John Fleming, who voted for Boehner but has disagreed with him previously, warned against retaliation. 'I think retaliation and revenge is the wrong way to go on this. When emotions and personalities come into play, it works against us,' Fleming said. Texas Rep. Louie Gohmert, who challenged Boehner for Speaker, agreed that seeking revenge would hinder efforts to unify House Republicans. 'There's going to be a fight,' Gohmert said. Multiple House GOP sources told CNN they had expected some opposition prior to the Speaker vote but were surprised by the actions of some members. New Jersey Rep. Scott Garrett said he discussed his intentions to support another candidate with GOP leaders ahead of time. He said, 'I'm looking forward to doing my job on the Budget Committee. I'm looking forward to doing my job on the Financial Services Committee.' When asked about the possibility of losing one of his committee positions, Garrett responded, 'I don't think that's the nature of John Boehner.' Boehner, questioned about further repercussions, reiterated, 'we’re going to continue to have a family conversation.'

Quelques heures après le vote, il était clair que certains dissidents subiraient des conséquences. Boehner a évoqué le vote divisé ainsi qu’une réunion à huis clos de tous les Républicains de la Chambre mercredi matin. Il a déclaré aux journalistes : « Je n’ai pas eu l’occasion de leur parler. » Il a ajouté : « Nous allons avoir une conversation familiale, comme ce matin, pour rassembler notre équipe. Et j’estime que ces conversations vont se poursuivre dans les jours à venir, et nous déciderons comment avancer. » Lors de la réunion, plusieurs alliés de Boehner ont insisté pour que les dissidents n’obtiennent pas de seconde chance, affirmant qu’il devait y avoir des conséquences pour ceux qui ont embarrassé le Président alors que les Républicains prenaient le contrôle des deux chambres du Congrès. Cependant, le représentant John Fleming de Louisiane, qui a voté pour Boehner mais a déjà eu des différends avec lui, a mis en garde contre la vengeance. « Je pense que la revanche et les représailles ne sont pas la bonne solution. Le représentant texan Louie Gohmert, qui s’est présenté contre Boehner, a lui aussi considéré que rechercher la revanche compliquerait l’unité des Républicains. « Il va y avoir une lutte », a dit Gohmert. Il a déclaré : « J’ai hâte de faire mon travail au sein du comité du budget et des services financiers. » À la question de savoir s’il pourrait perdre l’une de ses fonctions, Garrett a répondu : « Je ne pense pas que ce soit le style de John Boehner. » Concernant de possibles sanctions supplémentaires, Boehner a simplement réitéré : « Nous allons continuer à avoir une conversation familiale. »

article_content: In Muscat’s marshes, Omani environmental scientist Zakiya al-Afifi carefully measures mangrove bark to estimate the amount of carbon dioxide these trees can trap. Leading a group of university students through the Al-Qurm reserve, she points out that its 80 protected hectares absorb thousands of tons of CO2. 'Mangroves are the world’s top carbon sink,' she says. Oman, on the southeastern tip of the Arabian Peninsula and recognized for its oil production, is emerging as a Gulf leader in mangrove conservation. Inspired by the environmental legacy of the late Sultan Qaboos bin Said, Oman is now a center for mangrove restoration. Mangrove forests can pull carbon dioxide from the atmosphere much faster than traditional forests, locking it away in both their foliage and the muddy soil beneath. Al-Afifi highlights that a single hectare in Al-Qurm holds up to 80 tons of CO2 in above-ground biomass; the sediment below contains even more. The motivation for Oman’s rapid replanting is both the ancient loss of mangrove forests due to past climate events and the current threats from human-driven climate change—rising temperatures, more floods, and cyclones all risk further damage. Badr bin Saif Al Busaidi, representing Oman’s environment authority, demonstrates the transformation from barren mudflats to dense mangrove forests over the past two decades. What used to be empty at Al-Sawadi creek now spans 88 hectares of thick growth—part of about 1,000 hectares restored nationwide since 2001. Within just two years, Oman directly planted over 3.5 million mangrove seeds, including a record two million this year. Busaidi notes this acceleration will continue: 'We’re facing off with climate change. Without action, we’ll lose these resources.' Initially, Oman’s restoration relied on nurseries—in Al-Qurm alone, 850,000 seedlings have been grown—but drone-based planting didn’t yield strong results, so the focus shifted back to manual, targeted approaches. These efforts feed into the growing market for carbon credits, offering companies a way to offset their emissions by supporting tree-planting projects. Each credit symbolizes a ton of atmospheric CO2 removed, though experts question the reliability of credit schemes unless trees reach full maturity and avoid destruction. Now, the environment authority and MSA Green Projects Company plan to plant 100 million trees within four years, converting 20,000 hectares—some with artificial lakes in Al Wusta—into new mangrove habitat. The project aims to cut 14 million metric tons of CO2 and raise $150 million via carbon credit sales. Given Oman’s emissions of 71 million tons of CO2 in 2021, effective and lasting climate action is crucial. Student Israa al-Maskari, at the mangrove nursery, remarks: 'Our generation sees first-hand the impacts of climate change. We have to look after the environment for ourselves and those after us.'

Situé à l’extrémité sud-est de la péninsule Arabique et connu pour son pétrole, Oman devient un leader du Golfe en conservation des mangroves. Cela devrait permettre d’éliminer 14 millions de tonnes de CO2 et rapporter 150 millions de dollars en crédits carbone. Avec 71 millions de tonnes de CO2 émises par Oman en 2021, il devient urgent d’agir concrètement pour le climat. À la pépinière, l’étudiante Israa al-Maskari témoigne : « Notre génération constate les effets du changement climatique. Il faut préserver l’environnement pour nous et ceux qui viendront après nous. »

When Clark Kent wanted to transform into Superman, a quick change inside a phone booth was all it took. In reality, such transformations are far more complex. Herbert Chavez, a 35-year-old man from the Philippines, has undergone extensive cosmetic surgery to resemble his comic book hero, Superman.

Chavez, whose profession is a pageant trainer, has dramatically changed his appearance through a variety of surgical procedures since 1995. These procedures include chin augmentation and thigh implants. His devotion to Superman is evident not only in his physical transformation but also in his home in Calamba City, south of Manila, which is filled with life-size statues, action figures, clothing, comics, and posters—all themed around Superman. Much of his memorabilia remains in its original packaging, preserving its value for collectors.

His current look appears to combine features from both the comic book version of Superman and the many actors who have played the character on screen. Photos show Chavez posing among his extensive Superman memorabilia collection, sometimes striking heroic stances or showing off his Superman-themed clothing and decor.

According to a video report on the Philippines' Bandila News, translated by the RealSelf blog, Chavez has maintained his quest to look like Superman for more than two decades. A psychiatrist interviewed by Bandila News noted that Chavez might have body dysmorphic disorder, a condition characterized by a preoccupation with altering one’s appearance. Images document Chavez’s transformation from before his surgeries to his current Superman-inspired look.

article_content: Australian troops may begin withdrawing from Afghanistan within the next few months, with most potentially returning home by the end of next year, according to Prime Minister Julia Gillard. This plan represents an acceleration of Australia's previously stated timeline and aligns with other international troop drawdowns, reflecting growing confidence in Afghan security forces and waning support for the war among contributing countries. Gillard’s remarks came ahead of an upcoming NATO summit in Chicago, where coalition leaders are expected to make important decisions about the future of their mission in Afghanistan. More than 1,500 Australian soldiers currently serve in Afghanistan, primarily in Uruzgan province. Gillard noted that Afghan President Hamid Karzai is expected to announce soon the start of transferring security responsibilities to Afghan troops in several provinces, a process that could take 12 to 18 months to complete. Once this transition is finished, Australia’s involvement in Afghanistan will shift primarily to police training and specialized instruction for Afghan National Security Forces, with a possible limited special forces presence under certain conditions. Since 2001, Australia has contributed troops, supplies, and expertise to the NATO-led effort in Afghanistan, which began shortly after the September 11 terrorist attacks. Analysts, such as Jeffrey Dressler from the Institute for the Study of War, have praised Australia’s contributions, particularly in Uruzgan, while also warning that the transition should be careful to prevent setbacks. Australia’s 1,550 troops represent a small portion of the over 130,000 international soldiers currently in Afghanistan, including major commitments from the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and France. The number of Australian soldiers killed in the conflict stands at 32. Other countries, including France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Norway, have already started or completed their own troop withdrawals. The international military campaign was launched to dismantle al Qaeda’s presence and deny the terrorist group a safe haven in Afghanistan. CNN’s Jethro Mullen, Hilary Whiteman, and Joe Sterling contributed to this report.

Ce plan accélère le calendrier précédemment annoncé par l’Australie et s’inscrit dans la lignée d’autres retraits internationaux, traduisant une confiance croissante dans les forces de sécurité afghanes ainsi qu’un désengagement progressif des pays contributeurs. Les déclarations de Gillard interviennent à la veille d’un sommet de l’OTAN à Chicago, où les dirigeants de la coalition doivent prendre des décisions importantes sur l’avenir de leur mission en Afghanistan. Plus de 1 500 soldats australiens servent actuellement en Afghanistan, principalement dans la province d’Uruzgan. Gillard a indiqué que le président afghan, Hamid Karzaï, devrait prochainement annoncer le lancement du transfert des responsabilités sécuritaires aux troupes afghanes dans plusieurs provinces, un processus qui pourrait durer de 12 à 18 mois. Une fois cette transition achevée, l’engagement de l’Australie se concentrera principalement sur la formation policière et l’accompagnement spécialisé des forces de sécurité nationales afghanes, avec éventuellement une présence limitée des forces spéciales dans certaines conditions. Depuis 2001, l’Australie contribue à l’effort dirigé par l’OTAN en Afghanistan, initié peu après les attentats du 11 septembre. Des analystes, comme Jeffrey Dressler de l’Institute for the Study of War, saluent la contribution australienne, notamment dans l’Uruzgan, tout en insistant sur la nécessité d’une transition progressive pour éviter tout revers. Les 1 550 soldats australiens représentent une faible part des plus de 130 000 militaires internationaux actuellement présents en Afghanistan, principalement originaires des États-Unis, du Royaume-Uni, d’Allemagne et de France. Le nombre de soldats australiens tués pendant ce conflit s’élève à 32. D’autres pays, comme la France, l’Allemagne, le Royaume-Uni, le Canada et la Norvège, ont déjà entamé ou achevé leur retrait. La campagne militaire internationale avait pour but de démanteler la présence d’al-Qaïda et d’empêcher le groupe terroriste d’utiliser l’Afghanistan comme base. article_content: Polish migrants in the UK are increasingly pursuing well-paid, professional roles rather than the low-paid agricultural jobs many took a decade ago, according to Polish MP Agnieszka Pomaska. She credits this shift to their higher educational attainment and strong work ethic, which she claims often surpass those of their British counterparts. Speaking at a London conference, Pomaska, chair of the Polish Parliament’s European Affairs Committee, criticized UK politicians who blame EU immigration for British youth unemployment. She argued that the UK opened its labor market because it needed workers for jobs that were otherwise hard to fill. Now, as Polish migrants have improved their education and English skills, they are seeking more lucrative opportunities. Pomaska pointed to international education rankings showing Poland ahead of the UK, emphasizing the growing competitiveness of Polish professionals. She also defended the right of Poles in the UK to claim child benefits, even if their children live abroad, asserting that Polish migrants contribute taxes and spend their earnings in Britain. This issue became a point of contention after Prime Minister David Cameron suggested ending child benefit payments to non-UK resident children—a move opposed by both Pomaska and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk. At the same event, Conservative MP Priti Patel highlighted a skills gap in the UK and criticized the education system for lacking competitiveness. She argued that immigration from skilled individuals benefits the UK, but also lamented a culture of worklessness among some in the UK population. Since joining the EU in 2004, about 500,000 Poles have settled in the UK. In 2012, around 24,000 EU migrants received child benefit for non-resident children. Pomaska argued that singling out Poles for different treatment is unfair.

Elle attribue ce changement à leur niveau d'éducation élevé et à leur solide éthique de travail, qu’elle considère souvent supérieurs à ceux de leurs homologues britanniques. S’exprimant lors d’une conférence à Londres, Pomaska, présidente de la commission des affaires européennes du parlement polonais, a critiqué les politiciens britanniques qui imputent le chômage des jeunes britanniques à l’immigration en provenance de l’UE. Elle a souligné que le Royaume-Uni avait ouvert son marché du travail parce qu’il avait besoin de travailleurs pour des postes difficiles à pourvoir. Désormais, grâce à une meilleure éducation et une meilleure maîtrise de l’anglais, les migrants polonais visent des opportunités plus lucratives. Pomaska a cité les classements internationaux de l’éducation qui placent la Pologne devant le Royaume-Uni, mettant en avant la compétitivité croissante des professionnels polonais. Elle a également défendu le droit des Polonais du Royaume-Uni à percevoir les allocations familiales, même si leurs enfants vivent à l’étranger, affirmant que ces migrants paient des impôts et dépensent leur argent en Grande-Bretagne. Cette question est devenue un sujet de discorde après que le Premier ministre David Cameron a proposé de supprimer les allocations pour enfants qui ne résident pas au Royaume-Uni — une mesure à laquelle se sont opposés Pomaska et le Premier ministre polonais Donald Tusk. Lors du même événement, la députée conservatrice Priti Patel a mis en avant le déficit de compétences au Royaume-Uni et critiqué le manque de compétitivité du système éducatif. Elle a estimé que l’immigration de personnes qualifiées profitait au pays, tout en déplorant une culture de l’inactivité professionnelle chez certains Britanniques. Depuis l’adhésion de la Pologne à l’UE en 2004, environ 500 000 Polonais se sont installés au Royaume-Uni. En 2012, environ 24 000 migrants de l’UE ont perçu des allocations familiales pour des enfants ne résidant pas dans le pays. Pomaska a jugé injuste de traiter les Polonais différemment des autres contribuables britanniques.

article_content:
The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) is considering new limits on abiraterone, a drug widely prescribed to men with advanced prostate cancer in England. Under NICE’s proposal, patients would have to try chemotherapy before receiving abiraterone, a move that critics say could force men to endure harsh side effects of chemotherapy, like hair loss and fatigue, sooner than necessary.

More than 3,000 men used abiraterone last year through the Cancer Drugs Fund, largely before chemo. Many medical professionals and charities believe early use of abiraterone improves quality of life and delays chemotherapy, but NICE argues the cost isn’t justified for earlier treatment. While a month’s supply officially costs £3,000, the NHS secures it at a lower price thanks to a discount from supplier Janssen.

Paul Burstow, MP and former health minister, urges the Department of Health to oppose the proposed restrictions. He had previously helped stop a complete ban in 2012, ensuring the drug stayed available after chemo. Recent progress in treatment suggests abiraterone can benefit patients even earlier, reducing side effects and improving well-being before they face chemotherapy.

Groups such as Prostate Cancer UK, Cancer Research UK, and experts like Professor Paul Workman from the Institute of Cancer Research have spoken out against NICE’s plan. They say restricting access overlooks patient welfare and might deny men life-extending treatment. Experiences shared by patients like Terry Emerson—who enjoyed better health and quality time before his illness progressed—highlight the drug’s value.

A Department of Health spokesperson confirmed that abiraterone is still available through the Cancer Drugs Fund, and discussions about its future accessibility are ongoing between the NHS, manufacturers, and NICE.

Selon la proposition du NICE, les patients devraient d’abord recevoir une chimiothérapie avant de pouvoir accéder à l’abiratérone, ce que de nombreux professionnels de santé et associations jugent problématique, estimant que cela pourrait exposer les malades à des effets secondaires lourds, comme la perte de cheveux ou la fatigue, plus tôt que nécessaire.

article_content: A lesson in American history took a dangerous turn when three children were hospitalized after a cannon-related explosion during a Civil War re-enactment at a parade in Orem, Utah. The incident occurred at the parade’s outset on Saturday, according to the city's Department of Public Safety. Witnesses reported that a spark from the cannon set off a pouch of additional charges, causing an explosion. Two of the children were briefly engulfed in flames, with one young girl's clothing catching fire. Bystanders quickly responded, dousing the flames with water to help the children. The three injured youngsters were taken to a nearby hospital in stable condition. The full extent of their injuries was not immediately known.

article_content: St Helen’s Church, which stood for nine centuries in Eston, Teesside, nearly became a casualty of recurring vandalism and theft over the past few decades. To protect its history, locals decided on an ambitious plan: dismantle the entire building piece by piece and rebuild it 40 miles away in County Durham. Beamish Museum took on the entire funding for the reconstruction, beginning in 1998 beside the Georgian Pockerley Manor. Each stone was carefully numbered and stored, awaiting the necessary resources for the meticulous rebuilding process. Unfortunately, plenty of original masonry and interior pieces had already been stolen or damaged, and a fire had devastated the roof. The laborious task of dismantling and moving the church took four workers a month. Following 15 years of restoration, the external structure now stands completed, but insufficient funds prevent the church from welcoming visitors inside. Curator Jim Rees explained that while finances caused delays, the building is safe under a new roof and gutters. Inside, major tasks—plastering, laying flagstone floors, crafting new doors and windows, and installing Georgian box pews—are yet to be finished, as the original wood was lost to the fire. Landscaping and a new shelter for a historic 1828 hearse, reputedly the oldest in Britain, are also on the agenda. Throughout its long life, St Helen’s served both as a parish church and a cemetery chapel, adjusting to the changing needs of its community. Services last took place in 1962, but hopes remain that future gatherings could return once restoration is complete. At present, visitors to Beamish Museum can see the completed exterior, but full access awaits additional funding.
translated_content: L’église St Helen, qui était établie depuis neuf siècles à Eston, Teesside, a failli disparaître à cause du vandalisme et des vols à répétition ces dernières décennies. Pour préserver son histoire, les habitants ont lancé un projet audacieux : démonter l’église pierre par pierre et la reconstruire à environ 65 kilomètres de là, dans le comté de Durham. Le Musée Beamish a pris en charge tout le financement de la reconstruction, commencée en 1998 près du manoir géorgien de Pockerley. Chaque pierre a été minutieusement numérotée et mise en réserve en attendant la suite des travaux. Malheureusement, une grande partie des pierres et du mobilier d’origine avaient déjà été volés ou endommagés, et un incendie avait détruit le toit. Il a fallu un mois à quatre ouvriers pour démonter et transporter l’église. Après quinze ans de restauration, l’extérieur est terminé, mais le manque de fonds empêche l’ouverture au public. Le conservateur Jim Rees a expliqué que les finances expliquent le retard, même si l’édifice est désormais protégé grâce au nouveau toit et aux gouttières. À l’intérieur, il reste de nombreux travaux : plâtrage, pose de dalles, portes et fenêtres à fabriquer, ainsi que l’installation de bancs d’époque géorgienne, car tout le bois d’origine a disparu dans l’incendie. Des aménagements extérieurs et la construction d’un abri pour un corbillard historique de 1828 – probablement le plus ancien du Royaume-Uni – sont également prévus. Au fil des siècles, St Helen a été tour à tour église paroissiale et chapelle de cimetière, selon les besoins de la communauté locale. Les derniers services religieux ont eu lieu en 1962, mais la reprise d’évènements est envisagée après la rénovation. Pour l’instant, les visiteurs du Musée Beamish peuvent admirer l’extérieur restauré, l’intérieur restant fermé en attendant de nouveaux financements.

article_content: More than 64,000 operations were cancelled in NHS hospitals across England last year, marking the highest annual total in a decade. According to new data, 64,192 planned operations were called off at the last minute in 2013/14, with none cancelled for clinical reasons. The only higher recent figure was 68,569 cancellations in 2004/05. Additional figures from NHS England reveal that the health service failed to meet its four-hour waiting time target for A&E departments. In major A&E wards, only 92.2% of patients were seen within four hours, falling short of the 95% target. Across all emergency departments, including minor injuries units and urgent care centres, 94.9% of patients were seen within four hours. Andy Burnham, Labour’s Shadow Health Secretary, criticized Prime Minister David Cameron, accusing him of complacency regarding the NHS. Burnham stated that it has become harder to see a GP, tens of thousands of operations have been cancelled, and nearly a million patients waited longer than four hours in A&E last year—the worst figures for a decade. He also attributed the crisis to a £3 billion NHS reorganization that Cameron had previously promised would not occur.

D'autres chiffres de NHS England montrent que le service de santé n'a pas atteint son objectif de quatre heures pour la prise en charge aux urgences. Dans les principaux services d'urgences, seulement 92,2 % des patients ont été vus en moins de quatre heures, en dessous de l'objectif de 95 %. Dans tous les services d'urgences, y compris les unités pour blessures mineures et les centres de soins urgents, 94,9 % des patients ont été vus dans ce délai. Il attribue aussi la crise à une réorganisation du NHS de 3 milliards de livres sterling, que Cameron avait promis de ne pas entreprendre.

article_content: Liverpool are looking to strengthen their left-back position and are considering reigniting their pursuit of Ryan Bertrand. Bertrand, who spent last season on loan at Aston Villa from Chelsea, has been on Liverpool’s radar for over a year. Although Liverpool nearly signed him during the January transfer window, he joined Villa instead. Securing a deal for Bertrand may be difficult, as Chelsea are reluctant to conduct business with Liverpool, whom they now view as genuine title contenders, and would expect a transfer fee in excess of £8 million. Liverpool have also shown interest in young Atletico Madrid left-back Javier Manquillo, pursuing a potential two-year loan deal with an option to buy for £4.5 million. In addition, the club was keen on signing Sevilla’s Alberto Moreno, but negotiations have stalled with Sevilla unwilling to reduce their £16 million asking price. Liverpool had also targeted Ben Davies, but he has chosen to join Tottenham from Swansea as part of a deal involving Gylfi Sigurdsson and Michel Vorm.

Conclure un transfert pour Bertrand sera difficile, car Chelsea hésite à traiter avec Liverpool, qu’il considère comme un sérieux rival pour le titre, et demanderait plus de 8 millions de livres. Liverpool s’intéresse aussi au jeune arrière gauche de l’Atlético Madrid, Javier Manquillo, pour un prêt de deux ans avec option d’achat à 4,5 millions de livres. Par ailleurs, le club visait aussi l’Espagnol Alberto Moreno du Séville FC, mais les discussions bloquent car Séville refuse de descendre de ses 16 millions de livres. Enfin, Liverpool avait ciblé Ben Davies, mais il a préféré rejoindre Tottenham depuis Swansea dans le cadre d’un deal impliquant Gylfi Sigurdsson et Michel Vorm.

article_content: A crew member working on a BBC children's film about William Shakespeare was hospitalized after suffering serious injuries from falling off a lorry following a night out. The 27-year-old man was working on a film titled 'Bill,' a comedy based on Shakespeare's life, which was being filmed at Bolton Castle in Wensleydale, North Yorkshire. The production is part of the popular Horrible Histories children's series and has been ongoing throughout the month. The incident occurred near Redmire in the Yorkshire Dales. After being taken to James Cook Hospital in Middlesbrough, the man is reported to be in a stable condition. Police say the man was returning home after a night out when, at around 3:20 am on Sunday, March 9, he fell from the back of a truck at Sissy Bank Barn in Redmire. The 29-year-old driver of the truck, believed to be an Iveco, was arrested on suspicion of drink-driving and has since been released on bail. Police have confirmed they are pursuing further lines of inquiry. BBC crews have been using Bolton Castle as a filming location for the Horrible Histories production for the past month. Cast and crew members are staying in caravans beside the visitor attraction, as well as in local pubs and holiday cottages. Traffic Constable Martin Usher from the force's roads policing group appealed for witnesses, stating: 'If you were using the Leyburn to Redmire road in the early hours of Sunday 9 March 2014, please contact the police if you saw the Iveco truck or a man walking along the road.' The film is being produced by Cowboy Films and Punk Cinema for BBC Films. A spokesperson for BBC Films said the accident happened outside of production hours and is being investigated by police. Cowboy Films declined to comment, and no one from Punk Cinema was available for comment.

article_content: Former Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Attahiru Jega, described Nigeria’s 2023 general elections as 'credible in many substantial aspects.' In a live appearance on Channels Television’s 'Politics Tonight' on Monday, Jega clarified that his favorable assessment of the elections does not serve as a defense of the current INEC chairman, Prof. Yakubu Mahmood. The 2023 elections and their outcomes have drawn mixed reactions, with legal challenges, election petitions, and several decisions by the tribunals and the Court of Appeal generating continued debate. Jega stated, 'In many substantial aspects, it was credible.' He acknowledged that there were significant challenges during the election, some of which were avoidable. Jega said that it is common to blame the leadership of the electoral body, a criticism he has faced himself. He also argued that responsibility for failures during the election should be apportioned appropriately, noting that politicians played a direct role in areas where there were serious issues. Jega emphasized that political interference 'more or less circumscribed the powers' of INEC and its chairman. He concluded that while it is unfortunate these problems occurred during Mahmood’s tenure, there is no evidence to suggest Mahmood was complicit in any electoral misconduct.

Lors d’une intervention en direct dans l’émission « Politics Tonight » sur Channels Television lundi, Jega a souligné que son évaluation positive des élections ne constitue pas une défense du président actuel de l’INEC, le professeur Yakubu Mahmood. Les élections de 2023 et leurs résultats ont suscité des réactions contrastées, avec des contestations judiciaires, des requêtes électorales et plusieurs décisions des tribunaux et de la Cour d’appel qui continuent d’alimenter le débat. Jega a affirmé : « À de nombreux égards substantiels, elles étaient crédibles. » Il a reconnu que les élections ont rencontré d’importants défis, dont certains auraient pu être évités. Jega indique qu’il est courant de blâmer la direction de la commission électorale, une critique qu’il a lui-même déjà connue. Jega a précisé que les interférences politiques ont « en grande partie limité les pouvoirs » de l’INEC et de son président. Il a conclu qu’il est regrettable que ces problèmes se soient produits sous la direction de Mahmood, mais qu’il n’existe aucune preuve indiquant que Mahmood ait été complice d’une mauvaise conduite électorale.

article_content:
When I applied to Yale, I chose African American Studies as my major on a whim. I was unsure about my academic path but was deeply interested in W.E.B. Du Bois at the time, so I wrote my application essay about him. A few months later, I received my acceptance. I don’t know if this choice influenced my admission; Yale doesn’t admit by major, and it’s unlikely that studying African American Studies gave me an edge over applicants choosing political science or humanities, my dream major. Still, part of me wonders if being Black and selecting a smaller major played a role. Now that I’m here, I’m working hard to show I belong at Yale.

My decision to attend an East Coast school stemmed from big ambitions and a preference for Yale and Princeton over Harvard, which felt dull to me. I applied to nine schools, receiving acceptances from all but Princeton. When I learned I got into Yale, I had a headache and simply texted my parents, checked in on friends, and continued my day. The Princeton rejection showed that a Yale acceptance wasn’t guaranteed; both schools have low acceptance rates, so every detail likely mattered—including, perhaps, my race. I can’t help but consider whether that tipped the scale, sparking doubts that I didn’t truly deserve my spot. With the Supreme Court striking down affirmative action soon after I was admitted, I sometimes felt like I’d entered through a door that swiftly closed behind me.

Some of my unease comes from memories: telling my Yale interviewer I didn’t care much if I got in, and overhearing conversations that made me question my qualifications. I’ve considered the possibility that my race compensated for any shortcomings. Rather than rejecting that idea, I’ve accepted that it might be true. Perhaps my race helped my application, but I believe I would have succeeded elsewhere regardless.

Still, I push myself relentlessly—not just to reassure myself, but to show others that I deserve to be here. I joined Yale’s rigorous Directed Studies program, was accepted into every club I applied for, won the first-year prize debate at the Yale Political Union, and serve on the executive board of the Generational African American Student Association—all while staying true to myself. As long as I’m here, I’ll make the most of every opportunity, determined not to be seen as lazy or unworthy.

Before enrolling, I read “The Future of the Race” by Henry Louis Gates Jr. and Cornel West, in which Gates reflects on his time at Yale and being part of the first generation of Black students in integrated schools. I often think of that book and how far things have come—the Afro-American Cultural Center is a second home, the class of 2027 is 14% African American, and there are numerous affinity groups for Black students. Even though affirmative action was deemed unconstitutional, we’re already here. More Black students will join each year, and regardless of policy changes, we’ll continue to build community and work for a better future. That’s why I came to Yale.
translated_content:
Lorsque j’ai postulé à Yale, j’ai choisi la filière Études afro-américaines un peu par hasard. Je ne savais pas vraiment ce que je voulais étudier, mais j’étais très intéressé par W.E.B. Du Bois à l’époque, alors j’ai rédigé ma lettre de motivation sur lui. Quelques mois plus tard, j’ai été accepté. Je ne sais pas si ce choix a influencé mon admission ; Yale n’admet pas selon la filière, et il est peu probable qu’opter pour Études afro-américaines m’ait avantagé par rapport à ceux qui ont choisi sciences politiques ou mon rêve : les humanités. Pourtant, une partie de moi se demande si le fait d’être noir et d’avoir choisi une petite filière a pu jouer un rôle. Maintenant que je suis ici, je travaille dur pour prouver que j’ai ma place à Yale.

Mon choix d’étudier sur la Côte Est vient de grandes ambitions et d’une préférence pour Yale et Princeton plutôt que Harvard, que je trouvais fade. J’ai postulé à neuf universités et j’ai été accepté partout sauf à Princeton. Le jour où j’ai appris mon admission à Yale, j’avais mal à la tête ; j’ai juste envoyé un message à mes parents, pris des nouvelles de mes amis, et repris ma journée. Être refusé à Princeton m’a rappelé que l’admission à Yale n’était pas garantie ; leurs taux d’admission sont faibles, alors chaque détail devait compter, y compris peut-être ma couleur de peau. Je ne peux pas m’empêcher de penser que cela a pu jouer, ce qui m’a parfois donné l’impression de ne pas mériter ma place. Peu après mon admission, la Cour suprême des États-Unis a invalidé l’action affirmative, et j’ai eu l’impression d’être passé par une porte qui s’est rapidement refermée derrière moi.

Une partie de mon malaise vient de souvenirs : avoir dit à mon interlocuteur de Yale que mon admission ne m’importait pas beaucoup, ou encore avoir entendu des conversations qui mettaient en doute mon mérite. J’ai envisagé la possibilité que ma race ait compensé certains manques. Plutôt que de rejeter cette idée, je l’accepte. Peut-être que ma race a aidé ma candidature, mais je crois que j’aurais réussi ailleurs malgré tout.

Pourtant, je me donne à fond—notamment pour me rassurer, mais aussi pour montrer aux autres que je mérite d’être ici. J’ai intégré le programme sélectif Directed Studies de Yale, j’ai été accepté dans tous les clubs où j’ai postulé, j’ai gagné le débat de première année de la Yale Political Union, et je fais partie du bureau exécutif de la Generational African American Student Association, tout en restant authentique. Tant que je serai là, je saisirai chaque occasion, déterminé à ne jamais être vu comme paresseux ou illégitime.

Avant de commencer à Yale, j’ai lu « The Future of the Race » de Henry Louis Gates Jr. et Cornel West, où Gates raconte son passage à Yale comme l’une des premières générations de Noirs dans les écoles intégrées. Ce livre me revient souvent en tête, en voyant le chemin parcouru : le centre culturel afro-américain de Yale est comme une seconde maison, la promotion 2027 compte 14 % d’étudiants afro-américains, et il existe de nombreux groupes d’affinité. Même si l’action positive a été jugée anticonstitutionnelle, nous sommes déjà là. D’autres étudiants noirs nous rejoindront chaque année, et malgré les changements de politique, nous continuerons de bâtir une communauté et d’œuvrer pour un avenir meilleur. C’est pourquoi je suis venu à Yale.

article_content: Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg, known for his casual wardrobe, wore a suit and tie when he met Japanese Prime Minister Yoshihiko Noda during a recent visit. In their conversation, Zuckerberg shared that witnessing the destruction from Japan's tsunami inspired him to think about how Facebook could do more to help people during natural disasters, particularly in connecting survivors and providing critical updates. Zuckerberg remarked to Noda that he is 'very different' from the version portrayed in the movie 'The Social Network', sparking laughter and a relaxed atmosphere during their brief meeting. Earlier in the week, Zuckerberg and his long-term partner Priscilla Chan were spotted exploring Shanghai, China. Their casual appearance as tourists drew attention, prompting speculation about Facebook's business intentions for the Chinese market, as Zuckerberg has openly expressed interest in expanding there. While exploring the Fuxing Road area, Chan, who is Chinese-American, used her iPad to help the couple navigate when they became unsure of their location. Zuckerberg has been studying Mandarin and has publicly raised the importance of connecting people in China—a market with 1.6 billion residents—to Facebook's global network. Though Facebook has 845 million users around the world, it is currently blocked in China by government internet controls. Rumors circulated that Zuckerberg and Apple CEO Tim Cook arrived in China together on a private jet, further fueling speculation about possible business opportunities. Zuckerberg and Chan met while attending Harvard University and have been together since their student days, prior to Zuckerberg becoming a billionaire.

article_content: A domestic dispute in Brazil led to a widespread blackout impacting five towns after Reginaldo Rocha, 49, climbed a high-voltage electricity pylon following an argument with his wife. The incident began when Rocha, a painter and decorator from Sorocaba in Sao Paulo state, returned home late after spending over £150 on drinks with friends. During the ensuing argument, Rocha left the house and climbed a nearby pylon, threatening to jump. To prevent him from being electrocuted by the pylon's 80,000 volts, electricity officials shut down the power supply, which resulted in more than 600,000 people across the towns of Sorocaba, Capela do Alto, Ipero, Aracoiaba da Serra, and Boituva losing electricity. The power cut disrupted traffic signals, phone lines, and even the national emergency number 192. Fifty police officers and firemen, along with Rocha's family, spent over three hours persuading him to come down, while a large crowd watched below. Eventually, Rocha was safely removed from the pylon and taken to hospital for observation. He may face charges for endangering public safety and disrupting public utilities, offenses that could lead to up to five years in prison or a fine.

L'incident a commencé lorsque Rocha, peintre en bâtiment originaire de Sorocaba (État de São Paulo), est rentré tard chez lui après avoir dépensé plus de 150£ en alcool avec des amis. Au cours de la dispute qui a suivi, Rocha a quitté la maison et a escaladé un pylône voisin, menaçant de sauter. Pour éviter qu'il ne soit électrocuté par les 80 000 volts du pylône, les responsables de l'électricité ont coupé l'alimentation électrique, privant ainsi plus de 600 000 personnes d'électricité dans les villes de Sorocaba, Capela do Alto, Ipero, Aracoiaba da Serra et Boituva. Cette panne a perturbé les feux de signalisation, les lignes téléphoniques et même le numéro d'urgence national 192. Cinquante policiers et pompiers, ainsi que la famille de Rocha, ont passé plus de trois heures à tenter de le convaincre de descendre, sous le regard d'une foule nombreuse. Finalement, Rocha a été descendu du pylône en toute sécurité et transporté à l'hôpital pour observation. Il risque d'être poursuivi pour mise en danger de la sécurité publique et perturbation des services publics, des faits passibles de cinq ans de prison ou d'une amende.

article_content: U.S. law enforcement officials are preparing for the tough challenge of interrogating Ahmed Abu Khatallah, identified as the suspected ringleader behind the deadly 2012 attack on the American diplomatic post in Benghazi, Libya. Authorities believe Khatallah has had ample time to craft his narrative, raising concerns that questioning may prove difficult. However, intelligence experts, including veteran Navy agent Robert McFadden, suggest that with the right approach, it’s possible he could divulge key information—drawing upon previous experiences where detainees eventually cooperated under pressure from uncertainty and fatigue. Khatallah's capture was the result of months of targeted intelligence. According to General Martin Dempsey, U.S. Special Forces covertly entered Libya by sea, setting a trap in a villa near Benghazi with FBI support. Once apprehended, Khatallah and certain seized materials were transported by boat to the USS New York. Officials noted that conducting the operation at sea prioritized both security and logistics, as air transfer posed diplomatic obstacles in the region. Aboard the ship, FBI-led High Value Detainee Interrogation Group members are getting uninterrupted time to question Khatallah in a distraction-free environment. After a brief medical examination—necessary to confirm he was unharmed during the short, nonviolent arrest—interrogators will focus on extracting details vital to U.S. national security, such as terrorist networks, communications, and ongoing threats. The Libyan government has condemned the operation, referring to it as a breach of sovereignty and urging dialogue and transparency in future incidents. Libyan Justice Minister Salah Marghani emphasized the importance of safeguarding Khatallah's rights. Human Rights Watch also called for Khatallah to quickly access legal counsel and to be guaranteed a fair and prompt trial. Upon nearing U.S. shores, officials plan to transfer Khatallah by helicopter to land, where he will be tried in federal court. The Obama administration’s decision to pursue a civilian trial, rather than detention at Guantanamo Bay, has drawn criticism from some Republican lawmakers. Still, the track record of American civil courts in securing terrorism-related convictions—such as those of Faisal Shahzad, Umar Farouk Abdulmutallab, Abu Hamza al-Masri, and Sulaiman Abu Ghaith—argues in favor of this approach compared to far fewer outcomes from military commissions. Khatallah will soon face formal charges, which are expected to include offenses like killing during an attack on a federal facility and providing material support to terrorism. U.S. investigators have spent two years collecting evidence against him, countering his claimed innocence about his role during the embassy attack that killed Ambassador Christopher Stevens and information officer Sean Smith. Meanwhile, the controversial raid continues to stir debate in both Libya and the U.S., illustrating the ongoing complexities of international counterterrorism operations and cross-border justice.
translated_content: Les autorités américaines se préparent à l’interrogatoire difficile d’Ahmed Abu Khatallah, suspecté d’être le meneur de l’attaque meurtrière en 2012 contre le poste diplomatique américain à Benghazi, en Libye. Selon les enquêteurs, Khatallah a eu le temps de préparer son récit, rendant l’interrogatoire potentiellement ardu. Toutefois, des experts comme l’agent de la marine Robert McFadden pensent qu’il pourrait finir par collaborer avec la bonne approche, comme l’ont fait d’autres détenus motivés par l’incertitude ou la lassitude. La capture de Khatallah est le fruit de plusieurs mois de renseignement ciblé. Selon le général Martin Dempsey, des forces spéciales américaines sont entrées discrètement en Libye par la mer, avec l’appui du FBI, pour tendre un piège dans une villa près de Benghazi. Khatallah et divers supports saisis ont ensuite été transportés par bateau jusqu’au USS New York. Les responsables américains expliquent que l’option maritime était privilégiée pour des raisons de sécurité et de logistique, le transfert par voie aérienne soulevant des complications diplomatiques. À bord du navire, l’équipe d’interrogation de haute valeur dirigée par le FBI bénéficie de temps sans interruption pour questionner Khatallah dans un environnement calme. Après un contrôle médical rapide, confirmant l’absence de blessures lors de l’arrestation non violente, l’interrogatoire portera sur des informations cruciales pour la sécurité nationale—réseaux terroristes, communications et menaces potentielles. Le gouvernement libyen a condamné l’opération, la qualifiant d’atteinte à la souveraineté et a demandé davantage de transparence à l’avenir. Le ministre libyen de la Justice, Salah Marghani, a insisté sur la nécessité de protéger les droits de Khatallah. Human Rights Watch a également réclamé un accès rapide à un avocat et un procès équitable pour le suspect. À l’approche des côtes américaines, Khatallah doit être transféré en hélicoptère puis présenté à la justice fédérale. Le choix de l’administration Obama d’un procès civil, plutôt qu’une détention à Guantanamo, a suscité des critiques de responsables républicains. Cependant, les tribunaux civils américains ont montré leur efficacité avec plusieurs condamnations liées au terrorisme, contrairement au faible nombre de procès réussis à Guantanamo. Khatallah sera bientôt officiellement inculpé, notamment pour meurtre lors d’une attaque contre un site fédéral et soutien matériel au terrorisme. Les enquêteurs américains ont recueilli des preuves pendant deux ans, réfutant ses déclarations sur son rôle lors de l’assaut, qui a coûté la vie à l’ambassadeur Christopher Stevens et à l’informaticien Sean Smith. Cette opération controversée continue d’alimenter le débat en Libye et aux États-Unis, soulignant la complexité de la lutte antiterroriste internationale et des poursuites transfrontalières.

article_content: Four first responders who rescued a golden retriever from the icy Charles River outside Boston last month were unable to accept a Caribbean vacation gifted to them by talk show host Ellen DeGeneres as a reward for saving the dog's life. Wellesley, Massachusetts Fire Captain Jim Dennehy, Lieutenant Paul Delaney, Dave Papazian, and Joan Cullinan each received a personalized life vest from DeGeneres, in addition to the cruise offer. However, due to state ethics laws prohibiting municipal employees from accepting such gifts, they had to decline the vacation. According to Wellesley Fire Chief Richard DeLorie, the firefighters returned the vouchers to the Ellen Show in accordance with the law. On December 22, authorities responded to a 911 call about a dog trapped in the ice on the Charles River. Wellesley rescuers used GPS data from the owner's cell phone to locate the dog, Crosby, in the Elm Bank Reservation area. Crosby, a five-year-old golden retriever, was stranded about 40 yards from the shore in freezing water. The cell phone's location data was essential in directing the responders to the right spot. Firefighter Dave Papazian put on a cold water survival suit and entered the river to reach Crosby. Lieutenant Paul Delaney joined him, and together, with assistance from their team on shore using ropes, they managed to pull the frightened dog back to safety. Video footage showed the dramatic rescue. After being pulled from the river, Crosby appeared shaken but was in good health. Rescue workers quickly dried Crosby off and reunited her with her owner, Amy Kapinos, who expressed heartfelt gratitude to the first responders for their quick and brave actions.

article_content: Nearly half of high-achieving 11-year-olds do not go on to secure five strong GCSEs in core subjects, according to secondary school league tables. Of the 160,000 pupils who achieved good SATs results when leaving primary school, 84,000 did not achieve a C grade or above in the English Baccalaureate subjects: English, maths, science, history or geography, and a language. These figures have reignited the debate about mixed-ability classes, which both Labour and the Conservatives have pledged to address since 1997. Critics argue the absence of ability-based sets and streams can hold back the most capable students. In addition, 420 schools or sixth-form colleges did not produce a single student who gained three A-levels at grades AAB or above in subjects preferred by leading universities. The data also reveal that the number of underperforming schools has dropped since the Coalition government came to power. Of the 3,200 state schools in England, 154 fell short of the government’s target of at least 40% of pupils achieving five good passes at GCSE, including English and maths, putting them at risk of closure or conversion into academies. The number of underperforming schools was 61 fewer than the previous year, despite the benchmark being raised from 35% of pupils. As a result, 50,000 fewer children are now in underperforming secondaries compared to last year, or 244,000 fewer than in 2010. Education Secretary Michael Gove described the results as a ‘credit to the professionalism and hard work of teachers’. Tony Blair abandoned Labour’s traditional support for mixed-ability teaching in 1997, effectively acknowledging its shortcomings. Education ministers have since advocated for teaching by ability groups, suggesting it would raise standards. David Cameron supported this approach, stating every comprehensive school should include a grammar stream. However, Ofsted reports show that only 46% of state school classes are set or streamed, a rise of just one percentage point over 17 years. Conservative MP Graham Brady, a supporter of selective education, stated, ‘All of the evidence indicates that teaching by ability works best, whether it's within schools through sets and streams or between schools through a selective system.’ The league tables, based on Department for Education data, show the performance of more than 4,000 schools and colleges in England at GCSE, A-level, and other academic qualifications. Colyton Grammar School in Devon was the top-performing school for GCSEs for the second consecutive year. The data also show 202,000 pupils were entered for the EBacc subjects, compared to 130,000 in 2012, indicating that schools are increasingly following government advice to prioritize core academic subjects over so-called 'soft' options like drama and sociology. Teachers’ unions criticize league tables, claiming they do not accurately reflect school performance and can encourage teaching to the test. However, Simon Burgess, a professor of economics at the University of Bristol, argues that league tables are important for maintaining school standards, saying that removing them reduces average performance and increases inequality in achievement.

article_content: An underwater robot resembling a turtle, designed to assist archaeologists in exploring shipwrecks, is being displayed in the UK for the first time. Called U-CAT, the robot was developed by engineers at Estonia's Tallinn University of Technology's Centre for Biorobotics, to access places too dangerous or deep for human divers. U-CAT is part of the Science Museum's 'Robot Safari' exhibition in London, showcasing 13 nature-inspired machines, including a flying bat robot, glowing robotic fish, and a tumbleweed-inspired robot. Unlike traditional underwater robots with propellers, U-CAT uses four independently-driven fins, allowing it to maneuver in all directions without stirring up sediment, which keeps visibility clear inside shipwrecks. The robot can operate autonomously for several hours, inspecting wrecks before resurfacing. It is equipped with a camera to record underwater footage, which can later help reconstruct sites. The U-CAT was designed to be affordable for smaller organizations and can move backward, forward, upward, and turn in tight spaces. Developed as part of the EU-funded Arrows project, U-CAT aims to make underwater archaeology safer and more accessible. Other highlights of the Robot Safari exhibition include Jessiko, a luminous robotic fish from France designed to demonstrate how robots can work together; the Cheetah-cub, the fastest quadruped robot under 30kg, from Switzerland; Pleurobot, a salamander-inspired robot that aids in studying animal locomotion; Bat-Bot and iTuna, lightweight aquatic robots from Spain; and DodecaRob, a tumbleweed-mimicking robot from Romania. The exhibition features interactive demonstrations and workshops, letting visitors see how nature inspires robotics and even build or program their own simple robots. The event is free and suitable for all ages, but timed tickets are required, available at the museum or by phone.

U-CAT fait partie de l’exposition « Robot Safari » du Science Museum à Londres, qui présente 13 machines inspirées de la nature, dont un robot chauve-souris volant, des poissons robotiques lumineux et un robot inspiré du mouvement d’une herbe folle. Contrairement aux robots sous-marins traditionnels équipés d’hélices, U-CAT utilise quatre nageoires motorisées indépendamment, ce qui lui permet de se déplacer dans toutes les directions sans soulever de sédiments, maintenant ainsi la visibilité à l’intérieur des épaves. Le robot peut fonctionner de façon autonome pendant plusieurs heures pour inspecter des épaves avant de remonter à la surface. U-CAT a été conçu à un coût abordable pour les petites organisations et peut se déplacer en marche arrière, en avant, vers le haut et effectuer des virages serrés. Développé dans le cadre du projet européen ARROWS, U-CAT vise à rendre l’archéologie sous-marine plus sûre et plus accessible. article_content: At least 73 people have been killed and more than 21,000 left homeless after Tropical Storm Irina struck Madagascar, according to an official from the country’s disaster bureau on Wednesday. One person was reported injured, and two more are missing, said Setra Rakotomandrindra of the National Bureau of Natural Catastrophes. About 21,235 people are homeless and a total of 67,911 people have been affected, primarily in the island nation’s southeastern region. The government is using tents to shelter those in need, Rakotomandrindra stated. Irina is the second severe storm to hit Madagascar in two weeks, following Cyclone Giovanna, which caused significant damage the previous month, according to the IRIN news agency—part of the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. While many had advance warning of Cyclone Giovanna, Irina caught much of the island by surprise, destroying roads and houses that had already been weakened by the earlier storm. More than 100 people have died during this year’s cyclone season, which typically lasts from January to March, IRIN said. The majority of casualties were in the southeastern town of Ifanadiana, where a mudslide buried homes and triggered a minibus accident. As of Wednesday, main roads in Madagascar had reopened, Rakotomandrindra reported. CNN’s Pierre Meilhan and Christabelle Fombu contributed to this report.

Environ 21 235 personnes sont sans abri et un total de 67 911 personnes ont été touchées, principalement dans la région sud-est de l’île. Contrairement à Giovanna, dont la population a été largement avertie, Irina a pris l’île de court, détruisant routes et maisons déjà fragilisées par le cyclone précédent. Depuis mercredi, les routes principales de Madagascar ont été rouvertes, a rapporté Rakotomandrindra. Pierre Meilhan et Christabelle Fombu de CNN ont contribué à ce reportage.

article_content: Edward Fletcher, a seasoned industry executive, has been appointed as the new CEO of Curzon, where he will oversee the company's exhibition and distribution operations. Fletcher's appointment follows the departure of Philip Knatchbull. With a rich background in British film exhibition, distribution, and production, Fletcher brings years of experience to Curzon. His previous roles include managing cinemas in Croydon, Cambridge, and London’s ICA, moving into film distribution at ICA Projects, and co-founding Soda Pictures in 2002. Under his leadership, Soda Pictures grew its catalog to over 300 titles, featuring acclaimed British, international, and documentary films. In 2014, Soda Pictures was acquired by Canadian media group Thunderbird Entertainment and rebranded as Thunderbird Releasing. The Palme d’Or-winning 'Shoplifters' was the company’s most successful release before it shifted focus to television production. Fletcher later helped launch a film and TV division for Rebellion, a games and publishing company, and co-founded the independent production label Beef with producer Emma Biggins. Beef is currently developing projects from emerging British directors. A former board member of Film London, Fletcher now serves as vice chair of Film Cymru Wales. Charles S. Cohen, Chairman and Owner of Curzon, praised Fletcher’s deep knowledge of the UK film landscape and highlighted plans for Curzon to take a more active role in film production. Fletcher expressed enthusiasm for joining Curzon, noting its storied legacy, beloved cinemas, and leading distribution arm, and looked forward to expanding the company’s reach with the support of the Cohen Media Group.

Cette nomination fait suite au départ de Philip Knatchbull. Doté d'une solide expérience dans l'exhibition, la distribution et la production cinématographiques britanniques, Fletcher apporte de nombreuses années d'expertise à Curzon. Il a notamment géré des cinémas à Croydon, Cambridge et à l’ICA de Londres, travaillé dans la distribution au sein d’ICA Projects, puis cofondé Soda Pictures en 2002. Sous sa direction, Soda Pictures a enrichi son catalogue de plus de 300 titres, dont des films britanniques, internationaux et documentaires salués par la critique. En 2014, Soda Pictures a été acquise par le groupe canadien Thunderbird Entertainment et rebaptisée Thunderbird Releasing. Le film « Shoplifters », lauréat de la Palme d’Or, demeure le plus grand succès de la société avant son virage vers la production télévisuelle. Fletcher a ensuite dirigé la création d'un pôle cinéma et télévision chez Rebellion, une entreprise de jeux vidéo et d’édition, puis cofondé avec la productrice Emma Biggins le label indépendant Beef, qui développe actuellement des projets portés par de nouveaux réalisateurs britanniques. Ancien membre du conseil d'administration de Film London, Fletcher est aujourd’hui vice-président de Film Cymru Wales. Charles S. Cohen, président et propriétaire de Curzon, a salué la connaissance approfondie de Fletcher du marché cinématographique britannique et a mis en avant la volonté de Curzon de se positionner davantage dans la production de films. Fletcher s’est dit ravi de rejoindre Curzon, évoquant son héritage unique, ses cinémas emblématiques et son pôle de distribution de premier plan, et s’est déclaré impatient de contribuer à l’expansion de l’entreprise aux côtés de Cohen Media Group.

WASHINGTON (AP) — President Joe Biden and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet Wednesday in California for talks on trade, Taiwan, and the complex U.S.-China relationship, marking their first engagement in a year. The White House had anticipated the meeting would occur alongside the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in San Francisco, with negotiations continuing up to the start of the summit, which begins Saturday.

White House press secretary Karine Jean-Pierre stated that the leaders would discuss the “continued importance of maintaining open lines of communication” and ways to “responsibly manage competition and work together where our interests align, particularly on transnational challenges that affect the international community.”

On Friday, China’s Foreign Ministry confirmed that Xi would attend APEC from Tuesday to Friday at Biden’s invitation and participate in the U.S.-China summit. Two senior Biden administration officials, who spoke anonymously due to White House protocol, said the meeting would occur in the San Francisco Bay area but did not share more details for security reasons. Thousands of protesters are expected to gather in San Francisco during the summit.

Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng completed a second day of talks in San Francisco, part of ongoing high-level engagement aimed at relieving tensions. Yellen stated she emphasized the U.S. desire for a stable economic relationship with China, called on China to address activities by private companies and financial institutions that may be evading international sanctions to do business with Russia, and raised concerns about Chinese export controls on graphite and other key minerals essential for electric vehicle batteries. Yellen also accepted an invitation to return to Beijing next year, highlighting the importance of in-person diplomacy and productive groundwork for discussions between Biden and Xi.

The Biden-Xi meeting is not expected to result in major announcements, and core differences are unlikely to be resolved. Biden aims to “manage the competition, prevent the risk of conflict, and ensure channels of communication remain open,” according to an official. It is believed to be Xi’s first visit to San Francisco since his earlier Communist Party leadership years.

The leaders' agenda includes complicated topics. Tensions have increased during the past year, with Beijing objecting to new U.S. export controls on advanced technology, the U.S. downing a Chinese balloon that entered its airspace, and China expressing anger over U.S. engagement with Taiwanese President Tsai Ing-wen. China sees Taiwan as its territory. Biden is also expected to urge Xi to use China’s influence with North Korea and Iran, specifically regarding North Korea’s missile launches and arms transfers to Russia, as well as Iran’s role in the Israel-Hamas conflict. The U.S. believes China’s economic relationship with Iran affords it significant leverage.

Biden and Xi last met nearly a year ago at the G20 summit in Bali, Indonesia, where they discussed issues including Taiwan and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Xi insisted that Taiwan is central to China’s interests and a critical issue in U.S.-China relations. The Chinese Foreign Ministry said this year’s meeting will address “in-depth communications on the strategic, overall and directional issues of China-U.S. relations and major issues concerning world peace and development.”

The timing of the meeting is significant, as Taiwan’s presidential election is set for January and the U.S. will hold its presidential election in November. The U.S. acknowledges Beijing under the “One China” policy but maintains informal ties with Taiwan, seeing Taipei as a strategic partner in the Indo-Pacific. Biden intends to reaffirm that the U.S. does not support changes to the current status quo.

Disinformation experts have warned the Senate Intelligence Committee that Beijing could try to influence U.S. elections, particularly in areas with large Chinese-American populations. The Biden administration has warned China that any election interference “would raise extremely strong concerns from our side.” The U.S. is also pushing to restore military-to-military communications, which mostly ceased after then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taiwan in 2022.

Military tensions persist, with frequent close encounters between U.S. and Chinese ships and aircraft, such as a Chinese fighter jet coming within 10 feet of a U.S. B-52 bomber over the South China Sea. General CQ Brown Jr., the top U.S. military official, reiterated the need to renew direct military lines to avoid miscalculation. Biden will also reaffirm the U.S. commitment to the Philippines after recent incidents between Chinese and Filipino vessels in contested waters.

Security preparations are tight, with meeting locations kept undisclosed. Protests on various issues, including climate change and the Israel-Hamas conflict, are expected during the summit. San Francisco Police Chief Bill Scott said the city will support peaceful demonstrations but will not tolerate violence or property damage.

Associated Press writers Janie Har and Michael Liedtke in San Francisco, Fatima Hussein in Washington, and Ken Moritsugu in Beijing contributed to this report.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Le président américain Joe Biden et le président chinois Xi Jinping doivent se rencontrer mercredi en Californie pour discuter du commerce, de Taïwan et des relations complexes entre les États-Unis et la Chine, marquant ainsi leur première rencontre en un an. La Maison Blanche prévoyait que la réunion aurait lieu en marge du sommet de la Coopération économique Asie-Pacifique (APEC) à San Francisco, les négociations s’étant poursuivies jusqu’au début du sommet, prévu samedi.

La porte-parole de la Maison Blanche, Karine Jean-Pierre, a affirmé que les deux dirigeants évoqueraient « l’importance de maintenir des canaux de communication ouverts » et les moyens de « gérer la concurrence de façon responsable et de collaborer lorsque nos intérêts se rejoignent, notamment sur des enjeux transnationaux qui touchent la communauté internationale ».

Vendredi, le ministère chinois des Affaires étrangères a confirmé que Xi participera à l’APEC de mardi à vendredi à l’invitation de Biden et prendra part au sommet bilatéral. Deux hauts responsables américains, ayant requis l’anonymat selon le protocole de la Maison Blanche, ont indiqué que la rencontre aurait lieu dans la baie de San Francisco sans donner plus de précisions pour des raisons de sécurité. Des milliers de manifestants sont attendus à San Francisco pendant le sommet.

Par ailleurs, la secrétaire américaine au Trésor Janet Yellen et le vice-Premier ministre chinois He Lifeng ont terminé une deuxième journée de discussions à San Francisco, dans le cadre d’un dialogue de haut niveau visant à diminuer les tensions. Yellen a indiqué avoir souligné le souhait américain d’une relation économique stable avec la Chine, demander à Pékin de contrôler les sociétés privées et institutions financières soupçonnées de contourner les sanctions internationales pour commercer avec la Russie, et exprimé des préoccupations au sujet des restrictions chinoises sur le graphite et d’autres minéraux clés, essentiels aux batteries de véhicules électriques. Yellen a aussi accepté une nouvelle invitation à Pékin l’an prochain, insistant sur l’importance de la diplomatie en personne et sur les bases posées pour des discussions productives entre Biden et Xi.

La rencontre Biden-Xi ne devrait pas aboutir à des annonces majeures, les différends essentiels restant à résoudre. Un responsable a déclaré que Biden souhaitait « gérer la concurrence, prévenir le risque de conflit et garantir l’ouverture de canaux de communication ». Il s’agirait de la première visite de Xi à San Francisco depuis ses débuts dans la direction du Parti communiste.

L’ordre du jour comprend des sujets sensibles. Les tensions ont augmenté cette année : Pékin a critiqué de nouveaux contrôles américains sur les exportations de technologies avancées, les États-Unis ont abattu un ballon chinois ayant survolé leur territoire, et la Chine a réagi contre la visite de la présidente taïwanaise Tsai Ing-wen. Pékin considère Taïwan comme faisant partie de son territoire. Biden devrait aussi demander à Xi d’utiliser l’influence chinoise sur la Corée du Nord et l’Iran, notamment à propos des lancements de missiles nord-coréens et de la livraison d’armes à la Russie, ainsi que du rôle de l’Iran dans le conflit Israël-Hamas. Les États-Unis estiment que les liens économiques entre la Chine et l’Iran donnent à Pékin un certain poids diplomatique.

Biden et Xi s’étaient déjà rencontrés il y a presque un an lors du sommet du G20 à Bali, en Indonésie, où ils avaient discuté de Taïwan et de la guerre menée par la Russie en Ukraine. Xi avait souligné que la question de Taïwan demeure centrale et non négociable pour la Chine. Le ministère chinois des Affaires étrangères assure que cette réunion portera sur « des communications approfondies sur les questions stratégiques, globales et d’orientation des relations sino-américaines ainsi que sur les grands enjeux de la paix et du développement international ».

La rencontre survient avant l’élection présidentielle à Taïwan en janvier et celle aux États-Unis en novembre. Selon la politique “d’une seule Chine”, Washington reconnaît Pékin, mais maintient des liens non officiels avec Taipei, considérée comme un partenaire stratégique dans l’Indo-Pacifique. Biden entend réaffirmer le refus américain de modifier le statu quo.

Des experts en désinformation ont averti la commission du renseignement du Sénat du risque d’ingérence chinoise dans les élections américaines, surtout dans les districts avec de nombreux électeurs d’origine chinoise. L’administration Biden a informé Pékin que toute ingérence « soulèverait de très vives préoccupations ». Washington cherche également à rétablir le dialogue militaire, interrompu après la visite de Nancy Pelosi à Taïwan en 2022.

Les tensions militaires persistent, avec des incidents rapprochés entre navires et avions américains et chinois. Dernièrement, un chasseur chinois est passé près d’un bombardier américain B-52 en mer de Chine méridionale. Le général CQ Brown Jr., plus haut gradé américain, a réaffirmé l’importance de relancer le dialogue militaire direct pour éviter tout malentendu. Biden entend aussi réaffirmer l’engagement américain envers les Philippines après des incidents récents entre navires chinois et philippins dans des zones disputées.

La sécurité est renforcée, le lieu de la rencontre restant inconnu. Des manifestations sur divers sujets, dont le climat et la guerre Israël-Hamas, sont attendues toute la semaine. Le chef de la police de San Francisco, Bill Scott, a précisé que la ville tolérera les protestations pacifiques mais pas la violence ou les dégradations.

Les journalistes de l’Associated Press Janie Har et Michael Liedtke à San Francisco, Fatima Hussein à Washington et Ken Moritsugu à Pékin ont contribué à ce reportage.

article_content: Sam Bankman-Fried, former CEO of cryptocurrency exchange FTX, once considered whether it would be legal to pay Donald Trump not to run for U.S. president in 2024—and even explored how much it might cost, according to author Michael Lewis. In a recent '60 Minutes' interview, Lewis, who wrote 'The Big Short' and the new book, 'Going Infinite: The Rise and Fall of a New Tycoon,' revealed that Bankman-Fried received a potential price for the unusual idea. 'He did get an answer,' Lewis said. 'The number that was being discussed when I spoke with Sam was $5 billion.' However, it remains unclear whether this number came from Trump or his associates, or if it was ever a serious proposal. Bankman-Fried was known for spending his wealth on political donations. In the 2022 midterm elections, he reportedly donated $40 million to Democrats, while also admitting to being a significant donor to Republicans. For the 2024 election, Bankman-Fried considered making a different kind of political contribution, according to '60 Minutes' correspondent Jon Wertheim. 'One of the most striking parts of the book is the revelation that Sam thought about paying Trump not to run,' Wertheim said in an interview with Lewis. Bankman-Fried also reportedly questioned whether such a payment would be legal. Responding to the claims, Trump's spokesperson Steven Cheung dismissed Bankman-Fried as a 'liar,' 'fraudster,' and someone who 'can't be trusted.' Just a few years ago, Bankman-Fried, also known as SBF, was a leading figure in the crypto industry, estimated by Forbes to be worth $26.5 billion at his peak. But his status collapsed quickly after the downfall of FTX in 2022. FTX’s bankruptcy filings revealed that Bankman-Fried’s trading firm, Alameda Research, relied heavily on FTX's own tokens as collateral. These practices contributed to investor panic when crypto prices fell. Further reports showed that FTX had lent billions of dollars in customer funds to Alameda Research. Bankman-Fried is now being held in a Brooklyn detention center, facing seven federal charges, including wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, securities fraud, and money laundering. Bankman-Fried's attorney did not respond to requests for comment over the weekend.

Pour l’élection de 2024, Bankman-Fried envisageait une contribution politique différente, selon le correspondant de « 60 Minutes » Jon Wertheim. « L’un des passages les plus marquants du livre est la révélation selon laquelle Sam avait pensé à payer Trump pour qu’il ne se présente pas », a-t-il dit lors d’un entretien avec Lewis.
