article_content: Experts recommend that everyone over 50 take a new online cognitive function test to assess their risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. Launched on the Food For The Brain website, the 20-minute assessment features 37 questions covering lifestyle, diet, and memory—including topics like coffee consumption—and includes interactive memory exercises. Developed by Professor David Smith of Oxford University, a leading UK Alzheimer’s researcher, along with the charity Food For The Brain, the test is designed for people aged 50 to 70. It serves as both a screening tool and a source of personalized health advice. In addition to offering tailored recommendations to reduce long-term risk, the test provides an annual check-up feature so users can track the effects of diet and lifestyle changes on their cognitive health. After a pilot involving 200,000 participants—with 85% scoring in the ‘healthy’ zone—and further trials at Cornell University’s Medical Centre in New York, the test is now widely available, though not accessible on smartphones. Alzheimer’s disease, the most common form of dementia, currently affects about 850,000 people in the UK. One in four people over the age of 50 is projected to develop the condition. Risk factors include limited mental activity, lack of exercise, and diets low in vegetables and essential vitamins, with high sugar and fat intake also increasing risks. Users receive a score after completing the test; lower scores indicate better cognitive health, and those at higher risk are advised to consult their doctor. Some research suggests that fish oil supplements rich in omega-3 DHA may help improve memory and potentially slow cognitive decline, especially among those under stress. Dr. Carrie Ruxton, a public health nutritionist who reviewed recent evidence for supplement manufacturer Equazen, notes that oily fish consumption is declining and underscores the importance of prevention. Food For The Brain aims to use test results to help guide a national prevention strategy. To access the test or learn more, visit www.foodforthebrain.org.
translated_content: Les experts conseillent à toutes les personnes de plus de 50 ans de passer un nouveau test cognitif en ligne afin d'évaluer leur risque de développer la maladie d’Alzheimer. Lancé sur le site Food For The Brain, ce test de 20 minutes comprend 37 questions sur le mode de vie, l’alimentation et la mémoire — y compris la consommation de café — ainsi que des exercices interactifs de mémoire. Conçu par le professeur David Smith de l’Université d’Oxford, l'un des principaux chercheurs britanniques sur Alzheimer, et l'association Food For The Brain, ce test s'adresse aux 50-70 ans. Il sert à la fois d’outil de dépistage et de plateforme de conseils santé personnalisés. En plus de recommandations adaptées pour réduire le risque à long terme, le test propose un suivi annuel qui permet aux utilisateurs de suivre l’impact de leurs changements alimentaires et de mode de vie sur leur santé cognitive. Après une phase pilote rassemblant 200 000 participants — dont 85 % se sont classés en zone « verte » (bonne santé cognitive) — et des essais complémentaires au Centre médical de l’Université Cornell à New York, le test est désormais largement accessible, sauf sur smartphone. La maladie d’Alzheimer, forme la plus courante de démence, touche aujourd’hui environ 850 000 personnes au Royaume-Uni. Une personne sur quatre de plus de 50 ans pourrait développer la maladie au cours de sa vie. Les facteurs de risque incluent un manque de stimulation mentale, d’exercice physique, une alimentation pauvre en légumes et en vitamines essentielles, et une forte consommation de sucre et de graisses aggrave aussi les risques. Le score obtenu indique l’état de santé cognitive : plus il est bas, mieux c’est. Les personnes à risque élevé sont invitées à consulter leur médecin. Certaines études suggèrent que les compléments à base d’oméga-3 DHA issus d’huile de poisson peuvent aider à améliorer la mémoire et potentiellement ralentir le déclin cognitif, surtout chez les personnes stressées. Dre Carrie Ruxton, nutritionniste en santé publique ayant examiné des études récentes pour le fabricant de compléments Equazen, souligne la baisse de consommation de poissons gras et insiste sur l’importance de la prévention. Food For The Brain espère utiliser les résultats de ce test pour bâtir une stratégie nationale de prévention. Pour faire le test ou en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur www.foodforthebrain.org.

article_content: On October 28, 2011, a suspected radical Islamist attacker opened fire outside the US embassy in Sarajevo in what authorities describe as a terrorist act. The gunman, identified as 23-year-old Serbian national Mevlid Jasarevic, was seen walking calmly with a semi-automatic weapon before shooting at civilians and police. Initial reports indicated the suspect had been killed, but police later confirmed he was wounded, arrested on the scene, and transported to the hospital for treatment. Two police officers were injured, one suffering a leg wound and the other a head injury. The US embassy was immediately locked down while police secured the area and searched for possible accomplices nearby. Further details about the investigation were not immediately released. Bakir Izetbegovic, a member of the Bosnian presidency, condemned the attack and reaffirmed the strong relationship between Bosnia and the United States, highlighting America’s historical support for Bosnia. Authorities noted that Jasarevic was reported to have links to Wahhabism, a strict form of Islam followed by a small minority in Bosnia, which has faced challenges with extremism since the wars of the 1990s. Although the country is largely moderate, navigating interfaith relations remains complex. Previously, the US embassy in Sarajevo had closed briefly in 2002 due to a threat, but this marks the first direct attack on the building.

Bakir Izetbegovic, membre de la présidence de Bosnie, a condamné l'attaque et réaffirmé la solidité des relations entre la Bosnie et les États-Unis, rappelant le soutien apporté par l'Amérique lors des périodes difficiles de l'histoire du pays. Les autorités soulignent que Jasarevic aurait des liens avec le wahhabisme, une forme stricte de l'islam pratiquée par une petite minorité en Bosnie, où l'extrémisme est un défi depuis les conflits des années 1990. Malgré une majorité modérée dans le pays, les relations interreligieuses restent délicates. article_content: British graffiti artist Banksy has opened an art exhibition in Bethlehem to highlight poverty in the West Bank and attract tourists to the city, known as the traditional birthplace of Christianity. As part of the project, Banksy has decorated the controversial security barrier surrounding Bethlehem with spray paint and plaster artworks to comment on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Israel argues that the security barrier is intended to prevent terrorist attacks from the West Bank, while Palestinian leaders view it as an illegal land acquisition, unilaterally defining the borders for a future Palestinian state. The exhibition, titled 'Santa's Ghetto Bethlehem 2007,' is a collaboration featuring artists aiming to revitalize tourism and create connections with local residents in a difficult situation. Banksy's art on the barrier extends toward Manger Square near the Church of the Nativity, believed to be the birthplace of Jesus. Notable images include a dove in a bulletproof vest, a young girl frisking a soldier, and a donkey being checked for identity papers. According to the Santa's Ghetto website, Banksy initially intended the donkey image as ironic, but locals told him that animals are often asked for ID. Santa's Ghetto usually operates in December from a small shop on Oxford Street in London, showcasing underground artists' work. Banksy started the initiative six years ago, noting: 'I felt the spirit of Christmas was fading. It was becoming less commercial and more about religion, so we opened a shop to sell things nobody really needed.' The Bethlehem exhibition maintains a satirical tone. Beyond the barrier art, Santa's Ghetto features works by various artists throughout three floors of a building in Manger Square. Highlights include a painting by Palestinian artist Suleiman Mansour showing a man carrying Jerusalem on his back, and a montage by London artist Peter Kennard, with dollar bills printed on Jerusalem Post pages. Proceeds from the exhibition go to charity. Little is known about Banksy except that he was born in Bristol, England. Original works by Banksy have fetched over $1 million and are collected by celebrities like Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt. Previous political works by Banksy include hanging a picture of a caveman pushing a shopping cart in the British Museum and placing a Guantanamo Bay detainee doll in Disneyland. The doll was removed, but the museum kept the artwork. Bethlehem’s tourism has suffered, even during peak Christmas season, due to Israeli checkpoints limiting Palestinian movement and discouraging most tourists. This has led to high unemployment. Banksy, writing on the exhibition's website, assures visitors that traveling to the West Bank is safe. 'It would help if more people saw the situation firsthand,' he claims. 'If it’s safe for a group of artists, it’s safe for anyone.'
translated_content: L'artiste britannique de street art Banksy a ouvert une exposition à Bethléem afin de mettre en lumière la pauvreté en Cisjordanie et d'attirer des touristes dans la ville, reconnue comme le lieu de naissance traditionnel du christianisme. Dans le cadre du projet, Banksy a décoré la barrière de sécurité controversée autour de Bethléem avec des œuvres de peinture en bombe et de plâtre pour commenter le conflit israélo-palestinien. Israël affirme que la barrière vise à empêcher les attaques terroristes venant de Cisjordanie, alors que les dirigeants palestiniens la considèrent comme une acquisition illégale de terres, fixant unilatéralement les frontières d'un futur État palestinien. L’exposition, intitulée « Santa’s Ghetto Bethléem 2007 », est une collaboration d’artistes souhaitant relancer le tourisme et créer des liens avec les habitants locaux dans une situation difficile. Les œuvres de Banksy sur la barrière s’étendent jusqu’à la place de la Mangeoire, près de l’église de la Nativité, considéree comme le lieu de naissance de Jésus. Parmi les images marquantes : une colombe portant un gilet pare-balles, une jeune fille fouillant un soldat et un âne contrôlé pour ses papiers d’identité. Selon le site de Santa’s Ghetto, Banksy voulait au départ que l’image de l’âne soit ironique, mais les habitants lui ont expliqué que les animaux sont vraiment contrôlés. D’habitude, Santa’s Ghetto a lieu en décembre dans une petite boutique d’Oxford Street à Londres, présentant des artistes underground. Banksy a lancé l’initiative il y a six ans, déclarant : « Je sentais que l’esprit de Noël se perdait. Il devenait de moins en moins commercial et de plus en plus axé sur la religion, alors nous avons ouvert une boutique pour vendre des choses inutiles. » L’exposition de Bethléem garde ce ton satirique. En plus des œuvres sur la barrière, Santa’s Ghetto réunit des artistes variés sur trois étages d’un bâtiment situé place de la Mangeoire. Parmi les pièces phares, un tableau signé Suleiman Mansour montrant un homme qui porte Jérusalem sur son dos, et un montage du Londonien Peter Kennard avec des billets de dollar imprimés sur des pages du Jerusalem Post. Les profits de l’exposition sont reversés à des causes caritatives. On sait peu de choses sur Banksy hormis qu’il est né à Bristol, en Angleterre. Ses œuvres originales se sont vendues à plus d’un million de dollars et sont recherchées par des célébrités telles qu’Angelina Jolie et Brad Pitt. Ses œuvres politiques antérieures incluent un tableau d’homme préhistorique avec un chariot exposé au British Museum, et une poupée de détenu de Guantanamo placée à Disneyland. La poupée a été retirée, mais l’œuvre est toujours conservée au musée. Le tourisme à Bethléem a souffert, même pendant les fêtes de Noël, en raison des points de contrôle israéliens qui limitent la circulation des Palestiniens et découragent presque tous les touristes. Résultat : un chômage élevé. Sur le site de l’exposition, Banksy affirme qu’il est sûr de venir en Cisjordanie : « Cela serait utile que plus de gens voient la situation par eux-mêmes, » déclare-t-il. « Si c’est suffisamment sûr pour un groupe d’artistes, alors c’est sûr pour tout le monde. »

article_content: Four weeks after inconclusive elections left Italy without a functioning government, President Giorgio Napolitano on Friday asked center-left leader Pier Luigi Bersani to attempt to form one. The decision followed meetings this week between political leaders and President Napolitano, who sought solutions after February’s election resulted in a three-way split between the right, the left, and Beppe Grillo’s Five Star Movement. Bersani led a leftist coalition to a small majority in the lower house of parliament but was unable to secure a majority in the Senate. Power in the Senate is divided between Bersani’s coalition and former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi’s center-right alliance, anchored by his People of Freedom party. Both Bersani and Berlusconi are rivals and have indicated they will not work together. Post-election gridlock has affected Italy’s economy. After the inconclusive election, international ratings agency Fitch downgraded Italy’s credit rating from A- to BBB+, warning of further risks if political uncertainty persists and if reforms and austerity measures stall. Italy is experiencing its longest recession in 20 years. The country, Europe’s third-largest economy, has government debt of $2.6 trillion, according to the Treasury Ministry, and the economy shrank by 0.9% in the fourth quarter of 2012, Eurobarometer reports. CNN journalists Hada Messia and Barbie Latza Nadeau contributed to this report.

Cette décision a suivi des réunions entre les dirigeants politiques et le président Napolitano, cherchant des solutions après les élections de février qui ont donné une division à trois entre la droite, la gauche et le Mouvement 5 Étoiles de Beppe Grillo. Bersani a conduit une coalition de gauche à une courte majorité à la chambre basse du parlement, mais n’a pas obtenu de majorité au Sénat. Le pouvoir au Sénat est partagé entre la coalition de Bersani et l’alliance de centre-droit dirigée par l’ex-Premier ministre Silvio Berlusconi, basée sur son parti Peuple de la liberté. Bersani et Berlusconi sont des rivaux et ont indiqué qu’ils ne coopéreraient pas. Le blocage post-électoral a affecté l’économie italienne. Après ces résultats, l’agence de notation Fitch a abaissé la note de crédit de l’Italie de A- à BBB+, en avertissant de nouveaux risques si l’incertitude politique persiste et si les réformes et mesures d’austérité stagnent. L’Italie connaît sa plus longue récession depuis 20 ans. Le pays, troisième économie d’Europe, affiche une dette publique de 2 600 milliards de dollars selon le ministère du Trésor ; l’économie a reculé de 0,9 % au quatrième trimestre 2012, rapporte Eurobaromètre. Les journalistes de CNN Hada Messia et Barbie Latza Nadeau ont contribué à ce reportage.

article_content: Western nations often claim to prioritize human rights, yet many shy away from taking real action against anti-Muslim hate, frequently citing free speech concerns as a defense. Recent incidents like this summer’s Quran burnings in countries such as Sweden reflect a troubling trend rather than isolated events. Across Europe, the US, and other regions, there has been a noticeable increase in Islamophobia, often driven by global far-right groups. As someone working with the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), I have personally witnessed the serious effects these hateful acts have on Muslim communities and broader societal trust. Some efforts are being made to combat this rise: for example, after a Quran-burning episode in Sweden attracted major protests, the UN Human Rights Council introduced a resolution urging nations to prevent and penalize religious hate that incites violence or discrimination. Passed with support from 28 nations, the resolution faced opposition from influential countries—including the US, UK, Germany, and France—that argued it conflicted with free expression principles. Much of the international media chose to focus on the free speech controversy, overshadowing the actual dangers and everyday insecurity faced by Muslims. Lawmakers, especially in democratic countries, cannot continue to ignore this issue as far-right activists continue provocative acts, like targeting mosques or destroying the Quran, under the banner of 'free speech.' The resolution does not demand restrictions on criticism of Islam but encourages governments to clearly condemn hate-driven provocations and to update laws that currently leave room for religious incitement. Legal systems already distinguish between criticism and hate speech, a fact seemingly ignored by countries that rejected the proposal. While open debate about religion is protected, speech that dehumanizes or incites violence is not. By voting against the UN resolution, countries like the US missed a chance to publicly oppose Islamophobia, but they can still act. US Congress could strengthen hate crime laws to better address religiously motivated offenses, adapt hate speech laws for the digital era, create communication channels with religious communities, and support education promoting cultural understanding. Even if the most severe incidents appear to occur abroad, anti-Muslim acts impact societies everywhere. Far-right agitation is increasing in both Europe and the US, with overlapping networks and policies shaping extremist actions on each side of the Atlantic. If Western democracies are genuine in their human rights commitments, they must move past using free speech concerns as an excuse—and act decisively to stop Islamophobic hate from spreading. It’s crucial to ensure that every person, including Muslims, can live without fear and discrimination. The author’s views are their own.
translated_content: Les pays occidentaux affirment souvent donner la priorité aux droits humains, mais nombreux sont ceux qui rechignent à agir réellement contre la haine envers les musulmans, invoquant fréquemment la liberté d’expression comme justification. Les incidents récents, notamment les autodafés du Coran en Suède cet été, s’inscrivent dans une tendance préoccupante et non dans des faits isolés. Partout en Europe, aux États-Unis et ailleurs, on observe une montée de l’islamophobie, souvent alimentée par des groupes d’extrême droite internationaux. En tant que membre du Conseil des relations américano-islamiques (CAIR), j’ai constaté personnellement les effets graves de ces actes haineux sur les communautés musulmanes et sur la confiance au sein de la société. Certaines mesures sont prises pour contrer cette vague : par exemple, après un autodafé du Coran en Suède ayant provoqué d’importantes manifestations, le Conseil des droits de l’homme de l’ONU a soumis une résolution exhortant les pays à prévenir et à sanctionner la haine religieuse incitant à la violence ou à la discrimination. Soutenue par 28 pays, cette résolution a toutefois été rejetée par des États influents — dont les États-Unis, le Royaume-Uni, l’Allemagne et la France — qui ont estimé qu’elle portait atteinte à la liberté d’expression. La couverture médiatique internationale s’est beaucoup concentrée sur la controverse autour de la liberté d’expression, reléguant au second plan les dangers concrets et l’insécurité quotidienne vécus par les musulmans. Les responsables politiques, surtout dans les démocraties, ne peuvent plus ignorer ce problème, alors que les activistes d’extrême droite poursuivent leurs provocations, comme s’attaquer à des mosquées ou profaner le Coran, sous prétexte de défendre la liberté d’expression. La résolution ne réclame pas une interdiction de toute critique de l’islam, mais invite les gouvernements à condamner fermement les provocations haineuses et à combler les lacunes légales qui permettent encore l’incitation à la haine religieuse. Les systèmes juridiques distinguent déjà entre critiques et discours de haine, une différence que semblent négliger les pays opposés à la résolution. Les débats ouverts sur la religion sont protégés, mais la parole qui déshumanise ou incite à la violence ne l’est pas. En s’opposant à la résolution des Nations Unies, des pays comme les États-Unis ont raté une occasion de s’opposer publiquement à l’islamophobie, mais il est encore temps d’agir. Le Congrès américain pourrait renforcer les lois sur les crimes haineux pour mieux inclure les motifs religieux, adapter la législation sur le discours de haine à l’ère numérique, créer des canaux de communication avec les communautés religieuses et encourager l’éducation à la diversité. Même si les actes les plus graves semblent se dérouler à l’étranger, ils ont un réel impact partout. L’agitation de l’extrême droite progresse en Europe et aux États-Unis, avec des réseaux et des politiques qui s’influencent mutuellement entre les deux rives de l’Atlantique. Si les démocraties occidentales sont vraiment attachées aux droits humains, elles doivent dépasser les excuses liées à la liberté d’expression et agir fermement pour endiguer la haine islamophobe. Il est essentiel de garantir à chacun, y compris aux musulmans, de vivre sans peur ni discrimination. Les opinions exprimées sont celles de l’auteur.

article_content: Glenn Maxwell delivered a breathtaking performance in the Cricket World Cup, powering Australia to the semifinals with an unbeaten 201 runs off just 128 balls against Afghanistan. Despite intense cramps that left him unable to run, Maxwell unleashed an onslaught of 21 fours and 10 sixes—including a final-ball six—as Australia chased down a difficult target of 292. Australia was on the ropes at 91 for 7 in reply to Afghanistan's 291 for 5 before Maxwell's heroic innings turned the match around. Legendary former captains from Pakistan, Wasim Akram and Misbah-ul-Haq, lavished praise on Maxwell, with Akram calling his knock a 'one-man show' and admiring his grit under physical duress. Pat Cummins played a steady supporting role, remaining unbeaten on 12 and ensuring Maxwell stayed on strike. Misbah also pointed out Maxwell’s sheer strength and skill with the bat. With this sensational victory, Australia secured a semifinal place alongside India and South Africa, while Afghanistan’s hopes were dashed.

article_content: Romelu Lukaku is close to completing a £28 million move from Chelsea to Everton. The striker is flying from Belgium to finalize a five-year deal with the Toffees, reportedly earning £75,000 per week. Lukaku recently posted a picture on Twitter from a jet with the caption: 'Time to write a new chapter.' The 21-year-old Belgium international spent last season on loan at Everton, where he scored 15 Premier League goals in 31 matches after joining on the transfer deadline day. There was intense transfer speculation over the summer, with Atletico Madrid and Wolfsburg also interested, but Everton manager Roberto Martinez persuaded Lukaku to stay on Merseyside. Lukaku played a vital role in Everton’s push for a Champions League spot as they finished fifth in the Premier League last season. He will be eligible to play against Chelsea on August 30, when Everton host them at Goodison Park. Speaking on talkSPORT last week, Martinez said: 'Rom fits in really well at Goodison. We created a fantastic bond with the player and the fans, and we’d love to extend that.' Everton’s coaching staff have already designed a fitness program tailored to Lukaku after his recent run to the World Cup quarter-finals with Belgium. His training kit is ready for his arrival. Lukaku’s agent, Christophe Hentoray, also represents David Henen, an 18-year-old Anderlecht forward training with Everton who could complete a move soon. Another Belgian at Everton, Kevin Mirallas, is expected to return on August 7.

India has significantly strengthened its engagement with the Nordic-Baltic Eight (NB8) in recent years, as noted by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. Speaking at the second CII India Nordic Baltic Business Conclave in New Delhi, he highlighted India’s expanding diplomatic presence, pointing to new embassies in Tallinn, Estonia (opened in December 2021), and Vilnius, Lithuania (opened in March 2023), and plans to soon establish an embassy in Latvia. Finland has also enhanced ties by opening a consulate in Mumbai.

Increased direct flights between India and Finland and between India and Denmark are improving connectivity. Jaishankar said new institutional frameworks being set up are making business-to-business partnerships with NB8 countries easier. India and Finland have created partnerships focused on sustainability, digitalization, and education.

Relations with Denmark have grown stronger through a green strategic partnership, promoting cooperation in water solutions, wind energy, green hydrogen, and agriculture. India is also working to deepen relationships with the Faroe Islands and Greenland.

India’s role in leading industrial transition, highlighted by the partnership with Sweden’s LeadIT initiative, has resulted in over 260 Swedish companies operating in India in fields like innovation, construction, defense, and clean technology. Swedish company Saab plans to open a manufacturing facility in India.

Collaboration with Iceland focuses on geothermal energy projects in Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh, with similar initiatives planned for northeastern India. India is also working on a centre of excellence for fisheries. Cooperation with Norway now spans the blue economy, renewable energy, green shipping, water management, space, and healthcare.

India maintains official contacts with the Baltic nations and is seeking further cooperation in digital technology, e-governance, cybersecurity, defense, startups, and logistics. Although progress is noted, Jaishankar added that more can be achieved. He said the business conclave demonstrates the growing awareness of mutual opportunities, signaling both a new era of globalization and India's expanding influence.

Collectively, the NB8 nations have an economy of more than USD 2 trillion and a population of around 33 million with high living standards. Jaishankar referenced the two previous India-Nordic Summits (Stockholm 2018, Copenhagen 2022), which highlighted the importance of multilateral trade and global cooperation. Key summit topics included security, innovation, economic growth, digital transformation, and climate action, and Jaishankar noted both the Nordic and Baltic regions excel in innovation and technology.

L'Inde a considérablement renforcé ses relations avec les pays nordiques et baltiques du NB8 ces dernières années, d'après le ministre des Affaires étrangères S Jaishankar. Lors du deuxième Sommet d’affaires Inde-Nordique-Baltique à New Delhi, il a mis en avant la montée en puissance de la présence diplomatique indienne, avec des ambassades ouvertes à Tallinn (Estonie) en décembre 2021 et à Vilnius (Lituanie) en mars 2023, ainsi qu’une future ambassade prévue en Lettonie. La Finlande a consolidé les liens en ouvrant un consulat à Mumbai.

L’ouverture de vols directs entre l’Inde et la Finlande, ainsi qu’entre l’Inde et le Danemark, améliore la mobilité des échanges. Jaishankar a précisé que de nouveaux cadres institutionnels facilitent les partenariats économiques avec les pays du NB8. Avec la Finlande, l’Inde a développé des accords sur le développement durable, la digitalisation et l’éducation.

La relation avec le Danemark s’est affirmée autour d’un partenariat stratégique vert, avec des coopérations dans le domaine de l’eau, de l’énergie éolienne, de l’hydrogène vert et de l’agriculture. L’Inde souhaite également renforcer ses relations avec les îles Féroé et le Groenland.

La participation de l’Inde à la transition industrielle, via l’initiative LeadIT menée avec la Suède, a permis à plus de 260 entreprises suédoises d’opérer en Inde dans l’innovation, la construction, la défense et la technologie propre. L’entreprise suédoise Saab prévoit d’implanter une usine de fabrication en Inde.

La coopération avec l’Islande porte sur des projets d’énergie géothermique au Ladakh et en Himachal Pradesh, ainsi que des projets à venir dans le nord-est de l’Inde. Un centre d’excellence pour la pêche est également en préparation. L’Inde et la Norvège coopèrent activement dans l’économie bleue, les énergies renouvelables, les études polaires, la gestion de l’eau, la navigation verte, l’espace et la santé.

L’Inde entretient des échanges officiels avec les pays baltes et cherche à intensifier la collaboration dans les technologies numériques, la cybersécurité, la défense, les startups et la logistique. Jaishankar a noté que des avancées avaient été réalisées, mais que des efforts supplémentaires sont nécessaires. Il a ajouté que ce sommet d’affaires reflète la prise de conscience croissante des opportunités communes, caractérisant à la fois une mondialisation accrue et l’influence élargie de l’Inde.

Ensemble, les pays NB8 disposent d’une économie de plus de 2 000 milliards de dollars et d’une population d’environ 33 millions d’habitants, bénéficiant d’un niveau de vie élevé. article_content: Intense fighting has erupted at Donetsk airport in eastern Ukraine, despite the ceasefire agreed upon two months ago, according to Ukrainian military sources. Spokesman Andriy Lysenko reported heavy clashes at the airport over the weekend, stating that Russian special forces have been leading assaults. 'These are Russian special forces. This is the third day they've attempted to advance,' Lysenko told Reuters by phone. In the past 24 hours, at least three Ukrainian soldiers have been killed as the battle for control of the strategic airport escalates. Photos from Donetsk show stores and residential buildings in rebel-held neighborhoods damaged by shelling, reportedly from Ukrainian forces, though no civilian casualties have been confirmed. Lysenko’s comments come as both Ukrainian officials and NATO allege that Russia has further violated the ceasefire by sending advanced weaponry to support separatist fighters. Ukrainian authorities stated that a convoy of 106 vehicles crossed into eastern Ukraine from Russia without permission, accusing Moscow of using humanitarian aid shipments to smuggle in arms and ammunition. NATO Secretary-General Jens Stoltenberg commented: 'We observe a significant military buildup in and around Ukraine, with large transfers of Russian advanced weapons, equipment, and military personnel to the separatists.' Russia has denied using convoys to supply weapons and rejects Western and Ukrainian accusations of providing direct military assistance to the rebels. The Kremlin accuses the West and the Ukrainian government of waging indiscriminate violence in the eastern regions of Luhansk and Donetsk. More than 4,300 people are believed to have died in the conflict, which began nine months ago. Despite a peace agreement signed on September 5 by Ukraine, Russia, and separatist leaders, violations and fighting continue from both sides. Lysenko reported that, along with the three soldiers killed, fifteen more Ukrainian servicemen had been injured in intensified artillery attacks, which he linked to the arrival of additional Russian aid convoys conveying ammunition for heavy weaponry to the separatists. Prolonged fighting has left many in eastern Ukraine without sufficient food and medical supplies. While Russia regularly sends shipments labeled as humanitarian aid, Ukrainian officials argue these are used to channel military equipment to the rebels. Elsewhere, in Shchastya north of Luhansk, Ukrainian forces carried out military exercises. Addressing the recent convoys, NATO’s Stoltenberg stated that improving the humanitarian situation requires respecting the ceasefire and stopping ceasefire violations. NATO foreign ministers will meet in Brussels to discuss the ongoing crisis and review the alliance’s measures to boost defenses in Eastern Europe following Russia’s annexation of Crimea in March. These steps, including troop rotations and military exercises, will continue throughout 2015.

article_content: Ann Barnes, Kent’s Police and Crime Commissioner with a salary of £85,000, is facing an expanded investigation following a car accident in Dartford two months ago. The Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) is examining whether Barnes lacked proper business use insurance while driving her Mercedes sports car. Concurrently, the IPCC is investigating allegations that a police officer was obstructed during early inquiries by Kent Police into her insurance coverage. This incident occurred on September 16, 2014, when Barnes’s Mercedes was involved in a collision with another vehicle and subsequently struck a tree while she was en route to a meeting. Barnes sustained only minor injuries and later mentioned on social media that she was not feeling well but was otherwise unharmed. Should Barnes be found to have driven without valid business insurance, she could face a £300 fine and have six points added to her license. According to the IPCC, the inquiry will also seek to determine how long, if at all, Barnes conducted official business without adequate insurance. Barnes’s office has said it will withhold comment until the conclusion of the IPCC’s investigation. Barnes’s term as PCC, which began in 2012, has been marked by repeated criticism. She received substantial backlash for appointing Paris Brown as the UK’s first youth crime commissioner, only for Brown to resign after offensive social media posts surfaced referencing behavior such as drinking and drug use. Barnes attracted further ridicule after appearing in a documentary where she struggled to define her job or explain an organizational diagram she called the ‘Crime Onion.’ The Channel Four program led to comparisons with comedic television figures and prompted public stunts and demands for her resignation. Barnes continued to defend her actions, explaining her intention with the documentary was to inform the public about the PCC role. She has refused to step down amid ongoing criticism, acknowledging that the position is complex and lacks a clear job description. Additional controversy arose when Brown’s successor was temporarily suspended during an unrelated investigation. Barnes has justified funding projects such as her ‘Ann Force One’ vehicle, highlighting the value such spending brings relative to her office’s £317 million budget.

article_content: Robin Williams stood out as a one-of-a-kind performer, leaving a lasting mark as both a comedian and actor. He began in stand-up comedy before his breakout performance on 'Mork & Mindy' made him a Hollywood icon. Blending humor and emotion effortlessly, Williams delivered unforgettable performances throughout his film career. Here are five recommended movies that reveal different facets of his talent. In 'Dead Poets Society,' Williams plays John Keating, a passionate English teacher at a boys' boarding school in Vermont. His inventive teaching inspires students to think for themselves and live extraordinary lives. 'Mrs. Doubtfire' showcases Williams as Daniel Hillard, a father coping with divorce. To remain near his children, he hilariously disguises himself as the charming nanny, Mrs. Doubtfire, growing closer to his family. Williams earned an Academy Award for his role in 'Good Will Hunting,' where he portrays Dr. Sean Maguire—a therapist guiding the brilliant but troubled Will Hunting (Matt Damon) toward self-discovery and healing. In 'Good Morning, Vietnam,' Williams shines as Adrian Cronauer, an energetic radio DJ sent to entertain U.S. troops in Vietnam. His wit and music selection win hearts, while he faces challenges from his superiors and glimpses the harsh realities around him. Lastly, 'Jumanji' stars Williams as Alan Parrish, who re-emerges after decades trapped in a magical board game. Teaming up with new friends and an old ally, they work together to finish the game and restore normalcy. These films, available on various streaming and rental platforms, highlight Robin Williams’ remarkable cinematic legacy.

article_content: A father and son from Pennsylvania have been charged with making threats toward former Alaska Governor Sarah Palin, her family, and her lawyer. Shawn Christy, 47, and Craig Christy, 22, were indicted by an Alaska grand jury on Wednesday and arrested in Pennsylvania on Thursday, according to court documents and as reported by CNN affiliate WFMZ. The men are accused of calling Palin's attorney over 400 times between August 1 and August 9, leaving voicemails filled with profanity and threats of sexual assault, death, and kidnapping. One message allegedly said, 'I'm going to ransom your children. By the time I'm done you're going to be nobody.' Both Palin and her attorney had restraining orders against the men. Court documents indicate the callers admitted in some messages they knew they were violating the restraining order. CNN's Greg Morrison contributed to this report.

In a rare public ceremony, four members of a Marine special operations team were honored for their actions during a two-day ambush in Afghanistan's Helmand Province in July 2010. Secretary of the Navy Ray Mabus presented Marine Sergeant William Soutra Jr. with the Navy Cross at Camp Pendleton, California—the Navy’s highest honor and the military’s second highest award—for his bravery in caring for the wounded while guiding his platoon to safety. Three other team members, including Navy Corpsman Patrick Quill, Major James Rose, and Staff Sergeant Frankie Shinost Jr., each received the Silver Star for their actions.

Special operations missions are often classified, and the heroism of those involved is seldom publicly recognized. During the attack, Soutra, a 27-year-old canine handler from Worcester, Massachusetts, repeatedly risked his life under fire. After the team’s assistant leader was killed by an explosive, Soutra helped direct his team and administered aid, including applying a tourniquet and pulling a wounded commando to cover. He worked for more than an hour after the initial blast, helping to move casualties to safety through intermittent gunfire. Soutra’s military dog stayed by his side throughout the ordeal but was later euthanized after being diagnosed with cancer.

The four men felt the day was bittersweet due to the loss of their element leader, Staff Sgt. Chris Antonik, whom they remembered as a close friend and outstanding warrior. Soutra expressed his commitment to living up to Antonik's legacy.

Le secrétaire de la Marine, Ray Mabus, a remis la Navy Cross au sergent William Soutra Jr. au Camp Pendleton, en Californie — la plus haute distinction de la Marine et la deuxième plus haute distinction militaire — pour son courage exceptionnel, ayant soigné les blessés tout en guidant son peloton vers la sécurité. Trois autres membres de l’équipe, dont l’infirmier de la Marine Patrick Quill, le major James Rose et le sergent-chef Frankie Shinost Jr., ont chacun reçu la Silver Star pour leurs actes.

Les missions des forces spéciales sont souvent classifiées et le courage de ceux qui y participent est rarement reconnu publiquement. Lors de l’attaque, Soutra, maître-chien de 27 ans originaire de Worcester (Massachusetts), a risqué sa vie à plusieurs reprises sous le feu ennemi. Après la mort du chef adjoint de l’équipe, tué par un engin explosif, Soutra a aidé à diriger ses coéquipiers et a apporté des soins, notamment en appliquant un garrot et en mettant un commando blessé à l’abri. Il a œuvré pendant plus d’une heure après la première explosion, aidant à évacuer les blessés sous des tirs sporadiques. Le chien militaire de Soutra est resté à ses côtés durant toute l’épreuve, mais a ensuite été euthanasié après un diagnostic de cancer.

Les quatre hommes ont ressenti ce jour comme un moment doux-amer en raison de la perte de leur chef d’élément, le sergent-chef Chris Antonik, qu’ils considéraient comme un ami proche et un guerrier exemplaire. Soutra a affirmé sa volonté de perpétuer l’héritage d’Antonik.

Gary and Samantha Humphris were thrilled when their £400,000 cash offer secured them a four-bedroom house in Sidcup, Kent. Alongside their sons, Kallum and Mason, they moved in and invested an additional £70,000 into renovations. Their excitement turned to despair six months later, learning the solicitors responsible for the sale had absconded with the funds, resulting in the property’s repossession.

The solicitors failed to transfer the purchase money to the sellers, and instead, disappeared with the Humphrises’ life savings. Mdmustazur Rahman was later convicted of fraud and money laundering and sentenced to two and a half years in jail, while two others remain under police investigation. With their money gone, the family is now staying with Samantha’s parents.

Insurance failed to cover the loss because both solicitor partners were implicated in fraud, exploiting a loophole. The Solicitors Regulation Authority has intervened by closing the firm and investigating further claims, as the City of London Police continue their probe. The family is left awaiting resolution and the hope of regaining their lost savings.

Atlanta (CNN) -- The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported Wednesday that the death toll from a listeria outbreak linked to cantaloupes has reached 29, making it the deadliest such outbreak among adults and children since the agency began tracking listeria cases in 1973. The outbreak, first identified in September, has been traced to Jensen Farms in Granada, Colorado, and has sickened 139 people across 28 states. In addition to the fatalities, the CDC confirmed that a pregnant woman who became ill suffered a miscarriage. According to CDC spokeswoman Lola Russell, the current toll surpasses the 1985 California outbreak, which resulted in 28 deaths and 20 stillbirths and miscarriages.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) stated that while the exact source of the contamination remains unclear, unsanitary conditions at the packing facility were likely a contributing factor. The FDA's inspection revealed that some equipment used to wash and dry cantaloupes was difficult to clean and sanitize, and the same machinery was used for other raw agricultural products. Additionally, the facility lacked an adequate pre-cooling step to remove field heat from the cantaloupes before cold storage—a lapse that could have led to condensation and fostered the growth of listeria bacteria.

Identifiée pour la première fois en septembre, l'épidémie a été retracée jusqu'à la ferme Jensen à Granada, dans le Colorado, et a touché 139 personnes dans 28 États. En plus des décès, les CDC ont confirmé qu'une femme enceinte tombée malade a fait une fausse couche. L'inspection de la FDA a révélé que certains équipements utilisés pour laver et sécher les cantaloups étaient difficiles à nettoyer et à désinfecter, et que les mêmes machines étaient utilisées pour d'autres produits agricoles crus. De plus, l'installation ne prévoyait pas de pré-refroidissement adéquat pour éliminer la chaleur des champs avant le stockage à froid—un manquement qui aurait pu entraîner de la condensation et favoriser la prolifération de la bactérie listeria.

article_content: Ford is acquiring the electric charging startup Auto Motive Power (AMP) as it works to strengthen its electric vehicle (EV) strategy. AMP, a California-based company, develops battery management software and charging technology, including solutions for drones and hyperloop transport systems. According to Ford, AMP will be integrated into the automaker's operations to help revamp its charging technology and reduce the cost of its EVs. A Ford representative stated, 'AMP is an energy management company with a strong reputation in battery management and power conversion systems. They have talented engineers and technology that Ford is integrating into our EV plans.' The representative added, 'Ford is focused on speeding up EV adoption and enhancing charging experiences for as many customers as possible. This move is about accelerating that goal with excellence.' The AMP acquisition was first reported by TechCrunch. This announcement follows Ford's recent decision to delay $12 billion in EV investment and pause work on several major projects, including a new battery facility in Kentucky. After reporting third quarter results, Ford executives acknowledged that demand for electric vehicles has been slower than anticipated, but emphasized the company remains committed to EVs. In a recent interview with The New York Times, Ford executive chair Bill Ford noted that most consumers are not ready to pay a significant premium for electric vehicles, indicating that prices must drop for wider adoption. Other automakers, such as GM and Mercedes-Benz, have also taken a more cautious approach to EVs, scaling back targets as demand pressures mount. GM has dropped its goal to build 100,000 EVs in the latter half of 2023, while Mercedes-Benz CFO Harald Wilhelm called the market a 'pretty brutal space,' warning of its current unsustainability. Tesla, however, continues to perform well despite predictions that increased competition would threaten its position as the leading EV manufacturer in the Western market. article_content: In a creative publicity move, Andy Shovel and Pete Sharman, owners of London's Chosen Bun burger shop, managed to send a burger and chips into near space on their third attempt. The duo completed their mission two weeks ago, after previous efforts in June and August failed due to technical issues. Using a house-sized helium balloon, GPS tracker, GoPro camera, parachute, and simple supplies, they propelled the meal 112,000 feet above Earth. The burger eventually landed about 32 miles from its launch spot, with a GoPro capturing the entire journey—including the dramatic moment the balloon burst at eight meters high. The video of the adventure quickly gained nearly 89,000 views online. Shovel and Sharman, who both studied physics, spent around £2,000 on the project, admitting their main motive was simply to have fun. A Reddit user jokingly called the space-faring meal an 'Unidentified Frying Object.' When it returned to Earth, the burger was, unsurprisingly, cold.

En utilisant un ballon à hélium géant, un traceur GPS, une caméra GoPro, un parachute et quelques accessoires de fortune, ils ont propulsé leur repas jusqu’à 34 000 mètres d’altitude. article_content: The BBC has received a formal complaint from Argentina's ambassador in London, Alicia Castro, regarding a Top Gear episode filmed in Argentina. The complaint concerns Jeremy Clarkson's behaviour and the use of a Porsche with the license plate H982 FKL, which some have suggested alluded to the 1982 Falklands conflict. The Top Gear crew, including presenters James May, Jeremy Clarkson, and Richard Hammond, was forced to leave Argentina after protests erupted over the car's registration number, which some interpreted as a reference to the Falklands War. Clarkson has stated that the similarity was coincidental and not a deliberate stunt. Executive producer Andy Wilman denied that the choice of license plate was intentional. Clarkson said he was unaware of the plate's significance until it was highlighted on social media a few days into filming. The team later agreed to change the plate before entering Ushuaia, where sensitivities about the Falklands conflict are especially high. Despite changing the plate, tensions escalated, and the crew was forced to leave Argentina for their safety after being confronted by an angry crowd. Vehicles used in filming were damaged, and some, including the Porsche, were abandoned. Ambassador Castro's complaint alleged 'provocative behaviour and offensive remarks' by Clarkson, and referred to 'false accusations' that the crew was endangered. The BBC has said it will follow its usual complaints process. The Top Gear team maintains that the Porsche was purchased in the UK and that its registration was a coincidence. Clarkson insisted that, had the connection been intentional, he would have been dismissed. The incident is the latest in a series of international controversies for Top Gear. In 2011, the BBC apologized to the Mexican ambassador following disparaging remarks made by the presenters about Mexican culture. Public debate continues regarding the intentions of the Top Gear team and the BBC's handling of the incident.

article_content: There are more than three million buses operating in cities around the world. Buses carry passengers a total of 7 trillion kilometers every year. Unlike personal cars, buses are almost always in use, frequently stopping and starting. Traditionally, they have run on diesel, contributing significantly to greenhouse gas emissions and urban air and noise pollution. Decarbonizing city buses is a top priority, but which technologies will succeed? While several alternatives exist, global trends now point clearly in favor of battery electric buses—even if some regions are slow to adopt. The main climate actions start with electrifying transportation, commercial, residential, and industrial heating. Replacing fuel engines with electric motors and batteries in buses is becoming the standard. Previously, some buses were powered by overhead electrical lines, but this approach increased infrastructure costs and created busy streetscapes. Alternatives like compressed natural gas (CNG), hydrogen, synthetic diesel, and biodiesel have been tried. However, battery electric buses are set to dominate public transit in the coming decades. A primary example is China, where over 600,000 battery electric buses are in use, compared to only a few thousand powered by other fuels. China’s diverse climate and challenging geographies—from Mount Everest to tropical regions—show that electric buses can work effectively almost anywhere. Claims that certain countries are uniquely unsuited to electric buses lack factual support. Efficiency is a major reason for this success. Electric motors provide the most efficient transportation, and batteries are the best method for storing electricity so far. While trolley buses using overhead wires are even more efficient, these systems come with higher infrastructure costs and are generally limited to high-volume city routes. Hydrogen and synthetic fuels are much less efficient, require more energy, and remain expensive, in part because the fossil fuel industry supports these fuels for their own benefit. Synthetic fuels and CNG offer little improvement, and CNG, made of methane, is a potent greenhouse gas when it leaks. Biodiesel can reduce emissions from certain wastes but is costlier than electricity and carries similar air and noise pollution problems compared to diesel. Fully battery electric buses offer the lowest emissions and are quieter and easier to fuel—just plug into electricity. Transit systems worldwide, except in a few cases, are now choosing battery electric over alternatives. For example, Nigeria has ordered 12,000 battery electric buses from China’s Yutong. When hydrogen or other alternatives are chosen, it is usually due to significant subsidies. When subsidies end, agencies switch to electric buses. As electrification continues in the transport sector, the rule of thumb is: if electricity or batteries can be used, they are more cost-effective and climate-friendly than other technologies. The trend for buses reflects this reality, and the transition is expected to continue for other transport modes like trucks, which will be explored in the next article.
translated_content: Il y a plus de trois millions d’autobus en circulation dans les villes du monde entier. Les autobus transportent des passagers pour un total de 7 000 milliards de kilomètres chaque année. Contrairement aux voitures particulières, les autobus sont presque toujours en service, s’arrêtant et redémarrant fréquemment. Traditionnellement, ils fonctionnaient au diesel, contribuant considérablement aux émissions de gaz à effet de serre et à la pollution de l’air et du bruit urbain. Décarboner les autobus urbains est une priorité, mais quelles technologies s’imposeront ? Bien que plusieurs alternatives existent, les tendances mondiales privilégient clairement les autobus électriques à batteries — même si certaines régions tardent à adopter cette solution. Les principales actions pour le climat commencent par l’électrification des transports, du secteur commercial, des logements et de l’industrie. Remplacer les moteurs à combustion par des moteurs et des batteries électriques devient la norme dans les autobus. Autrefois, certains autobus étaient alimentés par des lignes électriques aériennes, mais cette approche augmentait les coûts d’infrastructure et encombrait les rues. Des alternatives comme le gaz naturel comprimé (GNC), l’hydrogène, le diesel synthétique et le biodiesel ont également été testées. Cependant, les autobus électriques à batteries sont appelés à dominer le transport public dans les décennies à venir. La Chine, par exemple, compte plus de 600 000 autobus électriques à batteries en service, contre seulement quelques milliers pour les autres carburants. La diversité climatique et géographique de la Chine — de l’Everest aux régions tropicales — montre que les autobus électriques peuvent fonctionner efficacement presque partout. Les arguments selon lesquels certains pays seraient inadaptés aux autobus électriques ne sont pas étayés par les faits. L’efficacité est l’une des principales raisons de ce succès. Les moteurs électriques offrent le transport le plus efficace, et les batteries sont actuellement la meilleure méthode de stockage d’électricité. Même si les trolleybus à lignes aériennes sont encore plus efficaces, ils impliquent des coûts d’infrastructure élevés et se limitent en général aux itinéraires urbains très fréquentés. L’hydrogène et les carburants synthétiques sont beaucoup moins efficaces, consomment plus d’énergie et restent coûteux, en partie parce que l’industrie des combustibles fossiles soutient ces filières pour ses propres intérêts. Les carburants synthétiques et le GNC n’apportent guère d’amélioration, et le GNC, composé de méthane, est un puissant gaz à effet de serre en cas de fuite. Le biodiesel permet de réduire les émissions issues de certains déchets mais coûte plus cher que l’électricité et produit des nuisances similaires au diesel en matière de bruit et de pollution de l’air. Les autobus 100 % électriques affichent les plus faibles émissions, sont plus silencieux et plus faciles à recharger — il suffit d’utiliser l’électricité. Partout dans le monde, à de rares exceptions près, les systèmes de transport en commun optent pour des autobus électriques. Par exemple, le Nigeria a commandé 12 000 autobus électriques au fabricant chinois Yutong. Lorsque l’hydrogène ou d’autres alternatives sont choisis, c’est presque toujours grâce à d’importantes subventions. Dès que les subventions s’arrêtent, les exploitants passent aux autobus électriques. Avec l’électrification du secteur des transports, la règle d’or est la suivante : si l’électricité ou les batteries peuvent être utilisées, elles sont plus rentables et meilleures pour le climat que les autres technologies. C’est la dynamique actuelle pour les autobus, et la transition devrait toucher d’autres modes de transport comme les camions — un sujet abordé dans le prochain article.

Nathaniel Thompson, 23, Helder Gomes, 22, and Daniel Jarvis, 26, were arrested after entering the pitch on three separate occasions, leading to the suspension of the match shortly before half-time. During the incidents, some pitch invaders took selfies with players such as Kyle Naughton and Jan Vertonghen, while wearing shirts featuring the headphone brand BassBuds. One invader remained on the field for up to five minutes, with Roberto Soldado and Mousa Dembele among those trying to remove the individuals. Tottenham were charged by UEFA after the repeated disruptions, and players and officials were clearly agitated by the incidents. BassBuds released a statement on Facebook condemning the pitch invasions and distancing themselves from the acts, stating they do not condone the interruption of sporting events. Police confirmed the three men have been bailed and will appear at Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court in North London on December 18. Daniel Jarvis is also due to report to a police station in January regarding a separate investigation for handling stolen goods.

article_content:
This year’s Australian Open has confronted players with some of the most challenging conditions on record, as temperatures exceeded 40°C. The extreme heat resulted in multiple players experiencing health problems, with instances of fainting, vomiting, and relentless attempts to cool down. Fourth seed Li Na of China narrowly escaped an early defeat to Czech Lucie Safarova. On match point, Safarova struck a backhand just five centimeters long, allowing Li to turn the match in her favor and ultimately prevail in three sets (1-6, 7-6(7-2), 6-3).

In response to the difficult weather, tournament organizers put in place an extra 10-minute break between the second and third sets of women’s matches, a policy Li Na said gave her the opportunity to recover. “That break really saved me,” Li noted after advancing to a fourth-round match against Russia’s Ekaterina Makarova. She acknowledged how close she came to elimination and celebrated her perseverance.

Tournament doctor Tim Wood justified the decision not to suspend play, explaining that humans have evolved to withstand such heat, though he recognized the discomfort involved. His perspective, however, may offer little consolation to athletes such as Britain’s Jamie Murray, who needed treatment for heatstroke.

Despite the brutal conditions, world No. 1 Serena Williams extended her record for most Australian Open match wins by a woman, recording her 61st tournament victory by defeating Daniela Hantuchova 6-3, 6-3. Next, Williams faces Ana Ivanovic, who came from behind to defeat Australian Samantha Stosur and end local hopes of a home-grown champion.

In men’s singles, defending champion Novak Djokovic progressed by beating Denis Istomin of Uzbekistan (6-3, 6-3, 7-5) beneath the closed roof of Rod Laver Arena, which provided cooler temperatures and slowed play. Djokovic will next play longtime friend Fabio Fognini of Italy, emphasizing that although they have a strong friendship, competition will take priority. Spain’s David Ferrer, Czech Tomas Berdych, and South Africa’s Kevin Anderson also advanced through this demanding edition of the Australian Open.

article_content: Tata Steel plans to seek regulatory and financial backing from the Dutch government to help implement its decarbonization objectives in the Netherlands. This move follows the 2021 reorganization that resulted in Tata Steel UK and Tata Steel Netherlands operating as separate entities. The company is finalizing a detailed proposal for reducing emissions and improving health standards at its Dutch facilities, particularly at the IJmuiden plant, which produces 7 million tonnes of steel each year. CEO TV Narendran highlights that support from Dutch authorities is critical as both parties work through the project terms. Tata Steel's broader ambition is to achieve carbon-neutral steelmaking in Europe by 2050. In parallel, Tata Steel secured a £1.25 billion investment deal with the UK government to decarbonize its Port Talbot steelworks, with government investment reaching up to £500 million. The company, employing 8,000 people in the UK, continues to lead in the European steel industry. Other business news covered includes Sweden’s Saab gaining approval for full foreign direct investment in India's defense manufacturing sector, an 8% profit increase for State Bank of India, and Byju’s reporting significant revenue growth despite ongoing losses.

article_content: President Obama strongly criticized the IRS on Tuesday following a critical Inspector General report that revealed the agency improperly targeted conservative groups seeking tax-exempt status. 'The report’s findings are intolerable and inexcusable,' Obama said in a statement, as the FBI began investigating IRS practices. The White House response came after the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration's audit, which confirmed that the tax agency singled out groups based on their policy positions. However, some critics argue the report fell short by not identifying the specific IRS personnel behind the discriminatory policy, with suggestions from some that the audit fails to fully address the episode. On Monday, at a White House press conference, President Obama condemned the IRS for its alleged discrimination, emphasizing that the agency's employees had failed the American public. 'The IRS must apply the law in a fair and impartial way, and its employees must act with utmost integrity,' Obama said. 'This report shows some employees failed that test.' The President explained that he has directed Treasury Secretary Jack Lew to hold those responsible accountable, and to quickly implement the Inspector General’s recommendations to prevent future misconduct. Attorney General Eric Holder also announced a criminal investigation into the IRS's actions, saying the Justice Department and FBI would look into whether any laws were broken. Holder called the IRS’s actions 'outrageous and unacceptable.' Holder’s remarks came after news that Acting IRS Commissioner Steven T. Miller repeatedly failed to inform Congress that Tea Party groups were targeted, even after being briefed. The IRS said Miller first learned in May 2012 that certain applications from Tea Party groups were unfairly scrutinized. The audit by the Treasury Inspector General cited 'insufficient oversight' in the IRS’s review of social welfare organizations seeking tax-exempt status. Specifically, the report states organizations with conservative keywords were flagged for extra scrutiny. So-called 501(c)(4) groups in U.S. tax code operate as social welfare organizations, often engaging in advocacy. The report noted that the IRS used inappropriate and shifting criteria, resulting in inconsistent treatment of organizations from 2010 to 2012. It recommended better documentation for group selections and resolution of applications left pending for years. Republicans criticized the report for not attributing responsibility, with Senator Orin Hatch stating that senior management in Washington was aware of the situation. Other lawmakers, such as Senator Mitch McConnell and Representative Dave Camp, vowed to thoroughly investigate and seek accountability. Democratic Representative Sander Levin agreed on the need for a thorough and bipartisan investigation. Terms like 'patriot,' 'tea party,' and '9/12' were flagged by the agency under the inappropriate criteria. The '9/12' movement, launched by Glenn Beck in 2009, aimed to recall post-September 11th unity. The IRS insisted the targeting was a matter of oversight rather than political bias, a stance echoed by agency officials Joseph Grant and Steven T. Miller. Despite apologies and assurances, political pressure continues to mount from both parties. Both the Senate Finance Committee and the House Committee on Ways and Means announced investigations, with requests for extensive IRS documentation. The IRS admitted its failure to cooperate fully with the House committee over a two-year investigation. At a White House briefing, Press Secretary Jay Carney said President Obama had no prior knowledge of the IRS's practices and first learned about them from media reports. Obama called the conduct 'outrageous,' demanding accountability and stressing that the IRS must maintain neutrality and public trust in enforcing the law.

Le rapport note que l'IRS a utilisé des critères inappropriés et changeants, ce qui a entraîné un traitement incohérent des organisations entre 2010 et 2012. Le représentant démocrate Sander Levin s’est dit d’accord sur la nécessité d'une enquête complète et bipartisane. Les comités des finances du Sénat et de la Chambre des représentants ont tous deux annoncé des enquêtes et demandé des documents détaillés à l'IRS. L’IRS a reconnu ne pas avoir pleinement coopéré avec la commission de la Chambre au cours de près de deux ans d'enquête. Lors d’un point de presse à la Maison-Blanche, le porte-parole Jay Carney a assuré que le président Obama n’était pas informé à l’avance des pratiques de l’IRS et qu’il avait pris connaissance de l’affaire via les médias. article_content: If the entire world population—currently about 7.2 billion people—were gathered together and placed into the Grand Canyon, they would only occupy a tiny fraction of its massive volume. This fascinating concept was illustrated by respected YouTube presenter Michael Stevens on his Vsauce channel, who created a graphic comparing the world's population to the enormous canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona. Even if all the humans who have ever lived throughout history (estimated at 106 billion people) were assembled together, they would only be able to make about 15 small piles across the Grand Canyon, far from filling it. The Grand Canyon itself is vast, stretching 277 miles (446 kilometers) in length and reaching depths of up to a mile (1.6 kilometers) in certain areas. Data visualization blogger Eesmyal Santos-Brault contributed to the calculations, noting that with an average human weight of 154 pounds (70 kilograms), seven billion people would have a combined weight of around 490 million tonnes. Since the average volume of a human is about 0.07 cubic meters, the combined volume of all these people would be 490 million cubic meters—equivalent to a cube with sides 788 meters long. For reference, if this cube were placed next to the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai (828 meters tall), it would actually be 40 meters taller than the skyscraper. Grand Canyon National Park is a major attraction, welcoming around five million visitors each year. About 90 percent of those tourists go to the South Rim, which sits at an elevation of 7,000 feet (2,134 meters). The Skywalk is one particularly popular spot for visitors to take in the breathtaking scenery.

article_content: While many holidaymakers return from their travels with t-shirts, candy, or trinkets, some choose far more dangerous souvenirs: butterfly knives, police batons, and even stun guns disguised as flashlights. UK customs officials have seized such items at the country's borders, including at Birmingham Airport, where some of these confiscated weapons were recently put on display. Between April 1, 2010, and March 31, 2011, UK border authorities confiscated 2,477 offensive weapons from travelers at various ports. At Birmingham Airport alone, 230 weapons have been seized since June, with a significant number originating from Bulgaria and Turkey. The UK Border Agency warns that attempting to bring dangerous souvenirs into the country, even unwittingly, risks prosecution. Strict laws govern weapon possession in the UK, and travelers can face serious consequences even if there was no criminal intent. Items like butterfly knives and batons are readily available for purchase in markets across Bulgaria, Turkey, Cyprus, and the Eastern Mediterranean. According to Alex Lawther, Assistant Director for the UK Border Agency in the Midlands, many people mistakenly believe they can bring these items home as mementos. "Those caught trying to smuggle these dangerous weapons into the country, or who are unaware of the regulations in place, should be aware that these items will be found and confiscated, and they could face prosecution," said Lawther. Officials note that these weapons can end up in the wrong hands, with some being highly sophisticated and potentially deadly. Young people, sometimes without their parents' knowledge, have been found carrying such items in their luggage. "Often, these weapons are found in the suitcases of adolescents, who are surprised when customs officers discover them. Occasionally, there are disputes with parents who insist the item is simply a souvenir," Lawther added. Confiscated items are either destroyed or displayed at the UK Border Agency's 'Seized' museum in Liverpool.

La possession d’armes est strictement encadrée au Royaume-Uni, et les voyageurs risquent de lourdes conséquences, même sans intention criminelle. "Ceux qui tentent de faire entrer ces armes dangereuses, volontairement ou non, doivent savoir qu'elles seront repérées et confisquées, et qu’ils risquent des poursuites", a averti M. Lawther. Les autorités précisent que ces armes peuvent se retrouver entre de mauvaises mains, certaines étant particulièrement sophistiquées et potentiellement mortelles. Des jeunes, parfois à l’insu de leurs parents, ont déjà eu de tels objets dans leurs bagages. Il arrive aussi que des parents protestent en disant qu’il ne s’agit que d’un souvenir", poursuit M. Lawther. article_content: A Latvian man who caused a baby girl to suffer a severe brain injury after crashing a lorry into a car driven by her off-duty police officer father has been jailed for nine months. Gendrihs Kuplovs-Okinskis, 44, a warehouse worker from Southend, admitted he hadn't driven a lorry in a long time but stated his employer, Peacock Foods, directed him to drive a bread delivery truck or risk job loss. Kuplovs-Okinskis veered into oncoming traffic and collided with a Vauxhall Zafira driven by David Moon. The crash destroyed the car and left Moon’s 15-month-old daughter, Maisie, with critical head injuries that required airlifting to Addenbrooke’s Hospital in Cambridge for emergency care. Maisie, now two, is still receiving physiotherapy and speech therapy due to her injuries. David Moon suffered a broken rib, and another daughter, Ella, had cuts and bruises. At Chelmsford Crown Court, prosecutor Samantha Leigh said Kuplovs-Okinskis, who held an HGV licence, over-corrected after avoiding low-hanging branches while driving in Earls Colne, Essex. He was not speeding, and the lorry was found to have no mechanical defects. The Moon family—Nicola and David, with daughters Maisie, Ella, and Melissa—has had support from Essex Air Ambulance. Defence lawyer Shauna Ritchie said Kuplovs-Okinskis had valid HGV licences in both Latvia and the UK but hadn't driven a lorry for some time. She said he was pressed into driving with little notice and did not want to do so. Ritchie noted his dangerous driving wasn’t prolonged, persistent, or aggressive, emphasizing his deep remorse. Ritchie stated, 'No sentence can compensate the Moon family, and custody won’t help either. He admits it was his mistake and a decision he will always regret. He should have refused and accepted the personal consequences. He genuinely struggles to live with what happened.' Kuplovs-Okinskis pleaded guilty to dangerous driving, was sentenced to nine months in jail, and received a two-year driving ban. Judge John Dodd QC commented, 'No sentence I can pass can properly reflect the seriousness of the injuries. I accept your genuine remorse. Your action resulted from undue pressure from your employer.' Police have taken action against Peacock Foods in Halstead, Essex, for operating without the required licence. After the hearing, David Moon said, 'We’re glad the case has ended, allowing us to focus on Maisie’s care and future needs. She’s doing well, but some effects of her brain injury are only just starting to become apparent, as doctors had predicted.'

Six stocks are under the Futures and Options (F&O) trade ban on Thursday, November 16, 2023. These are Delta Corp, Hindustan Copper, Indiabulls Housing Finance, Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX), Steel Authority of India (SAIL), and Zee Entertainment Enterprises (ZEEL). An F&O ban occurs when the open interest (OI) in a stock exceeds 95% of the market-wide position limit (MWPL) and is only lifted when the OI falls below 80%. This restriction does not affect index traders. 

As of Wednesday, the MWPL and OI, as reported by Trendlyne, were:
- Delta Corp: MWPL at 86.3%, OI at 13.7 million (no change from the previous session)
- Hindustan Copper: MWPL at 110%, OI at 36 million (no change)
- Indiabulls Housing Finance: MWPL at 89.9%, OI at 55.7 million (no change)
- SAIL: MWPL at 87.2%, OI at 118.8 million (no change)
- MCX: MWPL at 111.2%, OI at 3.1 million (no change)

In business updates, fast-bowling cricketer Mohammed Shami is in high demand among brands, with his endorsement fees doubling to approximately ₹1 crore per deal during the ongoing ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup, following his recent on-field successes.

Il s'agit de Delta Corp, Hindustan Copper, Indiabulls Housing Finance, Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX), Steel Authority of India (SAIL) et Zee Entertainment Enterprises (ZEEL). Une valeur est placée sous interdiction F&O lorsque l'intérêt ouvert (OI) dépasse 95 % de la limite globale de position sur le marché (MWPL) et l'interdiction est levée seulement lorsque cet intérêt redescend sous 80 %. Cette restriction ne concerne pas les traders d’indices.

Selon Trendlyne, les derniers chiffres de mercredi sont :
- Delta Corp : MWPL à 86,3 %, OI à 13,7 millions (inchangé)
- Hindustan Copper : MWPL à 110 %, OI à 36 millions (inchangé)
- Indiabulls Housing Finance : MWPL à 89,9 %, OI à 55,7 millions (inchangé)
- SAIL : MWPL à 87,2 %, OI à 118,8 millions (inchangé)
- MCX : MWPL à 111,2 %, OI à 3,1 millions (inchangé)
- ZEEL : MWPL à 94,1 %, OI à 98,7 millions (inchangé)

Les principaux indices boursiers indiens ont terminé en hausse mercredi, portés par de fortes opérations d’achat dans tous les secteurs. Les meilleurs secteurs ont été l’automobile, l’informatique et l’immobilier. Le S&P BSE Sensex a augmenté de 742,06 points (1,14 %) pour clôturer à 65 675,93, tandis que le Nifty50 a progressé de 231,90 points (1,19 %) pour finir à 19 675,45. L’indice Nifty Bank a gagné 310,45 points (0,71 %) pour finir à 44 201,70.

Côté réglementation, la Banque de réserve de l'Inde (RBI) a renforcé les exigences de fonds propres pour les prêts à la consommation non garantis, obligeant les banques à allouer plus de capital et à mettre en place une surveillance au niveau du conseil afin de limiter les risques dans le secteur.

Côté business, le joueur de cricket rapide Mohammed Shami est très sollicité par les marques, ses cachets publicitaires ayant doublé pour atteindre environ 1 crore ₹ par contrat pendant la Coupe du monde masculine de cricket ICC, à la suite de ses récentes performances remarquées.

Enfin, le ministère des Mines a écrit à Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL), insistant sur le fait que toute réorganisation d’activité devra obtenir l’approbation officielle du gouvernement.

article_content: A Florida man was denied bond on Monday after being charged with murder in connection to a weekend shooting that began as a dispute over loud music and ended with the death of a teenager. According to a statement from the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, a confrontation on Friday night in a gas station parking lot escalated when at least eight shots were fired at a car occupied by a group of teenagers. Seventeen-year-old Jordan Davis was fatally wounded in the incident. Michael Dunn, 45, of Brevard County, Florida, was arrested on Saturday and charged with the fatal shooting. Authorities said Dunn told them he asked the teens to turn down the loud music coming from their vehicle, which was parked beside his while he waited for his girlfriend to return from the gas station. Dunn reported that he felt threatened by the teens' response. Dunn's attorney, Robin Lemonidis, told CNN that Dunn claimed he fired his weapon after seeing what he believed to be a gun barrel in the teens' car and hearing threats against himself and his girlfriend, along with seeing the teens motion as if opening the car door. Lemonidis argued, 'When all the evidence is examined, I believe it will be clear that Mr. Dunn acted as any responsible firearm owner would under the circumstances.' The Sheriff's Office stated that eight or nine shots were fired at the car. No firearms were found in the teens' vehicle. Lemonidis said Dunn and his girlfriend left the scene, fearing they might encounter further danger, and spent the night at a hotel. They learned of Davis's death from the news the next morning before returning home, where Dunn was arrested by local police on Saturday. Dunn was arraigned on Monday, and Lemonidis entered a not-guilty plea on his behalf. Ron Davis, Jordan Davis's father, told CNN affiliate WAWS he is seeking justice through the legal system or divine retribution, saying, 'God's going to punish him for that, so I don't want to do anything to him.'
translated_content: Un homme de Floride s'est vu refuser une libération sous caution lundi après avoir été inculpé de meurtre en lien avec une fusillade survenue le week-end lors d'une dispute à propos de musique forte, qui s'est terminée par la mort d'un adolescent. Selon un communiqué du bureau du shérif de Jacksonville, une confrontation vendredi soir sur le parking d'une station-service a dégénéré lorsque au moins huit coups de feu ont été tirés sur une voiture occupée par un groupe d'adolescents. Jordan Davis, 17 ans, a été mortellement blessé lors de l'incident. Michael Dunn, 45 ans, du comté de Brevard (Floride), a été arrêté samedi et inculpé pour cette fusillade mortelle. Les autorités indiquent que Dunn leur a dit avoir demandé aux adolescents de baisser la musique forte provenant de leur véhicule, garé à côté du sien pendant qu'il attendait que sa petite amie revienne de la station-service. Dunn a déclaré s'être senti menacé par la réaction des adolescents. L'avocate de Dunn, Robin Lemonidis, a déclaré à CNN que Dunn avait affirmé avoir tiré son arme après avoir cru voir le canon d'une arme dans la voiture des adolescents et avoir entendu des menaces à son encontre et envers sa petite amie, ainsi que vu les adolescents faire un geste comme s'ils ouvraient la portière. Lemonidis a estimé : « Lorsque toutes les preuves auront été examinées, je crois qu'il sera clair que M. Dunn a agi comme tout propriétaire d'arme responsable l'aurait fait dans de telles circonstances. » Le bureau du shérif a précisé que huit ou neuf coups de feu avaient été tirés sur la voiture. Aucune arme n'a été retrouvée dans le véhicule des adolescents. Lemonidis a indiqué que Dunn et sa petite amie avaient quitté les lieux, craignant de s'exposer à de nouveaux dangers, et avaient passé la nuit à l'hôtel. Ils ont appris la mort de Davis aux informations le lendemain matin, avant de rentrer chez eux, où Dunn a été arrêté samedi par la police locale. Dunn a été présenté à une audience lundi, et Lemonidis a plaidé non coupable pour lui. Ron Davis, le père de Jordan Davis, a déclaré à CNN, par l'intermédiaire de la chaîne affiliée WAWS, qu'il cherche la justice par le système judiciaire ou la volonté divine, affirmant : « Dieu va le punir pour cela, donc je ne veux rien lui faire. »
