article_content: Extreme events like tropical cyclones not only have immediate impacts but also long-term consequences for societies. A new study published in Nature Communications reveals that factoring in the long-term effects of these storms increases the global social cost of carbon by over 20% compared to current policy estimates. This rise is mainly driven by projected increases in tropical cyclone damages to major economies such as India, the United States, China, Taiwan, and Japan as global warming intensifies. "Intense tropical cyclones can slow a country's economic development for more than a decade, our analysis shows. With global warming, the proportion of the most severe storms is expected to increase, making it less likely for economies to fully recover before the next event," explains Hazem Krichene, lead author and scientist at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) at the time of the study. Long-term effects like reduced economic growth due to tropical cyclones can ultimately harm development more than the immediate damage from the storms. The social cost of carbon (SCC) estimates the future expense to society from emitting one additional ton of carbon dioxide. It is a key metric for policy evaluation, allowing comparison between the costs of climate change and those of mitigation. "However, extreme events' long-term impacts are not currently accounted for, so present SCC values likely represent only a fraction of actual costs. This suggests that real costs are higher and that the benefits of climate mitigation are underestimated," notes co-author Franziska Piontek from PIK. For the study, researchers examined the economic damages caused by tropical cyclones in 41 cyclone-prone countries between 1981 and 2015, then projected outcomes under future global warming scenarios. Unlike previous research, this study factored in mostly negative long-term consequences on economic development. The results suggest that these long-term impacts raise the global SCC by more than 20% (from $173 to $212 per ton CO2), and by over 40% in the analyzed cyclone-prone countries, compared to estimates currently used in policy evaluations. "Much attention is given to the immediate damages from extreme events, but it's essential to better quantify total costs to inform society about the true costs of climate change and the benefits of effective action," concludes study author Christian Otto from PIK.

Avec le réchauffement, la part des tempêtes les plus violentes devrait augmenter, ce qui rend moins probable la reprise complète des économies entre deux événements », explique Hazem Krichene, auteur principal et chercheur à l’Institut de Potsdam pour la recherche sur l’impact du climat (PIK) au moment de l’étude. Des effets à long terme comme la baisse de la croissance économique due aux cyclones tropicaux peuvent nuire au développement encore plus que les dégâts immédiats causés par les tempêtes. Le coût social du carbone (CSC) estime la dépense future pour la société de l’émission d’une tonne supplémentaire de dioxyde de carbone. C’est un indicateur clé pour l’évaluation des politiques, permettant de comparer les coûts du changement climatique à ceux de l’atténuation. « Cependant, les effets à long terme des événements extrêmes ne sont pas pris en compte actuellement, si bien que les valeurs actuelles du CSC ne reflètent probablement qu’une part des coûts réels. Cela signifie que les vrais coûts sont plus élevés et que les bénéfices de l’action climatique sont donc sous-estimés », note la co-auteure Franziska Piontek du PIK. Pour l’étude, les chercheurs ont examiné les pertes économiques causées par les cyclones tropicaux dans 41 pays exposés entre 1981 et 2015, puis ont projeté les résultats selon différents scénarios de réchauffement climatique. Contrairement aux recherches précédentes, cette étude a pris en compte les conséquences négatives à long terme sur le développement économique. Les résultats indiquent que ces impacts à long terme augmentent le CSC de plus de 20 % au niveau mondial (de 173 $US à 212 $US la tonne de CO2) et de plus de 40 % dans les pays analysés, par rapport aux estimations actuellement utilisées dans les politiques. « On se concentre beaucoup sur les dégâts immédiats causés par les événements extrêmes, mais il est essentiel de mieux quantifier les coûts globaux pour informer la société sur le véritable coût du changement climatique et les bénéfices d’une action efficace », conclut Christian Otto, auteur de l’étude du PIK.

Vera McClure is celebrating her 90th year living in the same house in Masbrough, Rotherham—a place she says she could never imagine leaving. Her family has deep roots here: her grandparents, Herbert and Eliza Lounds, were the home's first tenants when it was built in 1912, followed by her parents, Edith and Sidney Swaine, and then Vera herself.

Born at the local hospital, Vera came home as a newborn and has lived in the house ever since, maintaining her independence throughout the decades. Despite encouragement from her family to move to a more modern property, Vera insists she feels most comfortable where she is. The home, once one of the best on the street due to its separate kitchen, has evolved over time—bath nights used to take place in a zinc bath in the cellar, and a stairlift has since been installed to assist her.

After marrying taxi driver Bill McClure in 1948, Vera and Bill made the decision to continue living with her parents so she could care for them, especially after her father was injured in a work accident. When Bill died in 1991, Vera remained determined to stay and purchased the house.

“It’s what you would call a real family home,” she reflects. Her three daughters—Lindsey McLaughlin, Teresa Beecher, and Pat Webster—were all born in the house’s front room, which also served as her hairdressing shop for many years. Vera gave up hairdressing in the 1960s to restore the space for family living.

Vera enjoys her garden and the comfort of her home, now featuring a kitchen, living room, and a converted bathroom. She lives independently, cooking and caring for herself, with regular visits and support from her daughters. She is also proud to have eight grandchildren and five great-grandchildren.

“I am so comfortable here,” Vera says. “Why should I ever want to leave? I’ve had some wonderful neighbors, and the stairlift has made life easier.” Her children think it’s special that the house remains a center for family memories, with each generation continuing the tradition of caring for loved ones in the same home.

article_content: Kolkata is grappling with a severe rat infestation, with rodents damaging large parts of the city's infrastructure. Rats have been found burrowing under the foundations of at least two flyovers, damaging underground sewerage, cables, and spreading across the city—from the slums and eateries of south and central Kolkata to key colonial-era buildings like the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and the Bidhan Sabha at Esplanade. This widespread issue has caused concern among city officials. The Trinamool Congress-led KMC has launched awareness campaigns on waste disposal, implemented temporary fixes, and sought advice from other states for rat control. Mayor Firhad Hakim acknowledged to The Indian Express that while the extent of wire and cable damage is not fully known, rats are creating major problems for the city's infrastructure. KMC officials note that central Kolkata—especially areas crowded with footpath eateries—and the slum regions of Dhakuria and Bhabanipore, are among the worst affected. Two years ago, KMC discovered that the approach road to Dhakuria Bridge was sinking, later finding extensive rat burrows beneath it. Mayor Hakim highlighted improper waste disposal by roadside eateries and the presence of unauthorized squatters as contributing factors. Rats have been blamed for damaging parts of the AJC Bose flyover by loosening the soil around foundational structures. With no long-term solution identified, KMC continues to reinforce damaged structures and fill holes with a blend of concrete, sand, and glass shards, with the hope (yet unproven) of deterring rats. Deputy Mayor Atin Ghosh said KMC is also running campaigns to educate eateries against dumping food outside, warning of possible legal action. Other major cities face similar challenges. Mumbai’s Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation reportedly eliminates hundreds of thousands of rats each year as part of its monsoon campaign. New York City has implemented steps like requiring lidded trash bins, appointing a 'Rat Czar,' and establishing rat exclusion zones, resulting in a reported 25% drop in rat sightings over the past year. In Kolkata, rat sightings are frequent. Residents and local workers near Dhakuria Bridge and AJC Bose flyover regularly encounter rats and have noted ongoing infrastructure damage. Some business owners report large holes in the pavement caused by rats, which have caused injuries. Prominent buildings such as the KMC headquarters and Assembly building have also suffered. Rats have destroyed wires and machinery in critical rooms, with KMC installing ultrasonic repellent devices in response. In the Assembly building, officials avoid using poison over health concerns but are seeking alternative solutions. Experts say rat populations are hard to assess reliably. Mukesh Thakur from the Zoological Survey of India says there is scant research on the rat population in Kolkata. Professor Shilanjan Bhattacharya of West Bengal State University identifies the main species as Rattus norvegicus and Bandicota indica. Biological methods, such as encouraging the presence of natural predators like owls, monitor lizards, and jungle cats, are considered the most sustainable controls, since chemical and mechanical methods often fail in Indian environments. Professor Madhav Gadgil suggests an unconventional solution—processing rats to remove harmful pathogens and using them as poultry feed, thereby reintroducing them to the food chain.

Certains commerçants évoquent de grands trous dans les trottoirs, causés par les rats et responsables d’accidents. Des bâtiments emblématiques comme le siège de la KMC ou l’Assemblée subissent aussi des attaques. Les rats y ont abîmé fils et équipements, et la KMC a installé des dispositifs ultrasoniques. À l’Assemblée, les responsables écartent le poison pour raisons sanitaires, tout en cherchant d’autres solutions. Les spécialistes estiment difficile d’évaluer la population de rats. Le professeur Shilanjan Bhattacharya (université d’État du Bengale-Occidental) identifie Rattus norvegicus et Bandicota indica comme principales espèces. Les méthodes biologiques — encourager la présence de prédateurs naturels comme les chouettes, varans et chats sauvages — semblent les plus durables puisque les méthodes chimiques et mécaniques échouent souvent en Inde. Le professeur Madhav Gadgil propose lui de transformer les rats, après élimination des agents pathogènes, en nourriture pour volailles afin de les réintégrer dans la chaîne alimentaire.

article_content: Martin Hermann is the CEO of BrightNight and a leading clean energy entrepreneur in the U.S. and globally. The urgency to transition to clean, sustainable power sources has increased worldwide. Yet, integrating these green energy technologies into existing power infrastructure brings unique challenges that continue to grow as renewables make up a larger share of the grid. With over 30 years of experience in renewable energy and technology entrepreneurship, Hermann observes a growing synergy between technological advancements and clean energy. He believes recent breakthroughs have brought the world to a pivotal moment for a sustainable energy transition. While U.S. Congress has voiced concerns over AI’s growth in multiple industries, the transformative potential of AI in enabling a global shift to clean energy has received less attention. Hermann shares his experience with AI-powered tools specifically developed for this industry and discusses future steps to increase their impact. Forecasting Renewable Production and Demand: AI significantly improves the accuracy of forecasting renewable energy generation at specific sites, leading to improved planning for both developers and utilities. AI also enhances demand prediction by analyzing variables such as weather, holidays, and historical usage, improving decisions about energy distribution and investment. Optimizing Project Design: Creating affordable, reliable clean power—especially with hybrid systems like solar, wind, and storage—requires a tailored, systemic approach. These complex challenges can be addressed with AI-powered tools, which, in combination with human expertise, quickly evaluate millions of project scenarios to select optimal solutions for grid integration. Smart Grid Management: AI can help develop smart grids that dynamically adapt to changes in energy supply and demand using real-time and historical data. This ensures stable power delivery while reducing reliance on fossil fuels. AI can also predict and respond to grid incidents, such as extreme weather, enhancing reliability and reducing disruptions. Optimizing Energy Storage: Renewable energy’s intermittency makes effective storage crucial. AI analyzes data to determine optimal times for energy storage tasks—like balancing grid frequency or providing peak capacity—maximizing project lifespan and grid value. Predictive Maintenance with AI: Maintenance is a significant challenge for assets like wind turbines and solar panels, often located remotely. AI-driven predictive systems analyze sensor data to forecast failures or maintenance needs, allowing for proactive scheduling, reducing cost, and ensuring reliable energy delivery. Facilitating Energy Trading: AI fosters decentralized energy trading platforms, where excess energy can be sold back to the grid or traded peer-to-peer. AI algorithms optimize pricing and trade timing, making clean energy more accessible and affordable. Accelerated Research and Development: By simulating scenarios and analyzing large datasets, AI can identify technological breakthroughs in renewables faster than before. Best Practices for AI in Renewable Energy: Leaders should define objectives, ensure data quality and availability, and promote continuous learning to achieve targeted AI deployment. High-quality data and an adaptable organizational culture are vital for success. Challenges in AI for Renewable Energy: Key challenges include a shortage of expertise blending AI and energy systems, and the importance of rigorous data validation. Improving data quality and refining models with real-world outcomes is crucial. In some cases, partnering with specialized AI companies may be more effective than building in-house technology. Conclusion: Integrating AI with renewable energy promises a cleaner, brighter future. Harnessing AI’s potential can streamline decarbonization and benefit both current and future generations, despite ongoing challenges. Il estime que les récents progrès nous placent à un tournant crucial pour une transition énergétique durable. Alors que le Congrès américain s'interroge sur la croissance de l'IA dans différents secteurs, le potentiel transformateur de l'IA pour accompagner la transition mondiale vers l'énergie propre reçoit moins d'attention. Hermann partage son expérience des outils basés sur l'IA, développés spécialement pour ce secteur, et évoque des pistes pour approfondir leur impact. Prévoir la production et la demande d'énergie renouvelable : l'IA améliore considérablement la précision des prévisions de production sur des sites spécifiques, permettant une meilleure planification pour les développeurs et les fournisseurs d'énergie. L'IA affine également la prévision de la demande en analysant des variables telles que la météo, les jours fériés et les historiques de consommation, facilitant des décisions optimisées pour la distribution et l'investissement énergétique. Optimisation de la conception des projets : Concevoir une production d'énergie propre, fiable et abordable—en particulier avec des systèmes hybrides tels que le solaire, l'éolien et le stockage—nécessite une approche adaptée et globale. Ces défis complexes peuvent être relevés grâce à des outils d'IA qui, alliés à l'expertise humaine, évaluent rapidement des millions de scénarios pour sélectionner les meilleures solutions d'intégration au réseau. Gestion intelligente du réseau : L'IA permet de développer des réseaux intelligents qui s'adaptent dynamiquement aux variations de l’offre et de la demande via l'exploitation de données en temps réel et historiques. Cela garantit une alimentation stable tout en réduisant la dépendance aux énergies fossiles. L'IA anticipe et gère aussi les incidents sur le réseau, comme les événements climatiques extrêmes, améliorant ainsi la fiabilité globale. Optimiser le stockage d'énergie : L'intermittence des énergies renouvelables rend le stockage efficace indispensable. L'IA analyse les données pour déterminer les moments optimaux de stockage—par exemple l’équilibrage de la fréquence ou la gestion des pics—afin de maximiser la longévité des projets et leur valeur pour le réseau. Maintenance prédictive grâce à l'IA : La maintenance est un défi pour des équipements tels que les éoliennes ou panneaux solaires, souvent installés dans des lieux isolés. Les systèmes de maintenance prédictive à base d'IA analysent les données des capteurs pour prévoir les défaillances, permettant une planification proactive, une réduction des coûts et une fiabilité améliorée. Faciliter le négoce d'énergie : l'IA favorise l’émergence de plateformes de négoce décentralisées où les surplus peuvent être vendus au réseau ou entre particuliers. Les algorithmes optimisent les prix et le timing, rendant l'énergie propre plus accessible et abordable. R&D accélérée : En simulant de nombreux scénarios et en analysant d’importantes données, l’IA identifie des innovations technologiques dans les énergies renouvelables plus rapidement qu’auparavant. Bonnes pratiques pour l’IA dans les renouvelables : Les dirigeants doivent préciser leurs objectifs, assurer la qualité et la disponibilité des données, et promouvoir l’apprentissage continu pour un usage ciblé de l’intelligence artificielle. Des données fiables et une culture d’innovation sont essentielles. Défis de l’IA pour les renouvelables : Les principaux enjeux concernent le manque d’expertises croisant l’IA et l'énergie ainsi que la validation rigoureuse des données. Améliorer la qualité des données et ajuster les modèles aux retours du terrain est primordial. Parfois, s’associer à des spécialistes de l’IA est plus efficace qu’un développement interne. Conclusion : L’intégration de l’IA aux énergies renouvelables promet un avenir plus propre et durable. Exploiter son potentiel accélérera la décarbonation au profit des générations actuelles et futures, malgré les défis restant à surmonter. article_content: The Mauritius Supreme Court has declared unconstitutional a law that criminalized consensual same-sex acts between adult men. This decision strengthens the movement in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) toward decriminalization. Now, a slight majority—nine out of 16 member states—do not prohibit gay and lesbian sexual relations. The African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, which oversees human rights on the continent, has not yet commented on this decision. Its 77th ordinary session, starting on 20 October 2023 in Arusha, Tanzania, presents an opportunity to do so. In 2014, the Commission issued guidance to African states on eradicating violence based on sexual orientation and gender identity. Mauritius Court Ruling: The Supreme Court found that section 250 of the 1838 Mauritius Criminal Code, criminalizing anal sex between two consenting adult men, violates the 1968 Mauritian constitution. The litigant, Ah Seek, a gay Mauritian man and board member of the NGO Collectif-Arc-en-Ciel, raised multiple constitutional points, but the court focused primarily on the right not to be discriminated against. The court drew on approaches from other SADC region courts, especially a 2021 Botswana Court of Appeal decision, which interpreted 'sex' in the constitution as encompassing 'sexual orientation'. A major argument was that the Mauritius constitution did not explicitly prohibit discrimination based on 'sexual orientation.' Section 16 forbids discrimination on seven grounds, including sex. The Supreme Court concluded that 'sex' in this context includes 'sexual orientation.' The ruling emphasized the country’s international human rights obligations, noting that as a state party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, Mauritius is expected to interpret its constitution accordingly. Another issue considered was whether few prosecutions meant the court did not need to decide the matter. Referring to a South African Constitutional Court judgment, Mauritius’ Supreme Court held that the threat of arrest, prosecution, and conviction remains harmful even without frequent prosecutions. The court found that the constitution protects all individuals from discrimination based on sexual orientation. When asked to justify this discrimination, the state cited the sensitivity of same-sex relations within Mauritian society. The court rejected these justifications, emphasizing that Mauritius is a secular state. Regional Trends: Societal acceptance of homosexuality can both cause and result from decriminalization. According to a recent Afrobarometer survey, tolerance of LGBT neighbors in Mauritius has grown from 2014 to 2022. Nine of the 11 African countries with above-average LGBT tolerance are SADC members; all except Eswatini have decriminalized 'sodomy laws.' Eswatini is showing some openness to LGBT rights, with a 42% acceptance rate and recent positive Supreme Court signals. Other SADC member states retaining 'sodomy' laws include Comoros, Malawi, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe—except for Comoros, these laws are colonial legacies. The Mauritius Supreme Court noted that section 250 was a colonial import and not an expression of local democratic will. Today, just over half of SADC states do not criminalize same-sex relationships between consenting adults. The Democratic Republic of Congo never legislated on this issue. In Lesotho (2012), Seychelles (2016), Mozambique (2015), and Angola (2019), lawmakers recently adopted new penal codes omitting these offenses. In Madagascar, the penal code only criminalizes same-sex acts with people under 21. The situation remains in flux. In Malawi and Namibia, court cases are ongoing regarding similar laws. Malawi's president in 2012 promised repeal, introduced a moratorium on arrests and prosecutions (2012-2016), and authorized a constitutional review. In Namibia, the Supreme Court held in 2023 that same-sex marriages validly concluded abroad must be recognized. Diverging Trend: In the rest of Africa, sexual minorities face a more precarious situation: 31 countries (about 58%) still criminalize consensual same-sex acts, with some toughening penalties. Uganda has passed the Anti-Homosexuality Act. Ghana is considering legislation, and Kenya’s Family Protection Bill proposes a 50-year jail term for same-sex acts, though its Supreme Court has allowed the National Gay and Lesbian Rights Commission to be registered. Many of these laws are private members’ bills, not driven by government policy, and are supported by anti-LGBT conferences among African parliamentarians. African Commission Role: Against this backdrop, the African Commission’s role is critical. The commission has sent mixed messages: affirming the right to dignity and integrity of sexual and gender minorities, but denying observer status to NGOs promoting these rights.
translated_content: La Cour suprême de l’île Maurice a déclaré inconstitutionnelle une loi qui criminalisait les actes consentis entre hommes adultes de même sexe. Cette décision renforce la dynamique de décriminalisation au sein de la Communauté de développement de l’Afrique australe (SADC). Désormais, une légère majorité — neuf des seize États membres — n’interdit pas les relations sexuelles entre personnes gays ou lesbiennes. La Commission africaine des droits de l’homme et des peuples, chargée de la surveillance des droits humains dans le continent, ne s’est pas encore prononcée sur cette décision. Sa 77e session ordinaire, débutant le 20 octobre 2023 à Arusha (Tanzanie), est l’occasion de le faire. En 2014, la Commission avait déjà publié des directives aux États africains pour lutter contre la violence fondée sur l’orientation sexuelle et l’identité de genre. Décision de la cour : La Cour suprême a jugé que l’article 250 du Code pénal mauricien de 1838, qui criminalisait les rapports anaux entre deux hommes adultes consentants, violait la Constitution mauricienne de 1968. Le requérant, Ah Seek, homme gay et membre du conseil de l’ONG Collectif-Arc-en-Ciel, a invoqué plusieurs arguments constitutionnels, mais la cour s’est principalement basée sur le droit de ne pas subir de discrimination. Elle s’est appuyée sur l’approche d’autres cours régionales, notamment celle de la Cour d’appel du Botswana en 2021 qui a interprété le mot « sexe » de la constitution comme englobant « l’orientation sexuelle ». Un argument clé était que la Constitution mauricienne n’interdisait pas explicitement la discrimination fondée sur « l’orientation sexuelle ». L’article 16 interdit la discrimination pour sept motifs, dont le sexe. La Cour suprême a retenu que le terme « sexe » inclut aussi l’orientation sexuelle. Le jugement met en avant les engagements internationaux de Maurice, qui, en tant qu’État partie au Pacte international relatif aux droits civils et politiques, doit interpréter sa constitution conformément à ce traité. Une autre question abordée concernait la faible fréquence des poursuites et la nécessité d’un jugement. S’inspirant d’une décision de la Cour constitutionnelle sud-africaine, la Cour suprême mauricienne a estimé que la menace d’arrestation et de condamnation restait néfaste même sans poursuites fréquentes. La cour a conclu que la constitution protège tout individu de la discrimination fondée sur l’orientation sexuelle. Lorsqu’il lui a été demandé de justifier cette discrimination, l'État a invoqué la sensibilité du sujet dans la société mauricienne. La cour a rejeté ces arguments, rappelant que Maurice est un État laïque. Tendances régionales : Une meilleure acceptation sociale de l’homosexualité peut encourager et découler de la décriminalisation. Selon un sondage récent d’Afrobarometer, la tolérance envers les voisins LGBT à Maurice a progressé entre 2014 et 2022. Neuf des onze pays africains ayant un taux de tolérance supérieur à la moyenne à l’égard des personnes LGBT appartiennent à la SADC ; tous sauf l’Eswatini ont supprimé les lois sur la « sodomie ». L’Eswatini montre une certaine ouverture avec un taux d’acceptation de 42% et des signaux encourageants de sa Cour suprême. D’autres membres de la SADC maintiennent encore des lois sur la « sodomie » : Comores, Malawi, Namibie, Tanzanie, Zambie et Zimbabwe — à l’exception des Comores, ces lois sont héritées de la colonisation britannique. La Cour suprême de Maurice rappelle que l’article 250 était une importation coloniale et non l’expression de la volonté démocratique locale. Aujourd’hui, un peu plus de la moitié des États de la SADC ne pénalisent plus les relations homosexuelles consenties entre adultes. La République démocratique du Congo n’a jamais légiféré sur cette question. Au Lesotho (2012), aux Seychelles (2016), au Mozambique (2015) et en Angola (2019), de nouveaux codes pénaux ont été adoptés sans intégrer de telles infractions. À Madagascar, le code pénal ne sanctionne ces actes qu’avec une personne de moins de 21 ans. La situation évolue encore. Au Malawi et en Namibie, des recours judiciaires sont en cours contre ces lois. En 2012, la présidente du Malawi avait promis leur abrogation, instauré un moratoire sur les arrestations (2012–2016) et lancé une révision constitutionnelle. En 2023, la Cour suprême de Namibie a exigé la reconnaissance des mariages de même sexe contractés à l’étranger. Tendance divergente : Ailleurs en Afrique, les minorités sexuelles vivent une situation bien plus fragile : 31 pays (près de 58 %) criminalisent toujours les actes consentis entre adultes de même sexe, et certains durcissent les sanctions. L’Ouganda a adopté une loi anti-homosexualité. Le Ghana examine un projet de loi similaire, tandis qu’au Kenya, la Family Protection Bill propose 50 ans de prison, même si la Cour suprême a autorisé l’enregistrement de la National Gay and Lesbian Rights Commission. Beaucoup de ces lois sont des initiatives privées, soutenues par des réunions de parlementaires africains opposés aux droits LGBT. Rôle de la Commission africaine : Dans ce contexte, la Commission africaine joue un rôle crucial. Mais elle reste ambivalente : elle réaffirme le droit à la dignité et à l’intégrité des minorités sexuelles et de genre, tout en refusant le statut d’observateur aux ONG qui défendent ces droits.

article_content: When Bobbi Brown debuted her own lipstick collection at Bergdorf Goodman in 1991, she was taken aback when all ten natural shades sold out immediately. Since then, she’s transformed her passion into a billion-dollar enterprise promoting natural beauty and self-confidence. Her cosmetics have been chosen by stars like Michelle Obama, Katie Holmes, and even the Duchess of Cambridge on her wedding day. The company has expanded from a modest mail-order operation to an international presence in 68 countries, redefining makeup essentials for people everywhere. Brown set out to design lipsticks that complemented natural lip tones—unlike many of the synthetic, heavily scented options then available. She credits her mother’s beauty rituals and her grandfather’s entrepreneurship for inspiring her early on, even as school was not her focus. With a degree in theatrical makeup, Brown moved to New York and relentlessly pursued her dream. Her big break came with a Vogue cover shoot featuring Naomi Campbell. Unimpressed by the overly bold makeup of the 1980s, she worked with a Kiehl’s pharmacist to develop a subtle, wearable lipstick—Brown Lip Color. Within just four years, her brand outperformed established names like Estee Lauder in department stores, leading to a company acquisition by Leonard Lauder. She accepted the offer on the condition that she maintained creative authority. Today, her products are estimated to represent about a tenth of Estee Lauder’s cosmetic sales. Brown believes women will always prioritize their tried-and-true beauty basics, regardless of trends or economic hardships. She acknowledges industry critiques but stresses that her aim—and that of many professionals—is to boost women’s confidence, not impose unrealistic ideals. Her activities reach beyond makeup, with ventures in eyewear design through a collaboration with Safilo and a leadership role at Yahoo’s beauty division. Brown also champions causes like the Pretty Powerful Campaign for Women and Girls, which donates all proceeds from special products to support disadvantaged females, and Dress for Success, supplying career resources and attire for women in need. At her New York SoHo headquarters, Brown fosters an upbeat and inclusive atmosphere reflective of her personality. Despite decades of achievement, she jokes about her lack of skills in sports and maintains that she’s always striving for more, never settling on past accomplishments. From her early makeup forays at shopping malls to leading a global brand, Bobbi Brown’s inspiring journey continues.

Ses cosmétiques ont séduit de grandes personnalités comme Michelle Obama, Katie Holmes, et même la Duchesse de Cambridge lors de son mariage. L’entreprise est passée d’un modeste service de vente par correspondance à une marque présente dans 68 pays, redéfinissant les essentiels du maquillage à l’échelle mondiale. Brown voulait des rouges à lèvres qui s’accordent avec les couleurs naturelles, contrairement aux produits artificiels et trop parfumés très répandus à l’époque. Elle doit son inspiration à sa mère et à son grand-père entrepreneur, bien que l’école ne l’ait jamais passionnée. Après un diplôme en maquillage artistique, Brown s’installe à New York et poursuit son rêve avec détermination. Son premier gros succès : une couverture de Vogue avec Naomi Campbell. Lassée des maquillages criards des années 80, elle crée avec un pharmacien de Kiehl’s un rouge à lèvres discret et facile à porter : le Brown Lip Color. En à peine quatre ans, sa marque dépassait des géants comme Estée Lauder dans les grands magasins, entraînant un rachat par Leonard Lauder. Brown a accepté, à condition de garder le contrôle créatif. Ses projets dépassent le maquillage, avec une ligne de lunettes conçue avec Safilo et un poste de responsable éditoriale chez Yahoo Beauté. De ses débuts à expérimenter le maquillage dans les centres commerciaux à la tête d’une marque mondiale, le parcours de Bobbi Brown reste inspirant.

article_content: Becci Woodward, aged 28 and living in Marks Tey, Essex, gave birth to her son Noah on her kitchen floor after unexpectedly going into labor. Noah weighed 10 pounds 7 ounces, making him about 3 pounds heavier than the average newborn. With no time to reach the hospital, Becci’s partner, Aaron Allport, and her mother, Christine, delivered Noah themselves before medical professionals could get there. Becci had intended to have her baby at Colchester General Hospital, but strong contractions started at 5 a.m. She called her parents for help, and as she was preparing to leave for the hospital, her water suddenly broke. Guided over the phone by a 999 operator, Aaron and Christine took charge of the delivery, welcoming Noah at 5:52 a.m. Ambulances and a midwife arrived quickly and confirmed both mother and baby were healthy. Aaron praised how everyone responded to the situation, and the family expressed joy over their unexpected home birth. Their older daughter, Isla, slept through the event and was a bit confused when she first met her brother. Noah is one of several large babies born recently in the UK. In Gloucestershire, George King was delivered naturally in February 2013 at 15 pounds 7 ounces—almost double the average baby’s weight. By six weeks, George wore clothing sized for a six-month-old. In August, in Sheffield, Eva Lily Margerrison was born weighing 12 pounds 6 ounces via emergency Caesarean, and her parents, Danica Slaving and Sam Margerrison, nicknamed her the 'Whopper.'

Arsene Wenger remains confident that his squad is ready to challenge for the Premier League title and believes Arsenal will reclaim the championship within three years. Despite being 13 points behind league leaders Chelsea and experiencing a lackluster start to the season—including only five league victories and an early departure from the Capital One Cup at the hands of Southampton—Wenger is optimistic about a turnaround.

Ahead of Arsenal's match against Southampton, Wenger, who has faced criticism from sections of the club’s supporters, insists his team can improve their fortunes. Key players such as Lukas Podolski and Alexis Sanchez have been active in training, with Laurent Koscielny, Aaron Ramsey, and Danny Welbeck among others preparing for the upcoming fixture. Welbeck recently scored against West Brom, highlighting his form.

When asked if he can secure a fourth league title before his contract expires in 2017, Wenger replied confidently: 'Of course. We've had a difficult start, but the squad has not been fully together since the season began, which is typical after a World Cup year. I believe we have what it takes, and now we must fight relentlessly to prove we can compete in every match.'

Arsenal last lifted the Premier League trophy ten years ago, but celebrated their first silverware since 2005 by winning the FA Cup last season. While Chelsea are considered the favorites for this season's title, Wenger maintains that the title race is far from decided: 'We have often been in contention. People always remember the winners, but the competition has been fierce in recent years. The Premier League is increasingly competitive, and Chelsea started very strongly. They’ll be tough to catch, but everyone will continue to challenge them. After 13 or 14 games, it’s too early to say the title race is over.'

For the fixture against Southampton at Emirates Stadium, Arsenal faces injury concerns over Nacho Monreal and Kieran Gibbs, possibly requiring Mathieu Flamini to play in defense. Nineteen-year-old Hector Bellerin is also on standby.

Widely celebrated as one of the world’s natural wonders, the Grand Canyon regularly draws visitors from around the globe who come to admire its vast panorama—usually stretching for miles across the 18-mile-wide chasm carved by the Colorado River over millions of years. However, this week, an uncommon weather event dramatically changed the scene. A thick fog, resulting from a rare phenomenon called a 'total temperature inversion,' rose from the canyon floor, nearly reaching the rim and rendering the canyon as if it floated above the clouds.

Thousands of guests, including photographers and hikers, gathered to witness and capture the stunning—if unusual—view. The spectacle, usually reserved for those flying above or atop the world’s highest mountains, happens at the Grand Canyon only every few years. This occurrence was triggered by recent rainfall in northern Arizona. In a total temperature inversion, warm air at the canyon’s top traps cooler, damp air below, preventing the two from mixing. As the colder air cools further, moisture left by the recent rains turns into dense fog. The warm air band acts as a lid, keeping the fog from rising away, and the effect persists until temperatures equalize, sometimes over several days.

Tourists hoping to glimpse the Colorado River below sometimes felt let down by the low visibility, but rangers, such as Erin Whittaker, explained the rarity and beauty of the event. Locals quickly spread the word, with many rushing to the rim to take photographs of the cloud-shrouded gorge. According to the National Weather Service, the lingering fog will likely clear as warmer conditions return this weekend.

Temperature inversions similar to this can also occur in cities, where trapped cold air leads to smog and health concerns. But in the Grand Canyon, the event transformed the iconic site, offering a breathtaking view not often seen.

article_content: A UK-based study found that formal childcare supported young children's vocabulary and communication skills during the first pandemic year, despite widespread lockdowns. The research recorded that children who attended childcare could speak an average of 29 additional words per day and understand 16 more, compared to those who stayed home. Notably, children from lower-income families benefited with gains in communication and problem-solving ability. Though many childcare centers faced closures or disruptions during the pandemic, the study's results suggest that early years education continued to have a strong positive impact, particularly in narrowing developmental disparities and reducing socioeconomic inequalities. Dr Catherine Davies, a language development expert at the University of Leeds and co-author, stressed the importance of expanding early childhood education access, especially for those who need it most. Researchers monitored over 600 children aged eight to 36 months across England, Scotland, and Wales, collecting data via parent questionnaires throughout three national lockdowns in 2020 and 2021. Parents reported on areas such as vocabulary, cognition, attention, behavior, and emotion for the paper, published in the Journal of Early Childhood Research. The team advocates for expanded access to formal childcare to address developmental setbacks associated with pandemic lockdowns—particularly for disadvantaged children—and to better prepare children for school. Dr Nayeli Gonzalez-Gomes, principal investigator and psychology reader at Oxford Brookes University, noted formal childcare also enhanced children’s personal and social competencies despite the challenges of the pandemic. The research underscores the need for greater promotion of and accessibility to formal childcare, stressing both its educational and care aspects, and recommends increased financial support for additional childcare spaces, especially for low-income families. Kathryn Ingold, a public health consultant at Leeds City Council, stated that local findings also indicated the pandemic had a notable impact on children's language abilities. Earlier in the year, the UK government revealed plans to broaden free childcare availability to all children from nine months old to assist working parents. Yet, some observers argue the policy may bring limited benefits, warning that proposed higher child-to-adult ratios could affect care quality.

article_content: Local councils and various public bodies in the UK have spent almost £4 million over two years to employ private investigators for covert surveillance operations. This includes monitoring members of the public as well as their own staff. A notable example is Anthea Orchard, a 999 call centre worker from Halifax, who was placed under investigation by West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Services. She was suspected of taking on additional work while on sick leave. Private investigators hired by the authority used a GPS tracker on her car and made fake calls offering her work, attempting to prompt a confession. Mrs. Orchard uncovered the operation by tracing the source of the calls and was also alerted by neighbors who noticed suspicious activity. She maintains she did not work illicitly while on sick leave. After agreeing not to pursue legal action for what she called 'unnecessary surveillance' and invasion of privacy, Mrs. Orchard received an £11,000 settlement and left her job. The case has raised significant concerns about the extent of state-funded surveillance and the need for regulation of private investigators. Keith Vaz, chairman of the Home Affairs Select Committee, voiced concerns over the growing use of private investigators by councils and other organizations. Nick Pickles, director of the privacy group Big Brother Watch, criticized the amount of public funds spent and the invasive tactics used against staff. Freedom of Information requests by Big Brother Watch found that 37 councils, several quangos, and the Department for Transport spent nearly £3.9 million on private investigators for cases involving fraud, misconduct, and other investigations. Other public bodies used private investigators for issues such as driving test fraud, insurance fraud, debt collection, fisheries surveillance, and internal disciplinary matters. Laws coming into effect next year will require private investigators to obtain licenses. Operating without a license will be a criminal offense, with penalties of up to six months in jail or a £5,000 fine. The use of GPS tracking and covert surveillance by private investigators remains a grey area legally, particularly in cases involving investigation of employees. While RIPA regulates certain public body surveillance, employment investigations typically fall under the Data Protection Act, which stipulates the need for necessity and proportionality. Mrs. Orchard described the surveillance as a serious violation of her privacy and said the experience harmed her health and family life. She is now self-employed, working full-time on her own business.

article_content: After more than 100 days on strike, SAG-AFTRA is preparing a counteroffer in response to a proposal from four major Hollywood CEOs, who met with union leaders on Tuesday. These CEOs, speaking on behalf of the Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers (AMPTP), sought to convey to SAG-AFTRA the significant economic consequences of the ongoing stalemate, according to Variety. Among their concerns were canceled television series and the need to overhaul the entire scripted TV schedule for 2024. While the CEOs intended to present the financial realities of the strike, SAG-AFTRA perceived their message as a threat. Negotiations reached an impasse over the union’s demand for a streaming royalty of 57 cents per subscription—an amount projected to total around $500 million annually. The studios rejected this request, calling it 'untenable,' and instead proposed a bonus system similar to the recent Writers Guild of America (WGA) agreement. Under this model, bonuses would go to successful shows or films viewed by at least 20% of a platform’s subscribers within the first 90 days of release—estimated to cost approximately $20 million per year, according to Variety. The report also notes that the AMPTP has often shared details of negotiations with the press through anonymous sources, a strategy that backfired in previous dealings with the WGA and has drawn criticism from SAG-AFTRA. article_content: With the 2024 U.S. presidential election a year away, it looks like Joe Biden and Donald Trump will once again face off—this time with Trump as the challenger. Many Americans are frustrated about having a repeat contest, and polls currently point to a close competition. However, history shows that even predictable elections can take unexpected turns. For example, the Iran hostage crisis shifted Jimmy Carter’s fortunes in 1979, and the pandemic reshaped 2020. Four potential surprises could change the race. Third-party candidates have played spoiler roles in the past, and 2024 could see this dynamic again. Ross Perot claimed nearly a fifth of the vote in 1992, affecting Republican chances. Ralph Nader’s vote share in Florida in 2000 has been credited with influencing the state's outcome, while Jill Stein was accused of hurting Hillary Clinton in 2016. This year, two high-profile independents—Cornel West and Robert F Kennedy Jr (who left the Democrats in 2023)—are running. Kennedy previously enjoyed notable Democratic support and may also draw votes from disaffected conservatives. Given the close contest, even a small third-party presence could be pivotal. Another important factor is age. Biden will be 82 and Trump 78 at inauguration in 2025. Both appear healthy now, but sudden health events could disrupt the election. If a major candidate becomes seriously ill or dies before the new year, their party can select another nominee. If tragedy strikes close to election day, however, their names would stay on the ballot—a rare but not unprecedented situation, as with Mel Carnahan’s posthumous Senate victory in 2000. Should a winning candidate die after the election but before inauguration, the vice president-elect would be sworn in and need to nominate a new VP, subject to congressional approval. Such scenarios highlight the unpredictability of the process and reinforce hopes that both Biden and Trump remain well. International issues also cast a shadow over the campaign. President Biden’s administration is defined by crises including Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the Israel-Hamas conflict, and increasing friction between China and Taiwan. The Biden team highlights his global leadership, and polling shows decent approval on these points. Nevertheless, some younger Democrats oppose his strong support for Israel amid rising Palestinian casualties. Rapid escalation in any of these conflicts—such as NATO being drawn in or Iranian-backed groups intensifying violence—could upend campaign strategies and voter sentiment. It remains unclear if international turmoil would harm Biden or benefit Trump, as voter attitudes toward U.S. involvement overseas evolve. Much depends on events out of any candidate’s control. Finally, Donald Trump faces 91 felony charges across four criminal cases, which may proceed during the campaign. His lawyers have tried to push cases past the election, recognizing that a president is largely shielded from prosecution except via impeachment. Being convicted does not prevent him from running or winning—historical precedents exist. In a highly unusual scenario, Trump could potentially become president while incarcerated. While a president could theoretically pardon themselves for federal crimes, state convictions are out of presidential reach, making for extraordinary legal and political situations. The country is heading into uncharted territory as these unprecedented events unfold.

Quatre grandes surprises pourraient encore influencer l’issue du scrutin. Les candidats indépendants ont déjà compliqué la donne, et 2024 ne fera peut-être pas exception. article_content: Millions of Iranians went to the polls on Friday during Iran's presidential election, while Iranian-Americans in the U.S. also turned out in record numbers to vote. Many say they feel passionate about participating, even from afar. 'I am passionate about voting because of my bloodline,' said Shahdad Kelishadi, 26, of Los Angeles. 'Even though I am not in Iran, my heart never left Iran. It is my duty to help Iranians if it means bringing positive results.' Across the U.S., from New York to California, there are 41 official voting sites in cities for Iranian citizens to cast absentee ballots and take part in the process. To vote, Iranian citizens living in the U.S., including dual citizens, must be over 18 and have a valid Iranian passport. Young people inside and outside Iran have played a major role in encouraging participation and starting conversations about the election. 'For most of us, part of our identity is back in Iran. We want to know we've made a difference,' said Kiana Karimi, a design student in San Francisco. Young Iranian-Americans are using social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube to build momentum, as well as grassroots efforts in their communities. 'We’re reaching people who want to help Iran—emails, phone calls, word of mouth—to encourage voting,' said Kelishadi, who publishes the magazine 'Coexistence.' Born in Los Angeles, Kelishadi, like many Iranian-Americans, hopes a new president will bring a better international perspective on Iran and its people. Ehsan Zahedani, 27, UCLA student and president of Iranian Future Leaders, said, 'It’s time to participate and be active in a government that makes decisions affecting my life and image.' Events like the 1979 Islamic Revolution still impact many Iranian-Americans both personally and culturally. Over thirty years later, the community still finds itself at a crossroads, trying to honor their heritage while also shaping their identity. Dr. Trita Parsi of the North American Iranian Council said that after the hostage crisis, many Iranian-Americans kept a low profile. Historically successful in business and academia, the community has tended to avoid U.S. politics, but after 9/11, many began to see civic engagement as important. The trend towards political participation has been growing. According to census data, about 1 million Iranian-Americans live in the U.S., with the largest group—about 72,000—in Los Angeles. Other hubs include New York, New Jersey, D.C., Seattle, and Houston. Dr. Hamid Dabashi of Columbia University noted that regardless of which candidate wins, the new wave of political dialogue among Iranians is significant. Should Ahmadinejad remain president, he won’t be able to ignore the turnout and public input. Many Iranian-Americans are hopeful that relations with the U.S. may improve under President Obama. 'There has been a change in tone from the American government, and I think Iran recognizes this. With Obama, there could be great progress,' said UCLA graduate Pouneh Behin. Not everyone shares the same enthusiasm. Dr. Ali Nayeri, a physics professor at UC Irvine, respects those who vote but chooses not to. He believes that none of the four candidates can make the real changes Iran needs, and that most authority remains with the supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. According to Nayeri, the Iranian president holds only about 20-25% of the country’s political power. Some Iranian-Americans worry that the Iran they remember may now only exist in memory. Dr. Mitra Sioshansi, a retired engineer, is still optimistic that increased participation by women in Iranian politics will lead to change. Whether or not they vote, Iranian-Americans are watching closely to see what direction Iran takes after the election. 'Whatever our political views, we have to recognize the grassroots nature of this democratic movement and celebrate coming from a country capable of reaching for democratic ideals,' Dabashi said.

Beaucoup disent être passionnés par leur participation, même à distance. « Je suis passionné par le vote à cause de mes origines », explique Shahdad Kelishadi, 26 ans, de Los Angeles. « Même si je ne suis pas en Iran, mon cœur ne l’a jamais quittée. C’est mon devoir d’aider les Iraniens si cela peut avoir des résultats positifs. » À travers les États-Unis, de New York à la Californie, il existe 41 bureaux de vote officiels pour que les citoyens iraniens déposent leur bulletin par procuration et participent au processus. Pour voter, les citoyens iraniens résidant aux États-Unis, y compris les binationaux, doivent avoir plus de 18 ans et un passeport iranien valide. Les jeunes, en Iran et à l’étranger, jouent un rôle majeur pour encourager la participation et lancer des discussions autour de l’élection. « Pour la plupart d’entre nous, une partie de notre identité est en Iran. Nous voulons savoir que nous avons eu un impact », confie Kiana Karimi, étudiante en design à San Francisco. Les jeunes Irano-Américains utilisent des réseaux sociaux comme Facebook, Twitter et YouTube pour mobiliser, mais aussi des efforts de proximité au sein de leurs communautés. « Nous contactons ceux qui veulent aider l’Iran — emails, appels, bouche à oreille — pour les encourager à voter », dit Kelishadi, qui publie le magazine « Coexistence ». Né à Los Angeles, Kelishadi, comme beaucoup d’Irano-Américains, espère qu’un nouveau président offrira une meilleure perspective internationale sur l’Iran et son peuple. Ehsan Zahedani, 27 ans, étudiant à l’UCLA et président d’Iranian Future Leaders, affirme : « Il est temps d’être actif dans un gouvernement qui prend des décisions affectant ma vie et mon image. » Des événements comme la révolution islamique de 1979 marquent encore de nombreux Irano-Américains aussi bien personnellement que culturellement. Plus de trente ans plus tard, la communauté reste à un carrefour, cherchant à honorer son héritage tout en forgeant une nouvelle identité. Le Dr Trita Parsi, du North American Iranian Council, explique qu’après la crise des otages, beaucoup d’Irano-Américains sont devenus très discrets. Historiquement réussie dans les affaires et le monde académique, la communauté participait peu à la politique américaine. Mais après le 11 septembre, l’engagement citoyen est devenu plus important, et le mouvement s’accélère. D’après les données du recensement, environ un million d’Irano-Américains vivent aux États-Unis, la plus grande communauté (environ 72 000) se trouvant à Los Angeles. D’autres pôles incluent New York, New Jersey, Washington D.C., Seattle et Houston. Le Dr Hamid Dabashi, de l’Université Columbia, note qu’indépendamment du candidat vainqueur, la nouvelle vague de dialogue politique parmi les Iraniens est significative. Si Ahmadinejad reste président, il ne pourra ignorer la foule mobilisée et les voix exprimées. Beaucoup d’Irano-Américains espèrent une amélioration des relations avec les États-Unis sous le président Obama. « Il y a eu un changement de ton du gouvernement américain, et je pense que l’Iran le reconnaît. Avec Obama, de grands progrès sont possibles », déclare Pouneh Behin, diplômée de l’UCLA. Mais tout le monde ne partage pas le même enthousiasme. Le Dr Ali Nayeri, professeur de physique à UC Irvine, respecte ceux qui votent mais choisit de s’abstenir. Il estime qu’aucun des quatre candidats ne peut apporter le vrai changement dont l’Iran a besoin, la majorité du pouvoir restant entre les mains du guide suprême, l’ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Selon Nayeri, le président iranien ne détient qu’environ 20 à 25 % du pouvoir politique. Certains Irano-Américains craignent que l’Iran de leurs souvenirs n’existe plus vraiment. La Dre Mitra Sioshansi, ingénieure à la retraite, reste pourtant optimiste que la participation croissante des femmes en politique entraînera un changement. Qu’ils choisissent de voter ou non, les Irano-Américains observent de près la direction que prendra l’Iran après les élections. « Quelles que soient nos opinions politiques, nous devons reconnaître la dimension populaire de ce mouvement démocratique et être fiers de venir d’un pays capable d’aspirer à des idéaux démocratiques », conclut Dabashi.

Levi Strauss & Co. CEO Chip Bergh recently advised at the Fortune Brainstorm Green conference that it's best never to wash your jeans. Instead, he suggests putting them in the freezer from time to time or cleaning up spots with a toothbrush or sponge. Bergh says he hasn't washed his own jeans in over a year, believing this approach helps jeans last longer and saves water.

While some people are uneasy about germs on unwashed jeans, Bergh thinks freezing can take care of odors and bacteria. This trend has even gotten online attention with how-to videos and blogs. Still, many question if freezing really deals with all the grime and germs that build up, especially once jeans are back at body temperature.

Stephen Craig Cary, a microbiology specialist at the University of Delaware, explains that most bacteria survive cold temperatures, so freezing won't get rid of them. He states that washing jeans is the simplest and most energy-efficient way to ensure cleanliness.

Some critics see Bergh’s approach as more of a marketing move aimed at fashion-conscious customers, rather than those who wear jeans for physical labor. For people working in tough conditions, clean jeans are a must.

Scientific evidence shows that although freezing can reduce some smell, it doesn’t truly sanitize jeans. Regular washing remains the best way to keep them clean and healthy.

Le PDG de Levi Strauss & Co., Chip Bergh, a déclaré lors de la conférence Fortune Brainstorm Green qu’il est préférable de ne jamais laver ses jeans. Il préconise plutôt de les placer au congélateur de temps à autre ou de nettoyer les taches à l’aide d’une brosse à dents ou d’une éponge. Selon Bergh, il n’a pas lavé son propre jean depuis plus d’un an, pensant ainsi prolonger leur durée de vie et économiser de l’eau.

Si certains s’inquiètent de l’accumulation de germes sur des jeans non lavés, Bergh est convaincu que le congélateur peut neutraliser les odeurs et les bactéries. Cette méthode a d’ailleurs pris de l’ampleur en ligne avec des tutoriels et des blogs. Pourtant, beaucoup doutent que le froid élimine vraiment la saleté et les microbes, surtout lorsque le jean revient à température corporelle.

Stephen Craig Cary, microbiologiste à l’Université du Delaware, affirme que la plupart des bactéries résistent au froid et que le congélateur ne suffit pas. Selon lui, laver ses jeans est la meilleure solution pour garantir une vraie propreté tout en économisant de l’énergie.

Certains estiment que le conseil de Bergh vise surtout les amateurs de mode, pas vraiment ceux qui portent des jeans pour un travail physique. Pour les personnes exerçant des activités exigeantes, rien ne vaut un jean propre.

Les scientifiques rappellent que même si le froid limite les odeurs, il ne désinfecte pas vraiment le tissu. Le lavage régulier des jeans reste la solution la plus efficace pour assurer hygiène et santé.

article_content: Knight Fintech, a startup specializing in banking infrastructure and lending solutions, is on the verge of raising $25 million in a funding round led by Accel, according to people familiar with the matter. There may also be a secondary transaction, giving early investors an opportunity to exit. Current backers like 3one4 Capital and Prime Venture Partners are expected to join this round, although the deal’s final details are still being settled. The company’s valuation is still under discussion, partly because some of the initial investors are considering exiting through the secondary sale. This upcoming investment underscores that, despite challenges in the overall funding environment, venture capitalists remain interested in core fintech infrastructure and B2B solutions. Other players in this space, such as Perfios and Lentra, secured sizeable investments earlier this year—$70 million and $27 million, respectively—pointing to ongoing demand for fintech infrastructure providers. Startups like 42 Card Solutions and Falcon are also actively seeking investors for upcoming funding rounds. Knight Fintech and similar early-stage companies are largely targeting smaller regional, cooperative, and specialized banks that often cannot afford to digitize core financial systems on their own. Initially, Knight Fintech aimed to raise $10-12 million earlier this year but increased the target due to new client acquisitions. Founded in 2019, Knight Fintech operates from Singapore and Mumbai. It is led by CEO Kushal Rastogi, who previously worked in asset management and established QuantMagnum Technologies. Parthesh Shah is the company’s other co-founder. Their main products include Knight Beacon (treasury management), Knight Ascent (corporate treasury), Knight Utopia (lending management), and Knight Quest (analytics and credit rating). These platforms are designed to assist banks with decision-making, compliance, automation, and risk management. Experts note that treasury management technology is particularly challenging, as banks must trust external providers with crucial operations. Knight’s Beacon platform, for instance, equips bank treasurers with advanced analytics and automation to support data-driven decisions and risk management. Providers such as M2P and Zeta have helped banks roll out new digital products and streamline onboarding, as fintech infrastructure evolves from simple card-based services to robust, embedded finance platforms. Industry insiders stress that early-stage infrastructure startups must focus on partnering with banks capable of long-term investment in technology. Both Knight Fintech and Accel Partners declined to comment for this story.

The largest strike in five years will cause major disruption across the UK tomorrow, impacting schools, courts, travel, and public sector services in what has become the most significant industrial action faced by the coalition government since its formation. Hundreds of thousands of teachers, lecturers, civil servants, and other public sector employees will participate in a 24-hour walkout to protest proposed pension changes, job cuts, and a pay freeze.

In London, all police leave has been canceled as authorities prepare for a large protest march and potential walkouts by civilian staff at Scotland Yard. Managers have been trained to conduct airport passport checks to offset staffing shortages, and significant delays are expected at major airports. Up to 15,000 schools could close, affecting around seven million children. Extra officers have been deployed to emergency call centers due to concerns that some activists may try to disrupt the march.

Some strike-related disruption may begin tonight, prior to the official start time of 12:01 am, as Border Agency staff are set to walk out early due to varied shift patterns. This could lead to major delays at Gatwick and Heathrow airports. A Border Agency spokesperson confirmed that although the strike formally begins at 12:01 am, effects may be felt earlier.

Tomorrow, Westminster Bridge and surrounding roads will be closed, and security at Parliament increased, in anticipation of large demonstrations. Mark Serwotka, head of the Public and Commercial Services Union, called it his union's most important strike, stating, "Everything we have ever worked for is under attack."

The strike will heavily impact services: up to 15,000 schools may close; severe delays at airports and seaports are likely; urgent court cases will proceed, but other trials may be postponed; Jobseeker's Allowance will be processed automatically; 350 colleges and 75 universities will close or partially close; Whitehall will operate with skeleton staff; driving test disruptions expected; coastguard services should operate normally; and most fire service staff oppose changes to retirement age but are not striking.

Prime Minister David Cameron criticized the strike, stating the proposed public sector pension changes are fair and that industrial action is unjustified while negotiations continue. In Parliament, he encouraged parents to send children to school if possible and suggested that Labour leader Ed Miliband failed to speak out due to union influence. Business leaders, including the British Chambers of Commerce, warned the strike would force many parents to stay home, affecting pay and productivity.

Employment law experts warn that workers taking time off to care for children during the strike could face disciplinary action, as the strike was announced well in advance and may not qualify as an emergency. Picket lines are expected at schools, courts, jobcentres, Parliament, driving test centers, and government buildings, organized by the NUT, ATL, PCS, and University and College Union.

Education Secretary Michael Gove stated that teachers may be required to notify head teachers if they plan to strike and suggested using CRB-checked parent volunteers to help keep schools open. He described the strike as “regrettable” and warned of its inconvenience for families and economic impact, urging teachers to reconsider. Mr. Gove also wrote to head teachers, stating that strikes “won’t improve the prestige of the profession.”

Labour leader Ed Miliband expressed understanding of teachers’ frustration but urged them to consider the impact on students. Business Secretary Vince Cable agreed that public sector pension reform is necessary but questioned the need for a strike during ongoing talks.

Arriving travelers are warned of expected delays due to striking immigration and customs officers, with airlines like Virgin Atlantic working to minimize passenger disruption. Eurostar services will operate as normal, with two extra trains added to meet increased demand.

London Mayor Boris Johnson urged schools to stay open, emphasizing the inconvenience closures create for working parents. Unions like GMB advised members not to cross picket lines, while Unison advised its members not to replace striking teachers, making it difficult for most schools to remain open.

NUT leader Christine Blower called the strike “regrettable but unavoidable,” citing increased pension contributions, extended working years, and reduced payouts. She said official reports affirm teachers’ pensions are affordable and argued that government motivations are ideological, not economic. Mark Serwotka encouraged union members to join the strike, emphasizing the stakes for jobs, pensions, and pay.

La plus grande grève depuis cinq ans provoquera une importante perturbation à travers le Royaume-Uni demain, touchant les écoles, les tribunaux, les transports et les services publics lors de ce qui constitue la plus sérieuse vague d’actions industrielles pour le gouvernement de coalition depuis sa création. Des centaines de milliers d’enseignants, de professeurs, de fonctionnaires et d’autres agents du secteur public cesseront le travail pendant 24 heures afin de protester contre des changements proposés aux retraites, des suppressions de postes et le gel des salaires.

À Londres, tous les congés de la police ont été annulés tandis que les autorités se préparent à une grande manifestation et à des absences possibles parmi les employés civils de Scotland Yard. Des responsables ont été formés pour effectuer les contrôles de passeport aux aéroports, face à la pénurie de personnel, et de sérieux retards sont attendus dans les principaux aéroports. Jusqu’à 15 000 écoles pourraient fermer, affectant près de sept millions d’enfants. Des agents supplémentaires sont dépêchés dans les centres d’appels d’urgence par crainte que certains activistes essaient de perturber la marche.

Certaines répercussions de la grève pourraient se faire sentir dès ce soir, avant le début officiel à 0h01, certains employés de la Border Agency devant cesser le travail plus tôt à cause des horaires décalés. Cela devrait entraîner d’importants retards dans les aéroports de Gatwick et Heathrow. Un porte-parole précise que même si la grève démarre officiellement à 0h01, ses effets risquent d’être ressentis plus tôt.

Demain, le pont de Westminster et les voies autour du Parlement seront fermés et la sécurité renforcée à Westminster en prévision de larges rassemblements. Mark Serwotka, dirigeant du syndicat Public and Commercial Services, a estimé qu’il s’agissait de la grève la plus importante de toute l’histoire de sa structure, déclarant : « Tout ce pourquoi nous avons œuvré est en jeu ».

La grève impactera fortement : jusqu’à 15 000 écoles fermées, de gros retards dans les aéroports et ports, seuls les cas urgents traités dans les tribunaux (le reste reporté), l’allocation chômage traitée de manière automatique, fermeture totale ou partielle de 350 collèges et 75 universités, effectifs réduits à Whitehall, perturbation des examens de conduite, continuité prévue chez les garde-côtes, et la majorité des pompiers opposés au report de l’âge de départ mais sans grève.

Le Premier ministre David Cameron a condamné la grève, jugeant les réformes « justes » et l’action « injustifiée » pendant que les négociations continuent. Au Parlement, il a encouragé les familles à envoyer leurs enfants à l’école et suggéré que l’absence de prise de parole d’Ed Miliband (Labour) s’expliquait par l’influence syndicale. Les milieux patronaux, dont la British Chambers of Commerce, préviennent que la grève privera beaucoup de parents d’une journée de salaire et nuira à la productivité.

Des experts juridiques soulignent que s’absenter pour garder ses enfants lors de la grève pourrait entraîner des sanctions, l’événement étant connu depuis longtemps et donc non considéré comme une urgence. Des piquets de grève seront présents devant écoles, tribunaux, jobcentres, au Parlement, dans les centres d’examen et bâtiments publics, menés par les syndicats NUT, ATL, PCS et University and College Union.

Le ministre de l’éducation Michael Gove a indiqué que les enseignants pourraient devoir prévenir leur chef d’établissement s’ils font grève et a proposé de faire appel à des parents bénévoles agréés pour maintenir l’ouverture des écoles. Il a qualifié la grève de « regrettable », prévenu des difficultés pour les familles et l’économie, et plaidé pour que les enseignants renoncent au mouvement. M. Gove a aussi écrit aux chefs d’établissements, notant que la grève ne rehausserait pas la réputation du corps enseignant.

Ed Miliband (Labour) a dit comprendre la colère des enseignants mais les a appelés à réfléchir à l’impact sur les élèves. Vince Cable (Business) a souligné la nécessité de réformes mais mis en doute la pertinence de la grève pendant le dialogue social.

Les voyageurs arrivant au Royaume-Uni doivent s’attendre à des retards suite à la grève des agents d’immigration et douanes, des compagnies comme Virgin Atlantic collaborant pour limiter les perturbations. Les trains Eurostar fonctionneront normalement, deux rames supplémentaires étant prévues.

Le maire Boris Johnson a invité les écoles londoniennes à rester ouvertes, insistant sur la gêne pour les parents si elles ferment. Des syndicats comme le GMB recommandent à leurs membres de ne pas franchir les piquets de grève, Unison déconseillant à ses adhérents de remplacer les professeurs grévistes, compliquant l’ouverture des écoles.

Christine Blower (NUT) qualifie la journée de « regrettable mais incontournable », évoquant des hausses de cotisation, la prolongation de la carrière et une baisse des retraites. Selon elle, des rapports officiels attestent de la soutenabilité des retraites enseignants et le gouvernement agit par idéologie plus qu’économiquement. Mark Serwotka encourage les syndiqués à participer à une mobilisation cruciale pour les emplois, les retraites et les salaires.

article_content: Juba, South Sudan (CNN) — South Sudanese citizens wept and celebrated their independence on Saturday, filling the streets of Juba with cheers, whistles, and dancing in a ceremony marking the birth of the world’s newest nation. “We are free at last,” some chanted, draping flags over their shoulders. One man knelt to kiss the ground. The new nation’s red, white, and green flag, which had been flown at half-staff the previous day, was raised over the capital. World leaders attending the historic event included United Nations Secretary General Ban Ki-moon, Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir, and South African President Jacob Zuma. Abuk Makuac, who fled to the United States in 1984 and returned for the celebration, said, “This is liberation, a new chapter. No more war. We were born, grew up, and married during war.” South Sudan’s independence formally splits Africa’s largest country into two, following a January referendum overwhelmingly approved by voters. This vote was part of a 2005 peace agreement that ended decades of civil war between a government dominated by Arab Muslims in the north and black Christians and animists in the south. About 2 million people died during the conflict. During the celebrations, some residents paid tribute to family members lost in the war. “It is very emotional. I'm excited, but also thinking of all the people who died for this to happen,” said Victoria Bol, who lost many relatives. South Sudan’s first president and former rebel leader Salva Kiir Mayardit reminded citizens of their difficult past, urging forgiveness and progress. He promised that South Sudanese would not be marginalized again. “As we celebrate our freedom and independence today, I want to assure the people of Darfur, Abyei, and South Kordofan that we have not forgotten you,” Kiir said, referencing regions still in conflict. “When you cry, we cry. When you bleed, we also bleed.” President Barack Obama recognized South Sudan’s sovereignty, releasing a statement that read, “Today is a reminder that after the darkness of war, the light of a new dawn is possible. A proud flag flies over Juba and the map of the world has been redrawn.” In Washington, there was joy and pride at South Sudan’s new embassy. People hugged, shook hands, and some wept as the flag was raised. “This day means a lot to me because we achieved our victory. We got our own country,” said Anai Aluong, who lost several family members during the civil war. “We are a new nation now; we are very happy because God answered our prayer.” British Foreign Secretary William Hague announced the opening of an embassy in Juba and the appointment of an ambassador. Omar al-Bashir attended and congratulated the South Sudanese despite his belief that a united Sudan would have been best, expressing his support for their aspirations. This offered some hope that both sides could move on from past bitterness. Despite the celebrations, significant challenges remain. South Sudan is among the world’s poorest nations, with returning refugees and little-developed infrastructure — few paved roads, and most villages lack electricity or running water. The United Nations reports that South Sudan ranks low on human development indices, including having the world’s highest maternal mortality and female illiteracy rates. Inequities persist between north and south. Moses Chol noted, “They have schools and clean water in the north, and their children don’t die from simple diseases. In the south, people still drink stagnant water and have little.” Violence remains a threat. Clashes have occurred recently in disputed border regions of Abyei and South Kordofan. Despite the 2005 peace deal, forces connected to both sides continue sporadic fighting. Abyei was a battleground in the civil war, and a referendum on its status has been delayed due to disagreements over voter eligibility. Key issues like borders, oil resources, and citizenship still lack resolution between the new neighbors. The U.N. Security Council voted to send up to 7,000 peacekeepers and 900 police officers to South Sudan, and will consider the nation’s membership this week. U.S. special envoy to Sudan, Princeton N. Lyman, cautioned, “Their economic prospects are dim unless the two sides can agree on sharing resources, economic cooperation, and supporting each other’s stability.” Lyman, who was present, added that both peoples desire food, education, security, freedom of expression, and the ability to choose their leaders. Makuac and others acknowledged the difficult road ahead, but set aside concerns to celebrate their long-awaited independence. “We have waited so long to get here ... I will worry about that later,” said Makuac. “This weekend, we celebrate.” CNN’s Nima Elbagir reported from Juba, South Sudan; Faith Karimi reported from Atlanta; with contributions from Jennifer Rizzo and Moni Basu.
