Nous sommes nés, avons grandi et nous sommes mariés pendant la guerre. » L’indépendance du Soudan du Sud sépare officiellement le plus grand pays d’Afrique en deux, à la suite d’un référendum en janvier massivement approuvé par les électeurs. Ce vote faisait partie d’un accord de paix de 2005 qui a mis fin à des décennies de guerre civile entre un gouvernement dominé par des Arabes musulmans au nord et des chrétiens noirs et animistes au sud. Environ 2 millions de personnes sont mortes pendant le conflit. Pendant les célébrations, certains habitants ont rendu hommage à leurs proches perdus pendant la guerre. « C’est très émouvant. Je suis excitée, mais je pense aussi à toutes les personnes mortes pour que cela arrive », a déclaré Victoria Bol, qui a perdu de nombreux membres de sa famille. Le premier président du Soudan du Sud et ancien chef rebelle, Salva Kiir Mayardit, a rappelé aux citoyens leur passé difficile et a appelé au pardon et au progrès. Il a promis que les Sud-Soudanais ne seraient plus jamais marginalisés. « Alors que nous célébrons notre liberté et notre indépendance aujourd’hui, je veux assurer aux peuples du Darfour, d’Abyei et du Kordofan méridional que nous ne vous avons pas oubliés », a déclaré Kiir, en référence à ces régions encore en conflit. « Quand vous pleurez, nous pleurons. Quand vous saignez, nous saignons aussi. » Le président Barack Obama a reconnu la souveraineté du Soudan du Sud dans une déclaration : « Aujourd’hui nous rappelle qu’après l’obscurité de la guerre, la lumière d’une nouvelle aube est possible. Un fier drapeau flotte sur Juba et la carte du monde a été redessinée. » À Washington, la fierté et la joie régnaient à la nouvelle ambassade du Soudan du Sud. Les gens se serraient dans les bras, se serraient la main et certains pleuraient à la levée du drapeau. « Cette journée signifie beaucoup pour moi car nous avons remporté la victoire. Nous avons notre propre pays », a déclaré Anai Aluong, qui a perdu plusieurs membres de sa famille pendant la guerre civile. « Nous sommes une nouvelle nation maintenant ; nous sommes très heureux car Dieu a exaucé notre prière. » Le secrétaire britannique aux Affaires étrangères, William Hague, a annoncé l’ouverture d’une ambassade à Juba et la nomination d’un ambassadeur. Omar al-Bachir a assisté à la cérémonie et félicité les Sud-Soudanais même s’il pensait qu’un Soudan uni aurait été préférable, exprimant tout de même son soutien à leurs aspirations. Cela fait naître un espoir que les deux parties puissent dépasser leur amertume passée. Malgré les festivités, d’importants défis demeurent. Le Soudan du Sud se classe parmi les nations les plus pauvres du monde, avec le retour des réfugiés et des infrastructures peu développées — peu de routes goudronnées, et la plupart des villages n’ont ni électricité ni eau courante. Selon l’ONU, le Soudan du Sud se situe au bas des indices de développement humain, dont les taux de mortalité maternelle et d’analphabétisme féminin les plus élevés au monde. Les inégalités persistent entre le nord et le sud. Moses Chol a déclaré : « Ils ont des écoles et de l’eau potable au nord, et leurs enfants ne meurent pas de maladies simples. Dans le sud, les gens boivent encore de l’eau stagnante et n’ont rien. » La violence reste une menace. Des affrontements ont récemment eu lieu dans les régions frontalières disputées d’Abyei et du Kordofan du Sud. Malgré l’accord de paix de 2005, des forces liées aux deux côtés continuent de se battre sporadiquement. Abyei était un champ de bataille pendant la guerre civile, et un référendum sur son statut a été repoussé à cause de désaccords sur les électeurs admissibles. Des questions vitales comme les frontières, les ressources pétrolières et la citoyenneté ne sont toujours pas résolues entre les nouveaux voisins. Le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU a voté l’envoi de jusqu’à 7 000 soldats de la paix et 900 policiers au Soudan du Sud, et examinera cette semaine la demande d’adhésion de la nouvelle nation. L’envoyé spécial américain au Soudan, Princeton N. Lyman, a averti : « Leurs perspectives économiques sont faibles à moins que les deux parties ne s’accordent sur le partage des ressources, la coopération économique et le soutien mutuel à la stabilité. » Présent lors de la cérémonie, Lyman a ajouté que les deux peuples souhaitent la nourriture, l'éducation, la sécurité, la liberté d'expression et la capacité de choisir leurs dirigeants. Makuac et d’autres reconnaissent la difficulté du chemin à venir, mais mettent leurs préoccupations de côté pour célébrer enfin l’indépendance tant attendue. « Nous avons attendu si longtemps pour en arriver là... Je m’inquiéterai plus tard », a déclaré Makuac. « Ce week-end, c’est la fête. » Nima Elbagir de CNN a rapporté de Juba, Soudan du Sud ; Faith Karimi a rapporté d’Atlanta, avec la contribution de Jennifer Rizzo et Moni Basu.

article_content:
Humanitarian aid agencies rushed on Monday to assist tens of thousands in need after Tamil separatists ended their 25-year struggle in Sri Lanka.

According to the United Nations, about 65,000 people have fled the north-eastern conflict zone in recent days, bringing the total number of internally displaced persons (IDPs) to 265,000. The UN High Commissioner for Refugees warned that this latest large influx—people who have endured extreme hardship—will put even more strain on transit and IDP camps already overwhelmed by the existing population. The agency pledged to erect 10,000 additional shelters to accommodate those arriving from the former combat area and reiterated its request for the Sri Lankan government to provide land for emergency shelters, water, sanitation facilities, and public buildings in areas including Vavuniya, Jaffna, Mannar, and Kilinochchi. It also urged the government to improve conditions at the 42 sites currently housing displaced people and ensure their adequate care and maintenance.

The UN noted recent restrictions on its access to Vavuniya sites, which has hampered its ability to monitor and distribute aid effectively.

Suresh Bartlett, national director of aid agency World Vision, emphasized that while the conventional war may be over, the real challenge is helping fractured and displaced Tamil communities heal and build a future. He stressed the importance of returning people to their homes as soon as possible—a process that could entail demining and rebuilding damaged structures. About a third of the camp population, some 80,000 people, are children, who need emotional, psychosocial, and educational support as well as physical aid. Bartlett underlined the urgency of restoring a sense of dignity and safety for these families. He reported that camps remain overcrowded, with several families sharing shelters meant for one, and that more land, shelters, and safe drinking water are desperately needed. Many new arrivals are malnourished, he added, and international support is crucial at this time. Civilian deaths in the conflict are estimated at 70,000 to 80,000, though the true number may never be known.

Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders), whose mission chief is Hugues Robert, was scaling up medical operations, staffing three hospitals, and focusing on screening, stabilizing, and treating incoming patients. As fighting has apparently ceased, the organization will shift many efforts to post-operative care, with mental health remaining a significant unaddressed need.

Amnesty International’s Asia-Pacific director, Sam Zarifi, called on the Sri Lankan government to ensure its forces fully respect international law and civilian protection. The organization called for full humanitarian access, independent observers to monitor the situation, and registration of displaced people to safeguard against forced disappearances. Zarifi also called on the international community to deploy monitors.

U.S. State Department spokesman Ian Kelly said the end of fighting is an opportunity for Sri Lanka to build a future rooted in democracy, tolerance, and respect for human rights. He stressed that providing food, water, shelter, health care, and sanitation for camp residents—and expediting their return home—should be a top priority for the government.

De nombreux nouveaux arrivants sont sous-alimentés, a-t-il ajouté, et un soutien international est indispensable à ce stade. Zarifi a également appelé la communauté internationale à déployer des observateurs.

Le porte-parole du département d’État américain, Ian Kelly, a déclaré que la fin des combats représentait une occasion pour le Sri Lanka de bâtir un avenir fondé sur la démocratie, la tolérance et le respect des droits humains. Il a insisté sur le fait que la fourniture de nourriture, d’eau, d’abris, de soins et d’assainissement pour les résidents des camps — et leur retour rapide chez eux — devait être une priorité absolue du gouvernement.

article_content:
Healthy gay and bisexual men should be offered preventive anti-viral medication to dramatically reduce new HIV cases, according to a groundbreaking study conducted in England. The PROUD study provides the first real-world evidence showing that pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) with the HIV drug Truvada can lower the risk of HIV infection in men who have sex with men by up to 86%.

The study enrolled 545 participants at 13 sexual health clinics, dividing them into two groups: one received Truvada immediately, while the other was scheduled to receive it a year later. Of the 276 men who started Truvada right away, only three contracted HIV over the following year. In contrast, 19 men in the deferred group became HIV positive during the same period. This clear difference underscores PrEP's effectiveness for individuals at high risk of HIV.

Lead researcher Professor Sheena McCormack of the Medical Research Council’s Clinical Trials Unit at University College London stated, 'These results are extremely exciting and show PrEP is highly effective at preventing HIV infection in the real world.' She added that concerns about PrEP's practical effectiveness were unfounded, and these findings support efforts to make PrEP available through the NHS.

Dr. Michael Brady, medical director at the HIV/AIDS charity Terrence Higgins Trust, described PrEP as a 'game-changer' in HIV prevention. While condoms remain essential, especially as condomless sex increases the risk of HIV, PrEP offers an important complementary line of defense. Brady emphasized that although PrEP is not a vaccine and may not suit everyone, its approval would greatly strengthen HIV prevention efforts.

Deborah Gold, chief executive of the National AIDS Trust, also praised the study’s results, highlighting that PrEP use did not lead to increased risk behaviors—rates of other sexually transmitted infections were similar across both groups. Gold stressed both the ethical and financial responsibility to provide PrEP, given the potential to prevent new infections and save the NHS millions in long-term treatment costs.

The findings were presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in Seattle, US. The study also found no significant change in condom use or rise in other STIs due to PrEP.

In a concerning development, scientists have identified a new, aggressive HIV strain known as CRF19, first reported in Cuba and studied by researchers at the University of Leuven in Belgium. This strain can progress from HIV infection to AIDS in as little as three years—much faster than the typical 5–10 years—and may not be immediately detected, emphasizing the continued importance of prevention and early testing.

Dr. Des Walsh of the Medical Research Council, which co-funded the PROUD study, reiterated the pressing need for additional HIV prevention strategies, particularly for those most at risk. The PROUD study's results suggest that PrEP could make a major impact in reducing HIV transmission rates in the UK.

Les hommes gays et bisexuels en bonne santé devraient se voir proposer un traitement antiviral préventif afin de réduire considérablement les nouveaux cas de VIH, selon une étude innovante menée en Angleterre. L’étude PROUD apporte les premières preuves concrètes que la prophylaxie pré-exposition (PrEP) avec le médicament anti-VIH Truvada peut diminuer le risque d’infection chez les hommes ayant des relations sexuelles avec d’autres hommes jusqu'à 86 %.

L’étude a recruté 545 participants dans 13 cliniques de santé sexuelle, répartis en deux groupes : l’un a reçu Truvada immédiatement, l’autre a commencé un an plus tard. Parmi les 276 hommes ayant débuté le traitement immédiatement, seuls trois ont contracté le VIH au cours de l’année suivante. En comparaison, 19 hommes du groupe différé sont devenus séropositifs pendant la même période. Cet écart marque clairement l'efficacité du PrEP pour les personnes les plus exposées au VIH.

La professeure Sheena McCormack, chercheuse principale de l’unité des essais cliniques du Medical Research Council à l’University College London, a déclaré : « Ces résultats sont extrêmement encourageants et montrent que le PrEP est très efficace dans la prévention de l’infection par le VIH dans la vie réelle. » Elle a ajouté que les inquiétudes concernant l’efficacité pratique du PrEP étaient sans fondement et que ces résultats justifient sa mise à disposition via le NHS.

Le Dr Michael Brady, directeur médical de l’association Terrence Higgins Trust, a qualifié le PrEP de « révolution » dans la lutte contre le VIH. Bien que les préservatifs restent essentiels, notamment car les rapports non protégés augmentent le risque de transmission, le PrEP constitue une défense complémentaire importante. Brady précise que le PrEP n’est pas un vaccin et ne conviendra pas à tout le monde, mais que son approbation renforcerait fortement la prévention du VIH.

Deborah Gold, directrice générale du National AIDS Trust, a aussi salué l’étude, soulignant que la prise de PrEP n’a pas conduit à des comportements sexuels plus risqués – les taux d'autres IST étaient semblables dans les deux groupes. Elle souligne la responsabilité éthique et financière de proposer le PrEP, étant donné son potentiel préventif et les économies pour le NHS.

Les résultats ont été présentés lors de la Conférence sur les rétrovirus et les infections opportunistes (CROI) à Seattle, États-Unis. L’étude n’a révélé aucun changement significatif dans l’usage du préservatif ni de hausse des IST dues à la prise de PrEP.

Par ailleurs, des scientifiques ont identifié une nouvelle souche agressive du VIH, appelée CRF19, signalée à Cuba et étudiée par l’Université de Leuven en Belgique. Cette souche peut faire évoluer l’infection vers le SIDA en à peine trois ans – beaucoup plus vite que la moyenne de 5 à 10 ans – et peut passer inaperçue, soulignant l’importance de la prévention et du dépistage précoce.

Le Dr Des Walsh, du Medical Research Council, qui a cofinancé l’étude PROUD, rappelle la nécessité de renforcer la prévention, surtout pour les populations les plus à risque. Les résultats indiquent que le PrEP pourrait avoir un impact majeur sur la diminution des transmissions du VIH au Royaume-Uni.

Authorities in Charlottesville, Virginia, are employing drones to aid in the search for missing University of Virginia student Hannah Graham, last seen in mid-September. The Federal Aviation Administration approved an Aeryon SkyRanger drone for this mission, a move that amplifies ongoing debates about balancing privacy with public safety.

A 2013 law in Virginia placed a moratorium on police drone operations over civil liberties concerns, with a review scheduled for July 2015. Charlottesville has taken an even stricter stance locally. Despite this, some civil liberties advocates recognize drones' usefulness in urgent situations, like locating Graham.

Activist David Swanson, who championed Charlottesville's drone ban, warns of threats to constitutional protections from drone surveillance. Conversely, Brendan Schulman, a legal advisor for drone operators, believes these privacy fears are often exaggerated, noting drones can be more cost-effective and efficient than helicopters. John Coggin, chief engineer with the Mid-Atlantic Aviation Partnership, points out drones can access areas unreachable to ground crews or conventional aircraft.

More than 50 law enforcement personnel have searched over 175 square miles. Jesse Matthew, last seen with Graham, faces charges of abduction with intent to defile.

Groups previously supporting the moratorium, like the Rutherford Institute, now back using drones for Graham’s case, urging continued attention to civil liberties protections. John Whitehead, the Institute’s president, supports employing any tool that could help, provided legal safeguards are maintained.

article_content: Ed Drew, a California Air National Guard aerial gunner, created the first tintype photographs taken in a combat zone since the Civil War. Seeking to capture the humanity of his fellow service members during the Afghanistan war, Drew asked them to sit for portraits on the battlefield. The tintype process is painstaking and time-consuming, and Drew often had to pause sessions to respond to his military duties, including helicopter missions. Drew was deployed in Helmand Province, Afghanistan, serving as an aerial gunner with a U.S. Air Force Combat Rescue Unit. 'To do this process in a war, let alone a foreign war, is historically significant,' he told the New Yorker. Wet-plate tintype photography is difficult to master even in ideal settings due to challenging chemistry and environmental factors. In Afghanistan, Drew faced a harsh climate, limited materials, and the stresses of war. Drew's striking images are available at Ed Drew Photography. Convincing his peers to pose for the laborious tintype process was initially difficult, but after seeing the results, many became eager participants. According to fstoppers.com, tintype is a slow, labor-intensive wet-plate photographic technique developed in the mid-19th century and widely used during the Civil War. The process involves hand-pouring a collodion mixture onto a metal plate, making it light-sensitive with a silver nitrate solution in a darkroom. The plate must be exposed and developed within minutes. Drew said engaging in this historic process helped him work through his own experiences in the war. 'As a photographer and artist, I wanted to create something physical, one-of-a-kind, and very unique,' Drew told PetaPixel. He referenced the Japanese aesthetic of 'Wabi-Sabi,' which embraces imperfection and impermanence, themes he hoped would be reflected in his Afghan portraits as metaphors for his wartime experiences. Despite challenging conditions and his peers’ initial reluctance, Drew’s fellow soldiers returned for more portraits after seeing the powerful results. He photographed them in front of the Air Force rescue helicopters they flew on missions. Drew chose tintype photography because he wanted a process that was both historic and required slow, deliberate focus on his subjects. Drew’s photographic goal was to 'show the humanity of war in the eyes of the airmen I fly combat missions with.' His work is the first battlefield tintype photography since Matthew Brady documented the Civil War. To thank his subjects, Drew provided each with a high-resolution scan and a print of their portrait. Balancing photography with active military missions was challenging, and Drew sometimes had to drop everything at a moment's notice. His Afghan images served as metaphors for his experiences, and switching between creative and tactical mindsets, while maintaining situational awareness, was demanding. Ultimately, the project helped him process and document his life following deployment.
translated_content: Ed Drew, mitrailleur aérien de la California Air National Guard, a réalisé les premières photographies en ferrotype prises dans une zone de combat depuis la guerre de Sécession. Cherchant à capturer l’humanité de ses camarades pendant la guerre en Afghanistan, Drew leur a demandé de poser pour des portraits sur le champ de bataille. Le procédé ferrotype est minutieux et chronophage, et Drew a souvent dû interrompre les séances pour répondre à ses devoirs militaires, notamment lors de missions en hélicoptère. Drew a été déployé dans la province du Helmand, en Afghanistan, en tant que mitrailleur aérien avec une unité de sauvetage au combat de l’U.S. Air Force. « Réaliser ce procédé durant une guerre, qui plus est à l’étranger, est historiquement significatif », a-t-il déclaré au New Yorker. La photographie sur plaque humide (ferrotype) est difficile à maîtriser, même dans des conditions idéales, en raison de la chimie complexe et des contraintes environnementales. En Afghanistan, Drew a affronté un climat rude, un manque de matériaux et le stress de la guerre. Les images saisissantes de Drew sont disponibles sur Ed Drew Photography. Convaincre ses pairs de poser pour le ferrotype, un procédé laborieux, a d’abord été difficile, mais après avoir vu le résultat, beaucoup sont devenus enthousiastes. Selon fstoppers.com, le ferrotype est une technique photographique sur plaque humide lente et fastidieuse, développée au milieu du XIXe siècle et largement utilisée pendant la guerre de Sécession. Ce procédé consiste à verser manuellement un mélange de collodion sur une plaque métallique, la rendant photosensible grâce à une solution de nitrate d’argent dans une chambre noire. La plaque doit être exposée et développée en quelques minutes. Drew explique que s’engager dans ce procédé historique l’a aidé à traverser ses propres expériences de la guerre. « En tant que photographe et artiste, je voulais créer quelque chose de physique, unique et singulier », a-t-il confié à PetaPixel. Il fait référence à l’esthétique japonaise du ‘Wabi-Sabi’, qui célèbre l’imperfection et l’impermanence, des thèmes qu’il voulait voir transparaître dans ses portraits afghans en tant que métaphores de ses expériences en temps de guerre. Malgré des conditions difficiles et la réticence initiale de ses camarades, ces derniers sont revenus pour de nouveaux portraits après avoir vu le résultat. Drew les a photographiés devant les hélicoptères de sauvetage de l’Air Force qu’ils pilotaient lors des missions. Il a choisi le ferrotype car il voulait une méthode à la fois historique et exigeant une concentration lente et réfléchie sur ses sujets. L’objectif photographique de Drew était de « montrer l’humanité de la guerre dans les yeux des aviateurs avec lesquels je vole pendant les missions de combat ». Son travail est le premier ferrotype de champ de bataille depuis que Matthew Brady a documenté la guerre de Sécession. Pour remercier ses modèles, Drew leur a offert un scan haute résolution et un tirage de leur portrait. Trouver l’équilibre entre la photographie et des missions militaires actives s’est avéré difficile, et Drew devait parfois abandonner soudainement ce qu’il faisait. Ses images d’Afghanistan sont devenues des métaphores de ses expériences ; passer d’un état d’esprit créatif à tactique tout en gardant sa vigilance a été exigeant. article_content:
This article was produced in collaboration with The Markup, Afro LA, and the Los Angeles Times. On September 23, 2021, Los Angeles Police Department detective Jeffry Poole’s inbox filled rapidly. Beginning at 3:30 a.m., he started receiving a stream of emails about alleged crimes. By afternoon, these alerts—sent every ten minutes—totaled 63, all from Neighbors, the Ring doorbell camera social platform. Neighbors, akin to the Nextdoor app, encourages residents with Ring devices to post about incidents in their area, sometimes including footage; posts can then be forwarded to police, who can view attached media.

Launched in May 2018, Neighbors described itself as a “new neighborhood watch,” uniting residents, the Ring News team, and local law enforcement to deter burglary, package theft, and make communities safer. Ring, owned by Amazon, has partnered with the LAPD, which receives hundreds of email alerts from Neighbors—one of more than 2,600 U.S. police departments working with Amazon's Ring network.

In collaboration with the NYCity News Service at the Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism, The Markup obtained records of over 200,000 emails sent to LAPD officers via Neighbors between July 2020 and September 2022. LAPD’s relationship with Ring reflects the department’s continued adoption of technologies to collect data, yet little evidence shows these practices boost policing effectiveness; they risk overwhelming officers, invading privacy, and distracting personnel.

Detective Poole, who did not respond to interview requests, was among 260 LAPD officers opting in to Neighbors crime alerts as of September 2022. During 18 months, he received over 10,000 crime-related emails and dozens of other alerts. When users label posts as “crime,” officers receive automated notifications, often including attached media. On Poole’s busiest day, approximately one-third of alerts referenced package theft; about one in ten described non-criminal 'suspicious behavior.'

Critics like Albert Fox Cahn of the Surveillance Technology Oversight Project argue that sifting through these alerts diverts officers from meaningful tasks. Ring, in response to questions, highlighted positive outcomes such as assisting with public safety and finding missing persons, and emphasized that both users and agencies control the notifications they receive.

Interviews with both officers and civilian LAPD employees reveal concern about these programs’ impact on privacy. Sarah Brayne of UT Austin relayed worries about indiscriminate data collection, while Peter Polack of the Stop LAPD Spying Coalition warned that Neighbors enables unchecked information gathering, extending law enforcement surveillance to entire communities.

Ring’s founder, Jamie Siminoff, originally marketed the company as a tool for convenience and doorbell security, later pivoting to a more aggressive public safety stance. The company has provided promotional materials and free devices to officers, developed direct communication portals for law enforcement, and enrolled LAPD officers in ambassador programs, all to encourage police adoption. Some cities have subsidized Ring camera purchases for residents.

After public backlash, Ring revised its policies in 2021, barring police from contacting users directly through the platform. Agencies must now publicly post requests for footage. Neighbors’ automated email alerts to officers, however, continue.

LAPD was the 240th agency to join Neighbors in May 2019; more than 2,600 agencies are now participating. The LAPD has also adopted controversial technology initiatives in the past, such as Operation LASER and predictive policing software PredPol/Geolitica. Both programs ended following concerns over privacy, data reliability, and racial bias.

Despite these partnerships and outreach efforts, the efficacy of Ring in lowering crime is uncertain. Public records indicate minimal dialogue between officers and residents on Neighbors, and little evidence suggests widespread arrests result from Ring footage. Critics, including legal scholars and technology policy experts, view the reliance on data-driven policing as ineffective and sometimes counterproductive.

The LAPD, when contacted for comment, downplayed its relationship with Ring, asserting it only works with citizens who own Ring devices as part of investigations and declined to elaborate further. The impact and value of LAPD’s continued engagement with Ring and similar technologies remain under question.

This project was supported by the Pulitzer Center’s AI Accountability Network.

Sarah Brayne (UT Austin) évoque des inquiétudes sur la collecte massive de données ; Peter Polack (Stop LAPD Spying Coalition) redoute que Neighbors permette une surveillance élargie de toute la population.

Jamie Siminoff, fondateur de Ring, avait initialement présenté son dispositif comme un outil de commodité et de sécurité, puis a réorienté sa stratégie pour cibler la sécurité publique. L’entreprise a fourni des caméras et du matériel promotionnel aux policiers, créé des portails de communication et des programmes ambassadeurs pour renforcer l’usage par la police. Certaines villes ont subventionné l’achat de caméras Ring pour leurs habitants.

Malgré ces initiatives et efforts, l’impact réel de Ring sur la criminalité reste incertain. Les dossiers publics montrent peu d’échanges entre policiers et résidents via Neighbors, et il existe peu de preuves que les vidéos Ring aboutissent à des arrestations. Des experts estiment que s’en remettre à la « police par les données » n’a pas prouvé son efficacité et peut s’avérer contre-productif.

Sollicité pour commenter, le LAPD a minimisé sa relation avec Ring, précisant qu’il ne travaille qu’avec des citoyens équipés de caméras Ring dans le cadre d’enquêtes, sans donner plus de détails. L’utilité de ces outils et l’engagement du LAPD restent donc des sujets débattus.

Ce projet a reçu le soutien de l’AI Accountability Network du Pulitzer Center.

article_content: On Wednesday, Mumbai's air quality remained in the 'Moderate' category, with an overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of 149 at noon, according to the System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research (SAFAR)-India. Some areas in Mumbai experienced 'poor' to 'very poor' air quality. At Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST), the state pollution control meter registered 'very poor' air quality at 7 am, prompting a health alert. AQI levels varied across the city: Bandra Kurla Complex recorded an AQI of 200 at 9 am (moderate), Colaba 151 (moderate), and Borivali East 141 (moderate). On Tuesday, air quality in Bandra Kurla Complex was in the 'poor' category, despite the city’s average AQI being 145 (moderate), as noted by SAFAR. The Bombay High Court issued interim directions to the Maharashtra government and Mumbai municipal authorities to address worsening air pollution, restricting firecracker use to three hours between 7 pm and 10 pm. Air quality remains a concern in metropolitan cities; in Delhi, the AQI was in the 'severe' category on Wednesday morning. According to CPCB data, the AQI in Anand Vihar was 452, with RK Puram at 433, Punjabi Bagh at 460, Sri Aurobindo Marg at 382, and Shadipur at 413, all classified as 'severe.' Many Delhi residents reported breathing difficulties and urged authorities to act swiftly against rising air pollution. A thick toxic haze, or 'smog,' continued to linger over Delhi, as confirmed by the Central Pollution Control Board. In business news, Tata Group acquired Wistron's manufacturing facility, becoming the first Indian company to assemble iPhones, with the deal valued at $750 million. India surpassed Mainland China in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2024, highlighting advances in education and research. Independent directors of Religare Enterprises Ltd (REL) raised allegations of fraud against the Burman family during their takeover attempt.

article_content: An intense cold wave sweeping across the eastern United States has proven deadly, and some police departments are using humor to relay safety messages. In Kentucky, Harlan City Police jokingly posted a social media 'warrant' for Elsa, the snow queen from Disney's 'Frozen,' describing her as a blonde in a blue dress often heard singing 'Let it Go.' Beneath the lighthearted post, their goal is to urge the public to take necessary measures against the dangerous cold, which has already led to ten deaths in Tennessee, five from hypothermia. Officials are stressing the importance of protecting yourself, your loved ones, neighbors, and pets during this weather. The deep freeze has blanketed nearly half the country, with 30 states under wind chill advisories. The frigid conditions have caused parts of Niagara Falls to freeze and put southern crops, including Florida's oranges, at risk—affecting about 185 million people. This trend of using humor isn't new for law enforcement. Recently, police in Merrimack, New Hampshire, lightheartedly blamed Punxsutawney Phil, the famous groundhog, for an overly snowy winter, highlighting his unreliable forecast. In previous winters, Phil has been humorously 'charged' over inaccurate predictions.

Derrière ce ton humoristique, leur objectif est d'insister sur la nécessité de prendre des précautions face au froid extrême, déjà responsable de dix décès dans le Tennessee, dont cinq liés à l'hypothermie. Les autorités rappellent l'importance de veiller sur soi, ses proches, ses voisins et ses animaux en cette période. Au fil des hivers, Phil a déjà été « inculpé » pour de mauvaises prévisions.

article_content: Following allegations of police brutality against Joe Ajaero, the president of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Nigeria’s primary labour unions—the NLC and Trade Union Congress (TUC)—have initiated a comprehensive shutdown of Imo State. This action, endorsed at an emergency labour leaders meeting, orders workers across sectors like electricity, fuel distribution, and aviation to suspend their services. No flights will operate in or out of Imo State starting midnight, November 8, 2023. These measures come after Ajaero was allegedly attacked by police in Owerri. Labour groups had previously issued a five-day ultimatum calling for the redeployment of Imo’s Police Commissioner and the prosecution of implicated government aides, with a warning to escalate action nationwide if demands were not addressed. While the police deny arresting Ajaero, stating he was moved for his safety, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma alleges that the labour chief was interfering in political affairs. The incident has drawn public ire and condemnation from various civil society groups and public figures including 2023 Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi and human rights lawyer Femi Falana.

Cette décision, prise lors d'une réunion d'urgence des dirigeants syndicaux, ordonne aux travailleurs de secteurs tels que l'électricité, la distribution de carburant et l'aviation de suspendre leurs services. Aucun vol n’entrera ni ne sortira de l’État d’Imo à partir de minuit, le 8 novembre 2023. Ces mesures surviennent après l’agression présumée d’Ajaero par la police à Owerri. Les syndicats avaient auparavant lancé un ultimatum de cinq jours exigeant la mutation du commissaire de police d’Imo et des poursuites contre les aides du gouvernement concernés, sous menace d’étendre la grève à tout le pays si leurs demandes n’étaient pas satisfaites. La police nie cependant avoir arrêté Ajaero, affirmant qu’il a été déplacé pour sa propre sécurité, tandis que le gouverneur d’Imo, Hope Uzodimma, accuse le leader syndical de s’immiscer dans la politique de l’État. Cet incident a provoqué l’indignation et la condamnation de multiples groupes de la société civile et personnalités publiques, dont Peter Obi, candidat à la présidentielle de 2023 du Labour Party, et l’avocat des droits humains Femi Falana.

article_content: Joseph Brooks, the composer of the pop hit 'You Light Up My Life,' died by apparent suicide on Sunday, according to New York police. Brooks, 73, was facing charges in connection with 11 alleged rapes and sexual assaults, Deputy Commissioner Paul Browne said. The Oscar-winning songwriter was discovered on the couch in his Manhattan home by a friend with whom he was supposed to have lunch at 12:30 p.m., Browne reported. A plastic dry cleaning bag and towel were wrapped around Brooks's head, connected by a tube to a helium tank. A suicide note was found nearby. In January, Brooks's son, Nicholas Brooks, was charged with the murder of his ex-girlfriend. According to the Manhattan District Attorney's office, swimsuit designer Sylvie Cachay, 33, was found dead with bruises at a New York hotel last December. 'You Light Up My Life', written as a movie title track, earned Brooks an Oscar, a Golden Globe, and a Grammy. Debby Boone's recording of the song was the top hit of 1977 on the Billboard pop chart. CNN's Susan Candiotti contributed to this report.

Un sac en plastique de teinturier et une serviette étaient enroulés autour de la tête de Brooks, reliés par un tuyau à une bonbonne d'hélium. Une note de suicide a été retrouvée à proximité. En janvier, le fils de Brooks, Nicholas Brooks, a été accusé du meurtre de son ex-petite amie. Selon le bureau du procureur de Manhattan, la créatrice de maillots de bain Sylvie Cachay, 33 ans, a été retrouvée morte avec des ecchymoses dans un hôtel chic de New York en décembre dernier. article_content: The Kano State Government is sponsoring 1,001 postgraduate students to pursue various programmes in India and Uganda. Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf announced the commencement of this scholarship scheme at a ceremony held at the Government House, Kano, on Thursday evening. The program is starting with an initial batch of 550 students. The foreign scholarship scheme was originally introduced by former Governor, Senator Rabi’u Musa Kwankwaso, and is credited with bringing significant positive impacts to Kano State and Nigeria as a whole. Some graduates of the program now hold key positions in the current administration, including Dr Yusuf Ibrahim Kofarmata (Commissioner for Higher Education), Prof. Aliyu Isa Aliyu (Statistician General of the State), and Dr. Bashir Muzakkir (Special Adviser on Innovation). Governor Yusuf acknowledged the legacy of Senator Kwankwaso, noting that during his administration, several batches of students were sponsored to study in about 16 different countries. This initiative produced many professionals, including PhD holders, and thousands with master's degrees and expertise in various fields such as medical sciences, engineering, natural sciences, piloting, and maritime studies. Governor Yusuf stated that Senator Kwankwaso’s efforts have provided strong motivation for continuing the policy, emphasizing its usefulness and popularity. The Governor officially flagged off the resumption of Kano State’s foreign scholarship program and the sponsorship of the first set of 550 scholars out of the total 1,001. Earlier, Senator Kwankwaso praised the state government for maintaining the program and advised the scholarship recipients to live up to expectations and contribute meaningfully to their families and the nation. The first batch of 550 students, who are expected to depart the country on Friday morning, received their scholarship offers and travel documents from Governor Yusuf during the occasion.

article_content:
Eric Friedman, Founder and CEO of eSkill, highlights a major global trend: a growing talent shortage, expected to result in 85 million unfilled jobs worldwide by 2030. Over the past decade, many organizations have adopted digital technologies and transformed workplace operations, creating new positions and eliminating obsolete ones. However, many job seekers’ skills have not kept up with these changes, widening the gap between employer needs and available talent. Recent surveys show that 71% of CEOs now see the skills gap as their top business challenge.

To address this, many businesses are prioritizing upskilling—training their current workforce to develop new, modern skills. Recruiting externally to fill gaps is costly and often results in high turnover, with employee replacement expenses reaching up to 60% of annual salary. The Association for Talent Development reports that 75% of hiring is for replacements rather than new roles. By focusing on upskilling, companies tap into existing employees’ potential, providing training so they can transition into crucial roles.

Upskilling brings several benefits: it increases productivity, enables innovation, and helps employees adapt to evolving job requirements. It also improves recruitment and retention by showing employees and candidates that organizations invest in their people.

Organizations can approach upskilling through:
• Assessing skills gaps, especially in vital areas like data literacy, AI, and cybersecurity.
• Designing personalized learning plans tailored to individual strengths and needs.
• Providing diverse training options, including online courses and hands-on experiences, often in partnership with education providers.
• Fostering a continuous learning culture linked to career growth, with recognition and assessment of progress.

Amazon, for example, has committed $1.2 billion to its Upskilling 2025 initiative, offering frontline employees access to education and specialized training through 2025. 

In summary, making upskilling a core strategy is crucial for organizations to overcome skill shortages and build a resilient, innovative workforce for the future.

article_content: Authorities have intensified their search for 12-year-old Autumn Pasquale, who disappeared over the weekend. Her parents and local prosecutors are offering a $10,000 reward for information leading to her location. Autumn was last seen around 12:30 p.m. on Saturday, leaving her home in Clayton, Gloucester County, while riding a white BMX bicycle. The FBI has joined police officers from approximately 40 departments to search through the night for any trace of Autumn. Volunteers like John Reed have been distributing flyers in hopes that someone has seen her. Autumn is described as white, about 5 feet 2 inches tall, around 120 pounds, with blue eyes and blonde hair, typically worn in a ponytail or bun. She was last seen wearing navy blue sweatpants, a yellow 'Clayton Soccer' T-shirt, bright blue high-top sneakers, and a silver or light gray cinch backpack with 'Reckless' printed on it. Her father, Tony Pasquale, told NBC News: 'It's not like her. Everyone’s working together to try and find her. We love her and we want her to come home.' On Sunday, hundreds of local residents met at a church to organize search parties and distribute flyers. Authorities requested residents avoid searching in local woods so bloodhounds could attempt to track Autumn’s scent. Gloucester County Prosecutor Sean Dalton’s office has partnered with the Pasquale family to offer a $10,000 reward for information. A signal from Autumn's cellphone was last detected by a tower in nearby Williamstown, but investigators believe the phone is now either turned off or out of battery. Michelle Connell, whose daughter is a friend of Autumn’s, shared with NBC News: 'People have been searching all day, everywhere—every park, railroad area, and school building. She’s a good kid. Everyone is upset.'

article_content: Former Alabama Governor Don Siegelman was denied a new trial and has been resentenced to six and a half years in prison for charges of bribery, conspiracy, mail fraud, and obstruction of justice, as announced by the Justice Department. At a hearing on Friday in federal court in Montgomery, District Judge Mark Fuller ordered that Siegelman serve 78 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and pay a $50,000 fine. Siegelman was first found guilty in 2006 on seven charges. Although an appeals court overturned two charges, five convictions stood, and the Supreme Court declined to take up the case. Siegelman was released on bail after less than a year in prison when the two charges were dismissed. Earlier this week, Siegelman requested a new trial, but the District Court reviewed and dismissed all his claims prior to his resentencing on Friday. The case centers on allegations that HealthSouth CEO Richard Scrushy paid $500,000 to obtain a seat on a state regulatory board. Siegelman was also found guilty of obstruction of justice related to an investigation into a suspected pay-to-play scheme involving another Alabama businessman. Assistant Attorney General Lanny Breuer said the case underscores the Justice Department’s dedication to holding corrupt public officials accountable.

Britain’s Got Talent has found a standout in Lettice Rowbotham, but her story isn’t the typical rags-to-riches tale. Raised in a privileged environment, Lettice’s mother, Sherree Valentine Daines, is a renowned impressionist painter whose works are acquired by celebrities and the British Royal Family. With individual pieces selling for as much as £10,000 and exhibitions at major galleries like the Tate and Barbican, Daines’s career supported Lettice through elite schools including the Purcell School of Music and Charterhouse.

Despite being approached to join the reality show Made In Chelsea, Lettice chose to concentrate on her musical pursuits—especially her electric violin skills. She currently resides with her parents in a grand 18th-century mansion in Surrey, which boasts lavish features such as a glass spiral staircase and a music room. While BGT judge David Walliams described her as ‘posh,’ Lettice emphasizes that her journey is rooted in talent rather than background.

With encouragement from her sisters Bunty and Felicity, Lettice tried out for BGT, candidly admitting she enjoys a vibrant social life and sometimes auditions after a night out. Still, she is deeply committed—spending up to six hours a day practicing violin and aspiring to emulate the success of artists like Beyoncé.

Lettice brings significant experience to the show, having performed with artists like Olly Murs, at Buckingham Palace for Prince Charles, and for Vladimir Putin’s daughter’s wedding. A Royal College of Music alumna, Lettice has played at major venues, collaborated with well-known musicians, and toured internationally with her previous group High On Heels. Her energetic character and talent have impressed the BGT judges, with Simon Cowell singling out both her ability and personality.

Her established résumé, alongside those of other seasoned contestants, raises questions about the nature of Britain’s Got Talent—challenging the traditional idea that the show discovers unknown performers.

article_content: Terry Probyn, Jaycee Dugard's mother, expressed deep emotion while speaking about the rescue of three missing women in Cleveland—a development that strongly echoed her own family's ordeal. At an awards gala hosted by the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children in Washington, Probyn called the event ‘another miracle,’ celebrating the survival of the three women. Probyn herself experienced a similar reunion nearly four years ago, when her daughter Jaycee, who had been held captive for 18 years, was finally freed in California in 2009. ‘We are still grieving those lost years,’ Probyn shared, ‘yet we are grateful for our reunion and are working through our foundation to support others facing similar trauma.’ The family's JAYC Foundation provides resources for families recovering from abduction and traumatic experiences. Both Dugard and her mother were awarded ‘Hope Awards’ by the Center at Tuesday’s event in recognition of their advocacy. Although the awards dinner was scheduled prior to the breaking news about Amanda Berry, Gina DeJesus, and Michelle Knight’s rescue in Cleveland, the timing lent the occasion extra significance. Dugard remarked, ‘Talking about hope now feels especially powerful, considering everything that’s happening.’

article_content: Argentina's upcoming presidential run-off features Sergio Massa, the centrist finance minister from the governing Peronist coalition, running against hard-right libertarian Javier Milei. Both candidates will inherit the challenge of addressing the country's high inflation, growing poverty, and mounting debt. In the first round of voting in October, Massa secured 37% while Milei garnered 30%, short of the 45% needed to win outright. The results were unexpected to many analysts, as Massa is overseeing an economy with 142.7% inflation and significant public dissatisfaction with the government. Massa’s campaign was aided by welfare initiatives and messaging about potential increases in utility prices if Milei, who pledges to reduce state subsidies, wins. Milei, a former TV personality and current congressman, is known for his outsider status, divisive rhetoric, and comparisons to Donald Trump. Milei and his running mate, Victoria Villarruel, have downplayed abuses during Argentina's military dictatorship, adding to public division. Years of economic hardship have driven some support for Milei, but his positions—including controversial comments about the Pope and support for organ sales—have alienated moderate voters in this mainly Roman Catholic country. Argentina is approaching its sixth recession in ten years, with about 40% of its population living in poverty. The impact of inflation is palpable. 'The price of basic goods has skyrocketed,' said Jorge Lopez, a Buenos Aires taxi driver. 'My earnings buy less every day.' Although Massa is part of a left-wing government, he represents the centrist Peronist faction. Since the 1940s, Peronism, a blend of industrial policy and subsidies, has been influential in Argentine politics. Massa is credited with negotiating a $7.5bn agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in August and expanding welfare and tax exemptions before the election; many expect that these measures will be reversed when the new administration takes office on December 10. Experts expect Massa to pursue gradual reductions in subsidies and aim for a budget surplus of 1% next year, after last year’s 2.4% deficit. However, Argentina owes around $43bn to the IMF and $65bn to bondholders from the 2020 restructuring, with significant repayments due in 2024 and 2025. Milei wants to cut government spending by 15% of GDP, remove utility subsidies, privatize state-owned firms, and reduce public health funding—a program analysts say could be socially and politically contentious. The country’s economic problems are intensified by the Central Bank's depleted reserves, ongoing currency devaluation, and a lack of access to international financial markets. Analysts suggest additional debt restructuring is likely, regardless of the election outcome. For everyday Argentines, the effects are acute. Malena Pesce, a teacher in greater Buenos Aires, says high prices have forced her to cut spending on essentials and leisure. Inflation averaged 50% from 2018 to 2022 and has worsened recently due to factors like the war in Ukraine, US Federal Reserve rate hikes, and a severe drought cutting export income. The government has declared bankruptcy nine times since 1816 and has often printed money to finance deficits, worsening inflation. Massa, as finance minister, has used this approach. Milei proposes abolishing the Central Bank and dollarizing the economy, steps experts say could destabilize the financial system and economy if reserves are insufficient. Despite the radically different proposals, both candidates face daunting economic challenges. Some voters are still optimistic. 'Despite everything, I’m optimistic,' said Pesce. 'I hope Argentines can one day afford their needs and live decent lives.'
translated_content: Le second tour de l'élection présidentielle en Argentine opposera Sergio Massa, ministre des Finances centriste de la coalition péroniste au pouvoir, à Javier Milei, libertarien de droite radicale. Le vainqueur devra faire face à une inflation élevée, à une pauvreté croissante et à une dette toujours plus importante. Au premier tour d'octobre, Massa a obtenu 37 % des voix, tandis que Milei en a recueilli 30 %, tous deux en deçà des 45 % nécessaires pour l'emporter dès le premier tour. Ces résultats ont surpris de nombreux analystes, alors que Massa est à la tête d'une économie connaissant une inflation de 142,7 % et un fort mécontentement populaire. Massa a mené campagne en lançant des programmes sociaux et en avertissant d'une possible augmentation des tarifs des services publics si Milei, qui a promis de réduire les subventions de l'État, venait à être élu. Milei, ex-animateur télé devenu député, est considéré comme un outsider et se distingue par ses propos clivants et des comparaisons avec Donald Trump. Milei et sa colistière Victoria Villarruel ont minimisé les abus de la dictature militaire argentine, ce qui alimente les divisions. L'accumulation de difficultés économiques a favorisé l'ascension de Milei, mais ses positions, y compris des propos polémiques sur le pape et le soutien à la vente d'organes, ont éloigné des électeurs modérés dans un pays majoritairement catholique. L'Argentine est au bord de sa sixième récession en dix ans, avec environ 40 % de la population vivant dans la pauvreté. L'inflation affecte directement les habitants. « Le prix des produits de base a explosé », témoigne Jorge Lopez, chauffeur de taxi à Buenos Aires. « Ce que je gagne vaut de moins en moins. » Bien qu'appartenant à un gouvernement de gauche, Massa représente l'aile centriste du péronisme. Depuis les années 1940, ce courant, mélange de politique industrielle et de subventions, domine la vie politique argentine. Massa est reconnu pour avoir négocié un accord de 7,5 milliards de dollars avec le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) en août et pour avoir élargi les aides sociales et exonérations fiscales avant l'élection ; de nombreux observateurs estiment que ces mesures pourraient être révisées après l'investiture du nouveau gouvernement, le 10 décembre. Les experts pensent que Massa cherchera à réduire progressivement les subventions et à viser un excédent budgétaire de 1 % l'an prochain, après un déficit de 2,4 % l'an dernier. Cependant, l'Argentine doit environ 43 milliards de dollars au FMI et 65 milliards aux détenteurs d'obligations depuis la restructuration de 2020, avec d'importants remboursements prévus en 2024 et 2025. Milei propose de diminuer les dépenses publiques de 15 % du PIB, de supprimer les subventions sur les services publics, de privatiser les entreprises d'État et de réduire les dépenses de santé—un programme que les analystes jugent risqué sur le plan social et politique. Les difficultés économiques du pays sont aggravées par les réserves épuisées de la Banque centrale, la dévaluation continue de la monnaie et l'absence d'accès aux marchés financiers internationaux. Selon plusieurs analystes, une nouvelle restructuration de la dette serait probable, quel que soit le vainqueur. Pour les Argentins, la crise se fait sentir au quotidien. Malena Pesce, enseignante dans la banlieue de Buenos Aires, explique qu’elle a réduit ses dépenses pour l’essentiel et pour les loisirs en raison de la hausse des prix. Entre 2018 et 2022, l’inflation a atteint en moyenne 50 %, s’aggravant récemment à cause de la guerre en Ukraine, des hausses de taux de la Réserve fédérale américaine, et d’une grave sécheresse ayant réduit les revenus d’exportation. L’État argentin a fait défaut neuf fois sur sa dette depuis 1816, recourant souvent à la planche à billets pour financer ses déficits, ce qui ne fait qu’aggraver l’inflation. Massa, en tant que ministre des Finances, a utilisé cette stratégie. Milei, lui, propose de supprimer la Banque centrale et de dollariser l'économie ; des mesures que des experts estiment dangereuses pour la stabilité financière si les réserves sont insuffisantes. En dépit de visions diamétralement opposées, les deux candidats devront faire face à d’importants défis économiques. Certains électeurs gardent espoir. « Malgré tout, je reste optimiste », affirme Pesce. « J’espère qu’un jour les Argentins pourront subvenir à leurs besoins et vivre dignement. »

article_content:
Dominic Sangma's film 'Rapture,' in the Garo language, received the Cultural Diversity Award at this year's Asia Pacific Screen Awards. As the second entry in Sangma's trilogy set in his native Meghalaya, the film tells the story of a boy with night blindness whose village is filled with fear due to rumors of kidnappings and organ trafficking. The local priest's prophecy of an extended darkness heightens anxiety until the boy has a mystical encounter.

'Rapture' premiered at the Locarno Film Festival and was featured at the Busan and Mumbai Film Festivals, winning the Netpac Award in Mumbai. The shoot took place in remote locations, requiring equipment to be brought in from other regions. Local villager Eva Gunme R. Marak provided accommodations for the crew and joined as a co-producer, working with Chinese and Indian producers and securing funding from international sources like the Hubert Bals Fund, Visions Sud Est, and Doha Film Institute.

Sangma, an alumnus of the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, previously earned recognition for 'Ma.Ama.' In interviews, he explained the shift from personal family themes to broader social commentary in 'Rapture,' exploring fears of outsiders, community divisions, and the complexities of Northeast India's cultural identity. The cast consists entirely of local talent from his village and the nearby city of Tura, underlining a commitment to authenticity.

With plans to show the film in select theaters in Northeast India and Bangladesh, Sangma joins a new wave of filmmakers from the region who are gaining visibility thanks to increased collaboration, industry support, and festival exposure. He seeks to establish himself as an auteur recognized for distinctive storytelling, not only for his representation of indigenous culture.
translated_content:
Le film « Rapture » de Dominic Sangma, réalisé en langue garo, a remporté le prix de la Diversité Culturelle lors des Asia Pacific Screen Awards cette année. Second opus d’une trilogie située dans la région natale de Sangma au Meghalaya, il raconte l’histoire d’un jeune garçon atteint de cécité nocturne, dans un village envahi par la peur à cause de rumeurs d’enlèvements et de trafic d’organes. La prophétie d’une obscurité prolongée par le prêtre local intensifie la tension, jusqu’à ce que l’enfant vive une expérience mystique.

« Rapture » a été présenté en avant-première au Festival du film de Locarno, puis projeté à Busan et Mumbai, décrochant le prix Netpac à Mumbai. Le tournage dans des lieux reculés a exigé l’importation de matériel depuis d’autres régions. Eva Gunme R. Marak, habitante locale, a hébergé l’équipe et co-produit le film, aux côtés de producteurs chinois et indiens, avec le soutien financier de la Hubert Bals Fund, Visions Sud Est et Doha Film Institute.

Diplômé de l’Institut Satyajit Ray du Cinéma et de la Télévision, Sangma s’est déjà illustré avec « Ma.Ama ». Il explique que « Rapture » porte le regard de ses récits vers des thèmes plus larges : peur de l’étranger, divisions communautaires et identité complexe du Nord-Est indien. Tous les acteurs viennent de son village ou de Tura, ajoutant à l’authenticité du film.

Des projections en salles sont prévues dans le Nord-Est de l’Inde et au Bangladesh, alors que Sangma fait partie d’une nouvelle vague de cinéastes du Nord-Est soutenue par une plus grande collaboration et la reconnaissance des festivals. Il aspire à être reconnu comme un auteur à la signature unique, au-delà de la représentation culturelle.

article_content: Civil society organisations and other stakeholders have highlighted insecurity and inadequate funding as primary reasons for the poor functionality of Primary Health Care Centres (PHCs) in North Central Nigeria. In interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday, stakeholders said that most PHCs were not operational, and those that were functional often could not provide essential healthcare services due to lack of funding. Mr. Steve Aluko of the Civil Liberties Organisation told NAN in Jos, Plateau State, that most PHCs in the state were closed, while those open often lacked basic facilities or adequate staff. He cited lack of funding, poor policy implementation, staff shortages, and insufficient political will as contributing factors. According to Aluko, 'Most PHCs in Plateau cannot provide essential healthcare services due to inadequate equipment, poor infrastructure, and lack of essential drugs.' He recalled that PHCs, established in the 1980s by then Minister of Health Prof. Olukoye Ransome-Kuti, once improved immunisation and preventive care in Nigeria. Over time, however, these gains have been lost, and the standard of PHCs has continued to decline. Aluko urged all levels of government to prioritise PHCs by increasing funding, releasing funds promptly, implementing policies effectively, and recruiting sufficient staff. Similarly, Gad Shamaki of CLEEN Foundation, an NGO, reported that most PHCs, especially in rural areas, are not operational. He said that, despite some local government efforts to deploy National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) doctors and nurses, more essential drugs and staff are needed. Some residents shared mixed experiences: Mrs. Ngozi Obi of Apata in Jos North LGA said her local PHC was not operational, whereas Mrs. Simi Chollom of Bukuru Lowcost in Jos said her PHC was open but often lacked essential drugs. Mr. James Paul of JMDB layout said their PHC was functional and provided some laboratory services. In Benue State, stakeholders said ongoing insecurity has rendered many rural PHCs inactive. Retired health worker Mr. Mbaiorga Kunde noted that each council ward once had at least one PHC, but frequent farmer-herder crises have made facilities unsafe. He cited five deserted council wards in Kwande LGA as examples. Miss Veronica Oche, a nurse in Makurdi, added that limited drug supplies, scarcity of non-medical materials, unreliable power, and staff shortages were significant challenges. Makurdi resident Mr. Theophilus Anhwange suggested reviving PHCs by equipping them with essential drugs, personnel, and basic facilities.

Dans des entretiens avec l'Agence de Presse du Nigéria (NAN) dimanche, des parties prenantes ont indiqué que la plupart des CSP n’étaient pas opérationnels et que ceux qui fonctionnaient ne pouvaient souvent pas fournir de services essentiels à cause du manque de financement. M. Steve Aluko, de la Civil Liberties Organisation, a déclaré à la NAN à Jos, dans l'État du Plateau, que la majorité des CSP étaient fermés, et que ceux ouverts manquaient souvent d'équipements de base ou de personnel adéquat. Il a évoqué le manque de financement, la mise en œuvre inefficace des politiques, la pénurie de personnel et le manque de volonté politique comme causes principales. Selon Aluko : « La plupart des CSP du Plateau ne peuvent pas offrir de services essentiels à cause d’un équipement insuffisant, d’infrastructures dégradées et du manque de médicaments ». Il a rappelé que les CSP, créés dans les années 1980 sous l’impulsion du professeur Olukoye Ransome-Kuti, alors ministre de la Santé, avaient permis d'améliorer la vaccination et la prévention au Nigéria. Selon lui, ces acquis se sont perdus avec le temps et la situation s’est dégradée. Aluko a exhorté tous les niveaux de gouvernement à accorder la priorité aux CSP en augmentant le financement, en débloquant rapidement les budgets, en mettant en œuvre les politiques et en recrutant davantage de personnel. De même, Gad Shamaki de la Fondation CLEEN, une ONG, a signalé que la majorité des CSP, surtout dans les zones rurales, ne sont pas fonctionnels. Il a salué certains efforts des gouvernements locaux pour déployer des médecins et infirmiers du NYSC, mais a estimé que plus de médicaments essentiels et de personnel étaient nécessaires. Des habitants ont partagé des expériences diverses : Mme Ngozi Obi, d’Apata (Jos North LGA), a déclaré que le CSP de sa communauté était inactif, tandis que Mme Simi Chollom, de Bukuru Lowcost (Jos), a affirmé que son CSP restait ouvert mais souvent sans médicaments de base. M. James Paul, du quartier JMDB, a indiqué que leur CSP fonctionnait et proposait certains services de laboratoire. Dans l’État de Benue, des parties prenantes ont expliqué que l’insécurité persistante a entraîné l’inactivité de nombreux CSP ruraux. Selon l’agent de santé retraité M. Mbaiorga Kunde, chaque quartier disposait d’au moins un CSP, mais les conflits fréquents entre agriculteurs et éleveurs ont rendu les structures peu sûres. Il a cité cinq quartiers désertés dans le Kwande LGA. Mme Veronica Oche, infirmière à Makurdi, a ajouté que la faible disponibilité des médicaments, le manque de fournitures non médicales, les coupures d'électricité et la pénurie de personnel constituaient des défis importants. M. Theophilus Anhwange, résident à Makurdi, a suggéré de redynamiser les CSP par l’approvisionnement en médicaments essentiels, des recrutements et des infrastructures de base.

As the year draws to a close, the tourism industry is looking ahead to the trends set to define vacations in 2024. Expedia Group, drawing on booking data from Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo, along with a global survey of 20,000 travelers, has identified several key travel motivations and destinations for the coming year.

One emerging trend is 'destination dupes,' where travelers seek lesser-known, often more affordable alternatives to crowded hotspots. For example, some are opting for Paros instead of Santorini, Liverpool instead of London, or Sapporo instead of Zermatt. Influencers on social media platforms like TikTok are fueling this movement by sharing these hidden gems.

'Tour tourism' is another rising phenomenon, inspired by the widespread influence of major music tours like Taylor Swift’s Eras and Beyoncé’s Renaissance. More than 40% of surveyed travelers would consider traveling to see a concert, using it as a reason to explore new cities such as Birmingham, Antwerp, and Warsaw, where nightly hotel rates average under $145.

Health-conscious travel is also on the rise, with over 40% of respondents interested in booking a detox or 'dry tripping' experience. Many travelers prefer hotels that provide accessible alcohol-free beverage options, and some cite staying in control and feeling better as primary motivations for drinking less while on vacation.

Creative celebrations, or 'go-ccasions,' are gaining popularity, with travelers finding new reasons for getaways, such as celebrating retirements, promotions, or other milestones with friends and family.

Additionally, the 'vibe' of hotels is becoming increasingly important. Nine in ten respondents say a hotel's atmosphere is now a top factor in their choice, with customer service mattering most—even above decor or music.

Finally, the impact of artificial intelligence is expected to grow in 2024. Around half of travelers are open to using generative AI for planning their trips, with uses ranging from finding accommodations to planning activities, comparing flights, and managing changes or cancellations.

article_content: El Fortin, Mexico (CNN) — Roselia Rios wept as news spread of a castaway's survival after more than a year lost at sea. The dramatic rescue in the Marshall Islands meant bittersweet news for Rios: Jose Salvador Alvarenga survived, but her son, who was with him, did not make it. "For me, it was a devastating blow," Rios told CNN last week. "The pain is so great I can't explain it. I wouldn't wish this on anybody. Losing a child is the hardest thing to bear in life." Her son, 23-year-old Ezequiel Cordova, left from Mexico with Alvarenga in late 2012. Both men belonged to a small fishing cooperative and planned to spend a day fishing for sharks. But disaster struck. According to Alvarenga, wind pushed them off course, a storm hit, and their engines failed. Alvarenga reported that, after four weeks adrift, Cordova died of starvation because he wouldn't eat raw birds and turtles. He eventually had to throw Cordova's body overboard. "What else could I do?" Alvarenga said. Now, as Alvarenga begins his return to El Salvador, Rios mourns her son, over a year after he disappeared. Cordova's bedroom at their home in El Fortin remains unchanged — a simple green plaid blanket lies on the bed. Jovani Cordova, Ezequiel's brother, remembers him as a kind and hardworking person. "He was responsible for my mother. He worked at sea for her," he said. "He wanted to better himself. He didn't want to stay poor like us." The rural roads are so poor that travel by boat is often easier. Ezequiel often took a short boat ride to his work in nearby Costa Azul. Fellow fishermen at their cooperative, who earn about $150 a week, recall the frantic search for Ezequiel and Alvarenga after their boat disappeared. "My colleagues went fishing, and the next day they told me over radio that the engine had failed and the GPS was wet. We searched for them for seven or eight days with the authorities," said Bellarmino Rodrigues, the boat owner. "The governor provided a small aircraft, but we couldn't find them." Back at home, Rios told CNN that she is focused on one thing. "As a mother, I demand that the authorities allow me to speak to the survivor," she said. "Only then will I know what happened and what was done with my son's body. I deserve the truth." CNN's Catherine E. Shoichet contributed to this report.

article_content: Following discussions with the Pakistani government, US Secretary of State John Kerry stated that the United States is making progress in the fight against terrorism and hopes to end drone strikes 'very soon.' Speaking to a Pakistani television station, Kerry noted that President Barack Obama has established a 'very real timeline' to end these operations, although he did not provide exact dates. 'We hope it's going to be very, very soon,' Kerry said Thursday, according to a State Department transcript. Kerry expressed confidence in the progress, saying, 'I believe that we're on a good track. I think the program will end as we have eliminated most of the threat and continue to eliminate it.' He emphasized that ending the strikes depends on 'a number of factors' and that US officials are working closely with the Pakistani government. Later, the State Department released a statement clarifying Kerry’s comments: 'Today, the secretary referenced the changes that we expect to take place in that program over the course of time, but there is no exact timeline to provide.' The department reiterated the goal of reaching a point where the threat is eliminated and drones are no longer necessary. Marie Harf, a State Department spokeswoman, added, 'Now, we're all realistic about the fact that there is a threat that remains and that we have to keep up...the fight in this and other places around the world.' She stressed that there has been no change in US policy and that these comments reinforce positions officials have expressed for months. The US significantly increased drone strikes in Pakistan's tribal regions during the early years of Obama’s presidency. However, the number has declined due in part to al Qaeda’s weakening presence in Pakistan and a shift in focus to threats in other countries, such as Yemen. In May, President Obama defended the use of drone strikes as a 'necessary evil,' while calling for stricter oversight and caution as US security needs evolve. He stated that the United States prefers to capture, interrogate, and prosecute terrorists, but acknowledged this isn’t always possible due to terrorists hiding in remote locations, making ground operations unfeasible. Obama cautioned that, 'To say a military tactic is legal, or even effective, is not to say it is wise or moral in every instance.' He stressed the need for discipline and oversight to prevent abuse of drone technology. Drone operations in regions bordering Afghanistan have generated strong opposition in Pakistan, mainly because of civilian casualties, and have strained US-Pakistani relations. Tensions further escalated after the 2011 US raid in Abbottabad that killed Osama bin Laden.

S'exprimant à la télévision pakistanaise, Kerry a précisé que le président Barack Obama avait établi un 'calendrier très réel' pour mettre fin à ces opérations, bien qu'aucune date précise n'ait été donnée. 'Nous espérons que ce sera très, très bientôt', a déclaré Kerry jeudi, selon un compte rendu du département d'État. Kerry s'est dit confiant quant aux progrès réalisés, affirmant : 'Je pense que nous sommes sur la bonne voie. Le programme prendra fin une fois que nous aurons éliminé la majeure partie de la menace et que nous continuerons à l'éliminer.' Il a souligné que la fin des frappes dépend de 'nombreux facteurs' et que les responsables américains collaborent étroitement avec le gouvernement pakistanais. Plus tard, le département d'État a publié une déclaration pour clarifier les propos de Kerry : 'Aujourd'hui, le secrétaire a fait référence aux changements que nous prévoyons dans ce programme au fil du temps, mais il n'y a pas de calendrier précis à fournir.' Le département a réaffirmé l'objectif d'atteindre un point où la menace est éliminée et où les drones ne sont plus nécessaires. Marie Harf, porte-parole du département d'État, a ajouté : 'Nous sommes tous réalistes quant au fait qu'une menace subsiste et que nous devons poursuivre... la lutte ici et dans d'autres régions du monde.' Elle a insisté sur le fait qu'il n'y avait aucun changement de politique américaine, et que ces commentaires réaffirmaient les positions déjà exprimées depuis des mois. Les États-Unis ont fortement augmenté les frappes de drones dans les régions tribales du Pakistan durant les premières années de la présidence Obama. Cependant, leur nombre a diminué, en partie à cause de l'affaiblissement d'al-Qaïda au Pakistan et du recentrage des menaces vers d'autres pays, comme le Yémen. En mai, le président Obama a défendu l’utilisation des frappes de drones comme un 'mal nécessaire', tout en appelant à plus de prudence et de contrôle avec l’évolution des besoins sécuritaires américains. Il a déclaré que les États-Unis privilégiaient la capture, l’interrogatoire et la poursuite judiciaire des terroristes, mais il a reconnu que cela n’était pas toujours possible, parce que les terroristes se cachent dans des lieux isolés, ce qui rend les opérations terrestres impossibles. Obama a mis en garde : 'Dire qu'une tactique militaire est légale, voire efficace, ne signifie pas qu'elle soit judicieuse ou morale dans chaque cas.' Il a souligné l'importance de la discipline et du contrôle pour éviter des abus liés à l'utilisation des drones. Les opérations de drones dans les régions frontalières de l’Afghanistan ont suscité une forte opposition au Pakistan, principalement à cause des victimes civiles, et ont tendu les relations américano-pakistanaises. Les tensions se sont accentuées après le raid américain à Abbottabad en 2011, qui a tué Oussama ben Laden.

The UK government has finalized new regulations for cryptocurrencies, which will be introduced in phases starting in early 2024. These changes place certain cryptocurrency activities under the supervision of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), following Prime Minister Rishi Sunak’s 2022 pledge to position the UK as a global leader in digital asset innovation. The measure aims to drive economic growth, draw investment, and enhance consumer protection while maintaining the stability of the British financial system.

A central aspect of the new guidelines is that crypto exchanges and wallet providers must comply with the FCA’s robust anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing rules. This approach seeks to support a vibrant digital economy while increasing security for UK users.

Treasury Minister Andrew Griffith has expressed strong approval of these finalized plans, underscoring the UK’s appeal as a destination for cryptocurrency enterprises. He cited the country’s solid regulatory regime, broad financial sector, and ongoing support for fintech as key advantages.

The new framework also aims to more closely integrate cryptocurrencies with mainstream financial regulations, including clarity on handling specific crypto-assets and certain NFTs. This is expected to give businesses and individuals improved certainty and stability as the sector expands.

NFTs that function primarily as art or collectibles will generally stay outside of financial regulations. However, those used in transactions involving other crypto-assets or financial products may still be subject to oversight, providing clearer guidelines for creators, investors, and users. People involved in such NFT activities are advised to keep up to date on regulations to prevent any compliance issues.

Le gouvernement britannique a finalisé de nouvelles réglementations sur les cryptomonnaies, qui seront mises en place progressivement dès le début de 2024. Certaines activités liées aux crypto-actifs seront désormais supervisées par la Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), conformément à la promesse faite en 2022 par le Premier ministre Rishi Sunak de faire du Royaume-Uni un leader mondial dans l’innovation des actifs numériques. Cette décision vise à stimuler la croissance économique, attirer des investissements et renforcer la protection des consommateurs, tout en assurant la stabilité du système financier britannique.

L’une des principales mesures impose aux plateformes d’échange et aux fournisseurs de portefeuilles de cryptomonnaies de respecter les normes strictes de lutte contre le blanchiment d’argent et le financement du terrorisme de la FCA. Ce cadre vise à soutenir un secteur numérique dynamique et à sécuriser davantage les utilisateurs au Royaume-Uni.

Le ministre du Trésor, Andrew Griffith, a salué ces nouvelles règles, insistant sur l’attractivité du Royaume-Uni pour les entreprises du secteur crypto. Il a souligné la robustesse du système réglementaire britannique, la diversité du secteur financier et le soutien continu du gouvernement à l’innovation fintech.

Le dispositif prévoit aussi une meilleure intégration des cryptomonnaies dans la réglementation financière traditionnelle, notamment en clarifiant la gestion de certains crypto-actifs et d’une partie des NFT. Cela doit apporter plus de clarté et de stabilité à ceux qui évoluent dans cet univers.

Les NFT à vocation artistique ou de collection resteront en principe en dehors du champ de la régulation financière. En revanche, les NFT utilisés pour des transactions impliquant d’autres crypto-actifs ou des produits financiers pourront être soumis à réglementation, offrant ainsi un cadre plus clair aux créateurs, investisseurs et utilisateurs. Toute personne concernée par ces activités doit donc se tenir informée de l’évolution de la réglementation pour éviter les risques de non-conformité.

article_content: This remarkable moment showcases a cloud over the Welsh countryside that took the shape of the iconic Concorde passenger jet. Roy Peckham, 66, of Pontypridd, South Wales, spotted and photographed the plane-shaped cloud as it drifted through the evening sky. Peckham explained he was astonished that the cloud maintained its distinctive form long enough to capture the image. He noted the cloud appeared to be coming from the direction of the Brecon Beacons and as it approached, it became even more defined, closely resembling Concorde flying across the countryside—a sight he described as a 'once in a lifetime' photograph. Peckham, who runs a pony sanctuary, has a personal interest in aeroplanes as his son worked for British Airways as an engineer. He remarked, 'I would have loved to have flown on Concorde. Concorde, built in the 1960s, entered commercial service in 1976 as the first supersonic passenger aircraft, capable of cruising at more than 1,300 mph.
