Les attaques de rançongiciels continuent de croître dans le monde entier, les États-Unis étant particulièrement visés (près de 46 % des cas recensés). Anne Neuberger, conseillère adjointe à la sécurité nationale pour la cybersécurité et les technologies émergentes, a souligné lors d’une conférence en ligne que la situation persistera tant que les criminels seront payés. Les pirates cryptent généralement les données d'une organisation et demandent une rançon pour les débloquer; ils peuvent aussi voler des informations sensibles et menacer de les divulguer. Neuberger mentionne également le recours à l’intelligence artificielle pour surveiller la blockchain et détecter les fonds illicites. Selon Chainalysis, une firme d’analyse blockchain, les paiements en cryptomonnaies aux rançonneurs pourraient atteindre cette année leur deuxième plus haut niveau jamais enregistré.

Oakley Orange, a young boy from Strood, Kent, experienced a life-threatening health crisis following an extreme allergic reaction to his epilepsy medication. Twelve days after beginning carbamazepine, prescribed for his epileptic seizures, Oakley developed headaches and a rash that rapidly turned into a serious emergency. His body broke out in blisters, his skin was shedding, and he lost both his hair and nails—clear signs of the rare condition known as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS).

This severe reaction also damaged Oakley’s internal organs, requiring life support and sedation for three weeks. His parents, Lorraine and Steven, have been told his chances of surviving are about 65 percent. Lorraine has since started advocating for improved medication labeling and greater public awareness of potential side effects, expressing her shock at the extreme consequences of what otherwise seemed to be a routine prescription.

Oakley's initial symptoms were mistaken for a virus and later measles before a dermatologist correctly identified SJS. The disease covered his entire body in painful blisters, leading to intensive medical care: powerful pain relief, full-body bandages, and continuous monitoring.

The family's ordeal has drawn widespread support, including from public figures like Coleen Nolan, Peter Andre, and Shane Byrne, and the community has raised over £3,000 to help with related expenses.

Stevens-Johnson Syndrome—and its more severe form, Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis—are extremely rare, occurring in about three out of every million people and carrying a high fatality risk. Both are listed as very rare side effects on the NHS and by carbamazepine's manufacturer, Novartis, who emphasize their commitment to patient safety and note that these risks appear in product documentation.

Lorraine Orange urges families to carefully read medication information leaflets and for pharmaceutical companies to strengthen warnings, noting that such severe reactions can arise from various medications. The family remains profoundly grateful for the kindness and support that has carried them through this incredibly difficult time. To help, visit the 'Oakley Donation Page' on Facebook or their GoFundMe site.

article_content: Playwright Larissa FastHorse, a 2020 MacArthur Fellow and co-founder of Indigenous Direction, is working to reshape perceptions of Indigenous culture in the arts. Four years ago, FastHorse and her creative partner Ty Defoe began advising organizers of the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to make the event more respectful of Indigenous peoples. Their input led to the removal of pilgrim characters from the parade and, in 2020, prompted a land acknowledgment recognizing the Lenape people, original inhabitants of Manhattan. 'Sixty million people heard it and everyone survived,' FastHorse remarked, emphasizing that acknowledging history doesn’t harm audiences. A member of the Sicangu Lakota Nation, FastHorse describes Thanksgiving's historical narrative as 'a wild mess of muckiness.' She explores these themes in 'The Thanksgiving Play,' a satirical comedy about four well-intentioned white people attempting to create a politically correct school play for Native American Heritage Month. Reflecting on the play’s reception, FastHorse recalls the relief and joy upon hearing audiences laugh at its opening preview, recognizing it as a turning point. 'The Thanksgiving Play' ran earlier this year on Broadway and has become one of the most-produced plays in America, staged at various universities and community theaters. FastHorse attributes the play’s creation to challenges she faced with casting: as a Native playwright, she was often told her plays, which featured Native American actors, were 'uncastable.' Determined to push through these barriers, she wrote a play for non-Indigenous, white-presenting actors. FastHorse also discusses her experiences as a comedy writer, noting that audiences often expect Indigenous works to be serious or somber. She describes her plays as 'satirical comedy' or 'farce,' and sometimes feels compelled to assure audiences it’s okay to laugh at Native-centered humor. Despite her eventual success, FastHorse spent years living below the poverty line, with funders often hesitant unless her work fit narrow expectations of 'Native American' themes. She stresses that any work she creates is inherently Native American because of her identity, regardless of venue. FastHorse acknowledges recent efforts to diversify Broadway but calls for more equitable support and development time for nonwhite playwrights. She believes genuine inclusion requires more than urgency, highlighting ongoing gaps in casting, cultural outreach, and audience engagement. Currently, FastHorse is adapting the musical 'Peter Pan' for Broadway. To address the problematic portrayal of Indigenous peoples in the original, her version retains Tiger Lily’s name but reimagines the character as leader of a group composed of people from extinct cultures around the world. This new narrative portrays Neverland as a refuge where these cultures can survive, preserve their traditions, and one day return to the world. The interview was produced and edited by Ann Marie Baldonado and Susan Nyakundi for broadcast, and adapted for the web by Bridget Bentz, Molly Seavy-Nesper, and Beth Novey.

Elle aborde ces thèmes dans « The Thanksgiving Play », une comédie satirique sur quatre personnes blanches bien intentionnées tentant de créer une pièce d’école politiquement correcte pour le mois du patrimoine amérindien. FastHorse raconte aussi son expérience de dramaturge comique, notant que beaucoup attendent des œuvres autochtones qu’elles soient sérieuses ou dramatiques. Elle décrit ses pièces comme des « comédies satiriques » ou des « farces », et se sent parfois obligée de rassurer les spectateurs qu’on peut rire de l’humour autour des cultures autochtones. Malgré sa réussite actuelle, FastHorse a longtemps vécu sous le seuil de pauvreté, les financeurs hésitant si son travail ne cadrait pas avec une vision étroite des « thèmes amérindiens ». Elle insiste sur le fait que toute œuvre créée est fondamentalement autochtone du fait de son identité, peu importe où elle est jouée. FastHorse remarque les efforts récents pour diversifier Broadway mais appelle à un soutien et un temps de développement équitable pour les auteurs non-blancs. Selon elle, une véritable inclusion nécessite plus qu’un sentiment d’urgence et suppose de combler des écarts persistants dans le casting, l’accompagnement culturel et l’engagement du public. Actuellement, FastHorse adapte la comédie musicale « Peter Pan » pour Broadway. Pour corriger les représentations problématiques dans la version originale, elle garde le nom de Tiger Lily mais la réinvente comme cheffe d’un groupe de personnes issues de cultures disparues à travers le monde. Ce nouveau récit fait de Neverland un refuge où ces cultures peuvent survivre, préserver leurs traditions, espérer un jour retourner dans le monde. L’entretien a été produit et monté par Ann Marie Baldonado et Susan Nyakundi, puis adapté pour le web par Bridget Bentz, Molly Seavy-Nesper et Beth Novey.

A devastating fire broke out in the early hours Monday at a family home in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, leading to the death of 15-year-old Shaun Van Straaten and leaving his family members seriously injured. Authorities suspect the blaze was set deliberately by David Potts, the ex-partner of Shaun’s mother, Tracy Jones. Potts, 39, also died shortly after the fire began around 4:50am.

Shaun, his mother Tracy, 18-year-old sister Cailin, and 4-year-old brother Zach were all hospitalized after suffering burns and smoke inhalation. Police confirmed that Shaun succumbed to his injuries while the others remain in critical condition.

Reports suggest Potts had recently endured a volatile breakup with Jones, and he had posted distressing messages on Facebook expressing his emotional turmoil. On the morning of the fire, he allegedly arrived at their Barlow Road residence, poured petrol over himself, and—following an argument—set himself on fire. Witnesses say he declared, 'If I can’t have you, no one will,' before igniting the blaze.

Neighbours described awakening to the sound of screaming and chaos as flames rapidly spread. Tracy and Cailin attempted to extinguish the fire, and neighbour Kevin Pearce managed to rescue Tracy through a window. Firefighters ultimately freed Shaun and Zach.

Police are treating the incident as suspicious but are not looking for further suspects. There had been previous police involvement regarding Potts’s behaviour toward Jones, and the case has been referred to the Independent Police Complaints Commission. Chief Superintendent Mark Roberts called the situation 'absolutely tragic' and requested information from the public to assist in the investigation.

Rickrolling has made its way to Vine, Twitter’s app for sharing six-second videos. On Monday, 16-year-old Cleveland native Will Smidlein found a way to bypass Vine’s strict time limit, uploading the entire 3-minute, 33-second song 'Never Gonna Give You Up' by Rick Astley—a classic '80s pop hit and an iconic Internet meme. 'I think I broke Vine,' Smidlein tweeted after his upload. Listed as a Web developer in his bio, Smidlein demonstrated his technical skills by sharing the full song with Vine’s 13 million users.

Smidlein took advantage of Vine’s launch on Google’s Android platform that day. With his experience in Android development, he decompiled the app’s code and modified the upload settings. In an interview with The Verge, Smidlein declined to share the technical details of how he bypassed the restriction and said his intent was merely to entertain his friends and followers.

After the video went live, a Twitter engineer contacted him to request removal, which he did, but the video had already gone viral. 'Sorry, Twitter/Vine engineers,' he wrote. 'I tried to keep it quiet, but the internet never forgets.' Twitter did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Smidlein stated he would share more about his discovery after the vulnerability is fixed and apologized to the developers for the trouble caused. However, many online commenters praised his ingenuity, suggesting he should be thanked or even hired by Vine.

The Rickrolling meme began in 2007 on 4chan, where users would be misdirected by links that unexpectedly led to Rick Astley’s hit. The meme has since become a widespread Internet phenomenon, with Astley’s video garnering over 64 million views on his official channel and another 68 million on a 'Rickroll’d' upload. It has also been used in April Fool’s jokes, including Google’s 2008 prank and a bipartisan stunt in Oregon’s legislature in 2011.

Lundi, Will Smidlein, un adolescent de 16 ans originaire de Cleveland, a réussi à contourner la limite stricte de temps de Vine, téléchargeant l'intégralité de la chanson « Never Gonna Give You Up » de Rick Astley (3 minutes et 33 secondes)—un tube des années 80 devenu un célèbre mème sur Internet. « Je crois que j'ai cassé Vine », a tweeté Smidlein après sa publication. Se décrivant comme développeur web dans sa bio, Smidlein a prouvé ses compétences en partageant la chanson complète avec les 13 millions d'utilisateurs de Vine.

Smidlein a profité du lancement de Vine sur la plateforme Android de Google ce jour-là. Grâce à son expérience en développement Android, il a décompilé le code de l'application et modifié les paramètres de téléchargement. Dans une interview accordée à The Verge, Smidlein a refusé de préciser la méthode utilisée pour contourner la restriction et a indiqué que son geste visait uniquement à amuser ses amis et abonnés.

Après la publication de la vidéo, un ingénieur de Twitter lui a demandé de la retirer, ce qu'il a fait, mais la vidéo était déjà devenue virale. « Désolé, ingénieurs de Twitter/Vine », a-t-il écrit. « J'ai essayé de garder ça discret, mais Internet n'oublie jamais. » Twitter n'a pas immédiatement répondu à une demande de commentaire.

Smidlein a expliqué qu'il partagerait plus de détails une fois la faille corrigée, et s'est excusé auprès des développeurs pour les désagréments causés. Cependant, de nombreux internautes ont applaudi son ingéniosité, certains suggérant même que Vine devrait le remercier ou l'embaucher.

Le mème Rickrolling est né en 2007 sur 4chan, où des internautes étaient redirigés vers la chanson de Rick Astley via des liens surprises. Ce mème est devenu un véritable phénomène sur Internet, la vidéo d'Astley ayant recueilli plus de 64 millions de vues sur sa chaîne officielle et 68 millions sur une version nommée « Rickroll’d ». Elle a aussi servi de blague pour le 1er avril, notamment lors du canular organisé par Google en 2008 et d'une plaisanterie bipartisane à la législature de l’Oregon en 2011.

The U.S. Department of Education is moving ahead with a revised plan to cancel student debt, this time using powers granted by the Higher Education Act of 1965. This follows the Supreme Court’s rejection of President Biden’s earlier proposal. The newly outlined process will involve extensive rulemaking, which includes several rounds of negotiations and public input sessions. Recently, officials released the list of negotiators and a briefing paper detailing the five main borrower groups the Department aims to support: borrowers with increased balances due to unpaid interest, those who qualified but did not enroll in relief programs, graduates whose debt outweighs their post-college earnings, borrowers who started repayment before new benefit programs were available, and individuals suffering financial hardship not properly addressed by current systems.

While exact eligibility criteria and relief amounts are undecided and subject to negotiation, these efforts underscore the Department’s focus on those facing payment challenges beyond their control. As the COVID-19 loan payment pause ends, millions of borrowers will have to restart payments. To ease the transition, there is a 12-month period in which missed payments will not affect credit reports. Despite setbacks, such as the Supreme Court’s action, lawmakers including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez remain hopeful, highlighting that alternative debt relief methods are being developed for rollout in the coming year.

Récemment, les autorités ont dévoilé la liste des négociateurs ainsi qu'un document précisant les cinq groupes principaux d’emprunteurs concernés : ceux dont le solde de prêt a augmenté à cause des intérêts impayés, ceux éligibles à une aide mais non inscrits, les diplômés dont la dette dépasse largement les revenus post-études, les emprunteurs ayant commencé à rembourser avant l’instauration de nouveaux avantages, et ceux qui affrontent des difficultés financières non prises en compte par le système actuel.

Les critères d’éligibilité précis et les montants de la remise restent à définir et pourraient évoluer au fil des négociations. Cette démarche montre l’engagement du ministère pour soutenir les personnes en difficulté face au remboursement de leur prêt. Avec la fin du report lié au COVID-19, des millions d’emprunteurs reprennent les paiements. Pour accompagner cette reprise, une période de transition de 12 mois est prévue durant laquelle les retards de paiement ne seront pas déclarés aux agences de crédit. Malgré les obstacles, comme le revers du côté de la Cour suprême, des responsables politiques comme Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez restent optimistes et rappellent que des solutions alternatives d’annulation de dette sont en cours d’élaboration pour l’an prochain.

article_content: A British man faced one of the UK’s largest phone bills after his mobile was stolen and used to rack up £15,000 in charges within two hours. Mike Clear, a 34-year-old advertising executive from east London, was pickpocketed while on holiday in Alicante, Spain. Thieves exploited his SIM card with specialized software, repeatedly calling a premium rate number costing up to £21 per minute. Experts believe the number was linked to the criminals’ own accounts.  Clear’s usual monthly bill of around £100 skyrocketed to nearly £15,000. For several days, he believed he would be forced to pay, but phone provider O2 investigated and canceled the fraudulent charges. Clear wants to warn others, explaining that SIM card fraud can be as harmful as credit card theft. He notes that even with a passcode, criminals can remove the SIM and use it in devices that generate enormous bills.  He urges anyone whose phone goes missing to immediately inform their provider and the police. Trading Standards stresses that prompt reporting offers fraud protections similar to those in other cases, like credit card fraud. O2’s fraud team identified the suspicious activity, swiftly blocked the account, and told Clear he wouldn’t be held responsible for the charges.  Clear, his wife Alana, and their young son are relieved but hope their experience serves as a cautionary tale. The episode highlights that losing a phone can have more severe consequences than losing a wallet, as phones can be used for significant financial fraud.

Mike Clear, cadre publicitaire de 34 ans originaire de l’est de Londres, a été victime de pickpockets alors qu’il était en vacances à Alicante, en Espagne. Les voleurs ont exploité sa carte SIM à l’aide d’un logiciel spécialisé, appelant sans relâche un numéro surtaxé facturé jusqu’à 21 £ la minute. Pendant plusieurs jours, il a cru devoir payer la totalité, mais son opérateur O2 a enquêté et a finalement annulé les frais frauduleux. Clear souhaite prévenir le public : la fraude à la carte SIM peut faire autant de dégâts qu’un vol de carte bancaire. Il explique que, même avec un code, les malfaiteurs peuvent retirer la SIM et l’utiliser dans des appareils qui génèrent des factures astronomiques.  Il recommande à toute personne dont le téléphone disparaît de prévenir immédiatement son opérateur et la police. Trading Standards rappelle qu’un signalement rapide permet de bénéficier de protections similaires à d’autres fraudes bancaires, comme le clonage de carte. L’équipe anti-fraude d’O2 a détecté l’activité suspecte, bloqué le compte sans délai et informé Clear qu’il ne serait pas redevable des frais.  Clear, son épouse Alana et leur jeune fils sont soulagés, mais espèrent que leur mésaventure servira d’avertissement. L’histoire montre que le vol d’un téléphone peut avoir des conséquences bien plus graves qu’un simple vol de portefeuille, car les mobiles peuvent ouvrir la voie à des fraudes de grande ampleur.

article_content: Six people, including three teenagers, lost their lives in a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 70 in Etna, Ohio, on Tuesday morning. The crash involved a charter bus carrying students from Tuscarawas Valley Local Schools, according to officials. More than a dozen individuals were injured. Authorities state the collision occurred just before 9 a.m. local time and involved five vehicles—a charter bus, two commercial vehicles, and two passenger vehicles—traveling westbound on the highway. At least three vehicles subsequently caught fire. Ohio Governor Mike DeWine called the situation a 'worst nightmare' and confirmed the bus was transporting students to the Ohio School Boards Association conference in Columbus. Jennifer Homendy, chair of the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), said investigators are still clarifying the sequence of events. An SUV carrying people associated with the bus group was traveling behind the bus. Some details of the crash remain conflicting. Three bus passengers—John Mosely, 18, of Mineral City; Jeffery Worrell, 18, of Bolivar; and Katelyn Owens, 15, of Mineral City—were pronounced dead at the scene. Fifteen students and the bus driver were taken to nearby hospitals. Three occupants of one passenger vehicle—Dave Kennat, 56, of Navarre; Kristy Gaynor, 39, of Zoar; and Shannon Wigfield, 45, of Bolivar—also died at the scene. The driver of a commercial vehicle suffered non-life-threatening injuries, while another driver was treated at the scene. The driver of the second passenger vehicle was also hospitalized. Derek Varansky, superintendent of Tuscarawas Valley Local Schools, said 54 students, parents, and teachers were on board the bus. Samantha Bosler, a 17-year-old student and saxophone player aboard the bus, described the impact. She recounted that a truck crashed into the back of the bus, lifting its tires off the ground and causing fire and smoke. Bosler recounted seeing classmates pinned and unconscious but said she was mostly unharmed. 'We lost people who mattered to our band today,' Bosler said, describing her heartbreak. Pioneer Trails stated it is cooperating fully with authorities to determine the cause of the accident. The company offered condolences and said it would make no further comment during the ongoing investigation. The NTSB will begin on-site investigation Wednesday, collecting evidence such as vehicle cameras. The full investigation is expected to take 12 to 18 months, with a preliminary report anticipated within weeks.

article_content: If you’re considering buying an electric vehicle (EV), it may be smart to wait until early 2024—though there are important details to consider. Starting in January 2024, both new and used federal EV tax credits will be available as immediate discounts or cash rebates at dealerships. Currently, buyers benefit from tax credits (up to $7,500 for new EVs and $4,000 for used ones), but have to wait until tax season to claim them. Since these credits only offset what you owe in taxes, buyers with lower tax bills—often those shopping for used vehicles—may not get the full benefit. Beginning next year, shoppers can transfer the EV credit to the dealer, who will then reduce the car’s price or offer a cash rebate. Dealer participation requires IRS registration, but dealers will be reimbursed within 72 hours by the IRS. Industry advocates, like Plug In America and Recurrent researcher Liz Najman, say this change should improve access to credits, especially for low- and middle-income buyers who gain more from upfront savings than delayed rebates. However, new IRS guidelines are coming, and EV credit eligibility for 2024 will depend on factors such as where the vehicle and its battery components are made, as well as whether materials come from 'foreign entities of concern.' For example, the Tesla Model 3 may only qualify for a partial credit next year, while other vehicles could become newly eligible. EY Americas’ Akshay Honnatti notes that some vehicles might not qualify for the full credit during the transition. Experts recommend that buyers weigh the potential benefits of waiting for the new rules in 2024, but should also check for late 2023 deals as dealers shift to the new program. Shoppers should remember that higher demand for instant rebates might raise used EV prices in 2024, and not all dealers may participate.

article_content: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar confirmed that India and Vietnam have aligned interests in bolstering cooperation throughout the Indo-Pacific, emphasizing ASEAN’s pivotal role and the contributions of the Quad alliance. Addressing the Diplomatic Academy of Vietnam, Jaishankar underlined how the two countries, through their autonomous policies, advance a multipolar and rule-based international system. The Quad—comprising the United States, India, Japan, and Australia—continues to increase cooperation, especially in defense and energy, amid heightened concerns over China’s expanding influence. The Indo-Pacific region, including critical maritime routes like the South China Sea, is a hotspot for territorial disputes involving China and several Southeast Asian countries such as Vietnam, the Philippines, Taiwan, Brunei, and Malaysia. China’s construction of artificial islands and military installations there has escalated tensions, and similar disagreements exist with Japan over the East China Sea. ASEAN, with its ten member states from Southeast Asia, serves as a central regional organization. India, together with other major countries like the US, China, Japan, and Australia, acts as a dialogue partner. Recent years have seen rapid growth in India’s relations with ASEAN, particularly focusing on trade, investments, security, and defense ties. On his trip, Jaishankar met Vietnam’s Foreign Minister Bui Thanh Son to discuss enhancing cooperation in sectors such as trade, energy, defense, and maritime security. These talks come in light of China’s increasing regional assertiveness. Jaishankar also took part in the 18th India-Vietnam Joint Commission meeting held in Hanoi. After Vietnam, his regional engagement will proceed with a visit to Singapore.

La zone indo-pacifique, comprenant notamment la mer de Chine méridionale, reste un foyer de litiges territoriaux impliquant la Chine et plusieurs pays d’Asie du Sud-Est, tels que le Vietnam, les Philippines, Taïwan, Brunei et la Malaisie. Les infrastructures militaires et îles artificielles construites par la Chine y exacerbent les tensions ; des différends similaires existent aussi entre la Chine et le Japon en mer de Chine orientale. L’ASEAN, qui rassemble dix pays d’Asie du Sud-Est, est une organisation régionale majeure. L’Inde ainsi que les États-Unis, la Chine, le Japon et l’Australie, sont partenaires de dialogue. Les relations entre l’Inde et l’ASEAN se sont nettement développées ces dernières années, surtout dans le commerce, les investissements, la sécurité et la défense. Au cours de sa visite, Jaishankar a rencontré son homologue vietnamien Bui Thanh Son afin d’approfondir la coopération bilatérale dans les domaines du commerce, de l’énergie, de la défense et de la sécurité maritime, dans un contexte de plus grande affirmation chinoise. article_content: Amoako Boafo, a leading figure in the art world, has returned to Ghana, where his self-portrait is currently exhibited. In conversation with journalist Stephen Smith, Boafo shared that he never initially intended to become an artist. Despite his international success, he remains a reluctant interviewee. Not yet 40, Boafo’s works have been shown by major dealer Larry Gagosian, who called him 'the future of portraiture.' Growing up in Accra, Ghana, Boafo enjoyed drawing superheroes with friends but did not consider art a career option. He noted that, as a child, he never realized portraiture was an art form artists of color could reference and study. Today, he finds it overwhelming that his work is so highly regarded. Boafo’s story is one of overcoming poverty to achieve global recognition. He supported his mother and grandmother as a child. Now, his portraits of Black subjects—often painted with his fingertips—can command seven-figure sums at auction. Remarkably, his artwork has appeared on Jeff Bezos’s rocket ship, making him among the first artists to exhibit in space. He is at the heart of a vibrant West African art scene that values collaboration and mutual support. Boafo recently returned to Accra to oversee an artists’ residency at his studio and participate in a group exhibition. Though based in Vienna, he remains connected to his home country and community. Born in 1984, Boafo lost his father at a young age, and his mother worked as a cook. He taught himself painting while she was away and briefly supported himself as a semi-professional tennis player. A patron funded his art school tuition, leading him to graduate top of his class at Ghanatta College of Art and Design in 2008. In 2014, Boafo moved to Europe with Austrian artist Sunanda Mesquita, who is now his wife. His breakthrough came in 2018 when renowned artist Kehinde Wiley discovered his work on Instagram and recommended him to major galleries. Wiley's early support inspired Boafo to foster a supportive artistic community. Boafo’s Accra studio, dot.ateliers, was designed by esteemed Ghanaian-British architect Sir David Adjaye. The sand-colored, breezeblock structure is cooled by ocean winds, with a winding staircase leading to his workspace, overlooking both the sea and city. The rooftop, with three points, pays homage to Jean-Michel Basquiat’s crown motif. In just a few years, Boafo has gone from selling paintings for about £100 ($125) in Ghana to having his works sold at international auctions for millions. Following the Black Lives Matter movement, his art attracted more attention as museums and collectors sought works by Black artists. Boafo is appreciative of the recognition but says his passion remains rooted in painting rather than publicity. Through his residency program, he provides opportunities for other artists, crediting his own success with giving him the chance to assist his creative community. Boafo's self-portrait features in the exhibition 'In and Out of Time,' curated by Ekow Eshun at Gallery 1957 in Accra, open until December 12. The painting, created with his fingertips, shows him from behind with arms raised, and he signs some works as 'Amoako Boafo King.' Gallery 1957, owned by Marwan Zahkem, was an early supporter of Boafo. Zahkem compares the current West African art scene to the Young British Artists movement, calling Boafo the 'Damien Hirst or Tracey Emin' of West Africa. Osei Bonsu from Tate Modern featured Boafo's 'Yellow Dress' on the cover of his book 'African Art Now,' with the painting selling for £675,000 at Christie’s. Boafo's current auction record reaches £2.5 million. Bonsu describes how Boafo’s art bridges classical portraiture and the modern 'selfie' era. Boafo himself says he would rather be painting than talking about his process, stating that non-painting activities are less exciting—except for playing tennis.

Bien qu’il vive à Vienne, il reste très attaché à son pays natal. Né en 1984, Boafo a perdu son père très jeune et sa mère travaillait comme cuisinière. Il a appris à peindre en autodidacte pendant l’absence de sa mère et a brièvement soutenu sa famille comme joueur de tennis semi-professionnel. Un mécène a financé ses études artistiques, lui permettant de terminer major de sa promotion à la Ghanatta College of Art and Design en 2008. En 2014, Boafo a déménagé en Europe avec l’artiste autrichienne Sunanda Mesquita, devenue sa femme. Sa percée a eu lieu en 2018 lorsque l’artiste renommé Kehinde Wiley a découvert son travail sur Instagram et l’a recommandé à de grandes galeries. Le soutien initial de Wiley a inspiré Boafo à encourager une communauté artistique soudée. L’atelier de Boafo à Accra, dot.ateliers, a été conçu par le célèbre architecte ghanéo-britannique Sir David Adjaye. Le bâtiment, couleur sable et en blocs de béton, est ventilé par la brise marine et possède un escalier en colimaçon menant à son espace de travail, avec vue sur la mer et la ville. Le toit à trois pointes fait référence à la couronne de Jean-Michel Basquiat. En quelques années, Boafo est passé de la vente de tableaux à environ 100 £ (125 $) au Ghana à des ventes atteignant des millions dans les enchères internationales. Suite au mouvement Black Lives Matter, son art a suscité plus d’intérêt alors que musées et collectionneurs cherchaient des œuvres d’artistes noirs. Boafo apprécie la reconnaissance mais reste avant tout passionné par la peinture plutôt que la promotion. Grâce à son programme de résidence, il offre des opportunités à d’autres artistes, estimant que sa réussite lui permet d’aider la communauté créative. L’autoportrait de Boafo figure dans l’exposition « In and Out of Time », organisée par Ekow Eshun à la Galerie 1957 à Accra, jusqu’au 12 décembre. Réalisé du bout des doigts, le tableau le montre de dos, les bras levés, et il signe certaines de ses œuvres « Amoako Boafo King ». La Galerie 1957, propriété de Marwan Zahkem, fut l’un des premiers soutiens de Boafo. Zahkem compare la scène artistique ouest-africaine actuelle à celle des Young British Artists, qualifiant Boafo de « Damien Hirst ou Tracey Emin » de l’Afrique de l’Ouest. Osei Bonsu de la Tate Modern a choisi « Yellow Dress » pour la couverture de son livre « African Art Now », l’œuvre s’étant vendue 675 000 £ chez Christie’s. Le record de Boafo atteint 2,5 millions de livres. Bonsu explique que l’art de Boafo crée un lien entre le portrait classique et l’ère du selfie. Boafo lui-même préfère peindre plutôt que d’expliquer son processus et dit que les activités en dehors de la peinture sont moins excitantes—sauf le tennis.

The Indian government is examining the legal prospects of transferring unclaimed funds from the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account to the Consolidated Fund of India, while maintaining a provision to refund investors who come forward with claims at a later stage. Renewed focus has been placed on these funds following the recent death of Sahara Group founder Subrata Roy.

According to official sources, since the account’s creation over a decade ago, there have been very few claimants seeking refunds. In 2012, the Supreme Court upheld an order by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), directing Sahara India Real Estate Corp and Sahara Housing Investment Corp to refund money to investors, with interest, by depositing it with the regulator after finding that the companies had raised money through optionally fully convertible debentures without SEBI’s permission.

The Supreme Court stated that if SEBI is unable to trace certain subscribers, those amounts could be appropriated by the government. Now, options are being assessed to transfer the money to the Consolidated Fund of India, with a separate account to ensure that future claimants can still be reimbursed. Officials suggest that unused funds could potentially support public welfare programs, though the matter will undergo further legal analysis.

As of March 31, 2023, approximately ₹25,163 crore had been recovered, with only ₹138 crore paid out to 17,526 applications covering 48,326 accounts. Earlier this year, after a Supreme Court order, ₹5,000 crore was transferred to the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies for legitimate claim payments to Sahara Group of Cooperative Societies depositors, and a dedicated portal for refunds was launched by Home and Cooperatives Minister Amit Shah in July. The latest court order mandates that this ₹5,000 crore be disbursed to eligible depositors within nine months, with any remaining funds returned to the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account.

The government’s ongoing review aims to balance public benefit with investor rights, ensuring appropriate legal channels remain open for potential claimants.

article_content: Shrien Dewani could face his first public questioning under oath regarding the murder of his wife Anni during their honeymoon in South Africa, as a UK inquest into her death may be resumed. The North London coroner has reportedly informed Dewani, a care home businessman, that resuming the inquest into the 2010 death—previously paused during the police investigation—is under consideration. A South African court in December acquitted Dewani of involvement in Anni's murder, though Anni's family expressed concerns that Dewani was not required to testify. South African prosecutors previously alleged Dewani, who is bisexual, arranged the murder to conceal his double life. However, Judge Jeanette Traverso dismissed the prosecution's case before Dewani could take the stand. North London coroner Andrew Walker has now contacted individuals involved, stating he is ready to resume the inquest, according to The Sun. Anni's father Vinod Hindocha and her uncle Ashok Hindocha are reportedly set to meet with Walker to discuss the case. MailOnline reached out to the coroner's office for comment but received no response. A formal complaint was recently lodged against Judge Traverso by the Higher Education Transformation Network (HETN), a group of South African academics and lawyers, alleging 'gross judicial bias and misconduct.' The judge halted the trial after Dewani's counsel argued the prosecution case was flawed. Dewani, 34, spent months contesting extradition in the UK before being sent to South Africa, where he was acquitted of orchestrating Anni's murder. Anni, who was raised in Sweden, was shot dead while the couple traveled through a suburb of Cape Town on November 13, 2010. Dewani was left at the roadside after the car she was in was hijacked. Anni's family, represented by Vinod and Ashok Hindocha, stated the trial did not allow the full case to be heard, particularly as Dewani did not testify. Three men—Zola Tongo, Mziwamadoda Qwabe, and Xolile Mngeni—were convicted for their role in the killing, claiming Dewani orchestrated a staged hijacking in which Anni would be killed and he would survive. Judge Traverso found their evidence unreliable and dismissed the case before Dewani could give evidence. Throughout the trial, delays and the dismissal of substantial evidence complicated proceedings. Key witnesses, such as German escort Leopold Leisser and self-proclaimed middleman Monde Mbolombo (who was granted immunity), were limited in their testimony. Dewani, who underwent psychiatric treatment in South Africa, was never called to testify and has always denied involvement in Anni's murder.

article_content: Surrey County Council is facing criticism for spending over £4,000 on a two-day workshop at historic Farnham Castle. The event involved 26 senior Conservative councillors and officers. Opposition politicians and some local residents have labeled the spending wasteful, arguing that taxpayer money was used inappropriately, especially as the council handles significant budget cuts that could lead to 650 job losses. The 12th-century Farnham Castle, known for its historic charm and 32 bedrooms, was chosen for the council's event. Chief Executive David McNulty defended the workshop, stating it was a cost-effective way to tackle complex challenges and that positive results are already evident. Communities Secretary Eric Pickles previously suggested councils should avoid pricey away days, advising them to use their own facilities or share spaces with neighboring councils to save money. Local resident Greg Tiller echoed public concerns, remarking that he would enjoy a break at a castle if he didn’t have to pay for it himself.

article_content: An anonymous 25-year-old man with diphallia—a rare condition in which a person is born with two penises—has published a memoir titled Double Header. The author first gained attention in January after posting photos of his genitalia to Reddit under the username DoubleD*ckDude. While he has openly discussed his condition, he chooses to remain anonymous, explaining to Rolling Stone magazine that going public would subject him to unwanted attention and define him solely by his condition. Diphallia affects approximately one in every six million boys in the U.S. Most cases involve surgical removal of one penis during infancy, but the author’s parents declined surgery due to concerns after his mother experienced two miscarriages before his birth in 1989. He expresses gratitude for his parents’ decision and support, especially during challenging teenage years. In his 76-page memoir, the author describes both the positive and negative aspects of living with diphallia. He reveals having one set of testicles and two fully functional penises, each capable of independent erection, climax, urination, and ejaculation. He has engaged in relationships with both men and women and claims to have had sexual experiences with over 1,000 partners. He says curiosity about his condition extends to both heterosexual and bisexual individuals. The author discusses how his anatomy has led to unique sexual experiences, including group encounters. He also mentions a medical challenge: his prostate fills with seminal fluid and requires regular release, a procedure he used to have performed by a urologist but can now do himself or with his boyfriend’s help. His openness about having diphallia has helped him connect with others who feel isolated. He hopes his book, published under the pen name Diphallic Dude, will encourage readers to accept their bodies, bringing positivity to a world he sees as sometimes negative.

In addition, renowned designer Karl Lagerfeld has revealed that Kendall will front his Spring/Summer 2015 campaign, joining established models Sasha Luss, Ming Xi, and Baptiste Giabiconi. The federal government is seeking greater transparency about nursing home ownership, aiming to empower consumers with better information about who runs these facilities. This move could help highlight problematic actors within the nursing home industry. However, unless the newly mandated disclosures are easily accessible, their benefit to prospective residents and families may remain limited.

Alongside new rules for disclosing nursing home owners and operators, the Department of Health and Human Services released a significant report examining the relationship between ownership and quality of care. Authored by David Stevenson, chair of the Department of Health Policy at Vanderbilt University School of Medicine, and colleagues, the report challenges the widespread belief that private equity firms are chiefly responsible for poor care in nursing homes. While private equity facilities show slightly lower quality and sometimes experience declines after acquisition, these firms accounted for only 5 percent of nursing homes in 2022 (about 900 out of 18,000), and their presence is shrinking.

Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), which own about 9 percent of nursing homes, have maintained steady shares since 2019 and display similar quality concerns. Other for-profit chains owned approximately 6,800 facilities, while 'mom-and-pop' owners and not-for-profits operated about 3,200 and 3,500 homes, respectively.

Evaluating nursing home quality remains challenging due to unreliable measures. Studies often rely on the government’s Nursing Home Compare five-star rating system, which better captures safety than patient experience or overall care. Deficiency reports from state inspectors are also inconsistent. Nevertheless, such studies provide a broad industry overview, typically assembled from multiple datasets (this report used six). However, it remains difficult for consumers to discover the ownership of specific facilities, especially when chains are involved. If a chain with a poor track record acquires a facility, its quality may deteriorate, yet consumers currently lack ways to assess this history. Between 2016 and 2021, about 3,000 facilities changed hands.

Tracking ownership is complex. Owners and operators are often different entities; sometimes an operator leases from a REIT or another company, and ownership is often buried within layered partnerships. In smaller operations, owners and operators are typically the same, but larger chains function differently. 

The new rules from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) require facilities to report detailed information on their ownership and management when applying for or renewing Medicare/Medicaid certification, or after ownership changes. Reporting now extends to entities with management or financial control, with CMS defining private equity and REITs for clarity. 

CMS has pledged to make this information public about a year after submission, though details on access are pending. Without straightforward, consumer-friendly access, the data may be of limited practical value. Although the Affordable Care Act of 2010 required such transparency, the rules were only finalized recently, previously resulting in restricted data being available.

Around 1.3 million Americans currently reside in nursing facilities. About half are there for long-term care, while the rest stay short-term post-hospitalization. Surveys show that location remains a primary factor in choosing a facility, but more information about quality and ownership could support more informed decisions.
translated_content:
Le gouvernement fédéral cherche à rendre la propriété des maisons de retraite plus transparente afin de donner aux consommateurs de meilleures informations sur qui gère ces établissements. Cette démarche pourrait aider à mettre en lumière les acteurs problématiques du secteur. Cependant, si les nouvelles obligations de divulgation ne sont pas facilement accessibles, leur utilité pour les résidents potentiels et leurs familles risque de rester limitée.

Parallèlement aux nouvelles règles sur la divulgation des propriétaires et gestionnaires de maisons de retraite, le Département de la Santé et des Services sociaux a publié un rapport important sur la relation entre la structure de propriété et la qualité des soins. Rédigé par David Stevenson, président du département des politiques de santé à la faculté de médecine de l’Université Vanderbilt, et ses collègues, ce rapport remet en question la croyance répandue que les fonds de capital-investissement sont principalement responsables de la mauvaise qualité des soins. Bien que les établissements gérés par ces fonds présentent une qualité légèrement inférieure et connaissent parfois une baisse après acquisition, ils ne représentaient que 5 % des maisons de retraite en 2022 (environ 900 sur 18 000), et leur part diminue.

Les sociétés de placement immobilier (REIT), qui détiennent environ 9 % des maisons de retraite, conservent une part stable depuis 2019 et présentent des préoccupations similaires en termes de qualité. Les autres groupes à but lucratif en possédaient environ 6 800, tandis que les propriétaires indépendants (« mom and pop ») et les organismes à but non lucratif exploitaient respectivement 3 200 et 3 500 établissements.

L’évaluation de la qualité reste difficile à cause de mesures peu fiables. Les études utilisent souvent le système de notation à cinq étoiles du gouvernement, qui mesure mieux la sécurité que l’expérience ou la qualité globale des soins. Les rapports d’inspection des États sont aussi inégaux. Malgré tout, ces études offrent une vue d’ensemble, fondée sur plusieurs bases de données (ce rapport en utilise six). Pourtant, il reste difficile pour les consommateurs de savoir à qui appartient précisément un établissement, surtout lorsqu’il s’agit de chaînes. Si une chaîne ayant un mauvais historique rachète un établissement, sa qualité peut baisser, mais aujourd’hui les consommateurs n’ont pas accès à ces données. Entre 2016 et 2021, environ 3 000 maisons de retraite ont changé de propriétaire.

Le suivi de la propriété est complexe. Propriétaires et exploitants sont souvent des entités distinctes : parfois, l’exploitant loue à une REIT ou à une autre société, et la propriété réelle est parfois dissimulée dans des structures complexes de partenariats. Pour les petites structures, propriétaires et exploitants sont souvent les mêmes, contrairement aux grandes chaînes.

Les nouvelles règles des Centres pour les services Medicare et Medicaid (CMS) imposent aux établissements de fournir des informations détaillées sur leur propriété et leur gestion lors de la demande ou du renouvellement d’agrément, ou en cas de changement de propriétaire. Les entités exerçant un contrôle financier ou de gestion doivent aussi être signalées, avec des définitions spécifiques du capital-investissement et des REIT par le CMS.

Le CMS promet de mettre ces informations à disposition du public environ un an après leur soumission, mais il n’est pas encore précisé comment cet accès sera organisé. Sans accès simple, clair et compréhensible, l’utilité pour le consommateur restera limitée. Même si la loi sur les soins abordables de 2010 prévoyait déjà cette transparence, les règles n’ont été finalisées que récemment, limitant jusqu’ici la portée des données disponibles.

Environ 1,3 million d’Américains vivent actuellement dans des maisons de retraite. Près de la moitié sont des résidents de longue durée, l’autre moitié bénéficient de soins de rééducation à court terme. L’emplacement reste le critère principal de choix pour beaucoup, mais disposer d’informations sur la qualité et la propriété aiderait à faire des choix plus éclairés.

article_content: A new study from Wright State University reveals that people are much more likely to use profanity on Twitter compared to in-person conversation. Conducted by PhD student Wenbo Wang, the study analyzed 51 million English-language tweets from 14 million users across one month. About 7.7% of all sampled tweets contained at least one swear word, equating to one in every 13 tweets. Surprisingly, just seven curse words accounted for over 90% of the offensive language observed. Swearing was most common late at night, particularly between midnight and 1:30 a.m., and peaked early in the week (Monday through Wednesday). Exploring emotional context, researchers found that cursing typically aligned with negative feelings such as anger and sadness, but was also sometimes used to stress positive emotions like happiness or affection. People tended to swear less in direct or private messages, opting to use profanity more in public tweets. The research also found men cursed more than women, with both genders likely to swear more in single-gender conversations. Presented at the ACM Conference on Computer-Supported Cooperative Work & Social Computing, these results suggest the impersonal and public nature of online platforms like Twitter may encourage users to speak more freely than they would in person.
translated_content: Une nouvelle étude de l’université Wright State révèle que les internautes sont bien plus susceptibles d’utiliser des jurons sur Twitter que lors de conversations en face à face. Menée par le doctorant Wenbo Wang, l’analyse a porté sur 51 millions de tweets en anglais issus de 14 millions d’utilisateurs sur un mois. Environ 7,7 % de tous les tweets examinés contenaient au moins un gros mot, soit un tweet sur treize. De façon surprenante, seulement sept jurons constituaient plus de 90 % du langage grossier détecté. L’utilisation de jurons atteignait un sommet tard dans la nuit, notamment entre minuit et 1h30, avec un pic en début de semaine (du lundi au mercredi). En étudiant le contexte émotionnel, les chercheurs ont remarqué que les insultes étaient majoritairement liées à la colère et à la tristesse, mais pouvaient également servir à renforcer des émotions positives comme la joie ou l’affection. Les utilisateurs avaient tendance à moins jurer dans les messages privés ou directs, préférant employer des gros mots dans les tweets publics. La recherche indique aussi que les hommes jurent plus que les femmes, et qu’hommes et femmes utilisent davantage de langage fort lors d’échanges avec des personnes du même genre. Présentés lors de la Conférence ACM sur le travail coopératif assisté par ordinateur et l’informatique sociale, ces résultats laissent penser que le caractère impersonnel et public des plateformes comme Twitter encourage les internautes à s’exprimer plus librement qu’en personne.

article_content: Google Chrome is preparing to enhance its compatibility with password managers, with new updates set for version 119. An experimental feature available within the developer settings (chrome://flags/#enable-autofill-virtual-view-structure) introduces an 'Autofill Options' menu on Chrome for Android, as identified by Leopeva64 on X and covered by Android Police. Once enabled, users can select between Chrome's default autofill—covering passwords, passkeys, payment methods, and addresses saved to Google—or other third-party providers configured via Android permissions. Currently, this functionality appears only in Chrome Dev and is accessible to a limited set of users as part of a field trial. The schedule for a wider release remains unclear. This move could significantly improve the autofill experience for those using third-party password managers. These managers often have trouble recognizing login forms in Chrome, which usually forces users to copy and paste credentials. The update aims to eliminate such inconvenience, giving users a smoother experience with various apps. Additionally, Google has rolled out a Credentials Manager app that enables logins using fingerprint or facial recognition and integrates smoothly with third-party managers. The company is also working on a revamped Google Password Manager interface, introducing new tabs for 'Passwords,' 'Checkup,' and 'Settings.'

Une fois activée, cette option permet aux utilisateurs de choisir entre la saisie automatique par défaut de Chrome — qui gère mots de passe, clés d’accès, moyens de paiement et adresses enregistrés chez Google — ou d’autres fournisseurs tiers configurés via les paramètres Android. Pour l’instant, cette fonctionnalité n’est visible que sur Chrome Dev et seulement pour un nombre limité d’utilisateurs dans le cadre d’un test. On ne sait pas encore quand elle sera déployée plus largement. Ce changement pourrait améliorer considérablement l’expérience de saisie automatique pour les utilisateurs de gestionnaires tiers, qui rencontrent souvent des difficultés à détecter les formulaires de connexion, les obligeant à copier-coller leurs informations. Cette mise à jour vise à rendre l’utilisation plus fluide avec d’autres applications. Par ailleurs, Google a lancé une application Credentials Manager qui permet de se connecter par empreinte digitale ou reconnaissance faciale, tout en étant compatible avec des gestionnaires concurrents. L’entreprise travaille aussi sur une nouvelle interface pour son propre gestionnaire de mots de passe, intégrant bientôt des onglets « Mots de passe », « Contrôle de sécurité » et « Paramètres ».

article_content:
Parents have expressed deep frustration over the deteriorating condition of their children's special school, St Clement's, and the prolonged 20-year struggle to secure a replacement building. Highland Council approved plans for a new £13 million school in 2021. However, last month the council failed to obtain Scottish government funding needed to move the project forward. St Clement’s currently has around 50 pupils, most from Easter Ross, with some traveling from Inverness, approximately 15 miles away.

Ms Robertson noted that while the curriculum differs for special needs students, the school still lacks essential facilities: there is no science department, no designated PE hall, and no physical education teacher. Ms MacLean highlighted a recent situation involving land behind the school, which parents were told was unsuitable for school development. That land is now being developed for a large retail shop.

According to Highland Council, 68 out of its more than 200 schools have been rated as being in poor condition, and another 74 as poorly suited for education. The council reports that the site behind St Clement’s was ruled out primarily due to flood risk criteria set by the Scottish Environment Protection Agency (SEPA).

Le conseil du Highland a approuvé des plans pour une nouvelle école de 13 millions de livres sterling en 2021. Cependant, le mois dernier, le conseil n'a pas réussi à obtenir le financement du gouvernement écossais pour faire avancer le projet. St Clement’s accueille actuellement environ 50 élèves, principalement d’Easter Ross et certains venant d’Inverness, à environ 24 kilomètres.

Mme Robertson a souligné que, bien que le programme soit adapté aux élèves à besoins spécifiques, l’école manque toujours d’installations essentielles : il n’y a pas de département de sciences, ni de salle de sport attitrée, ni d’enseignant d’éducation physique. Mme MacLean a évoqué une situation récente concernant un terrain derrière l’école, déclaré à l’époque inadapté à un établissement scolaire, mais aujourd’hui aménagé pour accueillir un grand magasin.

Selon le conseil du Highland, 68 de ses plus de 200 écoles ont été jugées en mauvais état et 74 autres comme étant mal adaptées à l’enseignement. Le conseil précise que le site derrière St Clement’s a principalement été écarté pour des raisons de risques d’inondation définis par l’Agence écossaise de protection de l’environnement (SEPA).

article_content: President Barack Obama has dispatched a special unit of CIA officers to the UK to investigate concerns about British Muslim extremism, amid rising fears in Washington that the UK may be becoming a center for terrorist radicalization. The agents arrived on an independent mission to consult senior security experts about the issue, instead of relying solely on information from MI5, MI6, or the US Embassy in London—a departure from usual practice. This move comes as UK security services acknowledge difficulties in monitoring the estimated 500 Britons who have traveled to the Middle East to fight with Islamic State (ISIS) forces in Syria and Iraq. Sources told The Mail on Sunday that the CIA agents aimed to assess the dynamics between Sunni and Shia Muslim communities within the UK. Fighters joining ISIS from the UK have largely been Sunnis, which has created tensions within the Muslim community. Professor Anthony Glees, Director of the Centre for Security and Intelligence Studies at Buckingham University, described the CIA mission, which occurred earlier this year, as evidence of Washington’s deep concern. He believes the problem is partly due to what he characterizes as lax UK immigration policies. ‘The US is worried about the British situation. They fear it could have consequences for them,’ said Professor Glees. ‘Although sectarian violence seen in Iraq and Syria has not spread to the UK, the threat is real. There is a possibility that Shia groups in the UK could target Sunni individuals planning to travel overseas to fight.’ He adds, ‘The US sees the UK’s immigration stance as problematic, believing it has contributed to the rise of militancy. In their view, the CIA must independently assess the situation rather than rely entirely on reports from MI5 or their embassy officers in London.’ A CIA source stated that British intelligence was notified of 'all outside contacts' made during the agents' visit to the UK, but also acknowledged ongoing concerns in Washington about the reliability of intelligence from MI5 and MI6, especially regarding young Muslims radicalized and recruited for conflicts abroad. The Obama administration is increasingly worried that similar radicalization could impact young American Muslims. There are close links between British and American extremists, and some believe UK efforts to identify recruiters have been insufficient. Spokespeople for both the CIA and the Home Office declined to comment.

Les agents sont arrivés pour mener une mission indépendante et consulter des experts en sécurité, sans s’appuyer seulement sur les informations du MI5, du MI6 ou de l’ambassade américaine à Londres — une démarche inhabituelle. Cette initiative intervient alors que les services de sécurité britanniques reconnaissent avoir du mal à surveiller environ 500 ressortissants britanniques partis au Moyen-Orient pour combattre avec l’État islamique (EI, ISIS) en Syrie et en Irak. Selon des sources relayées par le Mail on Sunday, les agents de la CIA cherchaient à comprendre la dynamique entre les communautés sunnite et chiite au Royaume-Uni. Les combattants rejoignant l’EI depuis le Royaume-Uni sont majoritairement des sunnites, ce qui a provoqué des tensions au sein de la communauté musulmane. Le professeur Anthony Glees, directeur du Centre d’études sur la sécurité et le renseignement à l’université de Buckingham, décrit la mission de la CIA, effectuée plus tôt cette année, comme un signe de l’inquiétude profonde de Washington. Il estime que le problème vient en partie de ce qu’il qualifie de politiques d’immigration laxistes au Royaume-Uni. « Les États-Unis s’inquiètent de la situation britannique. Ils craignent des répercussions chez eux », explique le professeur Glees. « Même si la violence sectaire observée en Irak et en Syrie ne s’est pas répandue au Royaume-Uni, la menace existe. Il est possible que des groupes chiites puissent viser des sunnites qui prévoient de partir combattre à l’étranger. » Il ajoute : « Les États-Unis jugent problématique la politique migratoire britannique, qu’ils estiment avoir favorisé la montée du militantisme. Selon eux, la CIA doit évaluer la situation de façon indépendante, sans se reposer uniquement sur les rapports du MI5 ou des agents de leur ambassade à Londres. » Une source à la CIA a affirmé que les services de renseignement britanniques avaient été informés de « tous les contacts » pris sur place par les agents, tout en reconnaissant les préoccupations persistantes à Washington quant à la fiabilité des renseignements du MI5 et du MI6, notamment concernant les jeunes musulmans radicalisés puis recrutés pour combattre à l’étranger. L’administration Obama s’inquiète de plus en plus à l’idée que le même phénomène de radicalisation puisse concerner aussi des jeunes musulmans américains. Il existe des liens étroits entre extrémistes britanniques et américains, et certains estiment que les efforts du Royaume-Uni pour identifier les recruteurs sont insuffisants. Les porte-parole de la CIA et du Home Office ont refusé de commenter.

article_content: A wave of snow and freezing conditions severely impacted air travel across the United States on Thursday, while much of the country struggled with record-breaking cold. Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport alone saw over 400 flight cancellations, with arrival delays averaging 45 minutes and departures lagging about 30 minutes, per the FAA. Other major travel hubs like Chicago’s Midway and Newark International in New Jersey also faced notable delays, causing a ripple effect nationwide. Meanwhile, meteorologists warned that a hazardous mix of ice and snow was moving through the Southeast, adding to the unusual cold spell which has dropped temperatures 10 to 35 degrees below average for the past fortnight. To assist stranded travelers, Delta Air Lines introduced weather waivers for affected passengers in Alabama, Arkansas, Georgia, Mississippi, and Tennessee, allowing them to reschedule without penalties through Saturday. The ongoing arctic blast, which started last weekend, has already been linked to at least seven fatalities. The National Weather Service predicted that most states east of the Rockies would face even colder conditions heading into the weekend. CNN’s meteorologists reported astonishingly low temperatures, especially along the Mississippi River, with Memphis reaching its coldest point in over a decade. Some homes, not built for such extremes, required city officials to intervene and provide heating to residents unable to pay bills. Authorities in Alabama cautioned drivers Thursday evening to avoid venturing out due to dangerous icy conditions and numerous reported wrecks, particularly from invisible black ice on bridges and overpasses. However, the University of Alabama’s football game also encouraged many residents to stay home. Other southern states weren’t spared. Arkansas was under a wind chill advisory as subzero readings and fierce winds settled in. Atlanta saw a dusting of snow Thursday night, leaving roads slick after two weeks of frigid temperatures. In a rare twist, Atlanta was even colder than Fairbanks, Alaska, that morning—a level of cold not seen in the U.S. in 15 years. Elsewhere, Florida declared a state of emergency to help protect its vital citrus and vegetable crops. Governor Charlie Crist temporarily lifted truck weight limits to expedite crop deliveries and minimize damages from the cold. Wildlife, too, felt the impact—officers rescued more than 100 sea turtles after frigid water temperatures threatened their survival. The Northern Plains also experienced bitter cold. In Bismarck, North Dakota, temperatures hovered 11 degrees below zero, with wind chills dropping as low as minus 35—and forecasts indicated possible wind chills down to minus 52 overnight. Snowfall ranging from 4 to 8 inches was predicted for regions from the upper Plains through the Northeast and south into Kentucky and Tennessee, with parts of Illinois already accumulating up to 7 inches. In Nebraska, Omaha and Lincoln school districts canceled classes as city budgets for snow removal were depleted, even with weeks of winter still ahead. Dallas, Texas, endured its longest cold spell in over ten years. Persistently low temperatures are expected across the Southeast through the weekend.

D’autres grands aéroports comme Midway (Chicago) et Newark International (New Jersey) ont également signalé d’importants retards, provoquant des répercussions dans tout le pays. Parallèlement, les météorologues ont averti qu’un dangereux mélange de glace et de neige gagnait le Sud-Est, accentuant une vague de froid inhabituelle ayant fait chuter les températures de 10 à 35 degrés en dessous des normales saisonnières depuis deux semaines. article_content: Paul the octopus, world-famous for his uncanny ability to predict football match results during the World Cup, received a 100,000 euro purchase offer from Russian bookmaker Liga Stavok. Co-owner Oleg Zhuravsky indicated the amount could increase, hoping to move Paul from his home at Sea Life Center in Oberhausen, Germany. However, the aquarium's PR team clarified that Paul is not for sale. Zhuravsky explained he wanted to assess Paul's prediction skills with Russian football matches and make Paul a symbol for his company, thanks to the octopus’s worldwide popularity. He expressed willingness to house Paul in the Moscow Aquarium, promising excellent care. Meanwhile, Spain's Madrid Aquarium also voiced interest and pledged to top any other proposals. Paul famously predicted Spain's final victory over the Netherlands, as well as other key matches, achieving a flawless eight-for-eight track record. Paul made his choices using two labeled boxes, each with a mussel and a competing team's flag, selecting the winner by choosing a box. Officials have since announced Paul’s retirement from making predictions, despite ongoing offers from international suitors. Public relations specialist Max Clifford commented that Paul's global stardom could have potentially turned him into a multimillionaire. The attention illustrates the blend of fascination and commercial opportunities prompted by Paul's unique talent.

Le copropriétaire, Oleg Zhuravsky, a précisé que la somme pouvait encore augmenter, espérant transférer Paul de son habitat du Sea Life Center à Oberhausen, en Allemagne. Even if key players like Xavi or Iniesta need a rest, others such as David Silva or Juan Mata are ready to step up, with Silva in particular seen as pivotal based on his performances at Manchester City. The author considers Spain and Brazil the main favorites, but also sees Argentina as a major threat, especially playing in South America, while Belgium’s talented side might make them an underdog to watch.

Stuart Hersh, an American injured in a 1997 suicide bombing in Jerusalem carried out by Hamas and reportedly supported by Iran, is pursuing legal action against The Warwick Hotel in Midtown Manhattan. The hotel has agreed to accommodate Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and his delegation during the United Nations General Assembly in late September. Hersh, who has a $12 million judgment against Iran for its alleged support of the bombing, has filed a request to prevent the hotel from accepting Ahmadinejad’s reservation, seeking to claim funds paid by Iran for the accommodation.

Ahmadinejad and his delegation have reportedly booked the 18th floor of The Warwick Hotel, with the stay costing an estimated $20,000 per night, according to the New York Post. The Iranian leader, who has made controversial remarks regarding the Holocaust and Israel, is scheduled to address the UN on September 26, which coincides with Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement.

Lawyers representing Hersh argue he has a legal right to proceeds paid by Iran, as he and other bombing survivors won a 2000 lawsuit against Iran seeking compensation for injuries. Hersh’s injuries from the 1997 attack include shrapnel wounds, burns, hearing loss, PTSD, and other long-term health problems, ultimately leaving him unable to work.

The decision by The Warwick Hotel to host Ahmadinejad has drawn criticism, as the leader's presence in New York is often protested. Editorials and Hersh’s legal team have spoken out against the hotel’s decision, pointing to the irony of Ahmadinejad spending significant sums on accommodations in the U.S. while outstanding judgments remain unpaid.

Israeli representatives, including Ron Prosor, have condemned Ahmadinejad's rhetoric and presence at the UN, especially on a significant Jewish holiday, stating it is contrary to the values of the international community. The Warwick Hotel declined to comment on the ongoing legal action.

Google will begin deleting inactive accounts—those not used for at least two years—starting December 1. If you have data in Gmail or other Google products linked to an account you haven’t accessed in some time, now is the time to act.

Inactive accounts and their associated content—including Gmail messages, Drive files, Docs, Meet, Calendar, Photos, and YouTube uploads—are at risk of removal. To prevent deletion, simply sign in to your Google account before this Friday.

According to a May blog post outlining the policy, recent activity on any Google service makes your account "active" and safe from deletion. Before deleting, Google says it will send multiple notifications to both the account’s email and any recovery email provided.

The account purge will happen gradually, starting with accounts created but never used. Exceptions exist: accounts managed by work, school, or organizations are not affected—this policy only covers personal accounts.

If you want to keep content from a specific Google product you haven’t used in a while (such as Drive photos), it’s wise to log in to that particular service. Google may also delete data within a specific product if it’s been inactive for two years, per each product’s inactivity policy.

Currently, accounts with YouTube videos aren’t slated for deletion under this policy: "We do not have plans to delete accounts with YouTube videos at this time," Google stated.

To backup data without maintaining the account, users can use the Google Takeout page to download and export data, or download individual folders, documents, and media files separately.

Google says it is enacting this policy as a security measure, since abandoned accounts are more susceptible to spam, phishing, and hijacking risks. Accounts unused for long periods are more likely to have outdated or reused passwords, lack two-factor authentication, and receive less attention from their owners, increasing vulnerability.

England edged past Samoa with a narrow 18-17 victory in Lille on Saturday, completing their fourth Pool D win at the Rugby World Cup. Despite a below-par performance, coach Steve Borthwick viewed the close contest as an important test for his team ahead of the quarter-finals. Danny Care's try seven minutes from fulltime secured the win for England, who are now building momentum for a likely knockout clash against Fiji.

"First things first, immense credit to Samoa—they played brilliantly, as if this was their World Cup final. They pushed us hard and forced plenty of errors," Borthwick said. "Looking ahead, we wanted a tough test and got it. The game was scrappy, but our players adjusted on the field and found a way to win."

England will learn their quarter-final opponent after Fiji face Georgia on Sunday, with Fiji needing only a point to finish second in Pool C ahead of Australia. Borthwick refuses to look too far ahead but is confident his squad can overcome challenges and silence critics. "A lot’s been said about this England team facing adversity. This team keeps believing and never stops. Some players were written off, but I always said we’d be ready—the big players step up on the big stages," he added.

Flyhalf Owen Farrell broke Jonny Wilkinson’s record for most points scored for England in test rugby, reaching 1,186 points after kicking two penalties and a conversion. "I haven’t thought much about it—it’s an honor just to be around long enough to achieve it. The lads gave me a framed picture in the changing room, which was a nice gesture," said Farrell.

Farrell also made World Cup history by becoming the first kicker to exceed the 60-second limit for a shot at goal, resulting in his attempt being disallowed. "I wasn’t aware of the time limit—I got lost in the moment. Luckily it didn’t cost us," he reflected.

L’essai de Danny Care, inscrit sept minutes avant la fin, a assuré la victoire à l’Angleterre, qui se prépare maintenant à un probable affrontement à élimination directe contre les Fidji.

« Tout d’abord, immense respect aux Samoa — ils ont joué brillamment, comme si c'était leur finale de Coupe du monde. Ils nous ont vraiment poussés et forcés à commettre beaucoup d’erreurs », a déclaré Borthwick. « Pour la suite, nous voulions un vrai test et nous l’avons eu. Le match était brouillon, mais nos joueurs ont su s’adapter sur le terrain pour trouver la solution. »

L’Angleterre connaîtra son adversaire en quart de finale après le match entre les Fidji et la Géorgie dimanche. Les Fidji n'ont besoin que d'un point pour terminer deuxièmes de la poule C devant l’Australie. Borthwick ne veut pas se projeter trop vite, mais il a confiance dans la capacité de son équipe à relever les défis et à faire taire les critiques. « Beaucoup ont douté de cette équipe d’Angleterre en difficulté. Mais elle garde la foi, elle n’abandonne jamais. Certains joueurs avaient été mis de côté, mais j’ai toujours dit que nous serions prêts — les grands joueurs répondent présents dans les grands moments », a-t-il ajouté.

L’ouvreur Owen Farrell a battu le record de points inscrits sous le maillot anglais en test, dépassant Jonny Wilkinson avec désormais 1 186 points grâce à deux pénalités et une transformation. « Je n’y ai pas trop pensé — c’est un immense honneur de pouvoir être là assez longtemps pour y arriver. Les gars m’ont offert une photo encadrée dans le vestiaire, c’était sympa », a déclaré Farrell.

Farrell a aussi marqué l’histoire de la Coupe du monde en devenant le premier buteur à dépasser la limite de 60 secondes pour une tentative, ce qui a invalidé son coup de pied. « Je ne regardais pas le temps — je me suis perdu dans le moment. article_content: The family of Kristen Fonseca, the 16-year-old girl who died in a jet ski accident involving an Australian tourist while on vacation in Hawaii, expressed their anger as the tourist was released from jail today. Tyler Dagley, 20, pleaded no contest to third degree negligent homicide – a misdemeanor – and was released due to time served following the August 5th accident, during which his jet ski collided with Fonseca's, resulting in her death the next day. Before the court’s decision was announced, Fonseca’s step-father, Mario Cantone, said: 'We have a huge hole in our family, all taken away from us in a split second by an individual who was negligent.' Kristen Fonseca and her sister Monique Sanchez posed with life vests before a jet ski adventure in Hawaii. Dagley was vacationing in Oahu, Hawaii with his girlfriend when the accident occurred. Hawaiian police said Dagley was standing up on his jet ski and posing for videos and photographs taken by his girlfriend before the collision. He was going about 40 miles per hour, which was four times faster than Kristen’s speed. The collision caused Kristen’s head to strike the steering column of her jet ski, throwing her into the water. At Oahu county jail today, Dagley faced members of Fonseca’s family, including her parents. Kristen’s parents witnessed the fatal crash and were upset that only misdemeanor charges were filed against Dagley. 'Our family's life is turned upside-down. We are unable to function at home. We go to sleep crying, wake up crying,' said Mario Cantone. Evangelina Fonseca, Kristen’s mother, said: 'I cry in the morning, I cry before I go to sleep, I cry randomly during the day looking for justice. I’m not trying to make this guy suffer, but I need him to understand there are consequences to every decision. That’s the kind of daughter she was — very forgiving. I know that's what she'd want me to do.' Tyler Dagley appeared distraught in court as he faced the Fonseca family and reportedly cried. Evangelina Fonseca read a poem Kristen wrote when she was eight, in which Kristen wondered if she would have children and expressed her wish to become a doctor. Dagley has been ordered to pay $78,000 in restitution to Fonseca’s family. Monique Sanchez, Kristen’s sister, told ABC News she witnessed the crash, describing Dagley as speeding and slamming into Kristen. Mario Cantone also recounted what he saw: 'I saw her head lunge forward, hit the steering wheel, and then she fell into the water.' Tyson Dagley and Natasha Ryan had saved for their trip to Hawaii. Mario Cantone told Fox 40: 'As far as I'm concerned, it’s not enough. He operated the jet ski in an unsafe and negligent manner.' The Fonseca family is now suing Dagley, stating they have suffered severe emotional distress and seeking damages, including medical and funeral expenses. The accident happened at Keehi Boat Harbor, about five miles from Waikiki Beach. Investigators reported that Dagley was standing on his rented jet ski when he struck Fonseca’s jet ski from behind. He was allegedly distracted by his girlfriend, who was taking photos and video. Natasha Ryan, 21, was charged with hindering prosecution after she falsely claimed Dagley was sitting and looking straight ahead. A forensic computer examiner recovered two deleted videos showing Dagley standing and someone shouting 'watch out.' Ryan was released on $500 bail and will appear in court Friday. Dagley suffered spinal injuries and a concussion in the crash. In court, he expressed deep regret and said he prayed for Kristen to be okay. At the scene, according to court documents, Dagley repeatedly apologized. The family has also filed a lawsuit naming Aloha Jet Ski, alleging the company failed to provide safety instructions or warnings about excessive speeds. Kristen was scheduled to begin a nursing work placement at Kaiser Permanente in Vacaville. Her family and friends are struggling to cope with the loss. Lyna Jackson, a friend, said: 'Just to know she’s not coming back is still unreal for us.' Another friend, Halie Cunningham, said: 'It's really hard to deal with, but we’ll get through it. We came out to support her and her family.'
