article_content: A new survey suggests that well-applied make-up can make women look significantly younger—sometimes by nearly a decade. The research, commissioned by beauty retailer Escentual.com, involved respondents viewing photos of well-known women both with and without make-up. Participants were asked to estimate the 'bareface age' and 'make-up age' for each, and averages were calculated. For example, Carol Vorderman, 51, was perceived to be 53 without make-up, but 46 when wearing cosmetics—a difference of seven years. Similarly, Madonna, 54, appeared seven years younger with make-up, while Cindy Crawford, 46, and Demi Moore, 49, looked six years younger. Kate Moss, 38, and Carol Vorderman demonstrated the biggest age reduction, both appearing nine years younger after applying make-up. Among the youngest participants, Britney Spears, 30, managed to look five years younger with make-up. Notably, at age 50, Demi Moore's 'bareface age' was guessed at 47, and her 'make-up age' at 43. The survey also asked women about their own use of make-up: 70% of women over 30 said it helped them look younger. This belief increased with age—62% for those aged 30–39, 73% for those 40–49, and 100% for women 60–69. When asked how much younger they felt they looked, 36% estimated one to three years, 29% said three to five years, 18% thought five to seven years, and 2% felt they looked up to ten years younger. The only group that felt make-up made them look older were women under 21. Overall, the findings suggest that both perception and self-perception of age can be influenced by skilfully applied cosmetics, especially among older women.

Kate Moss (38 ans) et Carol Vorderman ont montré la plus grande réduction d'âge, avec neuf ans de moins chacune après application du maquillage. article_content: Conchita Wurst, the bearded alter ego of Austrian artist Tom Neuwirth, found herself at the center of ongoing tensions between Russia and the West after winning the Eurovision Song Contest. Conchita’s victory, achieved with overwhelming public support, instantly transformed her into an international superstar—a development that frustrated many prominent Russians. Eurovision, a 58-year-old European cultural tradition, promotes unity and good relations across the continent. However, in practice, the competition often reflects cross-border rivalries and subtle political messages. This year, over 100 million viewers watched as Conchita took the stage in a golden dress, her well-groomed beard visible beneath flowing black hair. She performed 'Rise Like a Phoenix,' a song about personal transformation and triumph, captivating audiences across Europe. While Conchita’s performance resonated with millions, sparking a wave of public support and ultimately securing her victory, it also drew criticism from some quarters. In recent years, Russian President Vladimir Putin has positioned Russia as a conservative counterpoint to the West, especially regarding LGBTQ+ rights. Putin has restricted expressions of support for gay rights, casting himself as a guardian of 'traditional values.' Tensions at Eurovision intensified due to the crisis in Ukraine and the status of Crimea, which Russia had recently annexed. Organizers decided to count Crimea’s votes as Ukrainian. Meanwhile, petitions to disqualify Conchita were submitted by Russia, Belarus, and Armenia, and some officials called for editing her out of broadcasts. Despite opposition, viewers across Europe overwhelmingly voted for Conchita. Factors behind her victory included both her vocal abilities and the symbolic nature of her performance. During her press conference, Conchita addressed Putin directly, emphasizing, 'We are unstoppable.' For many in Russia, however, advocating for LGBTQ+ rights remains dangerous. Last year, Putin signed a law banning the so-called 'propaganda' of non-traditional sexual relationships, heightening anxieties among LGBTQ+ citizens. Conchita’s persona deconstructs conventional ideas of femininity and masculinity. Tom Neuwirth created Conchita in response to discrimination he faced in his youth, describing the character as having 'two hearts beating in my chest.' Russian officials, such as Vladimir Zhirinovsky and Dmitry Rogozin, harshly criticized Conchita's victory, with Zhirinovsky declaring it 'the end of Europe.' Calls emerged to withdraw Russia from future Eurovision contests. However, Conchita’s win highlights the growing embrace of diversity and inclusion within Europe. Ultimately, voters sent a clear message supporting individuality and progress. Conchita Wurst—her bearded face and elegant gown on full display—became a symbol of change at the heart of Europe’s cultural conversation.

Conchita Wurst — sa barbe et sa robe de soirée en pleine lumière — est devenue un symbole du changement au cœur de la conversation culturelle européenne.

article_content: Five former leaders of the Holy Land Foundation, once the largest Muslim charity in the United States, received long prison sentences on Wednesday from a federal judge. They had been found guilty of aiding Hamas, a Palestinian organization designated as a terrorist group by the U.S. government. Ghassan Elashi was sentenced to 65 years in prison following his conviction. Assistant Attorney General for National Security David Kris stated, 'These sentences should serve as a strong warning to anyone who knowingly provides financial support to terrorists under the guise of humanitarian relief.' The five leaders were convicted in November by a federal jury for providing funds and resources to Hamas. The case came after a 15-year investigation by the Justice Department. Shukri Abu Baker, age 50, and Ghassan Elashi, age 55, both from Texas, were also convicted of tax fraud. U.S. District Judge Jorge A. Solis sentenced both men to 65 years in prison at a federal court in Dallas. Among the other defendants, Mohammad El-Mezain, 55, of California, and Abdulrahman Odeh, 49, of New Jersey, each received 15-year sentences, while Mufid Abdulqader, 49, of Texas, was given 20 years. Federal authorities noted that Abu Baker, El-Mezain, and Elashi founded the Holy Land Foundation; Odeh and Abdulqader worked as fundraisers. The Bush administration shut down the organization in 2001, froze its assets, and accused it of raising millions for Hamas. Before its closure, the foundation, headquartered in Richardson, Texas, was regarded as the country’s largest Muslim charity. The Justice Department alleged that $12.4 million was directed to Hamas disguised as humanitarian donations. A first trial in 2007 ended in a mistrial, but the Justice Department refiled charges. The second trial, lasting two months, saw the jury deliberate for eight days before reaching a verdict. According to Kris, Wednesday's sentences marked the end of 'many years of painstaking investigative and prosecutorial work at the federal, state and local levels.'

Un premier procès en 2007 s’est soldé par un procès nul, mais le ministère de la Justice a renouvelé les accusations. Jay-Z has plenty of reasons to celebrate this week. Not only is he still happily married to Beyoncé, but his latest album, 'Magna Carta Holy Grail,' is a major commercial success. According to Soundscan, the album sold an impressive 527,000 copies in its first week, earning Jay-Z his 13th No. 1 album. This opening week surpasses the debuts of Daft Punk’s 'Random Access Memories' (339,000 copies) and Kanye West’s 'Yeezus' (327,000 copies), although Justin Timberlake's 'The 20/20 Experience' holds the year's top debut with 968,000 copies.

Additionally, Jay-Z and the RIAA already consider 'Magna Carta Holy Grail' platinum, thanks to downloads from the Samsung app. The album also set a new record for the most first-week streams on Spotify in the United States, achieving 14 million album streams and beating out previous record-holders like Daft Punk’s 'Random Access Memories' (9.5 million) and Mumford & Sons’ 'Babel' (8 million). It also broke Spotify’s record for the most streams in a single day.

Further adding to the excitement, Jay-Z and Justin Timberlake are starting their American stadium tour this weekend, opening with two shows at Yankee Stadium.

article_content: Sofia, Bulgaria (AP) — Bulgarian authorities have expelled a Russian journalist for allegedly engaging in activities that threatened the country’s national security. The State Agency for National Security announced that Alexander Gatsak, a correspondent for Russia’s state-run newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta, had his residency revoked and was barred from entering Bulgaria and other European Union member states. According to the agency, Gatsak was summoned on September 29 to receive the expulsion order at the Interior Ministry’s migration office. However, he did not appear, choosing instead to seek refuge at the Russian Embassy in Sofia. The agency stated that, with help from the Foreign Ministry, Gatsak departed Bulgaria on Wednesday. Officials did not specify what activities led to the expulsion, but emphasized the process complied with European democratic standards. 'The agency’s actions aim to protect national security, not to limit freedom of speech or opinion,' the statement said. BTA, Bulgaria’s national news agency, reported that Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova called the expulsion 'another unlawful move by NATO against Russian journalists' and threatened countermeasures. Last year, Bulgaria expelled 70 Russian diplomatic staff, which seriously strained relations between the two countries. This was Bulgaria’s largest expulsion of Russian diplomats in history. Bulgaria, a NATO and EU member, has strongly supported Western sanctions against Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine.

L'agence de presse bulgare BTA rapporte que Maria Zakharova, porte-parole du ministère russe des Affaires étrangères, a qualifié l'expulsion de « nouvelle mesure illégale de l'OTAN contre les journalistes russes » et a menacé de mesures de rétorsion. article_content: A recent analysis by PolicyBazaar revealed that a significant number of health insurance claims are rejected because policyholders don’t fully disclose existing health conditions, such as diabetes or hypertension, at the time of purchasing insurance. Reviewing 200,000 health insurance claims from April to September 2023, PolicyBazaar found that 30,000 were denied. About 25% of these rejections were due to non-disclosure of pre-existing medical conditions. Another quarter of claims were turned down when policyholders tried to claim for treatments not covered by their plans, such as outpatient department (OPD) visits or spectacles. Additionally, 16% of claims were denied because policyholders didn’t respond to information requests from insurers. Experts point out that claim denials due to non-disclosure can cause significant financial impact for policyholders, even when the withheld information doesn’t directly relate to the current health claim. In contrast, claims denied for non-covered treatments are usually low in value, often relating to excluded items like OPD consultations or eyewear. Amit Chhabra, Chief Business Officer–Health Insurance at PolicyBazaar, highlighted that misunderstanding of policy coverage is a leading cause for rejections. Segar Sampathkumar, Health Director at the General Insurance Council, emphasized the need for careful completion of application forms, as insurers may reject claims for missing disclosures, regardless of whether they pertain to the hospital visit. Insurance regulations require buyers to disclose all facts that could affect an insurer’s decision. Claims can be denied for not revealing existing conditions, even if those conditions are unrelated to the claim.

En examinant 200 000 demandes entre avril et septembre 2023, PolicyBazaar a constaté que 30 000 ont été rejetées. Environ 25 % de ces refus sont liés à la non-divulgation de maladies préexistantes. Un autre quart concerne des demandes pour des soins non prévus au contrat, comme les consultations ambulatoires (OPD) ou les lunettes. Par ailleurs, 16 % des demandes ont été refusées parce que les assurés n'ont pas répondu aux demandes d'information des assureurs. Les spécialistes précisent que les refus pour non-divulgation peuvent avoir un impact financier important pour les assurés, même si l'information non révélée n'est pas directement liée à la demande. À l'opposé, les refus concernant des prestations non couvertes portent en général sur de petites sommes, par exemple les consultations OPD ou les lunettes. Amit Chhabra, directeur commercial santé chez PolicyBazaar, souligne que le manque de compréhension des garanties reste une cause principale de refus. Segar Sampathkumar, directeur santé au General Insurance Council, rappelle l'importance de bien remplir les formulaires, car une omission peut mener à un refus, que l'élément soit ou non lié à la visite à l'hôpital. La loi impose aux assurés de déclarer tous les éléments qui pourraient influencer la décision de l'assureur. Une demande peut être rejetée pour non-déclaration d'une maladie existante, même si elle n'a pas de lien direct avec la demande.

article_content: Top executives in Wall Street and banking frequently sign noncompete agreements that prevent them from working for competitors after leaving. These clauses, typically lasting six months to two years, are designed to protect companies from intellectual property loss and client poaching. But New York may soon see a major shift—its legislature recently passed a bill to ban noncompete agreements entirely, reflecting a nationwide trend aimed at protecting workers across many sectors, from professionals to hourly staff. Low-wage employees, in particular, are sometimes bound by these clauses without fully realizing it. With attention turning to the broad effects on New York's influential industries, a powerful lobbying movement has formed. Large banks, media corporations, and alliances of businesses are encouraging Governor Kathy Hochul to oppose the ban or to limit its reach. Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, NBC Universal, Charter Communications, and many others have lobbied state officials. The Business Council of New York State has launched a $1 million campaign warning that banning noncompetes could harm innovation and talent retention. The Partnership for New York City, counting Blackstone and BlackRock among its members, has called for exceptions for high-compensation roles. Kathy Wylde, president of the Partnership, emphasizes that noncompetes are critical for high-level employees who earn millions and deal with sensitive information. As lobbying intensifies, Hochul faces rising pressure, especially from those who supported her election. Her administration is still evaluating the bill, with a decision expected by the end of the year. These agreements have become more widespread in recent years, sometimes catching low-wage workers unaware during the hiring process. State Senator Sean Ryan, the bill’s sponsor, argues that many workers sign noncompetes accidentally and that the ban would boost mobility and wages. Proponents of the ban also hope it will increase competition. President Biden’s administration and the Federal Trade Commission have proposed similar nationwide restrictions, and almost half of U.S. states have already imposed tough limits on noncompetes. States like Minnesota, Oklahoma, North Dakota, and especially California have enacted major restrictions or outright bans, with California’s refusal to enforce noncompetes being long-standing. Proponents cite Silicon Valley as evidence that such bans can foster immense growth and innovation. New York's global economic significance and its network-driven industries make this debate even more consequential. Many business coalitions advocate for a targeted ban focused only on lower-wage workers, allowing noncompetes for highly paid specialists. Though estimates vary, studies indicate that 18% to 45% of private-sector employees nationwide are subject to noncompetes. Those supporting the ban argue these agreements limit worker mobility and suppress wages; businesses counter that they protect confidential information and encourage investment in staff. Melanie Lee, a 29-year-old tattoo artist, found herself facing a $15,000 penalty under a noncompete after leaving a Queens studio. The resulting legal dispute forced her to testify to lawmakers about how the agreement restricted her and put her under financial strain. Opponents of the ban worry it could discourage companies from investing in employees and create problems for business sales that rely on noncompetes. Unlike Minnesota’s recent law, New York’s bill currently doesn’t include carve-outs for such cases, a detail some believe could dampen investment in the state. Legal expert John Siegal points out that a statewide ban would upend employment practices in fields heavily reliant on personal relationships, like real estate and finance, with far-reaching effects on how firms manage talent.

Mais New York pourrait bientôt connaître un changement majeur : son assemblée législative a récemment adopté un projet de loi interdisant totalement les clauses de non-concurrence, reflétant une tendance nationale à protéger les salariés de tous secteurs, des professionnels aux employés horaires. Les travailleurs à faible revenu, en particulier, se retrouvent parfois liés par ces clauses sans en être pleinement conscients. Alors que l’attention se porte sur les conséquences potentielles pour les industries influentes de New York, un mouvement de lobbying puissant s’est formé. De grandes banques, des médias et des alliances d’entreprises poussent la gouverneure Kathy Hochul à s’opposer à l’interdiction ou à en limiter la portée. Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, NBC Universal, Charter Communications et bien d’autres ont fait pression sur les responsables de l’État. Le Business Council of New York State a lancé une campagne d’un million de dollars pour alerter que l’interdiction des non-concurrences pourrait nuire à l’innovation et à la rétention des talents. La Partnership for New York City, qui compte Blackstone et BlackRock parmi ses membres, réclame des exceptions pour les postes à haut salaire. Kathy Wylde, présidente de la Partnership, affirme que les non-concurrences sont cruciales pour les employés haut placés qui gagnent des millions et traitent des informations sensibles. Alors que la pression augmente, Hochul est de plus en plus sollicitée, notamment par ceux qui ont soutenu son élection. Son administration examine toujours le projet de loi, une décision étant attendue d’ici la fin de l’année. Ces accords se sont répandus ces dernières années, piégeant parfois des employés à bas salaire sans qu’ils s’en rendent compte lors de l’embauche. Le sénateur Sean Ryan, auteur du texte, explique que beaucoup de travailleurs signent une clause sans s’en rendre compte, et que l’interdiction permettrait d’améliorer la mobilité et les salaires. Les partisans du texte espèrent aussi qu’il dynamisera la concurrence. Des États comme le Minnesota, l’Oklahoma, le Dakota du Nord ou surtout la Californie ont fortement restreint ou interdit les clauses de non-concurrence, la Californie refusant de longue date de les appliquer. Les défenseurs de l’interdiction citent la Silicon Valley comme exemple d’une croissance et d’une innovation immenses sans ces clauses. L’importance économique mondiale de New York et l’interconnexion de ses secteurs rendent ce débat particulièrement crucial. Beaucoup d’organisations patronales plaident pour une loi ciblée visant uniquement les bas salaires, maintenant la possibilité de non-concurrence pour les spécialistes hautement rémunérés. Les opposants à l’interdiction craignent qu’elle ne décourage les entreprises d’investir dans leurs salariés et ne complique les ventes d’entreprises qui reposent souvent sur de telles clauses. Contrairement à la loi récente du Minnesota, la proposition new-yorkaise n’inclut pas à ce stade d’exception pour ces cas, ce qui pourrait, selon certains, freiner l’investissement dans l’État. L’expert juridique John Siegal estime qu’une interdiction à l’échelle de l’État bouleverserait les pratiques d’embauche dans des secteurs tels que l’immobilier ou la finance, où les relations personnelles sont déterminantes, et aurait des conséquences importantes sur la gestion des talents par les entreprises.

article_content: Bedford-based brewery Charles Wells has issued guidance advising pub landlords to limit patrons’ alcohol consumption to the government’s recommended daily limits. A 'Drinkaware' leaflet sent to licensees advises staff to use a calculator to monitor units consumed, ensuring customers do not exceed 3-4 alcohol units per day as per government guidelines. The leaflet, referencing both the Royal College of Physicians and NHS Choices, details the unit count for a range of drinks, including the brewery’s flagship Bombardier beer (2.7 units per pint, advertised by Rik Mayall) and strong Erdinger lager (3 units per pint). The guidance suggests that drinking more than one and a half pints of either could exceed the advised daily limit. Some pub landlords oppose the advice, fearing business losses. One anonymous landlord from Bedfordshire commented: ‘If I limited customers to just one pint, I’d lose them and the pub could go bust.’ The leaflet, titled ‘Help your customers be Drinkaware,’ further encourages bar staff to help patrons make informed decisions about alcohol consumption, using a recommended calculation: Strength (ABV) x Volume (ml) ÷ 1,000 = alcohol units. NHS Choices provides unit breakdowns for various drinks, indicating, for example, that a standard glass of wine (175ml at 12% ABV) holds 2.1 units, and a single measure of spirits (25ml at 40% ABV) equals one unit. Charles Wells’ spokesperson stated: ‘As part of the Department of Health’s Public Health Responsibility Deal, we produced this leaflet to provide licensees with clear information on alcohol units and official guidelines, supporting informed choices for customers.’

article_content: On Sunday, Libyan government spokesperson Musa Ibrahim announced that a NATO airstrike in Tripoli killed Saif al-Arab Gadhafi, the youngest adult son of leader Muammar Gadhafi. Muammar Gadhafi and his wife were reportedly present during the strike but were unharmed. The attack also allegedly resulted in the deaths of several of Gadhafi's grandchildren and left the targeted home destroyed, with an unexploded bomb reported at the site. Ibrahim condemned the NATO action as illegal and a 'war crime,' stating that the Libyan government would seek retribution. He urged Libyans to unite, referring to Saif al-Arab as a symbol for the people. NATO officials, led by Lieutenant General Charles Bouchard, acknowledged the reports of deaths but emphasized that their mission focused solely on military targets linked to the regime’s attacks on civilians. They expressed regret over any unintentional casualties and stated that individuals are not specifically targeted. News of the airstrike sparked gunfire and drew large crowds of supporters near Gadhafi’s residence in Tripoli, as shown on state TV, where demonstrators chanted slogans about martyrdom and retaliation. The opposition, however, voiced doubts about the report. Abdul Hafiz Ghoga, representing the Transitional National Council, claimed that information on Saif al-Arab was scarce and suggested the regime might be inventing stories to gain sympathy. Meanwhile, Western officials, including those from the US, could not confirm the reported deaths, with some noting that Libyan insiders had passed along unverified information about a casualty within the regime. This episode recalls a 1986 US airstrike that reportedly killed Gadhafi’s adopted daughter and injured a young Saif al-Arab, according to previous Libyan accounts. Experts such as Bruce Riedel from the Brookings Institution argued that the loss could make a political solution even more difficult amidst Libya’s deeply tribal context and the influential role of the Gadhafi family.

Les responsables de l'OTAN, menés par le lieutenant-général Charles Bouchard, ont reconnu les informations faisant état de morts, mais ont précisé que leur mission ne ciblait que des objectifs militaires liés aux attaques du régime contre les civils. Ils ont exprimé leurs regrets devant toute victime involontaire et affirmé qu'ils ne visaient pas les individus. article_content: As the New Zealand cricket squad prepared for their warm-up under the setting Mumbai sun, Daryl Mitchell was prompted by a teammate to look to his right. There, recently installed at the stadium, stood a statue of Indian cricketing icon Sachin Tendulkar. Mitchell gazed at the figure, soon joined by his teammates, all pausing to pay silent respect. It was a reminder of the unique reverence cricketers receive in India—a stark contrast to New Zealand, where rugby holds a more prominent cultural position. Mitchell himself is no stranger to sporting heritage; his father has coached rugby across New Zealand, England, Australia, and South Africa. While the spotlight in New Zealand often falls on rugby, its cricket team has quietly established itself as a formidable competitor on the world stage. Despite its smaller population, New Zealand consistently performs above expectations at World Cups and other major tournaments, often emerging as genuine title contenders. One explanation comes from Nigel Muir, who served as CEO of Sport Tasman for thirteen years. Reflecting on the country's sporting success during the 2015 World Cup in Nelson—a small but vibrant coastal town—Muir pointed to the region’s many open spaces and sporting facilities. He emphasized the country’s strong community spirit: in New Zealand, one in three people participates in some form of sports volunteering. Whether coaching, providing motivation, assisting with logistics, or simply supporting young athletes, people of all ages contribute to the sporting landscape. Muir described sports events where the outcome is secondary to participation, inclusivity, and joy. A poster at the Saxton Oval administration office captured this: hundreds of smiling children celebrating together after a match, with little attention paid to winners or losers. 'We might have a few future stars, but our real aim is to help everyone become happier, kinder people,' Muir explained. This ethos contrasts with Australia’s strong emphasis on producing elite athletes and achieving competitive success. According to Muir, the Australian system invests significantly more in nurturing high-performance talent—a model that New Zealand has begun to consider, but balances cautiously against its core community values. Youth cricket engagement has fluctuated over the years. While participation among secondary school-aged students declined at one point, events like the 2015 and 2019 World Cups—buoyed by captains like Brendon McCullum and the team's dynamic style—have inspired renewed interest. Recent data from New Zealand Cricket show an increase in youth participation, approaching record numbers. Though cricket may not match rugby in popularity, the Black Caps remain perennial contenders who play an entertaining and inspiring brand of cricket, encouraging new generations to enjoy the sport amid New Zealand’s scenic open spaces.

Bridge jobs present a realistic option for individuals navigating career changes, returning to employment, or putting off retirement. Despite the ideal of equality in the U.S., job loss still carries stigma, and not having a financial safety net adds significant stress. Currently, professionals with college degrees, especially in white-collar roles, are experiencing tougher job markets due to slowed hiring—particularly in sectors affected by the so-called 'richcession.'

When job searches drag on, especially around the holidays, it might make sense to consider temporary, unrelated roles rather than waiting for better opportunities to come in the new year. Accepting a bridge job can be a smart, responsible step—especially given that employers like Macy’s, Target, Amazon, Walmart, and UPS are hiring tens of thousands of seasonal staff. Other options include warehouse gigs or rideshare driving with platforms like Uber. These temporary positions are a sound way to maintain your income and provide for your needs while between more permanent roles.

A bridge job, by definition, is a short-term placement meant to bridge the gap between more permanent career stages. These roles help keep a steady flow of income, provide benefits like health insurance, and support stability during uncertain times. They come in various forms—full-time, part-time, contract, or freelance—and often offer flexible schedules.

Taking on this kind of work helps prevent financial strain, pays the bills, and keeps employment gaps off your resume. It shows future employers that you are proactive, motivated, and maintaining your skill set. Moreover, temporary jobs help preserve daily routine, boost morale, and sometimes lead to unexpected opportunities for networking and skill-building in new fields.

During interviews for bridge jobs, you may need to address why you are applying for something outside your previous expertise. Being honest about industry shifts, showing sincere interest in the specific role, and emphasizing your willingness to contribute can reassure potential employers. By approaching these jobs with humility and an open mind, you can turn a difficult phase into a chance for personal and professional growth.

article_content: Surfers from around the world gathered in Huntington Beach, California, to honor Sean Collins with a heartfelt paddle out tribute. Collins, respected as a pioneer in wave forecasting, died suddenly at age 59 after collapsing during a tennis match in Newport Beach on December 26, 2011. His wife Daren watched with pride as hundreds of surfers created a large circle on their boards, commemorating his impact. Collins’ work fundamentally changed surfing. Before his contributions, surfers would embark on aimless searches for waves, but his innovations provided them with reliable guidance. Collins founded Surfline, which started as a telephone service featuring reports from experienced surfers along California’s coastline. The service later evolved into a widely used online platform, now attracting over 1.5 million visits each month. He was honored in 2008 by being inducted into the Huntington Beach Surfers’ Hall of Fame, where he wrote 'Follow Your Passions' in the commemorative concrete, a motto reflecting his outlook and commitment. Collins frequently credited his dedicated team for his success. Sean Collins began surfing in Seal Beach at age eight and cultivated a deep passion for weather tracking while sailing with his father. Mostly self-taught, he supplemented his knowledge with a few courses in meteorology at Long Beach Community College. Surfline’s phone reports, essential in the 1980s, became vital for everyone from early-morning wave seekers to contest organizers. Collins made a habit of alerting lifeguards and media about dangerous waves. He also launched the first live surfcam in 1996. Widely recognized for his innovations, Collins was named by Surfer Magazine as one of the 25 Most Influential Surfers of the Century and, in 2002, the eighth Most Powerful Surfer in the industry. After selling Surfline in 2000, Collins continued as president and chief forecaster. Collins leaves behind a lasting legacy and is survived by his wife Daren and their sons, AJ and Tyler.

Weyes Blood, the stage name of Los Angeles-born singer-songwriter Natalie Mering, is an artist shaped by the counterculture movements of the 1960s and 70s—eras her musician parents greatly influenced her with. Despite this, Mering, now 35, is wary of her generation becoming obsessed with nostalgia, which she feels can be counterproductive in a world that is rapidly evolving. She notes, “It’s harder today to have the life our parents had, or to offer that life to our own children,” as she readies her Holy Flux tour for the UK. She emphasizes how key milestones, such as buying a house or securing job opportunities post-college, have become more complex for younger generations.

Mering tries to balance her strong connection to the past with an acute awareness of the downsides of nostalgia, especially when it becomes politically charged. Musically, her lush, timeless folk-rock and baroque-pop style echoes icons like Karen Carpenter and Joni Mitchell, but her lyrics address modern concerns—environmental issues, technological change, and growing feelings of isolation. Her 2022 album, 'And In the Darkness, Hearts Aglow', released during the pandemic, was celebrated for tracks like “It’s Not Just Me, It’s Everybody,” which examine collective anxiety and disconnection.

This album topped The Times' year-end list, ahead of major artists such as Kendrick Lamar and Taylor Swift, and drew praise from other outlets for its cinematic depth and hopeful outlook. Mering has collaborated with artists like Lana Del Rey, The Killers, and John Cale, and worked with director Adam Curtis for the visuals of “God Turn Me Into a Flower.” The album stands as a more personal response to societal traumas compared to her previous work, 'Titanic Rising' (2019). She shares that empathy, rather than frustration at society’s lack of progress, shaped her approach this time.

Mering’s upbringing saw her parents transition from hippie and punk influences to born-again Christianity, making church music a significant part of her childhood. Although she later rejected her religious background, this experience informs her artistry. Through years spent in various US cities—California, Pennsylvania, Portland, Baltimore—she evolved through noise-rock and punk, even staging provocative performances, before moving toward the atmospheric solo sound for which she is now known.

Mering reflects fondly but critically on the changes social media and smartphone culture have brought to the DIY music scene, lamenting the loss of innocence but observing new forms of creative community taking shape among younger fans. She remains optimistic, noting that the new generation at her shows is unique, expressive, and seeks connection beyond digital life.

Recently, after performing at Glastonbury and walking the runway at New York Fashion Week, Mering is bringing her tour to the UK, with shows in Glasgow, Leeds, London, and Nottingham. Her concerts blend cathartic music, humor, and immersive visuals—a space she describes as a 'transportation device' for audiences to experience something transformative and personal.

article_content: Rob Gronkowski is often mentioned among the best tight ends in NFL history, but the New England Patriots star says he has a hard time being taken seriously. As an alumnus of the University of Arizona, which is known for its party scene, Gronkowski is famous for his playful antics. With the iconic 'Gronk Party Bus' arriving in Phoenix, the celebration could continue if the Patriots win Sunday’s Super Bowl. At a pre-Super Bowl press conference on Wednesday, Gronkowski posed with a magazine he received. When asked about the bus, he said: “We’ve got BodyArmor drinks, comfortable seating, good music, movies, and TV—no games, just movies.” Despite his party reputation, Gronkowski wants people to know about his hard work. “I feel like people underestimate the hard work and dedication that goes into preparing behind the scenes,” he told reporters. He added: “It’s not just about showing up on game day. You need to work out in the weight room, attend meetings, practice throughout the week, and take care of your body from morning until night, including getting enough sleep. Many don’t see how much effort goes into being ready for Sunday’s game.” Gronkowski is in much better health than he was during the Patriots’ last Super Bowl appearance in 2012, when he struggled with an ankle injury. He had injury issues the following two years but is now fully fit for the big game against the Seattle Seahawks. “It feels a lot better this time,” Gronkowski said. “A few years ago, everyone kept asking about my ankle. Now I can concentrate on the Seahawks, practice, and doing my job. It’s an awesome feeling.” The Patriots, including Tom Brady and Danny Amendola, have been practicing in Arizona as they prepare for Super Bowl XLIX at University of Phoenix Stadium against the Seattle Seahawks.

article_content: Dr. Jeff Wessler, founder of Heartbeat Health and clinical faculty at Northwell Health, reflects on his experience launching a healthcare startup. While technology is often seen as the core of innovation, Wessler’s story highlights that true impact comes from addressing real patient needs. Early at Heartbeat Health, the team built custom software for an ideal patient experience. However, several business pivots and five years later, Wessler realized their technology reached mostly younger, healthier, tech-savvy users instead of those most in need. Through regular data analysis, the company learned valuable lessons for any entrepreneur. Wessler outlines four main insights: 1. Technology should support—not define—your business. Their first app was well-liked but didn’t serve their mission to prevent heart disease. Clarifying goals before investing in new tools, and consistently evaluating outcomes with data, proved essential. 2. Technology can strengthen human connections. In 2019, Heartbeat Health expanded through employer partnerships, offering on-site cardiac screenings and immediate video consults with cardiologists. While technology streamlined the process, staff ensured patients received personalized care. Businesses should consider where human interaction, supported by tech, can improve the experience. 3. Keep technology simple for users. The COVID-19 pandemic prompted wider telemedicine use, especially for older adults on Medicare Advantage plans. Adoption increased when the team used easy solutions, like text links, instead of requiring app downloads. Wessler advises that working technology is often more valuable than flashy features. 4. Not everything needs to be built from scratch. During the pandemic, the team used commercial telemedicine software to move quickly. Lessons learned later shaped their own platform. Wessler recommends startups use available tools when possible and let market experience guide future tech investments. Ultimately, Wessler stresses that technology matters, but startups must first focus on delivering value to customers—customizing technology to fit those needs, rather than letting tech dictate the business.

Même si la technologie est souvent perçue comme le moteur de l’innovation, son parcours montre que l’essentiel est de répondre aux véritables besoins des patients. Au départ, l’équipe de Heartbeat Health avait conçu des logiciels sur mesure pour offrir une expérience patient idéale. Mais après plusieurs changements de direction et cinq ans d’activité, le Dr Wessler a constaté que leur technologie ciblait surtout des patients jeunes, en bonne santé et à l’aise avec le numérique, et non les profils les plus à risque. Grâce à une analyse régulière des données, l’entreprise a tiré des leçons utiles pour tout entrepreneur. Le Dr Wessler présente quatre grands enseignements : 1. La technologie doit soutenir, pas définir, votre entreprise. Leur première appli plaisait, mais ne servait pas vraiment leur mission de prévention des maladies cardiovasculaires. D’abord clarifier ses objectifs puis constamment évaluer les outils avec des données a été clé. 2. La tech peut renforcer la relation humaine. En 2019, Heartbeat Health a grandi avec des employeurs, réalisant des dépistages cardiaques sur site et proposant une consultation vidéo immédiate. La technologie a fluidifié le parcours, mais le personnel a assuré la prise en charge humaine. Les entreprises devraient identifier où l’interaction appuyée par la tech améliore l’expérience client. 3. Optez pour la simplicité côté utilisateur. Avec la pandémie, la télémédecine s’est développée, surtout pour les seniors de Medicare Advantage. L’adoption a décollé quand l’équipe a misé sur des liens SMS immédiats, sans téléchargement d’appli. Wessler insiste : une technologie simple et efficace prime toujours sur le tape-à-l’œil. 4. Ne cherchez pas à tout développer vous-même. Pendant la pandémie, l’équipe a utilisé des logiciels existants pour aller vite. Les expériences ont ensuite permis de créer leur propre plateforme. Le conseil de Wessler : privilégiez les outils disponibles et laissez l’expérience marché guider vos futurs investissements technologiques. Au final, il reconnaît l’importance de la technologie, mais rappelle qu’une start-up doit d’abord s’attacher à délivrer de la valeur à ses clients—et n’adapter la technologie qu’en fonction de cela, pas l’inverse.

article_content: Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida and Chinese President Xi Jinping held their first summit in a year, agreeing to seek a resolution through dialogue over the dispute regarding wastewater from the Fukushima nuclear plant, according to Kishida. He told reporters in San Francisco, 'I urged that this be handled calmly on a scientific basis. We will hold discussions based on science at an expert level.' Kishida described the summit as 'very meaningful.' Xi Jinping told Kishida that Japan’s wastewater discharge is of international public concern and called on Japan to manage the issue responsibly and constructively, as reported by China Central Television. The meeting took place a day after U.S. President Joe Biden expressed optimism about improving U.S.-China relations following his own talks with Xi, which helped pave the way for Japan to strengthen ties with China, its largest trading partner. Japan and China have ongoing disagreements on issues including semiconductors, nuclear waste, detained Japanese citizens in China, and a territorial dispute over uninhabited islands near Taiwan. Kishida pressed Xi to lift China’s ban on Japanese seafood imports, which was imposed in response to Japan’s release of treated wastewater from the damaged Fukushima plant. The International Atomic Energy Agency has stated that the release is safe. Chinese restrictions have negatively affected Japanese businesses such as cosmetics producer Shiseido Co., which recently reduced its profit forecast. Public opinion in Japan toward China has deteriorated, reaching its lowest level since 2014, according to a recent poll. During the meeting, Xi said both countries should focus on shared interests, manage disagreements properly, and reaffirm their strategic relationship. He highlighted the deep economic ties between the two countries and said it would not benefit anyone to disrupt these supply chains. Kishida responded with a commitment to creating a brighter future for Japan-China relations for the next generation. Japan has faced criticism from China for aligning with U.S. policies to strengthen export controls on technology sent to China. This week, the countries agreed to launch an export control dialogue, according to China’s commerce ministry. They also planned to restart high-level economic talks at an appropriate time, the Japanese Foreign Ministry stated. Kishida also voiced concerns about the East China Sea, where ships from both nations patrol disputed waters, and asked Xi to remove a Chinese buoy in Japan’s claimed exclusive economic zone. Last year, Japan labeled China as an 'unprecedented security challenge' and has since moved forward with its largest military buildup since World War II, a development that has unsettled Beijing. Kishida called for transparency in the legal processes and the release of Japanese citizens detained in China. One Japanese man received a 12-year sentence this month, while another, an employee of Astellas Pharma Inc., was indicted in October after earlier detention. Specific details of the cases have not been made public.

Il a déclaré aux journalistes à San Francisco : « J’ai insisté sur la nécessité de traiter ce sujet calmement et scientifiquement. Nous aurons des discussions d’experts basées sur la science. » Kishida a qualifié le sommet de « très significatif ». Xi Jinping a signalé à Kishida que le rejet japonais d’eaux usées est une préoccupation publique internationale et a incité le Japon à gérer ce dossier de façon responsable et constructive, selon la Télévision centrale de Chine. La rencontre s’est tenue un jour après que le président américain Joe Biden a salué l’amélioration des relations sino-américaines après ses propres discussions avec Xi, facilitant ainsi le rapprochement entre le Japon et la Chine, son plus grand partenaire commercial. Le Japon et la Chine restent en désaccord sur des questions comme les semi-conducteurs, les déchets nucléaires, la détention de citoyens japonais en Chine et un conflit territorial autour d’îles inhabitées proches de Taïwan. Kishida a demandé la levée par Xi de l’interdiction chinoise sur les fruits de mer japonais, décidée après le rejet par le Japon d’eaux traitées de la centrale de Fukushima. L’Agence internationale de l’énergie atomique considère ce rejet comme sûr. Les restrictions chinoises affectent négativement des entreprises japonaises, telles que le fabricant de cosmétiques Shiseido Co., qui a récemment baissé ses prévisions de bénéfices. L’opinion publique japonaise vis-à-vis de la Chine est à son niveau le plus négatif depuis 2014, indique un récent sondage. Xi a affirmé que les deux pays devaient privilégier leurs intérêts communs, gérer leurs différends avec soin et réaffirmer leur partenariat stratégique. Il a souligné les liens économiques étroits liant les deux pays et précisé qu’il est dans l’intérêt de tous de préserver ces chaînes d’approvisionnement. Kishida a confirmé vouloir œuvrer pour un avenir meilleur entre le Japon et la Chine au bénéfice des jeunes générations. La Chine a critiqué le Japon pour avoir suivi les États-Unis dans le renforcement du contrôle des exportations technologiques vers la Chine. Cette semaine, les deux pays ont accepté de lancer un dialogue sur le contrôle des exportations, d’après le ministère chinois du Commerce. Ils ont également prévu de reprendre des discussions économiques de haut niveau en temps voulu, selon le ministère japonais des Affaires étrangères. Kishida a exprimé de l’inquiétude concernant la mer de Chine orientale, où les navires des deux pays patrouillent dans des eaux contestées, et a demandé à Xi de retirer une bouée chinoise de la zone économique exclusive revendiquée par le Japon. En 2022, le Japon a qualifié la Chine de « défi sécuritaire sans précédent » et prépare son plus grand renforcement militaire depuis la Seconde Guerre mondiale, une décision qui a irrité Pékin. Kishida a demandé plus de transparence dans les procédures judiciaires et la libération de citoyens japonais détenus en Chine. Un Japonais a vu sa condamnation à 12 ans confirmée ce mois-ci et un salarié d’Astellas Pharma Inc. a été inculpé en octobre après une détention plus tôt. Les détails des accusations n’ont pas été rendus publics.

article_content: Central Americans crossing the U.S. border in large numbers have been described as immigrants or refugees. This distinction is important, as it can determine whether a migrant is eligible to remain in the United States under asylum or is subject to deportation to their home country. An immigrant is someone who chooses to resettle in another country. The United States has a legal process by which immigrants may seek legal residency and, eventually, citizenship. However, many immigrants lack legal status and are therefore undocumented, making them subject to removal or deportation. The U.S. has an estimated 11 million undocumented immigrants, contributing to widespread agreement that the immigration system is in need of reform. Congress has been deadlocked for years over how to address these issues. Economic migrants, according to the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, move to improve prospects for themselves or their families. Refugees, on the other hand, are forced to leave their home country to protect their lives or freedom. A refugee is a person who has been compelled to flee their home country. Refugees may apply for asylum in the United States, though the process can take years. Gaining refugee status is challenging; applicants must prove they would face serious harm if they returned home, due to their race, religion, nationality, membership in a particular social group, or political opinion. According to the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, refugees are typically outside their home country and unable or unwilling to return out of fear of serious harm. Most Central Americans crossing the U.S.-Mexican border are from Honduras, Guatemala, and El Salvador. Many cite violence related to drugs and gangs as the reason for fleeing. However, general violence does not always qualify as grounds for refugee status—it must be shown that an individual is specifically targeted, which can make these cases complex. Additionally, a law signed by President George W. Bush in 2008, the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act, offers special protections for unaccompanied minors. The law ensures that children entering the U.S. receive a full immigration hearing rather than being automatically turned away or returned. These hearings determine if children have valid asylum claims. This law is one reason cited for the increase in unaccompanied children at the border, with projections of up to 90,000 children from Central America and Mexico crossing into the U.S., compared to 39,000 detained the previous year. Asylum is a form of protection for people who are already in the United States or seeking entry at a U.S. border. Reporting contributed by CNN's Tom Cohen.
translated_content: Les Centraméricains traversant la frontière américaine en grand nombre sont qualifiés d'immigrants ou de réfugiés. Cette distinction est importante, car elle peut déterminer si un migrant peut rester aux États-Unis en tant que demandeur d'asile ou s'il risque une expulsion vers son pays d'origine. Un immigrant est une personne qui choisit de s’installer dans un autre pays. Les États-Unis disposent d’un processus légal permettant aux immigrants de demander la résidence légale puis la citoyenneté. Cependant, beaucoup d’immigrants n’ont pas de statut légal et sont donc en situation irrégulière, ce qui les expose à une expulsion. On estime à 11 millions le nombre d’immigrants sans papiers aux États-Unis, d’où un consensus sur la nécessité de réformer le système d’immigration. Le Congrès est bloqué depuis des années sur ces questions. Selon le Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés, les migrants économiques se déplacent pour améliorer leur avenir ou celui de leur famille. Les réfugiés, à l’inverse, sont contraints de quitter leur pays afin de protéger leur vie ou leur liberté. Un réfugié est une personne obligée de fuir son pays d’origine. Les réfugiés peuvent demander l’asile aux États-Unis, bien que cela soit un processus long. Obtenir le statut de réfugié est difficile ; les demandeurs doivent prouver qu’ils risqueraient de graves préjudices à leur retour, en raison de leur race, religion, nationalité, appartenance à un groupe social particulier ou de leurs opinions politiques. Selon les services américains de citoyenneté et d’immigration, les réfugiés sont généralement à l’extérieur de leur pays d’origine et ne peuvent ou ne veulent pas y retourner à cause de craintes sérieuses. La plupart des Centraméricains franchissant la frontière américano-mexicaine viennent du Honduras, du Guatemala et du Salvador. Beaucoup fuient des violences liées à la drogue et aux gangs. Toutefois, la violence en général ne permet pas toujours d’obtenir le statut de réfugié : il faut démontrer qu’une personne est spécifiquement ciblée, ce qui complique ces dossiers. De plus, une loi signée par le président George W. Bush en 2008, la loi William Wilberforce sur la protection des victimes de la traite, accorde des protections particulières aux mineurs non accompagnés. Cette loi garantit que les enfants entrant aux États-Unis bénéficient d’une audience complète devant l’immigration, au lieu d’être automatiquement refoulés. Ces audiences déterminent si les enfants ont droit à l’asile. Cette loi est citée comme l'une des raisons de l’augmentation du nombre d’enfants non accompagnés à la frontière, avec jusqu’à 90 000 enfants centraméricains et mexicains attendus cette année, contre 39 000 ayant été retenus l’an dernier. L’asile est une forme de protection destinée aux personnes déjà présentes aux États-Unis ou cherchant à y entrer à la frontière. Contribution de Tom Cohen pour CNN.

article_content: A recent study led by Ruxandra Malina Petrescu-Mag of Babes-Bolyai University, published in PeerJ Life & Environment, explores how media narratives shape public perception and awareness of microplastic risks. Microplastics—tiny plastic particles that contaminate both land and water ecosystems—have drawn considerable attention from scientists, the media, and the public in recent years. The study highlights a gap between how scientists and the media depict the dangers of microplastics over time. Titled 'The Influence of Media Narratives on Microplastics Risk Perception,' the research addresses the need to understand the social factors that affect public awareness and perceptions of risks caused by microplastics. The study had two main objectives: to assess whether media narratives impacted awareness of microplastics in Romania, and to examine how media influenced perceptions of health and environmental risks related to microplastics. An online survey with 417 Romanian respondents used 21 questions to measure awareness of microplastics, perceptions of associated health and environmental risks, exposure to media narratives, and demographic data. The data was analyzed using binary logistic regression to pinpoint which media stories most influenced awareness and risk perception. Results showed that media narratives play a crucial role in increasing public awareness. The narrative 'Microplastics in the sea threaten fish stocks' significantly heightened awareness about microplastics among respondents. Additionally, older participants were more likely to be aware of microplastics, suggesting age is also a contributing factor. The perceived health danger of microplastics was strongly shaped by the narrative 'Leakage of harmful chemicals from microplastics affects the soil.' This emphasizes the media's growing influence on how people view environmental and health issues. The study underlines the importance of delivering clear, accurate information to the public about microplastics to prevent misinformation and support informed choices. Understanding public attitudes can help develop targeted strategies to reduce plastic use and lessen microplastic pollution, benefiting both human health and the environment. Overall, the study is an important step toward clarifying how media stories influence perceptions of microplastics. Its findings can inform future research and policymaking as concerns about plastic pollution grow worldwide.
translated_content: Une étude récente menée par Ruxandra Malina Petrescu-Mag de l'Université Babeș-Bolyai, publiée dans PeerJ Life & Environment, analyse comment les récits médiatiques influencent la perception et la sensibilisation du public aux risques liés aux microplastiques. Les microplastiques—de minuscules particules de plastique qui contaminent les écosystèmes terrestres et aquatiques—ont suscité une attention considérable de la part des scientifiques, des médias et du public ces dernières années. L'étude met en évidence un écart entre la façon dont les scientifiques et les médias présentent les dangers des microplastiques au fil du temps. Intitulée « L'influence des récits médiatiques sur la perception des risques des microplastiques », la recherche insiste sur la nécessité de comprendre les facteurs sociaux qui affectent la sensibilisation du public et la perception des risques causés par les microplastiques. L'étude avait deux objectifs principaux : évaluer si les récits médiatiques influençaient la sensibilisation aux microplastiques en Roumanie, et examiner comment les médias affectaient la perception des risques sanitaires et environnementaux associés aux microplastiques. Une enquête en ligne auprès de 417 participants roumains comportait 21 questions pour mesurer la sensibilisation aux microplastiques, la perception des risques pour la santé et l'environnement, l'exposition aux récits médiatiques, ainsi que des données démographiques. Les données ont été analysées à l'aide d'une régression logistique binaire pour identifier les récits médiatiques ayant le plus d'impact sur la sensibilisation et la perception du risque. Les résultats ont montré que les récits médiatiques jouent un rôle crucial dans l'accroissement de la sensibilisation du public. Le récit « Les microplastiques dans la mer menacent les stocks de poissons » a considérablement accru la sensibilisation aux microplastiques chez les répondants. De plus, les personnes plus âgées étaient plus susceptibles de connaître les microplastiques, ce qui suggère que l'âge est également un facteur. La perception du danger sanitaire posé par les microplastiques a été fortement influencée par le récit « Les fuites de produits chimiques nocifs issus des microplastiques affectent le sol ». Cela souligne l'influence croissante des médias sur la manière dont les gens perçoivent les enjeux environnementaux et sanitaires. L'étude souligne l'importance de fournir au public des informations claires et exactes sur les microplastiques afin de prévenir la désinformation et d’encourager des choix éclairés. Comprendre les attitudes du public peut aider à développer des stratégies ciblées pour réduire l'utilisation du plastique et la pollution par les microplastiques, au bénéfice de la santé humaine et de l'environnement. Dans l'ensemble, l'étude constitue une étape importante pour mieux comprendre l'influence des récits médiatiques sur la perception des microplastiques. Ses résultats pourront orienter de futures recherches et politiques alors que les préoccupations liées à la pollution plastique grandissent dans le monde.

article_content: B Y Vijayendra has been named the new president of the BJP in Karnataka and will formally start his role on November 15. As part of his new position, Vijayendra visited veteran politicians H D Deve Gowda (JD(S) leader), S M Krishna, and Basavaraj Bommai at their homes to receive their blessings. During their meeting, Deve Gowda stressed the importance of unity, encouraging the BJP and JD(S) to present a united front in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections, and to avoid misunderstandings. The JD(S) joined the BJP-led NDA alliance in September, and both parties plan to finalize seat sharing soon for the national polls. Vijayendra stated that Gowda was pleased about his appointment and advised him to travel across Karnataka, following the example of his father B S Yediyurappa, to mobilize public support. Gowda also emphasized resolving all issues amicably and attracting more young people into politics. After meeting Bommai, Vijayendra revealed that the former Chief Minister pledged support for the BJP’s election campaign under Vijayendra’s leadership. Regarding his appointment, Vijayendra credited Prime Minister Modi, Amit Shah, JP Nadda, and B L Santhosh for their roles, stating that senior party leaders are happy with the decision, and discouraged any negative speculation. Vijayendra also visited S M Krishna, who joined the BJP in 2017 after a long political career with Congress, serving as both Karnataka's Chief Minister and India's External Affairs Minister, seeking his blessings. Elsewhere, Indian tax authorities are looking into Apple, Google, and Amazon for potential tax shortfalls, Indians have become the biggest property buyers in Dubai, and Razorpay is contemplating relocating its parent holding to India, possibly incurring a substantial US tax bill.

article_content: If your business is focused on community-building, it’s important to ensure real, mutual value is present. Building communities around a brand is a growing trend, described by McKinsey as the 'big idea' for the 2020s. However, this effort is ineffective without providing tangible value to community members. Mutual value can be offered both through the community you create and the products or services your business provides. By focusing on both, you can build a strong brand that stands out over time. Research shows the power of brand communities: 64% of consumers want brands to connect with them. When they do, 57% of consumers increase spending, and 76% will choose a connected brand over a competitor. Social media gives companies a way to interact with customers, but its effectiveness varies. Some companies post rarely or respond slowly to messages, even though nearly 40% of consumers expect a reply within an hour. While valuable, social media isn’t the only way to build a community. Blogs, newsletters, and other content channels are also effective—but they must deliver real value, not just promotions. Brands that succeed in community-building start meaningful conversations, ask questions, share insights, and interact authentically. Acting as a hub for like-minded individuals makes a business influential within its industry. Despite these efforts, a business must provide real value through its offerings. For example, Eric Mao’s SnapSync created a smartwatch that allows children with mental and physical disabilities to control devices and toys using gestures. SnapSync started in a rehabilitation hospital and focused on the unique needs of that community. Parents not only pledged over $400,000 to its crowdfunding campaign but also helped improve the product through feedback. Across industries, brands that connect deeply with their audiences and solve specific pain points in meaningful, personalized ways stand out. Achieving this requires understanding the needs of your community and delivering effective solutions. When businesses deliver real value, communities notice and talk about it. For example, 74% of people leave online reviews for local businesses, 54% of online shoppers read at least four reviews before purchasing, and 82% look at reviews to learn about businesses. In today’s marketplace, businesses can’t focus only on online communities or solely on product development. Both are essential and should work together. Community-building efforts can provide insights into your audience, informing product development and refining services. Likewise, the real value offered by your business should guide community engagements, even if content isn’t purely promotional. The strongest communities are built when businesses create mutual value—engaging audiences while providing excellent products or services. This encourages lasting loyalty and ensures your brand remains relevant.

En vous concentrant sur ces deux aspects, vous pouvez bâtir une marque forte qui se distingue dans le temps. Certaines entreprises publient rarement ou répondent lentement aux messages, même si près de 40 % des consommateurs attendent une réponse en moins d’une heure. Bien qu’utiles, les réseaux sociaux ne sont pas le seul moyen de bâtir une communauté. Les blogs, newsletters et autres canaux de contenu sont aussi efficaces — à condition d’apporter une vraie valeur, pas seulement des promotions. Les marques qui réussissent lancent des conversations, posent des questions, partagent des idées et interagissent de façon authentique. Être un point de rencontre pour des personnes partageant les mêmes valeurs rend une entreprise influente dans son secteur. Par ailleurs, une entreprise doit apporter une vraie valeur à travers ses offres. Par exemple, SnapSync d’Eric Mao a créé une montre connectée permettant à des enfants ayant des handicaps physiques et mentaux de contrôler des appareils et des jouets par des gestes. SnapSync a commencé dans un hôpital de rééducation, répondant aux besoins spécifiques de cette communauté. Les parents ont non seulement soutenu la campagne de financement participatif à hauteur de plus de 400 000 $, mais ont aussi aidé à améliorer le produit avec leurs retours. Dans tous les secteurs, les marques qui se connectent réellement à leur public et répondent à leurs besoins de façon personnalisée se démarquent. De même, la valeur réelle offerte par l’entreprise doit inspirer les interactions communautaires, même si le contenu n’est pas purement promotionnel. Les communautés les plus fortes sont créées quand les entreprises apportent une valeur mutuelle : en impliquant leur public et en offrant d’excellents produits ou services. Cela encourage la fidélité et garantit la pérennité de la marque.

article_content: New York officials are seeking penalties from Donald Trump that may exceed the $250 million already demanded, as revealed during testimony on Thursday by Donald Trump Jr. At the end of his appearance in the New York civil fraud trial, it was disclosed that Trump could now face millions more in penalties. A lawyer for the state attorney general's office stated in court that the state is seeking a portion of the $60 million Donald Trump received earlier this year. That sum came from Bally's, which paid Trump to take over the former president's lease for a public golf course in the Bronx. The specific amount New York intends to pursue from the $60 million was not clarified in the Manhattan courtroom as the trial entered its fifth week. This new development was revealed during a lighthearted exchange. "This is a big one," said Colleen Faherty, a lawyer representing the state AG, referring to a document related to the sale. She had referenced a prior joke made by Trump Jr. about signing a lengthy 2019 letter. The current document was the nearly 400-page agreement of sale for the golf course lease, signed by Trump Jr., who is the president of Trump Ferry Point LLC. Faherty joked that she would not ask Trump Jr. to review the entire document, to which he responded in kind. She then asked him to confirm his signature on page 34, which he identified as his own. Faherty confirmed with Trump Jr. that the transaction had closed. At this point, defense attorney Christopher Kise objected, arguing that the lease sale was not relevant to the $250 million lawsuit and that the Bronx golf course was not involved in any alleged fraud. Faherty responded by introducing the term 'disgorgement,' a legal process requiring the repayment of unlawfully gained money, and argued that the sale proceeds were relevant because they could be subject to disgorgement. Judge Arthur Engoron allowed the sale agreement to be entered into evidence, and its contents were displayed in court. Faherty asked Trump Jr., as president of Trump Ferry Point LLC, how much he made from the transaction. Amid further objections, Trump Jr. replied, 'I didn't make any.' He said the sale price was $60 million but that there were other costs involved over the years, so he did not know the net profit. The AG's office has said it will seek at least $250 million in total disgorgement from the lawsuit's defendants: Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Allen Weisselberg, and Jeffrey McConney. This figure includes millions gained from favorable loan terms and property sales, including from Trump's sale of the Old Post Office lease for the Trump International Hotel in Washington, DC. The exact disgorgement amount will be decided by the judge after trial testimony concludes in late December.

Le montant exact que New York prévoit de réclamer sur les 60 millions de dollars n’a pas été précisé dans la salle d’audience de Manhattan, alors que le procès entamait sa cinquième semaine. Ce nouveau développement a été révélé lors d’un échange détendu. "C’est une grosse affaire", a déclaré Colleen Faherty, avocate du bureau du procureur général, à propos d'un document lié à la vente. Elle faisait référence à une blague précédente de Trump Jr. sur la signature d'une longue lettre en 2019. Faherty a plaisanté en disant qu'elle ne demanderait pas à Trump Jr. de lire tout le document, ce à quoi il a répondu avec humour. Elle lui a ensuite demandé de confirmer sa signature à la page 34, qu'il a reconnue comme la sienne. Faherty a confirmé avec Trump Jr. que la transaction avait bien été finalisée. À ce moment-là, l’avocat de la défense, Christopher Kise, s’est opposé, soutenant que la vente du bail n’était pas pertinente pour la plainte de 250 millions de dollars et que le terrain de golf du Bronx n’était pas impliqué dans une fraude présumée. Faherty a répliqué en introduisant le terme « restitution » (« disgorgement »), un procédé juridique forçant le remboursement d'argent obtenu illégalement, et a affirmé que le produit de la vente pouvait être soumis à restitution. Le juge Arthur Engoron a autorisé que l'accord de vente soit admis comme preuve, et son contenu a été présenté au tribunal. Faherty a demandé à Trump Jr., président de Trump Ferry Point LLC, combien il avait tiré de cette opération. Malgré d'autres objections, Trump Jr. a répondu : « Je n'ai rien gagné. » Il a précisé que le prix de vente était de 60 millions de dollars mais que d'autres coûts avaient été engagés au fil des années, il ne connaissait donc pas le bénéfice net. Le bureau du procureur général a déclaré vouloir obtenir au moins 250 millions de dollars en restitution de la part des défendeurs : Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Allen Weisselberg et Jeffrey McConney. Ce montant inclut des millions obtenus via des prêts avantageux et des ventes de biens, notamment la vente du bail de l’Old Post Office par Trump pour l’hôtel Trump International à Washington, DC. Le montant exact de la restitution sera fixé par le juge une fois les témoignages terminés fin décembre.

article_content: Members of Pope Francis' commission on sex abuse have openly criticized his recent remarks suggesting it is acceptable for parents to physically discipline their children as punishment for misbehavior. Pope Francis stated that parents should discipline their children, 'do the right thing, and then move on,' and he gestured as if smacking a child lightly. The commission responded that there is no place for physical discipline in parenting and indicated that recommendations would be made to the Pope to protect children from corporal punishment. During his weekly general audience in St Peter's Square, Pope Francis recalled a conversation with a father who said, 'At times I have to hit my children a little, but never in the face so as not to humiliate them.' The Pope responded approvingly, saying, 'That's great. He had a sense of dignity. He should punish, do the right thing, and then move on.' Commission member Peter Saunders, himself a survivor of sexual abuse by a priest, said the committee would recommend the Pope revise his remarks, noting that 'millions of children around the world are physically beaten every day.' Saunders emphasized, 'Even if it starts as a light tap, the concept is about inflicting pain. There is no place today for physical punishment as disciplinary practice.' Dr. Krysten Winter-Green, another commission member from New Zealand working in the US, added, 'There is no form of corporal punishment for children that is acceptable. There must be positive parenting, approached differently.' This week, the full commission of 17 members convened for the first time and reported progress in drafting policies to hold bishops accountable if they cover up abuse by priests. The commission will also organize educational sessions for Vatican officials and bishops to enhance child protection measures. Pope Francis sent a letter this week to Catholic clergy leaders, stressing the need for cooperation with the new sex abuse inquiry, even if it reveals further scandals. In a strongly worded letter to bishops' conferences and religious orders, he demanded 'full and complete' cooperation with a new Vatican child protection watchdog, stating, 'Families need to know that the Church is making every effort to protect their children.' He added that concerns over avoiding scandal must not take precedence over child protection, as there is no place in ministry for those who abuse minors. The Pontifical Commission for the Protection of Minors is tasked with advancing reforms on the issue, which has greatly impacted the Church’s credibility worldwide. Separately, Pope Francis recently apologized to large Catholic families after previously suggesting that there was no need to 'breed like rabbits,' advocating instead for responsible parenthood. He had commented that having three children might be 'about right.' Archbishop Giovanni Becciu issued an apology on behalf of the Pope, affirming that the Pope did not mean to undervalue large families or their contributions.

Le pape François a déclaré que les parents devaient discipliner leurs enfants, « faire ce qu’il faut, puis passer à autre chose », tout en mimant une légère tape. La commission a répondu qu’il n’y avait aucune place pour la discipline physique dans l’éducation et a indiqué qu’elle ferait des recommandations au pape pour protéger les enfants contre les châtiments corporels. Lors de son audience générale hebdomadaire place Saint-Pierre, le pape François a raconté une conversation avec un père qui lui a dit : « Il m’arrive parfois de donner une petite tape à mes enfants, mais jamais au visage pour ne pas les humilier. » Le pape a répondu positivement : « C’est bien. Il avait un sens de la dignité. Il doit punir, faire ce qu’il faut, puis passer à autre chose. » Peter Saunders, membre de la commission et lui-même survivant d’abus sexuels commis par un prêtre, a déclaré que le comité recommanderait au pape de revoir ses propos, notant que « des millions d’enfants dans le monde sont frappés chaque jour ». Saunders a souligné : « Même si cela commence par une petite tape, l’idée est d’infliger de la douleur. Il n’y a plus de place aujourd’hui pour la punition physique comme méthode disciplinaire. » La Dre Krysten Winter-Green, autre membre de la commission originaire de Nouvelle-Zélande et travaillant aujourd’hui aux États-Unis, a ajouté : « Il n’existe aucune forme de châtiment corporel acceptable pour les enfants. Il faut une éducation positive, adoptée différemment. » Cette semaine, les 17 membres de la commission se sont réunis au complet pour la première fois et ont annoncé des avancées dans l’élaboration de politiques visant à rendre les évêques responsables s’ils dissimulent des abus commis par des prêtres. La commission organisera également des sessions éducatives pour les responsables du Vatican et les évêques afin de renforcer la protection des enfants. Le pape François a envoyé cette semaine une lettre aux responsables du clergé catholique, soulignant la nécessité de coopérer avec la nouvelle enquête sur les abus sexuels, même si cela entraîne la découverte de nouveaux scandales. Dans une lettre ferme adressée aux conférences épiscopales et aux ordres religieux, il a exigé une coopération « totale et complète » avec un nouveau comité de protection de l’enfance au Vatican, déclarant : « Les familles doivent savoir que l’Église fait tout son possible pour protéger leurs enfants. » Il a ajouté que l’on ne devait pas privilégier la volonté d’éviter un scandale à la protection des enfants, car il n’y a pas de place dans le ministère pour ceux qui abusent des mineurs. La Commission pontificale pour la protection des mineurs est chargée de faire avancer les réformes sur ce sujet, qui a gravement affecté la crédibilité de l’Église dans le monde. Par ailleurs, le pape François a récemment présenté ses excuses aux familles catholiques nombreuses après avoir suggéré qu’il n’était pas nécessaire de « se reproduire comme des lapins », plaidant plutôt pour une parentalité responsable. Il avait indiqué que trois enfants semblaient être un « bon nombre ». L’archevêque Giovanni Becciu a présenté des excuses au nom du pape, affirmant que ce dernier ne voulait absolument pas dévaloriser les familles nombreuses ou leurs contributions.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has dismissed suggestions that the conflict with Russia has reached a stalemate, countering claims from some officials and media reports. At a news conference in Kyiv with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Zelenskyy stated, “Time has passed, people are tired… But this is not a stalemate.” He also rejected assertions that Western nations are pushing Ukraine to engage in peace talks with Russia, emphasizing, “No one among our partners is pressuring us to sit down with Russia, talk to it, and give it something.” Zelenskyy noted that while such pressure existed at the start of the war in February 2022, this is no longer the case, as neither EU nor US leaders are advocating for negotiations on Russia’s terms.

Expressing frustration with persistent media reports about diplomatic pressure, Zelenskyy underscored his intent to follow the will of the Ukrainian people. The war, now entering its 20th month, has seen limited movement along the front lines and Ukraine facing challenges in its counteroffensive. Zelenskyy continues to meet with Western leaders, seeking to maintain international support despite signs of conflict fatigue.

He acknowledged that the war between Israel and Hamas has diverted global attention from Ukraine, which he claims is “Russia’s goal.” Nonetheless, Zelenskyy voiced confidence in Ukraine’s resilience, adding, “I am absolutely sure we will overcome this challenge.” Western backers, including the United States, remain committed to providing military and financial support to Ukraine for as long as necessary.
