article_content: It is often said that behind every powerful man is a strong woman, and a cheeky remark by senior Liberal Democrat Danny Alexander suggests that this holds true for the Deputy Prime Minister. Danny Alexander, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, joked that Nick Clegg starts his text messages with 'OMG', meaning 'On Miriam’s Guidance', referring to Clegg's wife Miriam. The comment was made in a lighthearted manner during an informal lunch with journalists. A spokesperson for Mr. Clegg confirmed the remarks were made as a joke and that the Deputy Prime Minister found them amusing. Alexander's comments came after it was revealed that David Cameron signed text messages 'LOL'—standing for 'lots of love'—to Rebekah Brooks, the former News International executive. Alexander quipped, 'Rebekah Brooks and I have more than red hair in common. I have also received unusual texts from a senior government member, but mine are from the Deputy Prime Minister, not the Prime Minister.' He explained, 'Initially, during our first few months in office, I was concerned because every text from Nick Clegg began with 'OMG'. As it turns out, in the Clegg household, this stands for ‘On Miriam's Guidance’.' Nick Clegg’s wife, 44-year-old Miriam González Durántez, is a senior lawyer specializing in European Union trade and government affairs, currently working at Dechert LLP after leaving DLA Piper earlier in the year. During the 2010 general election, Mrs. Clegg appeared alongside her husband and expressed willingness to help with the campaign. However, unlike Samantha Cameron, she noted she could not take extended time off from her own career and family to participate fully. She told a Spanish newspaper she would consider leaving her job if her husband became Prime Minister and it was necessary for the country, saying, 'There are a number of reasons why I would quit my job... if Nick were Prime Minister and I had to support the country, I would have no problem in doing so.' The Cleggs married in 2000. Mr. Clegg has shared that he was 'bewitched' by Miriam when they met in Belgium, even learning Spanish to win her over. In an interview with Grazia magazine, Miriam said she is often asked how she balances her three children and demanding career, remarking, 'I always get surprised by this, because my husband also has three children, a busy career, and a busy wife.' She praised Mr. Clegg’s efforts to balance fatherhood with his political responsibilities. Miriam González Durántez, who is Roman Catholic, chose Spanish names for their sons: Antonio, Alberto, and Miguel, explaining that they needed something more distinctive than the Clegg surname. She rarely appears in public but has featured in fashion publications, including Vogue. Danny Alexander concluded his remarks by emphasizing the significant contribution of the Liberal Democrats to government, stating the party continues to 'anchor this government firmly in the centre ground.'

North Korea has announced the closure of several diplomatic missions abroad as it continues to struggle with international sanctions and economic challenges. So far, missions in Spain, Hong Kong, Angola, and Uganda have been affected, and analysts estimate up to 10 embassies—roughly 20 percent of Pyongyang’s overseas presence—could be closed.

A spokesperson for North Korea’s foreign ministry stated on Friday: “We are carrying out operations to withdraw and establish diplomatic missions in accordance with the changing global environment and our national foreign policy.” The spokesperson added that while some embassies would close, others may open, calling the changes “a routine part of external relations aimed at promoting national interests.”

According to South Korea’s Ministry of Unification, North Korea maintains diplomatic ties with over 150 countries, but operates relatively few embassies and consulates. The last major wave of closures occurred in the 1990s during a severe famine. Now, experts note, North Korea’s difficulties are mounting due to sanctions that restrict its ability to earn foreign currency through secretive activities such as manufacturing, IT services, cyber operations, or military deals.

The Unification Ministry interprets the closures as evidence that “strengthened sanctions have disrupted North Korea’s foreign currency earnings” and made it harder for even close allies to do business. “This is a glimpse of North Korea’s dire economic situation, where maintaining even minimal diplomatic relations with traditional partners has become difficult,” the ministry stated.

Cho Han-bum, a senior research fellow at the Korea Institute for National Unification, said economic hardship is the main factor: “Cyber hacking is not enough to sustain the economy. Economic struggles and depleted currency reserves are the main reasons for the embassy closures.” 

The situation worsened after North Korea sealed its borders during the COVID-19 pandemic. Analysts say the closures also reflect a diplomatic strategy shift: Pyongyang is focusing less on old partners from the Non-Aligned Movement, like Angola and Uganda, and more on key countries such as China and Russia.

Thae Yong-ho, a former North Korean diplomat who defected to South Korea, commented: “North Korea will reinforce its so-called new Cold War diplomacy with important countries like China, Russia, Syria, Iran, and Cuba, while withdrawing from more difficult or costly postings. Still, the overall result will be a reduced diplomatic capability.”

La Corée du Nord a annoncé la fermeture de plusieurs missions diplomatiques à l’étranger, alors qu’elle fait face à des sanctions internationales et à une économie affaiblie. À ce jour, les représentations en Espagne, à Hong Kong, en Angola et en Ouganda sont concernées. Les analystes estiment qu’au total jusqu’à 10 ambassades, soit environ 20 % de la présence diplomatique de Pyongyang, pourraient être fermées.

Un porte-parole du ministère des Affaires étrangères nord-coréen a déclaré vendredi : « Nous procédons à des retraits et à de nouvelles installations de missions diplomatiques, en fonction de l’évolution de l’environnement international et de notre politique étrangère. » Il a ajouté que, tandis que certaines ambassades fermeront, d’autres pourraient ouvrir, qualifiant ces modifications de « démarches régulières pour promouvoir les intérêts nationaux dans nos relations extérieures ».

Selon le ministère sud-coréen de l’Unification, la Corée du Nord entretient des relations diplomatiques avec plus de 150 pays, mais dispose de peu d’ambassades et de consulats. La dernière vague majeure de fermetures avait eu lieu dans les années 1990 lors d’une grave famine. Aujourd’hui, selon les experts, les difficultés du pays s’accroissent à cause des sanctions qui freinent ses revenus en devises grâce à des activités discrètes comme la fabrication, les services informatiques, le piratage ou les ventes militaires.

Le ministère sud-coréen de l’Unification considère que ces fermetures montrent que « le renforcement des sanctions perturbe les revenus en devises de la Corée du Nord » et complique même les échanges avec ses alliés proches. « C’est le reflet de la situation économique critique du pays, où entretenir au minimum des liens diplomatiques avec des partenaires traditionnels devient difficile », a expliqué le ministère.

Cho Han-bum, chercheur émérite à l’Institut coréen pour l’Unification nationale, affirme : « Le piratage informatique ne suffit pas à faire tourner l’économie. Ce sont bien les difficultés économiques et la fuite des devises qui expliquent ces fermetures d’ambassades. »

La situation s’est aggravée depuis que la Corée du Nord a fermé ses frontières à cause de la pandémie de COVID-19. Les analystes ajoutent que ces fermetures montrent aussi un changement de stratégie diplomatique : Pyongyang se concentre moins sur ses anciens partenaires du Mouvement des non-alignés, comme l’Angola ou l’Ouganda, et davantage sur des pays clés tels que la Chine et la Russie.

Thae Yong-ho, ex-diplomate nord-coréen ayant fait défection en Corée du Sud, commente : « La Corée du Nord va renforcer sa soi-disant diplomatie de ‘nouvelle guerre froide’ avec des partenaires majeurs comme la Chine, la Russie, la Syrie, l’Iran et Cuba, tout en mettant fin aux missions difficiles ou coûteuses. Mais cela conduira inévitablement à une capacité diplomatique globale réduite. »

A French prosecutor has closed an investigation into former International Monetary Fund chief Dominique Strauss-Kahn regarding a potential gang rape in Washington, as announced on Tuesday. The case was dropped after the young Belgian woman whose testimony prompted the inquiry withdrew her statement and indicated she would not press charges, according to the Lille prosecutor's office. With her withdrawal and lack of further testimony, authorities stated there was no basis to proceed.

Strauss-Kahn remains under investigation in France for alleged involvement in a prostitution ring known as the 'Carlton affair.' He has denied any wrongdoing and has not been convicted of any crime. The gang rape inquiry originally emerged from statements during the prostitution ring investigation, which led police to refer the Washington incident to Lille prosecutors earlier this year.

In August, the Belgian woman's lawyer informed authorities that his client would not provide any judicial statement about the matter. In a subsequent letter, she stated that her relations had been consensual and that she would not press charges. She also did not file a complaint when interviewed by French and Belgian investigators late last year.

The prosecutor's office concluded that, in light of all these circumstances, the offense of rape could not be established, and decided to take no further action.

Strauss-Kahn previously faced attempted rape allegations in New York last year, but those charges were dismissed after questions were raised about the witness's credibility.
translated_content:
Un procureur français a classé sans suite l'enquête visant l'ancien chef du Fonds monétaire international, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, concernant une possible agression sexuelle en réunion à Washington, d'après une annonce faite mardi. L'affaire a été abandonnée après que la jeune Belge à l'origine de l'enquête a retiré ses déclarations et indiqué qu'elle ne porterait pas plainte, selon le parquet de Lille. En l'absence de son témoignage et de nouvelles déclarations, les autorités ont estimé qu'il n'y avait pas de fondement pour poursuivre la procédure.

Strauss-Kahn reste cependant sous enquête en France pour une implication présumée dans un réseau de proxénétisme, connu comme l'« affaire du Carlton ». Il nie toute faute et n'a pas été condamné. Cette enquête pour agression sexuelle en réunion trouve son origine dans des déclarations pendant l'enquête sur l'affaire du Carlton, ce qui a conduit la police à transmettre l'incident de Washington au parquet de Lille plus tôt cette année.

En août, l'avocat de la Belge a informé les autorités que sa cliente ne souhaitait pas faire de déclaration judiciaire à ce sujet. Dans une lettre, elle a précisé que les relations avaient été consenties et qu'elle ne souhaitait pas porter plainte. Elle n'avait d'ailleurs pas déposé de plainte lors de son audition par les enquêteurs français et belges à la fin de l'année dernière.

Le parquet a conclu qu'au vu de l'ensemble de ces éléments, l'infraction de viol ne pouvait pas être retenue et a décidé de classer l'affaire sans suite.

Strauss-Kahn avait déjà été visé l'année dernière par des accusations de tentative de viol à New York, mais ces charges ont été abandonnées après des doutes sur la crédibilité du témoignage.

article_content: Shortly after Maharashtra Chief Minister Eknath Shinde inaugurated the regional office of the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar-headquartered Maharashtra State Wakf Board in Mumbai, Abdul Sattar, Minister for Minorities Development and Wakf, announced a significant increase in funding for the Maulana Azad Minorities Financial Development Corporation (MAMFDC). This key agency for providing education and business loans will see its credit guarantee expand from Rs 30 crore to Rs 500 crore, and working capital from Rs 700 crore to Rs 1,000 crore. Sattar stated, 'We will increase the scholarship amount for minority students as the corporation receives more funds.' He spoke at two meetings organized by the Indian Minorities Foundation at Birla Matoshree and Islam Gymkhana. Additional measures for the minority community include the plan to establish an Urdu Ghar, strengthen the Urdu Academy, and promote the madrassa modernization scheme. Separately, the NGO Praja Foundation reported that, from 2018 to 2022, 61% of rape cases in Mumbai involved minors. The report further notes that 73% of 3,360 cases investigated under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in 2022 were still pending. Activists are calling for the creation of special courts, additional judges, better-trained police, and a multi-stakeholder approach to tackle child sexual abuse. The findings also revealed that underage girls in consensual relationships could be classified as rape victims under current laws. The state forensic science laboratory in Kalina faces a backlog of over 25,390 cases due to personnel shortages. In Nepal, new school and laboratory buildings at Shree Gautam Buddha Secondary School in Kapilvastu District have been inaugurated with support from the Government of India under the Nepal-India Development Cooperation initiative. Conducted with the District Coordination Committee, the project features a double-storey school building, a three-storey laboratory building, and the procurement of furniture and lab equipment. Prasanna Shrivastava, Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu, highlighted the importance of this project in strengthening India-Nepal development relations. Since 2003, India has completed 488 High Impact Community Development Projects (HICDPs) in Nepal, including five in Kapilvastu. In other news, a Delhi court is set to decide on January 11, 2024, whether to accept the closure report of the Delhi Police regarding a sexual harassment complaint against BJP MP Brij Bhushan Singh, filed by a minor wrestler. The hearing was adjourned as the order was pending. The wrestler expressed satisfaction with the police investigation and did not oppose the closure report, which was sought after the wrestler’s father admitted the complaint was false.

article_content: As the war in Ukraine reached its 606th day on October 22, 2023, diplomatic efforts intensified. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed that Turkey would join upcoming peace negotiations after a conversation with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. Zelenskyy made this announcement via Telegram, confirming Turkey’s involvement in the Peace Formula discussions set to take place in Malta on October 28 and 29. These talks are a continuation of meetings previously held in Jeddah and Copenhagen.

article_content: Israeli ground forces have stepped up their campaign in Gaza, encircling Gaza City and advancing into areas previously controlled by Hamas in the north. Backed by air and naval support, the IDF reports seizing 11 Hamas outposts and finding more than 130 tunnel entrances. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared that Hamas has effectively lost control in northern Gaza, with Israeli forces operating within the city. Over 100,000 residents have moved south from northern Gaza in the past two days, responding to IDF advisories to evacuate via humanitarian corridors for safety. The conflict began after Hamas's large-scale attacks on Israel on October 7, with roughly 9,500 rockets, missiles, and drones launched toward Israel since then. The IDF says some have landed in Gaza, including near hospitals, and claims about 900 launches originated from civilian locations like mosques and schools. Clashes on the Israel-Lebanon border have intensified, with Hezbollah attacks causing over 20 Israeli injuries and six Israeli soldiers killed in the past month. Israel responded to Hezbollah fire with airstrikes on positions in Lebanon, and reports indicate 71 Hezbollah members have been killed since the outbreak of fighting. The Iron Dome intercepted rocket barrages over Galilee and Haifa, and Israeli artillery struck launch sites and infrastructure. Southern Israel has also come under attack: a drone exploded in a school yard in Eilat, which was crowded with children. The IDF responded by striking a Syrian-based militia thought responsible, stating Israel would act forcefully against attacks from Syrian territory. In addition, a ballistic missile launched from Yemen by the pro-Iranian Houthis was intercepted by Israel's Arrow 3 system. Tensions remain high at Gaza hospitals. The IDF reports Hamas fighters fired anti-tank weapons at Israeli troops from near Al-Quds hospital, triggering return fire. At Al-Shifa hospital, Israeli officials claim Hamas prevented hospital staff from accepting an Israeli fuel delivery, although the hospital reported critical fuel shortages impacting patient care. The conflict has prompted global demonstrations. In London, around 300,000 people joined a pro-Palestinian march on Armistice Day, sparking debate about its timing and message, as well as clashes with far-right groups. British leaders, including Prime Minister Rishi Sunak and Home Secretary Suella Braverman, have condemned the protests and called for strong action against hate crimes. Meanwhile, rallies supporting Israel are happening in Latin America, Europe, and the United States. Paris hosted over 100,000 participants, including government officials and former presidents, in a protest against increasing antisemitism. In Washington, Jewish groups are organizing a demonstration demanding the release of hostages held by Hamas and unified efforts against antisemitism. In Los Angeles, investigators are examining the death of Paul Kessler, a 69-year-old Jewish man who died from injuries after an altercation during opposing protests. His death has been ruled a homicide. Despite ongoing violence, Israel’s cyber sector is thriving: U.S. company Palo Alto Networks recently announced acquisitions exceeding $1 billion for two Israeli cybersecurity firms, contributing to a record year for the industry. A documentary produced by the IDF, 'Bearing Witness,' was recently screened at Hollywood’s Museum of Tolerance, depicting the brutal October 7 attacks by Hamas with graphic footage captured by the attackers. The disturbing scenes led some viewers to leave before the film concluded.

Le conflit suscite des manifestations mondiales. À Londres, près de 300 000 personnes ont défilé pour la cause palestinienne lors de l’Armistice, ravivant débats sur le sens de la date et entraînant des heurts avec des groupes d’extrême droite. Des responsables britanniques comme Rishi Sunak ou Suella Braverman ont condamné ces rassemblements et exigent une tolérance zéro face aux crimes haineux. En parallèle, des rassemblements de soutien à Israël ont lieu en Amérique latine, en Europe et aux États-Unis. À Los Angeles, la police enquête sur la mort de Paul Kessler, 69 ans, décédé après une altercation lors de manifestations opposées. Sa mort a été classée homicide. Malgré les violences, le secteur cyber israélien ne faiblit pas : Palo Alto Networks, société américaine, vient d’annoncer plus d’un milliard de dollars d’acquisition de deux entreprises locales, participant à une année record pour la sécurité informatique nationale. À Hollywood, un documentaire réalisé par les FDI, « Bearing Witness », a été projeté au Museum of Tolerance. Le film retrace les attaques atroces du 7 octobre par le Hamas via des images particulièrement choquantes, qui ont poussé certains spectateurs à quitter la salle avant la fin.

A couple's romantic evening took an unexpected turn when they discovered a large cockroach in their meal at Mughli Restaurant on Manchester's Curry Mile. Stu Beevers, 28, and his girlfriend Natalie Roberts, 27, both from Stockport, were dining when Beevers found the insect, which he described as being the size of a two pound coin, in his chicken Kerala dish. Distressed by the discovery, the couple left the restaurant without paying and plan to report the incident to Manchester Council. Beevers said the incident left him physically ill for the rest of the night.

According to Natalie Roberts, the couple pointed out the cockroach to the staff, requesting an apology, but felt their concerns were dismissed. 'We just felt sick and wanted to leave,' Roberts said. She added that she kept the evidence and took a picture for documentation.

After being notified, Mughli Restaurant closed temporarily to conduct an internal investigation and reopened later that week. The restaurant, which has been open for 23 years and also operates a location in Knutsford, holds a four-star 'very good' food hygiene rating from Manchester Council, last inspected in October 2012.

A spokesperson for Mughli stated that they took immediate action by apologizing and suspending food service to investigate the matter. They noted there is no evidence the insect was cooked into the dish and emphasized the seriousness with which such allegations are handled. The restaurant maintains regular visits from hygiene specialists and reported that no prior evidence of cockroach activity was found. Mughli says they remain proactive in managing local vermin issues and are committed to finding out how the incident occurred.

Après avoir été informé, le restaurant Mughli a fermé temporairement pour mener une enquête interne, puis a rouvert plus tard dans la semaine. Mughli indique rester proactif dans la gestion des nuisibles locaux et s’engage à déterminer comment l’incident a pu se produire.

article_content: Despite China’s economy not achieving the post-pandemic rebound that many expected, the country’s movie industry has thrived. Between June and September, box office revenue reached a record high of 23.44 billion yuan ($3.2 billion), according to industry data from Dengta and Maoyan cited by CNN. This surge was led by especially strong ticket sales from June to August, totaling $2.8 billion and surpassing the previous 2019 record of $2.4 billion. CNN highlighted that women made up 61% of audiences for the top five films during this period, with approximately 570 million movie-goers in the summer, and about half of viewers aged between 20 and 29. Unlike in the US, where 'Barbie' and 'Oppenheimer' were the major hits, China’s most popular films were domestically produced, including titles such as 'No More Bets,' 'Lost in the Stars,' and 'Creation of the Gods I: Kingdom of Storms.' However, China still faces broader economic challenges, including an unstable property market, slowing growth, weak trade, and declining consumer confidence. Some experts have cautioned that issues in the real estate sector could trigger a situation similar to the 'Lehman moment,' with major defaults and widespread repercussions. Alfredo Montufar-Helu, head of the China Center at the Conference Board, said that 'the boom that characterized the property sector over the last decade is over.' He noted that China is at a crucial juncture: they must continue supporting the supply side to prevent further economic slowdown while also pursuing demand-side reforms. He expressed hope that these intentions alone can boost market confidence.

Cette hausse a été portée par des ventes de billets particulièrement élevées de juin à août, atteignant 2,8 milliards de dollars et dépassant le précédent record de 2019, qui était de 2,4 milliards de dollars. CNN a souligné que les femmes représentaient 61 % du public des cinq films les plus populaires pendant cette période, avec environ 570 millions de spectateurs cet été, dont près de la moitié étaient âgés de 20 à 29 ans. Contrairement aux États-Unis, où « Barbie » et « Oppenheimer » dominaient le box-office, les films les plus populaires en Chine étaient des productions locales, comme « No More Bets », « Lost in the Stars » et « Creation of the Gods I: Kingdom of Storms ». Cependant, la Chine fait toujours face à des défis économiques plus larges, notamment un marché immobilier instable, un ralentissement de la croissance, une faiblesse du commerce et une baisse de la confiance des consommateurs. Certains experts ont averti que les problèmes du secteur immobilier pourraient déclencher une situation similaire à une « crise Lehman », avec des défauts majeurs et des répercussions potentielles. Alfredo Montufar-Helu, directeur du China Center au Conference Board, a déclaré que « le boom qui a caractérisé le secteur immobilier au cours de la dernière décennie est terminé ». Il a souligné que la Chine se trouve à un moment crucial : elle doit continuer à soutenir le secteur de l’offre afin de prévenir un ralentissement économique, tout en menant des réformes du côté de la demande. Il a exprimé l’espoir que ces intentions suffiront à renforcer la confiance sur le marché.

article_content: Kate Middleton’s hair has become an object of global fascination, drawing as much attention as iconic features of past celebrities like Betty Grable’s famous legs. Every change—whether a wave, a color update, or a new style—sparks widespread media and public interest. London’s top salons vie for the credit of tending to the Duchess of Cambridge’s celebrated locks, with stylists eager to associate themselves with her signature look. The competition for this prestige has fostered professional rivalries, reminiscent of political intrigue, only more stylish. Throughout her engagement and wedding preparations, Kate—alongside her mother and sister—regularly visited the Richard Ward Salon in Chelsea. James Pryce, her main stylist at the time, was responsible for crafting her romantic half-chignon on the royal wedding day. Both Pryce and Richard Ward’s profiles rose dramatically following their work with Kate, but professional tensions eventually led to an acrimonious split. Since then, Pryce has joined Josh Wood Atelier, a salon known for attracting prominent stylists, many of whom have experienced similar professional disputes. The atelier prides itself on a collaborative and discreet environment, focusing on the craft rather than the politics of hairdressing. Adding to the competition, Italian stylist Rossano Ferretti claims to have revived Kate's hairstyle using his proprietary 'method,' reportedly priced at £600 per session. However, reports suggest the Duchess may have only attended a salon event rather than receiving a haircut from Ferretti. The true ongoing presence behind Kate’s hair is believed to be royal court stylist Amanda Cook Tucker, who has a long history styling members of the Royal Family. For those seeking similar hair, the article recommends several products: Ojon Volume Advance Thickening Spray for volume, John Frieda Full Repair Deep Conditioner for restoring hair, Boots Hair Loss Treatment with minoxidil, Superior Hair supplements, and Wella System Professional Shine Define Shampoo for added gloss. The article transitions into the author’s personal health journey, chronicling efforts to adopt healthier habits with the help of the Bodyism wellness program created by James Duigan. Despite remaining at 32% body fat, the columnist notes feeling less fatigued and making progress with small dietary changes, such as eating a nut-based breakfast instead of less nutritious options. Evening routines remain challenging, as cravings for wine and desserts are tough to resist. Trainer Rebecca recommends Bodyism’s Serenity shake to curb sweet cravings and assist with sleep, which the author finds surprisingly enjoyable as a night-time alternative. Additional notes include a recommendation of the Urban Decay Naked Palette 3 eyeshadow and a warning about low-energy lightbulbs, as new research has found they emit UVA rays that may contribute to premature skin aging. Using moisturizers with SPF 15 or higher is suggested for those spending extended time under such lighting.

article_content: After a violent incident at Canada's parliament, UK security agencies, including MI5 and Scotland Yard, held urgent consultations to reassess safety precautions for Parliament and prominent sites in London. The review follows an attack in Ottawa where Michael Zehaf-Bibeau killed a soldier at the National War Memorial and then entered the parliament building, where Sergeant-at-Arms Kevin Vickers intervened and neutralized the threat. Prime Minister David Cameron stressed the importance of constant vigilance in the UK against ongoing terrorist risks. He assured the public that security measures at key institutions are regularly evaluated and updated in response to emerging threats. Britain's terror threat level remains 'severe,' reflecting the substantial possibility of an attack. In response to the events in Canada, UK parliamentary committees are set to re-examine emergency response protocols and may issue revised guidance to staff at Westminster. Leaders such as Commons Leader William Hague and Labour leader Ed Miliband have voiced support for Canada, underscoring the strong ties and structural similarities between the two countries' parliaments. Sergeant-at-Arms Kevin Vickers is being commended across Canada for his swift and courageous actions that ended the attack—a rare use of his firearm during his long tenure. Video footage from inside Parliament captures the tense moments as security personnel responded, ultimately protecting parliamentarians and staff after the death of soldier Nathan Cirillo. UK officials remain wary of the potential for imitation attacks and continue refining security measures to safeguard Parliament and the public.

article_content: A hiker who became stranded at more than 13,000 feet in Colorado’s Rocky Mountains was rescued after search teams tracked fresh footprints in the snow and found the person alive but experiencing severe hypothermia, according to Chaffee County Search and Rescue North. Caught unprepared by sudden bad weather, the individual had no food, water, or proper cold-weather clothing—only a cotton hoodie and nothing to generate heat. As night fell and their condition worsened, the hiker abandoned the main trail and descended an avalanche chute—a natural path left by repeated avalanches—in hopes of reaching a road. Around 25 rescuers braved a fierce snowstorm to search for the lost hiker. At about 12:42 a.m. Thursday, members of the team discovered footprints in up to eight inches of fresh snow and followed the trail. After tracking the prints for nearly two hours, they came across what appeared to be an oddly shaped rock, which was actually the hiker, sitting upright in a fetal position and covered in snow. The rescuers found the hiker alive but with extreme hypothermia. It took them three hours to stabilize the person’s temperature before carefully lowering them down the slope using ropes. Once confident, the hiker managed to walk the rest of the way to a waiting ambulance. The rescue operation took place in Chaffee County, central Colorado, on the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains near the Continental Divide.

article_content: When I was a child in Adelaide, Australia, I loved games with clear, unambiguous rules, tough but fair puzzles, and the abstract simplicity of numbers and symbols. Unsurprisingly, I have been drawn to mathematics for as long as I can remember. Throughout my childhood, solving mathematical problems and equations was one of my favorite activities. I even participated in international high school mathematics competitions, racing to solve tricky problems within a few hours. I still recall the realization in college at Flinders University in Australia that mathematics was not just an abstract game but a tool to analyze and understand the modern world. Why are some statistics trustworthy and others not? Why are some investment strategies sound while others are risky? How can a computer search the entire internet in seconds but struggle to read a slightly distorted printed word? Why can satellites determine our locations with great accuracy but not predict the weather two weeks ahead? Knowledge of mathematics can answer these questions, making the world understandable and orderly instead of mysterious. Once I saw the power of this knowledge, and experienced the satisfaction when everything 'clicks,' I was hooked. I wanted to use mathematics to explore and understand as much of the world as possible. In 1992, at age 16, I moved to the United States to begin my Ph.D. at Princeton University in New Jersey. For several years, I divided my time between Australia and the United States, but by 1999 I had secured a permanent position in the Department of Mathematics at UCLA. By 2002, I married an American in the United States, and last year I became a U.S. citizen, while retaining my Australian citizenship. Of course, my life is more than just my work. I am a husband and father, and a proud citizen of both Australia and the United States. I identify strongly with both countries. I also enjoy good food, vacations, and movies, like anyone else. But mathematics is not only my profession—it is my hobby, and the area where I feel I contribute the most. So if I had to answer the question 'Who am I?' I would say, 'a mathematician.' The opinions expressed in this commentary are solely those of Terence Tao.

Sans surprise, les mathématiques m'ont attiré depuis aussi longtemps que je me souvienne. Durant toute mon enfance, résoudre des problèmes et des équations mathématiques était l'une de mes activités préférées. J'ai même participé à des concours internationaux de mathématiques au lycée, où il fallait résoudre des problèmes complexes en quelques heures. Je me souviens encore de la prise de conscience, à l'université Flinders en Australie, que les mathématiques n'étaient pas qu'un simple jeu abstrait, mais un outil pour analyser et comprendre le monde moderne. Pourquoi certaines statistiques sont-elles fiables et d'autres non ? Pourquoi certaines stratégies d'investissement sont-elles solides alors que d'autres sont risquées ? Comment un ordinateur peut-il rechercher tout Internet en quelques secondes mais peiner à lire un mot imprimé légèrement flou ? Pourquoi les satellites peuvent-ils déterminer notre position avec une grande précision mais sont incapables de prévoir la météo à deux semaines ? La connaissance des mathématiques peut répondre à ces questions, rendant le monde compréhensible et ordonné au lieu de mystérieux. Une fois que j'ai compris la puissance de ce savoir, et ressenti la satisfaction quand tout « s'emboîte » parfaitement, j'ai été conquis. Je voulais utiliser les mathématiques pour explorer et comprendre le monde autant que possible. En 1992, à 16 ans, j'ai déménagé aux États-Unis pour commencer mon doctorat à l'université de Princeton, dans le New Jersey. Pendant plusieurs années, j'ai partagé mon temps entre l'Australie et les États-Unis, mais en 1999, j'ai obtenu un poste permanent au département de mathématiques de l'UCLA. En 2002, j'ai épousé une Américaine aux États-Unis et, l'an dernier, je suis devenu citoyen américain tout en gardant ma citoyenneté australienne. Bien sûr, ma vie ne se résume pas à mon travail. Je suis mari et père, et fier citoyen de l'Australie et des États-Unis. Je m'identifie fortement à ces deux pays. J'apprécie aussi la bonne cuisine, les vacances et les films, comme tout le monde. Mais les mathématiques ne sont pas seulement ma profession, c'est aussi mon loisir, et le domaine où j'ai l'impression d'apporter le plus. Si on me demandait « Qui suis-je ? », je répondrais : « un mathématicien ». Les opinions exprimées dans ce commentaire sont uniquement celles de Terence Tao.

Luis Suarez has committed to Liverpool by agreeing to a new four-and-a-half-year contract. The Uruguayan forward, who leads the Premier League with 17 goals in 11 matches, is vital to Liverpool’s efforts to win the league title.

Arsenal sought to sign Suarez during the last transfer window with two bids, both of which Liverpool declined. Although Suarez’s previous contract ended in 2016, his impressive performance motivated him to continue at Anfield. In statements on Liverpool’s website, Suarez shared his enthusiasm, praising his teammates and expressing his ambition to win trophies with the club.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers described Suarez as a top-tier player and was delighted to secure his long-term services, emphasizing that Suarez is central to the club’s future.

Since joining Liverpool from Ajax in January 2011 under Kenny Dalglish, Suarez made an immediate impact. However, his tenure in England has included controversies—firstly, an eight-game suspension for racially abusing Manchester United’s Patrice Evra, and later a ten-game ban after biting Chelsea’s Branislav Ivanovic.

Amid rumors regarding a possible exit after these incidents, Arsenal submitted a £40 million plus £1 offer intended to activate a release clause, but Liverpool rejected it. Suarez returned from suspension in late September and quickly regained favor with fans, who are eager for Liverpool to reclaim their footballing dominance. Suarez has credited supporter loyalty as a significant reason for remaining at the club.

Looking forward, Suarez is expected to feature prominently for Uruguay in the next World Cup, where they will encounter England in the group stage.

article_content: Modern medicine has transformed lives, but many people still lack access to essential healthcare. In countries such as the United States and Cameroon, people are suffering because they cannot get the care they need. Three individuals—Georges Bwelle, Richard Nares, and Laura Stachel, recognized as top CNN Heroes—are making a real difference. Georges Bwelle: In Cameroon, there is just one doctor for every 5,000 people, according to the World Health Organization. In contrast, the United States has one doctor for every 413 people. Poverty is widespread, with two out of every five people living below the poverty line. Nearly three-quarters of healthcare spending is private, placing further strain on families. Motivated by the hardships faced by his father and fellow Cameroonians, Bwelle became a vascular surgeon at Yaounde's Central Hospital. He founded ASCOVIME, a nonprofit that provides free weekend clinics in rural areas. Since 2008, ASCOVIME and its volunteers have helped nearly 32,000 people, offering treatments for diseases like malaria, tuberculosis, and malnutrition. They also provide eyeglasses, crutches, and birth certificates, and perform minor surgeries with local anesthesia, often in improvised locations such as schoolhouses. Each clinic can serve about 500 people, some of whom travel up to 60 kilometers on foot. Richard Nares: In San Diego, families with children battling cancer often face difficulties traveling to chemotherapy appointments. Nares experienced this firsthand when his young son, Emilio, was treated for leukemia. He saw that transportation was a major barrier for many families. After Emilio passed away, Nares began driving families to appointments himself, and soon established the Emilio Nares Foundation in 2003 with hospital staff. The foundation set up a formal system to ensure no child misses vital cancer treatment due to lack of transportation. The program now helps many families across the county. Laura Stachel: While visiting Nigeria in 2008, Stachel, an obstetrician-gynecologist, saw the dangers mothers and babies faced because clinics lacked reliable electricity. Inadequate lighting delayed or compromised urgent care, and some women were even turned away. Alongside her husband, solar energy educator Hal Aronson, she developed portable solar energy kits to power medical equipment and provide proper lighting. Since 2009, these kits have been used in healthcare facilities throughout Africa, Asia, and Central America, improving conditions for patients and staff. Stachel hopes every woman can deliver her baby safely and with dignity.

Motivé par les difficultés rencontrées par son père et ses compatriotes, Bwelle est devenu chirurgien vasculaire à l’hôpital central de Yaoundé. Il a fondé ASCOVIME, une organisation à but non lucratif qui propose des cliniques gratuites le week-end dans les zones rurales. Depuis 2008, ASCOVIME et ses bénévoles ont aidé près de 32 000 personnes, en soignant des maladies comme le paludisme, la tuberculose et la malnutrition. Richard Nares : À San Diego, les familles d’enfants atteints de cancer rencontrent souvent des difficultés pour se rendre aux séances de chimiothérapie. Nares a vécu cela personnellement lorsque son jeune fils, Emilio, était soigné pour une leucémie. Il a constaté que le transport était un obstacle majeur pour de nombreuses familles. Après la disparition d’Emilio, Nares a commencé à conduire lui-même les familles à leurs rendez-vous, puis a fondé en 2003 la Emilio Nares Foundation avec le personnel de l’hôpital. La fondation a mis en place un système formel pour que jamais un enfant ne manque un traitement vital contre le cancer faute de transport. Le programme aide maintenant de nombreuses familles à travers tout le comté. Laura Stachel : Lors d’une visite au Nigeria en 2008, Stachel, obstétricienne-gynécologue, a constaté les dangers encourus par les mères et les bébés en raison du manque d’électricité fiable dans les cliniques. Un éclairage insuffisant retardait ou compromettait les soins d’urgence, et certaines femmes étaient même refoulées. Avec son mari, Hal Aronson, éducateur spécialisé en énergie solaire, elle a conçu des kits solaires portables permettant d’alimenter le matériel médical et d’éclairer correctement les lieux. Depuis 2009, ces kits sont utilisés dans des établissements de santé à travers l’Afrique, l’Asie et l’Amérique centrale, améliorant les conditions pour les patients et les équipes médicales. Stachel espère que chaque femme pourra un jour accoucher en toute sécurité et dignité.

article_content:
A recent study suggests that almost all extreme flooding events across Europe can be anticipated by examining major past floods in similar regions of the continent. So-called "megafloods," such as the catastrophic event on the Rhine’s tributaries in Germany in 2021, are rare and exceptionally severe, causing extensive damage and fatalities. These events are typically difficult to predict locally due to their infrequency and the limited availability of relevant data—often leaving flood defenses and emergency plans inadequate, which increases the impact on affected communities.

To understand the patterns behind these extreme floods, a team of European scientists, including experts from the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH), analyzed river discharge records—the volume of water flowing in a channel each second—from 8,000 monitoring stations across Europe spanning 1810 to 2021. Their research identified historic megafloods and found that 95.5% of these could have been forecast by referencing similar previous events in regions with comparable climates and variability in river discharge driven by factors such as rainfall and temperature.

Jamie Hannaford, Principal Hydrologist at UKCEH and a co-author of the study (published in Nature Geoscience), commented: “While the most extreme floods can be shocking for local communities, they are not usually surprising when assessed from a continental perspective. In the UK, risk assessments already consider events outside of local catchments, but this is generally limited to within national borders. Extending this approach to a European scale could offer crucial information about vulnerability to severe floods, helping to create ‘worst-case scenarios’ for more robust flood defense planning.”

The study cites the July 2021 flooding along the Rhine’s tributaries (affecting Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg) as being up to four times larger than any previously recorded event in the area. These floods caught residents and authorities off guard, resulting in over 200 deaths and causing an estimated $40 billion in damages. However, the researchers noted the discharge from this event was similar to that of the 2002 floods in northern Austria.

Other examples include the 2009 floods in the Derwent catchment in Cumbria, UK, which had a discharge 58% greater than the region’s second-largest recorded event—though still less extreme than similar events in Norwegian catchments.

The research, conducted by 56 scientists from 29 countries and led by the Vienna University of Technology, builds on a 2019 study that showed flood events are becoming more severe in north-western Europe—particularly in northern England and southern Scotland—while decreasing in intensity in southern and eastern parts of the continent.

article_content: For decades, consumer goods companies favored bold, lively packaging filled with bright colors, catchy text, and illustrations to catch shoppers’ eyes. The prevailing belief was that with thousands of products competing in supermarkets and big-box stores, every effort was needed to make products stand out. Recently, however, a shift toward simplicity has emerged. Minimalist packaging—simple, sparsely designed, and reminiscent of the minimalist art movement of the 1960s—has become more common. In art, minimalism stripped away the unnecessary, favoring spareness and abstraction. So why are companies now embracing simple, clean packaging? Recent research led by the author, together with marketing professors Rosanna K. Smith and Julio Sevilla, investigated whether shoppers actually prefer minimalist packaging—and if so, why. When Less is More To explore this, the research team studied over 1,000 consumer products like shampoo, deodorant, crackers, and cereal sold by the largest U.S. supermarket chain. Two research assistants rated each product’s packaging as simple or complex, and these ratings were averaged for a 'simplicity score.' The analysis revealed that products in simpler packaging typically had higher retail prices compared to similar products in more elaborate packaging. This suggests shoppers are willing to pay more for simplicity. Further experiments recruited university students, who evaluated various products for price willingness, perceived number of ingredients, and perceived purity. The findings indicated that consumers associated simple packaging with purity, assuming these products had fewer ingredients, preservatives, artificial colors, or flavors. People are often willing to pay more for products perceived as free from additives and chemicals, whether food, cleaning supplies, or personal care items. This perception occurred regardless of the product’s actual ingredient count. Many brands have adopted minimalist packaging. Kashi’s cereal boxes use muted colors and minimal product claims. Siggi’s yogurt features plenty of white space and clear imagery with key details. Native’s deodorant and body wash have simple backgrounds and clear typography. Hair care brands like OUAI and Hims use simplified typography and subdued colors to communicate essential information. When Less is Less However, minimalist packaging does not always spell success. The study found that generic brands—products with no prominent brand name and typically lower prices—didn’t benefit from minimalism in the same way. This may be because shoppers perceive simple packaging on generic products as a sign of low investment and potentially lower quality, rather than as an indicator of purity. Consumer goals also influence packaging preferences. When seeking healthier options, shoppers show a preference for simpler packaging and pay more. In contrast, when indulging in treats or junk food, people are more drawn to complex packaging, associating it with flavor and variety. In summary, minimalist design in packaging can increase a product's appeal, especially for health-conscious consumers, but its effect varies depending on the brand and consumer motivations. "Less is more" can hold true in packaging, but, at times, less is simply less. (Article republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. translated_content: Pendant des décennies, les entreprises de biens de consommation ont privilégié des emballages audacieux et colorés, remplis de textes accrocheurs et d’illustrations pour attirer l’attention des clients. On pensait alors qu’avec des milliers de produits en concurrence dans les grandes surfaces et supermarchés, il fallait tout faire pour se démarquer. Récemment, cependant, une tendance vers la simplicité s’est développée. Les emballages minimalistes — épurés, sobres et rappelant l’art minimaliste des années 1960 — deviennent de plus en plus répandus. Dans l’art, le minimalisme supprimait le superflu en préférant la simplicité et l’abstraction. Pourquoi les entreprises adoptent-elles maintenant des emballages simples et épurés ? Des recherches récentes menées par l’auteur, en collaboration avec les professeurs de marketing Rosanna K. Smith et Julio Sevilla, ont examiné si les consommateurs préfèrent réellement les emballages minimalistes — et pourquoi. Quand moins c’est plus Pour étudier ce phénomène, l’équipe de recherche a analysé plus de 1 000 produits comme des shampoings, déodorants, biscuits et céréales vendus par la plus grande chaîne de supermarchés des États-Unis. Deux assistants de recherche ont évalué la simplicité ou la complexité des emballages de chaque produit et ces notes ont été moyennées pour obtenir un ‘score de simplicité’. L’analyse a révélé que les produits au design d’emballage plus simple affichaient généralement des prix de détail plus élevés que des produits similaires aux emballages plus élaborés. Cela suggère que les clients sont prêts à payer plus pour la simplicité. D’autres expériences menées auprès d’étudiants universitaires leur ont demandé d’évaluer différents produits en fonction de leur disposition à payer, du nombre perçu d’ingrédients, et de la pureté ressentie. Les résultats montrent que les consommateurs associent la simplicité de l’emballage à la pureté, pensant que ces produits contiennent moins d’ingrédients, de conservateurs, de colorants ou d’arômes artificiels. Les gens sont souvent prêts à payer plus pour des produits perçus comme sans additifs ni produits chimiques, qu’il s’agisse d’aliments, de produits d’entretien ou de soins personnels. Cette impression existe quel que soit le nombre réel d’ingrédients. De nombreuses marques ont adopté ce style d’emballage minimaliste. Les boîtes de céréales Kashi utilisent des couleurs sobres et peu de revendications produit. Les yaourts Siggi’s offrent de grands espaces blancs et des images claires avec les informations essentielles. Les emballages Native pour le déodorant et le gel douche jouent la carte de la simplicité et de la typographie lisible. Les marques de soins capillaires comme OUAI et Hims utilisent aussi une typographie simple et des tons atténués pour communiquer l’essentiel. Quand moins c’est… moins Cependant, la simplicité ne fonctionne pas toujours. L’étude a constaté que les marques de distributeurs — c’est-à-dire sans nom de marque mis en avant, souvent vendus à bas coût — ne profitent pas autant de l’emballage minimaliste. Cela pourrait être parce que les clients perçoivent un emballage simple sur ces produits génériques comme un signe de faible investissement et de qualité potentiellement inférieure, plutôt qu’un gage de pureté. Les objectifs des consommateurs influencent aussi leurs préférences en emballage. Lorsqu’ils recherchent des options plus saines, ils préfèrent les emballages simples et acceptent de payer plus cher. En revanche, s’il s’agit de se faire plaisir avec des gourmandises, ils sont attirés par des emballages plus complexes, synonymes de goût et de variété. En résumé, le design minimaliste peut renforcer l’attrait d’un produit, surtout pour les consommateurs soucieux de leur santé, mais son effet varie selon la marque et la motivation du client. "Moins, c’est plus" est souvent vrai en matière d’emballage… mais parfois, moins, c’est juste moins. (Article republié de The Conversation sous licence Creative Commons. Retrouvez l’article original sur : https://phys.org/news/2023-11-food-toiletry-beauty-companies-minimalist.html)

article_content: A fatal accident occurred in rural Irkutsk Oblast, southern Russia, when a drunk tractor driver collided with a people carrier. According to authorities, Jacob Gavrilov, 43, was five times over the legal alcohol limit and was driving at night without headlights. His tractor crossed into the path of a vehicle carrying Joseph Zhdanov, 32, his wife Maria, 28, and a friend. All three occupants died instantly as a result of the crash. The impact crushed the car's roof beneath the tractor, causing fatal injuries. Gavrilov, who was not injured, fled the scene but was apprehended within hours after police tracked his footprints in the snow. Police spokesman Andrew Ankudinov said: "The tractor's scoop struck the car, killing those inside instantly. They had no warning, as the tractor had no lights. The driver tried to escape but was still over the legal limit when arrested."

article_content: John Higgins, the 2009 snooker world champion, is at the center of match-fixing allegations but remains firm that he has maintained integrity throughout his career. The News of the World, a British newspaper, claims Higgins, aged 34, agreed to accept a $398,000 bribe to deliberately lose frames in future matches, based on a covert meeting with journalists in Kiev, Ukraine. Making a statement on the BBC, the Scottish player categorically denied any involvement, saying, 'My conscience is completely clear. I have never fixed a snooker match or accepted a bribe. I’ve never deliberately missed a shot, lost a frame, or a match.' In response to the allegations, the sport’s governing body—the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA)—suspended Higgins from forthcoming tournaments pending investigation. The statement also revealed that Higgins’s manager, Pat Mooney, resigned from the WPBSA board after being linked to the Kiev meeting. Higgins, who has claimed the world title three times (1998, 2007, and 2009), acknowledges this as the biggest challenge of his career and has pledged full cooperation with the inquiry. He stressed his commitment to honesty over the years, saying, 'This is the most significant match of my life. I will work closely with snooker authorities throughout the investigation.' This is not the first scandal of this type in snooker—Australian player Quinten Hann was banned for eight years in 2006 for match-fixing breaches. Match-fixing is often driven by illegal betting groups offering bribes to manipulate sporting events. According to Simon Clare, spokesperson for British bookmaker Coral, strict gambling regulation helps prevent such corruption. Clare highlights that in countries with highly regulated betting, like Britain, there is no incentive for licensed companies to engage in corruption, as it would jeopardize their entire business. He adds that the real danger is present in places where gambling is illegal or unregulated.

Dans une déclaration à la BBC, le joueur écossais a nié formellement toute implication, déclarant : « Ma conscience est absolument tranquille. Je n’ai jamais truqué un match de snooker ni accepté de pot-de-vin. Je n’ai jamais raté un coup exprès, ni perdu intentionnellement un frame ou un match. » Suite à ces accusations, l’instance dirigeante du snooker—la World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA)—a suspendu Higgins des tournois à venir, en attendant les résultats de l’enquête. Le communiqué précise aussi que Pat Mooney, le manager de Higgins, a quitté le conseil d’administration de la WPBSA après son implication présumée dans la rencontre de Kiev. Je vais travailler main dans la main avec les autorités du snooker durant toute l’enquête. » Ce n’est pas la première fois qu’un scandale de ce genre secoue le snooker : l’Australien Quinten Hann a été suspendu huit ans en 2006 pour manipulation de matchs. article_content: Prince Charles visited GCHQ Scarborough today to celebrate 100 years of operations at the world’s oldest continuously running signals intelligence station. During his visit, the Prince unveiled a plaque to mark the centenary and officially opened new accommodation facilities at the site. He was then given a guided tour, which included viewing an exhibition about the site’s Second World War bunker—active until the 1970s. One highlight was a demonstration of the iconic Enigma encryption machine, used by British codebreakers to intercept and decode German messages during World War II. Charles learned about Scarborough’s major role in tracking the German battleship Bismarck before its sinking in 1941. Mike, a former GCHQ historian, demonstrated how the Enigma machine worked, while Charles had the opportunity to try it for himself. Meanwhile, the Duchess of Cambridge also shares a connection to historic codebreaking. She recently visited Bletchley Park, where her grandmother, Valerie Glassborow, served during the war. There, the Duchess met Lady Marion Body, who worked alongside her grandmother and Mary, Valerie’s twin, as part of the team that helped break the codes of the German Enigma machine. As a long-time patron of the intelligence services, this marked Prince Charles’s first visit to the North Yorkshire GCHQ facility, which now focuses on tackling major crime and cybersecurity threats. A GCHQ spokesperson expressed pride in hosting the Prince during such a significant year, emphasizing his ongoing support for the work of the UK’s intelligence agencies.
